issue:1000.body:
## Context

Split from #439 (closed). The two non-UI asks from that issue are already done: unbuffered long-running launches (#611) and the agent documentation (`skills/code-engineer/SKILL.md`). The remaining ask is tracked here.

## What's wanted

The session/job UI should show a process-level heartbeat for long-running work — live CPU, RSS, and last-output time — rather than relying on log-file mtime (or a quiet log) alone. Today a long job whose output is block-buffered looks stuck even while the process is busy.

## Scope / approach

TBD — the UI interaction still needs to be decided: where the telemetry lives, what granularity, how often it samples. Design to be confirmed before implementation.

Related: #434, #439.

issue:102.body:
> Sub-task of #84.

### Scope

The Python side of evolve can already start standalone; the TS orchestration layer (`services/api/src/evolution/`) needs to be migrated in.

### Dependencies

**Prerequisites:**

- #87 Adapter core: auth, connection pool, run and event log, storage and proxy framework: reverse proxy framework
- #91 Models, providers and global settings: the LLM callback proxy must use JiuwenSwarm's model configuration
- #96 runner, environment and execution pass-through: candidate programs are scored in the sandbox
- #98 artifact / provenance / CAS service (including papers): scorecard and CAS
- #101 idea-tree service: idea-tree is split out first so that evolve can be delivered on its own


### Interface list

5 in total: adapter-implemented 1, standalone backend 4. **1 need wrapper adaptation (approximate mapping + adapter-implemented).**

| Method | Path | Handling | Target | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/evolve/runs` | standalone backend | evolve service |  |
| GET | `/api/evolve/runs/:runId/events` | standalone backend | evolve service | JSON or SSE |
| GET | `/api/evolve/runs/:runId/candidates/:codeHash` | standalone backend | evolve service |  |
| POST | `/api/evolve/runs/:runId/stop` | standalone backend | evolve service /runs/:id/stop |  |
| POST | `/internal/evolve-llm/:runId/v1/chat/completions` | adapter-implemented | adapter LLM proxy | evolve sandbox callback, run-level token, no user auth |

### Non-interface tasks

- [ ] Migrate the TS orchestration layer (orchestrator, proposal, scorecard, dataset, preflight, store, etc.) into the evolve service, with its own storage
- [ ] LLM callback proxy `/internal/evolve-llm/:runId/v1/chat/completions`: run-level token, model pinned to the run, provided by the adapter
- [ ] Run event SSE, candidate source, stop
- [ ] No overlap with JiuwenSwarm's RSI and auto-harness (the former evolves candidate science programs, the latter evolves skills and harnesses)

### Acceptance

- [ ] Every interface row in the table above has an L1 contract diff case, or is explicitly marked "no migration needed"
- [ ] The events involved have an L2 golden trace
- [ ] Corresponding E2E cases, to be added once the 10-case list is settled
- [ ] For interfaces that need a wrapper, evaluate whether it can be eliminated (goal see #84), and record the conclusion in this issue

issue:1029.body:
## Summary

The containment added by #857 stops an escaped scheduler write from killing the API (the #816 defect), but two recovery gaps around it remain. Both were raised as `medium, suggestion` in the 2026-11-09 review of `9bf5077f7b4104564bdee110c4f001f7b1d4a403` (F5 and F4), and neither is implemented here.

### 1. An escape raised while re-reading the run list skips the backoff entirely

`services/api/src/runs/index.ts:3738` is the file's own `finally`:

```ts
    } finally {
      scheduledSessions.delete(sessionId);
      const remaining = await store.listSessionRuns(sessionId);
```

If that read rejects (an unreadable `session-runs/` directory — the same ownership/ACL misconfiguration the cap path exists for), the promise rejects before `schedulerEscapes` is touched or `setTimeout` is reached. The `.catch` at `:3762` logs `run_scheduler_failed` and that is all: no timer, no counter, no `run_scheduler_stopped`. The comment at `:3767-3773` names this read as one of the escape sites and states the reschedule "is delayed and capped", which is not true for it.

Measured on `9bf5077f` with `listSessionRuns` mocked to reject: exactly 2 calls, no retry, no rejection reaches the process. The session silently stops scheduling while a run is still `queued`.

**Fix shape suggested in the review:** make the `finally` body tolerant so the escape still takes the backoff branch.

```ts
      let remaining: SessionRun[] = [];
      try { remaining = await store.listSessionRuns(sessionId); } catch { /* fall through with escaped already set */ }
```

### 2. After the cap, the queued run has only a server log

`services/api/src/runs/index.ts:3747`: the sixth consecutive escape (delays 500 + 1000 + 2000 + 4000 + 8000 ms ≈ 15.5 s) logs `run_scheduler_stopped` and stops. The run stays `queued` on disk, and nothing schedules it again in process — `recoverSessionRuns` only handles `running`/`blocked`, so recovery depends on the bootstrap sweep (`services/api/src/bootstrap/platform.ts:747-770`) or another HTTP-triggered `scheduleSessionRuns`.

Measured on `9bf5077f` with `updateSessionRunStatusIfCurrent` made to fail and then to succeed: **6** transition attempts and **12** `listSessionRuns` calls in 19.5 s, then **0** attempts after the fault cleared, with the run still `queued`. Realistic causes are an ownership/ACL problem that outlives 15 s, a full disk, or a long scanner hold.

**Impact:** the chat never starts and the user sees neither a failure nor a message, while #816's expected result asks for an actionable error on the affected run when persistence cannot recover.

## What it should do

- An escape raised inside the `finally` must take the same delayed-and-capped path as an escape raised inside the loop; the comment already promises it.
- After the cap, the affected run should carry an error the API returns (mark it `failed`, or `interrupted` with a reason), or the stop should become a slow fixed retry — `SCHEDULER_RETRY_MAX_MS` already allows 30 s.

## Why this is not in #857

The review classified both as `medium, suggestion`, and the second is marked `[Needs a person]`: choosing between "fail the run with an actionable error" and "retry slowly forever" changes what a user sees after an unrecoverable state write, so it is a decision, not a mechanical fix. #857 carries only its must-fix (the retry closure dropped `executionGovernance`).

## Not implemented

Nothing in this issue is implemented and no pull request is open for it.

issue:1034.body:
## What happens

`test/journey-custom-mcp.spec.ts` → **"Agent uses selected custom MCP servers across runs"** (test declared at `:203`, step 6 `等待修复并恢复调用`, body at `:314`) fails at `test/journey-custom-mcp.spec.ts:332`:

```
  1) [mocked] › ../test/journey-custom-mcp.spec.ts:203:1 › journey-custom-mcp.spec › Agent uses selected custom MCP servers across runs › 6. 等待修复并恢复调用

    Error: expect(received).toBeGreaterThan(expected)

    Expected: > 2
    Received:   2

      330 |       expect(terminal.status, terminal.error).toBe("completed");
      331 |       const recovered = await invocations();
    > 332 |       expect(recovered.length).toBeGreaterThan(before);
          |                                ^
```

Everything before the assertion in step 6 succeeds: the repair card `执行受阻` shows `等待 MCP 修复` with the disabled source id, `GET /api/sessions/<id>/mcp/invocations` stays at 2 while blocked, the server is re-enabled, `已修复，重新检查` is clicked, and `waitForRunTerminal` returns `completed`.

What the run then shows: the assistant's last message in that run is `MCP RECOVERED`, which the scripted model only emits **after** its `mcp_recovered_call` step (`test/journey-custom-mcp.spec.ts:243-247`):

```ts
[
  { tool: "mcp_readiness", arguments: { action: "wait", reason: "This task requires the selected echo source", sourceIds: [second.id] } },
  { tool: "mcp_recovered_call", arguments: { sourceId: second.id, toolId: second.toolId, input: { text: "mcp recovered" } } },
  { text: "MCP RECOVERED" },
],
```

So the scripted model did emit `mcp_recovered_call`, and the run continued past it, but no MCP invocation was recorded for that turn: `/api/sessions/<id>/mcp/invocations` still lists exactly the 2 invocations from the earlier runs (`custom-cbf8e…`, `custom-cea28…`), and the captured trace resource `0000f751….json` holds the same 2. The recovered call therefore never reached `McpSourceCatalog`/broker (`packages/artifact-manager/src/mcp-workspace-tools.ts` `mcpReadiness.invoke`), and the failure is silent to the user: the run completes and the message claims recovery.

## Where it is seen (evidence only)

The same journey, same assertion, fails on three unrelated heads:

| run | job | head | shard window (UTC) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [42619667305](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42619667305) | [129188246374](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42619667305/job/129188246374) | `9bf5077f7b` (#857 tip) | 13:38–13:58 failure |
| [42622133086](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42622133086) | [129181494939](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42622133086/job/129181494939) | `87c5da950b` (`codex/conversation-proxy-resources`) | 13:39–13:59 failure |
| [42615122979](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42615122979) | [129160327871](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42615122979/job/129160327871) | `127bb1fdef` (merge queue, `pr-1005`) | 12:34–12:54 failure |

It also passes on other heads in the same window, including main running the journey while the two 13:3x failures were in flight:

- main `c3678320ac`: run [42621321893](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42621321893) job [129188930633](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42621321893/job/129188930633), `✓ 21 … Agent uses selected custom MCP servers across runs (44.4s)` at 13:39:17Z, shard success (13:34–13:49).
- main `9feafa2730`: run [42562181452](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42562181452) job [128981184690](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42562181452/job/128981184690), `✓ 21` at 04:38:35Z. That shard job is red overall because of a different journey (`journey-first-run.spec.ts:59`), so the shard verdict alone does not describe this journey.

`L2 E2E (mocked, standard-config)` outcomes for completed runs created between 11:30Z and 14:00Z (jobs read one by one; cancelled runs excluded): **3 failure / 16 success**, and the three failures are the table above. Two of the green runs are `dev2/fix/upload-windows-reserved-names` `0c5f26ab03` (13:33:34Z) and `dev/884-bug-comparing-two-binary-artifact-versio` `cefe1ebd79` (13:25:34Z).

## Not caused by the #857 diff

#857 (`9bf5077f7b`) changes exactly two files, `services/api/src/runs/index.ts` and `services/api/src/runs/index.test.ts` (+210/−23); the merge ref `fdf61b56798086e573368bc82120e91e8c5cc52b` for its failing job has parents `9feafa27` + `9bf5077f` and nothing else. The two other failing heads carry none of that diff. The failing journey exercises custom-MCP registration, the repair wait and `mcp_recovered_call` — not the scheduler's delayed retry pass. #857 is linked only because its shard run is one of the three observations, not as the cause.

## What is not yet known

Whether this is a product race (the recovered call is dropped or rejected after `catalog.refresh`, so a real user also loses the recovered invocation while the message claims it ran) or a test that stops waiting too early (it asserts the invocation list immediately after the terminal state). The two need different fixes, and the 3-of-19 rate above is the only discriminator so far: a deterministic loss is a product gap, an occasional one points at the wait.

Not run: local reproduction of the journey (20 consecutive runs on a local stack). The stack could not be started in the reporting environment — the pnpm store lives on a read-only home, the pinned Chromium download did not complete, and the JiuwenSwarm virtualenv install had not finished when this was filed. No code was changed for this report.

issue:107.body:
## Background

ScienceDiscovery is strengthening its end-to-end test coverage. We want to collect the complete user journeys that the community believes must remain continuously protected.

This RFC does not prescribe an implementation. It focuses on four questions: **What task is the user trying to complete? What outcomes must be observable? Does the scenario require a real model? Should it run as a pull-request gate or as a scheduled test?**

## How to contribute

Copy the comment template below and add one row for each proposed test scenario. Maintainers will periodically consolidate actionable feedback into the main table.

Guidelines:

- **Test scenario**: describe a complete flow from the user's goal, rather than an internal function or an isolated component.
- **Observations**: list user-visible outcomes and critical states, such as the final answer, tool calls, permissions, artifacts, citations, and recovery after a refresh.
- **Test method**: use `Mock LLM`, `Real LLM`, or `Both`, and explain why a real model is necessary when applicable.
- **Estimated token usage**: use `0 (scripted)` for Mock LLM cases; for Real LLM cases, estimate total input and output tokens for one run.
- **Estimated duration**: give the target duration for one case, excluding first-time dependency installation.
- **Priority**: use `P0` for basic platform availability, `P1` for core scientific capabilities, and `P2` for enhancements or corner cases.
- **Notes**: record environment requirements, external services, credentials, cost, side effects, candidate benchmark sources, or stability risks.

## Initial candidates

The following entries are both examples of the requested format and an initial backlog. The community is welcome to refine their priority, observations, estimates, and execution method.

| Test scenario | Observations | Test method (Mock or Real LLM) | Related feature | Estimated token usage | Estimated duration | Priority | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| Basic multi-turn conversation and refresh recovery | The run completes; the second turn uses conversation history; message order, terminal state, and refreshed content remain consistent | Mock LLM | Session, Agent Loop, History, SSE | 0 (scripted) | 2–3 min | P0 | No external network |
| Tool call, permission, and continued reasoning | Permission moves from pending to allowed; the tool executes once; its result returns to the model; the Agent continues and finishes | Mock LLM | Tool, Permission, Runner, Agent Loop | 0 (scripted) | 2–3 min | P0 | Use a safe local tool fixture |
| Plan creation, update, and completion | Plan and step states remain ordered and correct; updates do not block tools; the final state persists and recovers | Mock LLM | Plan, Context, Workspace UI | 0 (scripted) | 2–3 min | P0 | Use a deterministic tool-call sequence |
| Subagent delegation and result return | The child Agent lifecycle is complete; tool ownership is correct; the result returns to the lead Agent; reasoning continues; refresh restores the state | Mock LLM | Subagent, Team, Tool, Context | 0 (scripted) | 3–4 min | P0 | No external provider |
| Generate and deliver an artifact | The file exists; deliverables are distinct from temporary files; preview and download work; provenance is traceable; the final answer references the artifact | Mock LLM | Workspace, Artifact, Provenance, Tool | 0 (scripted) | 3–4 min | P0 | Use a local Python or Shell environment |
| Literature review | The Agent searches multiple sources, retrieves and extracts selected papers, produces traceable citations, handles source failures, and delivers a review artifact | Both | MCP, Literature Sources, Governed Download, PDF Extraction, Citation, Review | 0 mocked; 20k–60k real | 10–30 min | P1 | Real run requires network access and may depend on source availability |
| Evolve a solution | The Agent defines an objective and evaluation, runs iterative candidates, preserves checkpoints and logs, compares results, and delivers the best reproducible solution | Both | Evolve, Runner, Artifact, Provenance, Review | 0 mocked; 15k–50k real | 10–30 min | P1 | Candidate source: Terminal-Bench-Science |
| Data analysis | The Agent inspects an input dataset, selects and executes a valid analysis, validates intermediate results, and delivers reproducible code, figures, and conclusions | Both | Workspace, Python/R, Artifact, Provenance, Review | 0 mocked; 10k–40k real | 10–25 min | P1 | Candidate source: BiomniBench-DA |
| AI model workflow | The Agent prepares valid model inputs, invokes the model workload, exposes execution progress, preserves outputs and environment metadata, and explains the result | Both | Scientific Environment, Runner, NPU, Artifact, Provenance | 0 mocked; 10k–40k real | 15–60 min | P1 | Candidate tools/models: Protenix, ProteinMPNN, and similar workloads; hardware availability may constrain scheduling |
| Simulation tool workflow | The Agent prepares a valid simulation, invokes the selected simulator, reports progress and failures, and delivers reproducible configuration, logs, and results | Both | Scientific Environment, Runner, Tool, Artifact, Provenance | 0 mocked; 10k–40k real | 15–60 min | P1 | Real cases may require licensed software, large dependencies, or specialized hardware |
| Memory graph | Research outputs are written to the graph with correct identities and relations; retrieval returns relevant prior context; graph-backed citations remain traceable after refresh | Both | Memory Graph, Context, Provenance, Citation | 0 mocked; 8k–25k real | 5–20 min | P1 | Mocked case can use the local backend; scheduled case may use Neo4j |
| Agent team collaboration | The lead Agent decomposes work across multiple specialists; child scopes remain isolated; progress is observable; results return to the lead and are synthesized without loss or duplication | Both | Agent Team, Subagent, Context, Permission, Trajectory | 0 mocked; 15k–50k real | 10–30 min | P1 | Include concurrent child execution and one recoverable child failure |
| Idea Tree research | The Agent starts an Idea Tree run, expands and evaluates candidates, supports pause and resume, persists the tree, and delivers the selected result with its reasoning trail | Both | Idea Tree, Evolve, Workspace UI, Artifact, Provenance | 0 mocked; 15k–50k real | 10–30 min | P1 | Validate both tree state and the user-visible explorer |

## Comment template

Copy this table into a comment. Add more rows when proposing multiple scenarios.

| Test scenario | Observations | Test method (Mock or Real LLM) | Related feature | Estimated token usage | Estimated duration | Priority | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| Describe the complete user journey | List user-visible outcomes and critical states | Mock LLM / Real LLM / Both | List related capabilities | Estimate | Estimate | P0 / P1 / P2 | Add environment, cost, dependency, or stability notes |

## Suggested areas

- Agent Loop, tools, permissions, planning, and Agent teams;
- MCP, skills, Web Search, and Web Fetch;
- literature retrieval, paper download, PDF extraction, and scientific databases;
- artifacts, provenance, evidence, claims, citations, and review;
- context compression, long-running task continuity, and error recovery;
- local and remote Runners, scientific environments, NPU workloads, and background tasks;
- settings, onboarding, observability, and critical usability journeys;
- scenarios that can reveal issues only with a Real LLM or a real external service.

## Expected outcome

Community feedback will form a prioritized E2E case backlog, divided into:

- fast Mocked E2E cases executed for every pull request;
- comprehensive Mocked and Real LLM E2E cases executed on a schedule;
- real scientific-task acceptance tests executed before a release.

This issue is for collecting and clarifying test requirements. Implementation can be split into follow-up issues and pull requests by scenario.

issue:1165.body:
## 🚀 Background Description

#400 defined the desktop delivery design for Windows and macOS. The Windows implementation has landed through #639, #643 and #666. This feature completes the macOS side so that research users can install, configure, run and update ScienceDiscovery without using a terminal-based source workflow.

**Current status (2026-11-17):** PR #1156 has been merged into `main` as `5058334f09a7b28c7c56dbbdb199b2adf13adf74`. The 47-commit feature branch was squashed on merge, producing a tree byte-identical to reviewed head `43d54632`. Implementation and code review are complete; this issue remains open for the unchecked release-acceptance criteria below.

Related: #400 (parent delivery design), #666 (Windows shell counterpart), #34 (desktop window origin).

### Feature scope

- Adapt the shared Electron shell to macOS menus, window and quit behavior, data/log locations, system proxy and process-group lifecycle.
- Add a main-process Seatbelt startup probe and a sandbox-health status row. *(Updated by #1336, 2026-11-26: a probe failure no longer blocks startup — the bilingual standalone failure page was retired; the status row in Settings › Connection › Sandbox network is the single surface.)*
- Provide reproducible macOS payload assembly, DMG/ZIP packaging, Developer ID signing, notarization and staple.
- Support first acquisition through DMG and visible, prompt-only updates through notarized ZIP and `latest-mac.yml`.
- Provide in-app data cleanup plus an offline uninstall/reset companion script.
- Preserve Windows behavior through the `win_desktop/` → `application/` rename and packaging/CI updates.

### Target user journey

1. Download the signed DMG.
2. Drag ScienceDiscovery into Applications.
3. Choose the data directory on first launch.
4. Let the shell run Seatbelt and runtime startup checks in the background; sandbox health is shown in the Settings status row. *(Updated by #1336: a failed probe continues unsandboxed; the standalone error page is retired.)*
5. Configure the model and run a local scientific-research task.
6. Install later updates through the visible notarized ZIP/OTA flow.

## Design Ideas

### Architecture

Reuse JiuwenSwarm as the Agent foundation. This feature connects the scientific-research services and productizes them for macOS desktop users; it does not create a second Agent stack.

```text
Electron shell
Windows, menus, first-run wizard and process management
        ↓
Scientific-research services
API, task execution and runtime adaptation
        ↓
JiuwenSwarm
Existing Skills, Tools and Agent capabilities
```

Seatbelt is checked before execution and blocks entry to the main UI on failure. Data and logs are written outside the signed `.app` so the bundle remains read-only.

### Runtime and packaging entries

`application/` is one shared shell, not two applications. `main.ts` is the common Electron runtime entry; `platform/index.ts` reads `process.platform` and dispatches platform decisions.

```text
application/src/main.ts
        ↓
platform/index.ts
        ├── win32.ts    Windows paths, venv, tray and window behavior
        └── darwin.ts   macOS paths, venv, Dock and menu behavior
```

Runtime entry and packaging entry are separate concerns:

| Platform | Runtime entry | Packaging entry |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Windows | `application/src/main.ts` → `platform/index.ts` → `platform/win32.ts` | `scripts/package-sd-windows.sh`; payload assembly defaults to `win32-x64` |
| macOS | `application/src/main.ts` → `platform/index.ts` → `platform/darwin.ts` | `application/scripts/build-mac.sh`; clean machines start with `build-mac-from-scratch.sh`; payload uses `darwin-arm64` |

### Key decisions and constraints

| Decision | Implementation | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Platform facade | Shared types, `win32`, `darwin` and dispatch under `application/src/platform/` | One application with isolated, testable platform decisions |
| Sandbox | Seatbelt by default; #1336 adds an installation-level direct-execution opt-in (off by default), and a probe failure now continues unsandboxed with the status row in Settings › Connection › Sandbox network | Default installs stay sandboxed; unsandboxed operation is an explicit, documented choice rather than a silent degradation |
| Bundle integrity | Redirect writes out of `.app`; copy-mode bootstrap; propagate `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE`, including to MCP sidecars | A signed/notarized bundle must remain read-only |
| venv relocation | Convert build-host absolute symlinks to relative links into the bundled Python tree | Matches POSIX venv structure and makes the payload relocatable |
| Desktop runtime | v1 uses the build machine's uv-installed Python, as the Windows chain does. Darwin entries in `scripts/binary-release/runtimes.json` are for auditing and a possible future single-file edition; desktop assembly does not consume them in v1 | Aligns the delivery record with the actual DMG/ZIP payload |
| Signing modes | Ad-hoc smoke builds by default; Developer ID + notarization + staple require `SD_MAC_SIGN=1` | Prevents smoke builds from silently using release credentials |
| Updates | Notarized ZIP + `latest-mac.yml`, prompt-only, backend drain before restart | ZIP is the electron-updater carrier; DMG is acquisition-only |
| Architecture | arm64 only for v1 | Intel/x64 timing is deferred until there is concrete demand |
| CI boundary | Windows desktop distribution is covered by CI; macOS packaging and real-Mac acceptance currently rely on local evidence | Makes the current verification boundary explicit |

### Platform behavior

| Area | Windows | macOS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Installation | NSIS / `setup.exe` | DMG drag-install; notarized ZIP for updates |
| Runtime layout | `Scripts/`, `python.exe`, DLL | `bin/`, `python`, symlinks |
| Execution safety | Existing Provider path | Seatbelt by default; explicit direct-execution opt-in (#1336) |
| System proxy | Registry | `scutil --proxy` |
| Uninstall | Uninstaller + optional deep cleanup | Trash + in-app cleanup + offline uninstall/reset script |

Both platforms share the Electron shell, Node services, Python runtime and JiuwenSwarm.

### Uninstall and reset behavior

The Help menu provides in-app uninstall/data cleanup. `application/scripts/uninstall-mac.command` adds four offline modes: full uninstall, app-only uninstall, data reset and read-only path inspection. It backs up selected critical data, moves deleted items to Trash and checks for leftover backend processes. The script is a separate Release asset and is not embedded in the DMG/ZIP.

### UI and failure states

The packaged desktop flow does not display the SPA `SetupWizard` self-check step. The main process probes Seatbelt once per session in the background: the verdict — success or failure — is surfaced as a status row in Settings › Connection › Sandbox network. A failure no longer blocks initialization; the standalone bilingual error page was retired with it (owner decision recorded in #1336, 2026-11-26).

The SPA self-check component remains covered by component tests, but its pending, success and in-component failure renders are not part of the packaged desktop user journey and are therefore not presented as product screenshots here.

**Sandbox health status row (设置 › 连接 › 沙箱网络)**

The standalone Seatbelt error page (`seatbelt-error.html`) and its launch-blocking gate were retired in #1336 (2026-11-26): a failed probe no longer replaces the window — the app continues unsandboxed while the status row shows the failure with actionable diagnostics, and the opt-in direct-execution tier keeps its per-run confirmation armed.

### Non-goals for this delivery

- No Keychain/safeStorage migration; retain AES-256-GCM + `0600` file-based secrets.
- No simultaneous Intel/x64 release.
- No `.pkg` installer.
- No second Agent framework or duplicate JiuwenSwarm capability stack.
- The website `/install` Mac card and telemetry changes are outside this repository.

## Involved Public APIs

No backend public API changes. The shell exposes `sdShell.platform` through preload so the renderer reads the main-process platform value rather than relying on UA sniffing. The platform facade is internal to the shell, and the backend start-stack contract remains unchanged.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

| Module | Relevance and required verification |
| --- | --- |
| `application/scripts/assemble-backend.mjs`, `application/scripts/lib/assemble-platform.mjs` | Add platform-aware payload assembly; Windows remains the default dialect. Verify payload layout and required files for both platforms. |
| `scripts/binary-release/runtimes.json` | Contains darwin audit entries that desktop assembly does not consume in v1; do not treat them as evidence of a separately pinned desktop Python runtime. |
| `application/scripts/after-pack-trim-locales.cjs` | Supports Windows dash-pak and macOS `.lproj` layouts; verify both packaging paths. |
| `scripts/package-sd-windows.sh` | Supports `application/` with compatibility fallback; Windows install, upgrade and uninstall require regression coverage. |
| `application/src/main.ts`, `stack.ts`, `proxy.ts`, `sandbox-probe.ts`, `updater.ts`, `uninstall-data.ts` | Own shell lifecycle, networking, safety, updates and cleanup; verify platform dispatch and failure paths. |
| `apps/desktop/src/views/SetupWizard.tsx` and text contracts | The packaged shell opens this wizard at model configuration and skips its self-check step; verify that handoff and retain component-test coverage for the non-packaged flow. |
| `services/api` MCP sidecar launch | Propagates `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE` into the SDK's minimal child-process environment; verify child-process behavior remains unchanged on other platforms. |

## Test Design and Test Plan

### Test environment

Existing local development-machine evidence was collected on:

**macOS (arm64)**

| Item | Environment |
| --- | --- |
| Model | MacBook Pro, MacBookPro17,1 |
| Chip | Apple M1, 4 performance cores + 4 efficiency cores |
| Memory | 8 GB |
| Architecture | arm64, Apple Silicon |
| OS | macOS 14.8.9, build 23J631 |
| Node.js | v24.22.1 in the local terminal |

**Windows (x64)**

| Item | Environment |
| --- | --- |
| Model | Lenovo laptop |
| CPU | AMD Ryzen 7 5800H, 8 cores / 16 threads, 3.2 GHz, 16 MB L3 |
| Memory | 32 GB (2×16 GB DDR4-3200, dual channel) |
| GPU | NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 Laptop GPU (8 GB GDDR6) + integrated Radeon |
| Disk | SK hynix 1TB NVMe SSD |
| OS | Windows 11 Pro 64-bit, Build 26300 |

These environments document existing local evidence; they do not replace release acceptance on a clean macOS machine.

### Measured timing data (v0.4.0)

Wall-clock measurements captured on the machines above. First initialization excludes network downloads (the runtime ships inside the package); first-conversation latency includes the round trip to the connected model API.

| Platform | Installer size | Install time | First initialization | Warm start | First conversation | Uninstall |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| macOS (arm64, DMG) | 578 MB | 43s | 12.3s | 7.2s | 9.8s | — |
| Windows (x64, setup.exe) | 587 MB | 1min30s | 11.4s | 10.5s | 10.6s | 25.4s |

> *Reference measurements of WorkSwarm on the same machines:*
>

> **The startup timing guard: per-component hang ceilings** (`application/scripts/perf-budget.json`, first-session table; the warm table keeps the same ceilings with shorter baselines and no unpack).
>
> What the three numbers mean, to avoid misreading:
> - **Hang ceiling (hard red line):** a component still short of its ready/healthy event past this value — or a missing event pair — is judged a hang: the gate exits 1, CI goes red. It is a loose tripwire, **NOT an expected duration**.
> - **Measured baseline (expected reference):** what the signed build actually takes on a healthy launch.
> - **Regression line (soft):** baseline × 1.4 — warn first, hard-fail on the second consecutive strike. Gradual drift trips here long before the ceiling.
>
> | Component (event pair) | Hang ceiling | Measured baseline (expected reference) | How the ceiling was derived |
> | --- | --- | --- | --- |
> | shell-boot (module-load → stack-spawned) | 30s | 6.2s | Loosened from measurement: unpack is ~1GB I/O-bound, 20s+ on slow disks; re-reviewed 20s → 30s |
> | unpack (first sessions only) | 30s | 2.0s | ~1GB I/O-bound extract, 20s+ on slow disks; same 30s floor as shell-boot |
> | runner-ready | 30s | 0.2–0.4s | Sub-second op; the 30s is a stall floor (GC/disk contention), not a multiplier |
> | memory-graph-ready | 45s | 0.6–2.9s | Healthy range already spans ~5× (cold imports); 45s covers the worst healthy case |
> | evolve-ready | 45s | 0.8–2.9s | Same: healthy range spans ~4×; 45s covers the worst healthy case |
> | api-ready (api-spawn → HEALTH-200, full-stack marker) | 60s | 3.2–3.6s | Cold-runner dependency imports can take tens of seconds; 60s covers the worst healthy case |
> | jw-ready (spawn-jw-app → IS-UP) | 120s | 4.8s (warm) / 7.9s (first) | Loosened: a from-scratch reinstall can take minutes |
> | agent-ready | 180s | 8.2–18.8s | **Pinned to the runtime constant `AGENT_READY_TIMEOUT_MS`** (= jw 120s + 60s watch/adapter margin; the gate and the runtime blow together, a unit test reads the source to keep them from drifting) |
> | shell-ui (AGENT-READY → loadUi-loadURL) | 15s | 0.1–0.2s | Sub-second UI load; 15s is the minimum floor against GC/Spotlight stalls (event pair corrected in review) |
> | warmup-done (AGENT-READY → [warmup] 200) | 60s | 0.4–1.3s | **Pinned to `FIRST_CHAT_WARMUP_TIMEOUT_MS`**; cold full-catalog measured ~48s, 60s just covers it (only 25% headroom — raise together if the catalog grows) |
>
> Derivation (why so wide): the ceiling only waits for events that never arrive — width changes how soon a hang is reported, not whether it is, and gradual drift trips the regression line (baseline × 1.4) first. The big multipliers come from the reference frames differing: the baseline column is a healthy dev machine's median, while the ceiling is sized for the **worst healthy case** (slow disk / loaded runner / cold caches / fresh install — warmup-done's 60s covers the measured 48s cold-catalog path, not the 1.3s warm path; jw-ready's 120s covers a from-scratch reinstall; agent-ready's 180s mirrors the runtime constant `AGENT_READY_TIMEOUT_MS`; sub-second components get a ~15s floor against transient stalls). Worst-case serial chain 320s < the 600s cold-start backstop.

#400 确定了 Windows 和 macOS 双平台桌面交付设计，Windows 侧已经通过 #639、#643 和 #666 落地。本需求补齐 macOS 侧能力，让科研用户无需通过终端运行源码，也能完成 ScienceDiscovery 的安装、配置、任务执行和更新。

**当前状态（2026-11-17）：** PR #1156 已合入 `main`，合并提交为 `5058334f09a7b28c7c56dbbdb199b2adf13adf74`。原功能分支的 47 个提交在合并时压缩为一个提交，合并后的代码树与评审头 `43d54632` 逐字节一致。实现和代码评审已经完成；本 Issue 继续跟踪下方尚未完成的发布验收项。

关联：#400（交付总设计）、#666（Windows 桌面壳）、#34（桌面窗口起点）。

### 需求范围

- 让共用 Electron 壳适配 macOS 菜单、窗口与退出行为、数据和日志目录、系统代理及进程组生命周期。
- 由主进程在启动时检查 Seatbelt，沙箱健康显示于设置的状态行。*（#1336 于 2026-11-26 更新：探测失败不再阻断启动——中英文独立错误页已退役，设置 › 连接 › 沙箱网络的状态行是唯一展示面。）*
- 提供可复现的 macOS 载荷组装、DMG/ZIP 出包、Developer ID 签名、公证和 staple。
- 首次安装使用 DMG，后续更新使用公证 ZIP 和 `latest-mac.yml`，更新过程可见且只提示、不静默。
- 提供应用内数据清理，以及独立的离线卸载／重置脚本。
- 在 `win_desktop/` 更名为 `application/` 后，保持 Windows 行为、打包链和 CI 兼容。

### 目标使用流程

1. 下载签名 DMG。
2. 将 ScienceDiscovery 拖入 Applications。
3. 首次启动时选择数据目录。
4. 由桌面壳在后台执行 Seatbelt 和运行时启动检查；沙箱健康状态显示在设置的状态行。*（#1336 更新：探测失败时继续无沙箱启动，独立错误页已退役。）*
5. 配置模型并运行本地科研任务。
6. 后续通过可见的公证 ZIP／OTA 流程完成更新。

## 设计思路

### 技术架构

继续复用 JiuwenSwarm 的 Agent 底座。本需求负责接入科研服务并完成 macOS 桌面产品化，不再另建一套 Agent 能力。

```text
Electron 桌面壳
窗口、菜单、首启向导与进程管理
        ↓
科研服务
API、任务执行与运行时适配
        ↓
JiuwenSwarm
复用既有 Skills、Tools 与 Agent 能力
```

Seatbelt 在执行前先自检，沙箱健康状态显示于设置的状态行；数据和日志写入签名 `.app` 之外，保证应用包保持只读。*（#1336 更新：探测失败不再阻断启动，继续无沙箱运行。）*

### 运行时入口与出包入口

`application/` 是双平台共用的一套桌面壳，不是两套应用。`main.ts` 是公共 Electron 运行时入口，`platform/index.ts` 根据 `process.platform` 分发平台决策。

```text
application/src/main.ts
        ↓
platform/index.ts
        ├── win32.ts    Windows 路径、venv、托盘与窗口行为
        └── darwin.ts   macOS 路径、venv、Dock 与菜单行为
```

运行时入口和出包入口不是一回事：

| 平台 | 运行时入口 | 出包入口 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Windows | `application/src/main.ts` → `platform/index.ts` → `platform/win32.ts` | `scripts/package-sd-windows.sh`，载荷默认按 `win32-x64` 组装 |
| macOS | `application/src/main.ts` → `platform/index.ts` → `platform/darwin.ts` | `application/scripts/build-mac.sh`；干净机器先执行 `build-mac-from-scratch.sh`，载荷按 `darwin-arm64` 组装 |

### 关键决策与约束

| 决策点 | 当前实现 | 原因 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 平台门面 | `application/src/platform/` 放置公共类型、win32、darwin 和统一分发入口 | 保持一套应用，隔离平台差异并便于单测 |
| 沙箱 | 默认 Seatbelt 沙箱；#1336 新增安装级直连执行 opt-in（默认关闭），探测失败时继续无沙箱启动并在状态行显示 | 默认安装保持沙箱；无沙箱运行是显式、有文档的选择而非静默降级 |
| 签名包完整性 | 写入改道到 `.app` 外；bootstrap 使用拷贝模式；`PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE` 传递到 MCP sidecar | 签名、公证后的应用包必须保持只读 |
| venv 搬迁 | 把构建机绝对路径符号链接改为指向包内 Python 的相对链接 | 符合 POSIX venv 结构，保证载荷可以迁移 |
| 桌面运行时 | v1 使用构建机上由 uv 安装的 Python，与 Windows 链一致；`scripts/binary-release/runtimes.json` 的 darwin 条目用于版本审计和未来可能的单文件版本，桌面组装暂不消费 | 让交付说明与 DMG/ZIP 的实际载荷一致 |
| 签名模式 | 默认 ad-hoc 冒烟；显式设置 `SD_MAC_SIGN=1` 才使用 Developer ID、公证和 staple | 避免冒烟构建误用正式凭证 |
| 更新 | 公证 ZIP＋`latest-mac.yml`，只提示，重启前停稳后端 | electron-updater 使用 ZIP，DMG 只负责首次安装 |
| 架构 | v1 仅支持 arm64 | Intel/x64 等有明确需求后再安排 |
| CI 边界 | Windows 桌面包分发由 CI 看护；macOS 出包和真机验收目前依靠本地证据 | 明确当前验证边界 |

### 平台行为差异

| 方面 | Windows | macOS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 安装 | NSIS / `setup.exe` | DMG 拖拽安装，公证 ZIP 用于更新 |
| 运行时结构 | `Scripts/`、`python.exe`、DLL | `bin/`、`python`、符号链接 |
| 执行安全 | 既有 Provider 路径 | 默认 Seatbelt；显式直连执行 opt-in（#1336） |
| 系统代理 | 注册表 | `scutil --proxy` |
| 卸载 | 卸载器＋可选深度清理 | 废纸篓＋应用内清理＋离线卸载／重置脚本 |

双平台共用 Electron 壳、Node 服务、Python 运行时和 JiuwenSwarm。

### 卸载与重置行为

帮助菜单提供应用内卸载和数据清理。`application/scripts/uninstall-mac.command` 提供四种离线模式：完全卸载、只卸载应用、数据重置和仅查看路径。脚本会备份指定的关键数据，将删除内容移入废纸篓，并检查后端残留进程。该脚本作为 Release 独立资产分发，不放进 DMG/ZIP。

### 界面与失败状态

打包后的桌面流程不展示 SPA `SetupWizard` 中的自检步骤。主进程在后台探测 Seatbelt（每会话一次）：探测结果——成功或失败——统一显示为设置 › 连接 › 沙箱网络的状态行。失败不再阻断初始化；中英文独立错误页随之退役（owner 决策见 #1336，2026-11-26）。

SPA 自检组件仍由组件测试看护，但其自检中、自检通过和组件内失败状态不属于打包桌面版的真实使用流程，因此不再作为产品截图展示。

**沙箱健康状态行（设置 › 连接 › 沙箱网络）**

Seatbelt 独立错误页（`seatbelt-error.html`）及其启动阻断门禁已于 #1336（2026-11-26）退役：探测失败不再替换窗口——应用继续无沙箱启动，状态行显示失败详情与可操作诊断；opt-in 直连执行档保持每次运行确认武装。

### 本期非目标

- 不迁移 Keychain/safeStorage，继续使用 AES-256-GCM＋`0600` 文件密钥方案。
- 不同时发布 Intel/x64 版本。
- 不增加 `.pkg` 安装器。
- 不另建 Agent 框架，也不重复实现 JiuwenSwarm 已有能力。
- 官网 `/install` 的 Mac 卡片和遥测改动不在本仓范围内。

## 涉及的公开接口

后端公开 API 没有变化。壳层通过 preload 增加 `sdShell.platform`，让前端读取主进程的真实平台值，而不是通过 UA 猜测。平台门面属于壳内部实现，后端起栈契约保持不变。

## 测试设计与测试计划

| 安装包运行时完整性 | Python、依赖、符号链接、补丁和字节码完整 | `build-mac.sh`、`pyc-budget.test.ts`：A1 导入冒烟、A1b 运行时探针、A2 必需文件、A6 字节码，以及路径、符号链接和补丁链门禁 |

| 启动性能看护 | 健康启动不悄悄退化成挂死：每个组件都在报错上限内到达 ready/healthy 事件 | `perf-gate.mjs` 两层看护接入 CI（`macos-desktop` job，`--hang-only`）：经 `perf-smoke-mac.sh` 真实启动打包后的 `.app`，用 `perf-budget.json` 报错上限（H1-H9）判定首启 `shell.log`；实测日志以 `perf-smoke-shell-log-<sha>` artifact 上传——经 #1374 落地 |

启动性能看护在上述矩阵之后加入：它是针对「静默挂死」类的机器检查层，判定的正是真机发布验收所读的同一份日志。

## 验收标准

### 工程检查

### 发布验收

- [ ] **干净 macOS 环境验收**：下载 DMG → 拖入 Applications → 完成向导 → 跑通一个小任务；没有意外的 Gatekeeper 拦截，`spctl` 对 `.app` 和 DMG 均放行。

- [ ] **发布 CI 策略**：明确 v1 是否接受人工真机证据作为发布门禁，还是必须增加 macOS CI 任务。*更新：macOS CI 耗时看护已经 #1374 落地（`macos-desktop` job 冒烟启动打包 `.app` 并以 `--hang-only` 判定首启 `shell.log`，上传实测日志）——人工真机证据仍为基线来源，门禁在每个 PR/push 上覆盖静默挂死类风险。等 owner 对此记录签字确认。*

适用的工程检查和出包检查必须通过以下命令：

```bash
bash application/scripts/build-mac.sh

```

## 补充信息

- 合并提交 `5058334` 记录 application 测试 **345/345**（macOS 上完整执行 `pnpm --dir application test`）。上游合入的导出相关测试分布在三个文件：`export-history.test.ts`（7 项）、`export-state.test.ts`（4 项）与 `export-tokens.test.ts`（5 项）。`apps/desktop` **30 项通过**为 `pnpm --dir apps/desktop test` 的全量结果（`tests/*.test.ts(x)`）。类型检查通过；Windows 分发门禁的 CI 契约检查通过。
- v0.4.0 冒烟 DMG 为 **578 MB**；从零出包流程已完成三次递进的 clean-room 复验。
- 签名、公证链已经实测通过。v1 凭证持有人与发布执行人（F1）：Developer ID Application 证书属 **Haowen Zhong**（Apple Developer 团队 **UGV44NUA6W**）；公证所用 App Store Connect 密钥与 `sd-notary` 钥匙串档案同由其保管，正式 macOS 发布亦由其执行。
- 官网 `/install` 和遥测工作需要在本仓之外单独跟踪。
- Intel/x64 分发继续后置。
- **启动性能看护（已合并，#1374 → `9c74af8b`）。** shell/start-stack/jiuwenswarm 打进 `shell.log` 的毫秒级打点现在由两层门禁判定：绝对 **hang 层**（报错上限 H1-H9 落在 `application/scripts/perf-budget.json`；缺失事件对即挂死信号；agent-ready 上限与运行时常量 `AGENT_READY_TIMEOUT_MS` 对齐，门禁与运行时同时引爆）+ 机器本地 **regression 层**（基线 × 1.4，warn-first、二振出局——只在有基线的机器上判定，因此 CI 以 `--hang-only` 运行）。`macos-desktop` CI job 真实启动打包后的 `.app`（`perf-smoke-mac.sh`：向导状态备份/恢复、轮转安全的日志增量锁定、信号陷阱），以 `--hang-only` 判定首启日志并上传实测日志（`perf-smoke-shell-log-<sha>`，14 天）作证据。合并前已在真实 macOS runner 端到端实证（fork Package@macos run 45541198600：ok 10 / hang 0 / exit 0，agent-ready 实测 20.9s，远低于 180s 上限）。解析器/判定层/门禁/冒烟均为纯新增，不改任何运行时行为。P2（向导/reuse 路径打点）与 P3-2（发布跑基线采集）留作后续。

> **启动性能看护：组件报错上限表**（`application/scripts/perf-budget.json` 首启档；热启档上限同值、基线更短、无 unpack）。
>
> 三层数值语义，防误读：
> - **报错上限（硬红线）**：组件超过该值仍未到达 ready/healthy 事件、或事件对缺失 → 判「挂死」→ 门禁 exit 1 → CI 红。它是宽松探测线，**不是预期值**。
> - **实测基线（预期参考）**：签名包健康启动的实际耗时——预期量级。
> - **回归警戒线（软线）**：基线 × 1.4；超先警告，连续第二次硬失败。渐进退化在此提前报警，不用等到碰上限。
>
> | 组件（事件对） | 报错上限 | 实测基线（预期参考） | 上限如何而来 |
> | --- | --- | --- | --- |
> | shell-boot（module-load → stack-spawned） | 30s | 6.2s | 实测放宽：unpack 为 ~1GB I/O 主导，慢盘机器可 20s+，复审从 20s 放宽到 30s |
> | unpack（仅首启档） | 30s | 2.0s | ~1GB 解压 I/O 主导，慢盘可 20s+，与 shell-boot 同 30s 地板 |
> | runner-ready | 30s | 0.2~0.4s | 亚秒操作；上限是防瞬时卡顿（GC/磁盘争用）的地板值，非按倍数定 |
> | memory-graph-ready | 45s | 0.6~2.9s | 健康范围近 5 倍（冷依赖导入）；45s 罩最坏健康场景，防卡顿地板 |
> | evolve-ready | 45s | 0.8~2.9s | 同上：健康范围已达 4 倍，45s 罩最坏健康场景 |
> | api-ready（api-spawn → HEALTH-200，全栈标志） | 60s | 3.2~3.6s | 冷 runner 依赖导入可达几十秒，60s 罩最坏健康场景 |
> | jw-ready（spawn-jw-app → IS-UP） | 120s | 4.8s（热）/ 7.9s（首） | 实测放宽：从零重装可到分钟级 |
> | agent-ready | 180s | 8.2~18.8s | **对齐运行时常量 `AGENT_READY_TIMEOUT_MS`**（= jw 120s + watch 轮询/adapter 启动 60s 余量；门禁与运行时同时引爆，单测读源码钉死防漂移） |
> | shell-ui（AGENT-READY → loadUi-loadURL） | 15s | 0.1~0.2s | 亚秒 UI 加载；15s 是防 GC/Spotlight 瞬时卡顿的最低地板（事件对曾误配，复审已修正） |
> | warmup-done（AGENT-READY → [warmup] 200） | 60s | 0.4~1.3s | **对齐 `FIRST_CHAT_WARMUP_TIMEOUT_MS`**；冷态全量 catalog 实测 ~48s，60s 恰好罩住（余量仅 25%，catalog 膨胀需同步上调） |
>
> 推导口径（为何这么宽）：上限只等「永不到来」的事件——宽窄只影响报警早晚、不影响是否报警，渐进变慢由回归警戒线（基线 × 1.4）先抓。倍数看着大是因为参照系不同：基线列是开发机健康启动的中位数，上限对着的是**最坏健康场景**（慢磁盘/高负载 runner/冷缓存/从零安装——warmup-done 60s 罩的是冷态 catalog 实测 48s 而非热态 1.3s，jw-ready 120s 罩从零重装，agent-ready 180s = 运行时常量 `AGENT_READY_TIMEOUT_MS` 的镜像，亚秒组件另有 ~15s 起的防瞬时卡顿误报地板）。串行最坏 320s < 冷启兜底 600s。

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] The environment and the exact run are named below, so this is reproducible from the job log alone.

## 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

The `UT` job reports **success** while executing **no Python test at all**. A failing Python case therefore cannot turn the gate red — the suites exist, are tagged, and are silently never run.

### What was observed

On PR #1231 (head `49354a23ca6a262bc79a6022c38dc675798143ba`), job **`UT`** = `134700142074` in run `44274693462` finished `success`. Its executed plan contains 681 entries:

| extension | count |
| --- | --- |
| `.ts` | 474 |
| `.tsx` | 159 |
| `.mjs` | 43 |
| none | 5 |
| **`.py`** | **0** |

Two independent greps over the same job log:

```
services/evolve/tests   -> 0 occurrences
.py::                   -> 0 occurrences
```

The environment for Python *was* prepared in that same job, so this is not a skipped setup:

```
2026-11-18T09:20:34.3171967Z Prepare: uv sync --project services/evolve --locked --extra test --extra candidates
2026-11-18T09:20:35.6487682Z Prepare: uv pip install --python .../services/evolve/.venv/bin/python coverage>=7.6,<8
```

### What the runner is supposed to collect

`test/support/tagged/profiles.mjs:112-113`:

```js
export const pythonProjects = Object.freeze(['paper', 'gateway', 'memory-graph', 'evolve', 'adapter']);
export const pythonSources = project => `services/${project}/tests/test_*.py`;
```

`test/support/tagged/shared.mjs:257-261`:

```js
if(needUT)for(const project of pythonProjects){
  const dir=join(outputDir,`collect-${project}`);mkdirSync(dir,{recursive:true});
  const sources=[...globSync(pythonSources(project),{cwd:root})].sort();
  catalog.push(...collect({root,files:sources,outputDir:dir,python:python(project),pytestPlugins:pythonPlugins[project]??[],env:projectEnv(env,project)}));
}
```

So for `evolve` the scope is `services/evolve/tests/test_*.py` — 20+ files exist there — and that loop runs under the same `needUT` that produced the `uv sync` above.

### Why it matters

Every Python suite under `services/*/tests` is currently unguarded on PRs. This is not theoretical: PR #1231 adds two regression cases for a UTF-8 decode bug, both tagged `category:ut`, and neither is executed by the job that is supposed to gate them. Any existing Python test could regress without any PR check noticing.

Note that the same plan shows no `.py` for **any** of the five `pythonProjects`, not only `evolve`.

## Detailed Environment Information Description

- Repository state: `main` at `eb5f66e80ac7308bb49a1842737d8bafb3bd2a4e`; the run above is on PR #1231 head `49354a23ca6a262bc79a6022c38dc675798143ba`.
- CI: GitHub Actions, the `UT` job of `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, run `44274693462`, job `134700062...`/`134700142074`, `ubuntu` runner, 2026-11-18T09:18Z.
- Toolchain: `pnpm@11.1.2`, Node 22, Python 3.12 through `uv` (the job's own `Prepare:` lines above).
- Local contrast: running the same files directly works — `python3 -m pytest services/evolve/tests/test_idea_research.py` collects and runs them under a normal interpreter, so the files themselves collect; the discrepancy is in the tagged runner's catalog.

## Additional Information

Reproduce without any code change: open any recent `UT` job log and count `Run N/M:` lines by extension — the Python ones are absent while `Prepare: uv sync --project services/<name>` lines are present for all five Python projects.

Possibly related: `collect()` shells out to `python -m pytest ... --collect-only` (`test/support/tagged/coordinator.mjs:98`). If that collection returns zero entries or fails quietly, the run still reports success because nothing was planned. Worth checking whether the pytest invocation in the runner resolves the project interpreter and the `science_tags` plugin, and whether an empty catalog for a `pythonProjects` entry should be an error rather than silence.

I found this while fixing #1229 in #1231; that PR deliberately does **not** touch the collection code — it is the encoding fix only.

## Version Information

- `main`: `eb5f66e80ac7308bb49a1842737d8bafb3bd2a4e` (2026-11-18)
- Affected job: `UT`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
- Runner files: `test/support/tagged/profiles.mjs`, `test/support/tagged/shared.mjs`, `test/support/tagged/coordinator.mjs`

issue:1237.body:
## 🚀 Background Description

`Nightly` (`.github/workflows/nightly.yml`) is the L4 `daily` gate on `main`. It is triggered by a 16:00 UTC cron (`- cron: "0 16 * * *"`, line 33) and by `workflow_dispatch` (line 34). The workflow has no `concurrency` block and no guard job. Its own header already says GitHub "drops or delays runs when its queue is busy — treat a missing night as a scheduling miss and re-dispatch rather than as a build failure".

GitHub is now consistently creating the scheduled run hours late. The ten most recent `event=schedule` runs returned by the Actions API are:

| Scheduled 16:00 UTC | Run created (UTC) | Lateness | Run |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-11-17 | 2026-11-17T23:26:00Z | 7 h 26 m | [44199315530](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44199315530) |
| 2026-11-16 | 2026-11-17T00:07:02Z | 8 h 07 m | [43984975918](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/43984975918) |
| 2026-11-15 | 2026-11-15T20:56:52Z | 4 h 56 m | [43760882196](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/43760882196) |
| 2026-11-14 | 2026-11-14T20:33:14Z | 4 h 33 m | [43638096527](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/43638096527) |
| 2026-11-13 | 2026-11-13T21:52:47Z | 5 h 52 m | [43514552368](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/43514552368) |
| 2026-11-12 | 2026-11-12T22:09:58Z | 6 h 09 m | [43317329014](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/43317329014) |
| 2026-11-11 | 2026-11-11T22:35:07Z | 6 h 35 m | [43112992255](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/43112992255) |
| 2026-11-10 | 2026-11-10T21:44:15Z | 5 h 44 m | [42907916462](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42907916462) |
| 2026-11-09 | 2026-11-10T00:04:30Z | 8 h 04 m | [42725463331](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42725463331) |
| 2026-11-08 | 2026-11-08T20:20:32Z | 4 h 20 m | [42519625781](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42519625781) |

The times above are the run's `created_at` from the API, i.e. when GitHub created the run, not when a step started. Every one was created between **4 h 20 m and 8 h 07 m after the 16:00 UTC occurrence** it belongs to. The run before these ten, [42409367796](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42409367796), was created at 2026-11-07T20:05:46Z and was 4 h 05 m late, so this is not a single bad night.

16:00 UTC is 00:00 in Asia/Shanghai, and the workflow header intends the run to start overnight and "finish by the working morning". A run created at 04:20–08:07 Asia/Shanghai has not done that, and its long real-model suite runs after that creation time.

There is also a same-day dispatch on 2026-11-18: [run 44361037291](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44361037291) was created at 2026-11-18T17:39:13Z as a `workflow_dispatch` by `agent-ci-infra-bot`. At the time of the API read (2026-11-18T19:37Z) there was still no `event=schedule` run for that day's 16:00 UTC occurrence. The API does not record why the dispatch was started; it is consistent with the re-dispatch the workflow header describes.

The result is that the normal 16:00 UTC start depends on GitHub's cron queue, and the workaround is a manual or one-off bot re-dispatch. The plan below makes the normal start independent of that queue and keeps the cron only as a guarded fallback.

## Design Ideas

Both parts below are one plan, not alternatives. Part 1 moves the normal start out of GitHub's cron queue. Part 2 makes the cron safe when it does arrive, so it cannot cancel a running dispatch run or create a duplicate after a successful one.

### Part 1 — start the run from the bot schedule

In the bot console, ask the management assistant, or add a project scheduled task on the project's `定时任务与通知` page. Schedule it shortly after 16:00 UTC (for example 16:05 UTC, or 00:05 Asia/Shanghai if the page uses local time) with this instruction:

> start nightly.yml on main; first check that no run of it is queued or in progress, and if one is, start nothing

That gives the project a primary start that is not GitHub's cron queue, and the check keeps it from adding a run when a person or the fallback has already started one. Keep `workflow_dispatch` so the same task, or a person, can still start the workflow.

### Part 2 — change the workflow

Keep `workflow_dispatch`. Keep `schedule` with `- cron: "0 16 * * *"` only as a fallback. Add a workflow-level `concurrency` group with `cancel-in-progress: false`, so a scheduled run waits for a running dispatch run instead of cancelling it. Add a first `guard` job that, on `schedule` only, checks whether a `workflow_dispatch` run of `nightly.yml` succeeded since the most recent 16:00 UTC; if one did, it sets `run=false` and every other job is skipped. On `workflow_dispatch` it always sets `run=true`.

This is the concrete adaptation for the existing `stamp`, `gate` and `report` jobs:

```yaml
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 16 * * *"   # fallback only; the bot schedule starts the run
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  # A scheduled run queues behind a running dispatch run instead of cancelling it.
  group: nightly-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  guard:
    name: Check for a successful dispatch run
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      actions: read        # gh run list
      contents: read
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.check.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: check
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          run=true
          if [[ "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" == "schedule" ]]; then
            # The most recent scheduled time: 16:00 UTC today, or yesterday
            # when a delayed run is created before 16:00 UTC.
            since=$(date -u -d '16:00 today' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
            if (( $(date -u +%s) < $(date -u -d "$since" +%s) )); then
              since=$(date -u -d '16:00 yesterday' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
            fi
            count=$(gh run list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" -w nightly.yml \
              -e workflow_dispatch -s success --created ">=$since" \
              --limit 1 --json databaseId --jq 'length')
            if (( count > 0 )); then
              run=false
            fi
          fi
          echo "run=$run" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  stamp:
    name: Stamp the build
    needs: guard
    if: needs.guard.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.stamp.outputs.version }}
    steps:
      - id: stamp
        run: |
          date=$(TZ=Asia/Shanghai date +%Y%m%d)
          echo "version=nightly-${date}-${GITHUB_SHA::7}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  gate:
    name: Gate
    needs: [guard, stamp]
    if: needs.guard.outputs.run == 'true'
    uses: ./.github/workflows/ci.yml
    secrets: inherit
    with:
      profile: daily
      release-version: ${{ needs.stamp.outputs.version }}

  report:
    name: Report the outcome
    needs: [guard, stamp, gate]
    if: always() && needs.guard.outputs.run == 'true'
    # ... the existing report steps are unchanged ...
```

The guard job declares `actions: read`; the workflow-level `contents: read` stays. It uses the workflow's own `github.token`, not a new secret. The `--created ">=$since"` filter and `-s success` mean only a successful dispatch created at or after the scheduled time suppresses the fallback; a failed or cancelled dispatch does not. `gh run list --limit 1` is enough because only the existence of a match matters. If the `gh run list` call itself fails, the guard job fails and the workflow is red; it does not silently guess that no dispatch exists.

GitHub keeps at most one pending run per concurrency group. With one bot start and one cron fallback that is enough: the fallback waits for the running dispatch, and after the dispatch succeeds the guard skips the duplicate. A third run arriving while one is running and one is already pending could replace the older pending one; that is GitHub's queue behaviour and is not changed by `cancel-in-progress: false`.

## Involved Public APIs

No product API, UI, CLI or schema changes. The change is limited to `.github/workflows/nightly.yml` and the project-level bot schedule.

The guard job declares `actions: read` so `gh run list` can read workflow runs; the workflow-level `contents: read` remains. No new repository secret or credential is needed: `github.token` is the existing per-run token. The bot scheduled task uses the existing `workflow_dispatch` entry point. The cron trigger stays in place.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- **L4 `daily` gate:** `stamp` produces the `nightly-YYYYMMDD-<sha>` version, `gate` calls the reusable `ci.yml` with `profile: daily`, and `report` writes the outcome. Their bodies and inputs do not change; only the guard condition is added.
- **Release:** `release.yml` is a separate workflow and is not affected by this plan.
- **Product code and tests:** no product path changes. The real-model journeys, case selection and evaluation are untouched.
- **Project automation:** the bot console / `定时任务与通知` task is project automation, not repository code; it needs no repository change from this Issue.

## Test Design and Test Plan

This Issue recommends a change; it does not implement it. The repository's implementation should verify the following, none of which requires a paid real-model run:

- `actionlint` (or at least a YAML parse) passes on the updated `nightly.yml`.
- A `workflow_dispatch` run still executes `stamp`, `gate` and `report`; the guard sets `run=true` for that event.
- A scheduled run with no successful dispatch created since 16:00 UTC sets `run=true` and executes the three jobs normally.
- A scheduled run with a successful dispatch created since 16:00 UTC sets `run=false`; `stamp`, `gate` and `report` are skipped, and the run's conclusion is success rather than a red `report` failure.
- A failed or cancelled dispatch does not suppress the scheduled run, because only `-s success` matches.
- With a dispatch run in progress, a scheduled run queues in the same concurrency group and does not cancel the dispatch; after the dispatch succeeds, the scheduled run's guard skips the duplicate.
- The project scheduled task starts exactly one run when none is queued or in progress, and starts nothing when one is.
- If the repository adds a workflow-contract test, assert the guard's `-e workflow_dispatch -s success` filter and the `needs`/`if` values on `stamp`, `gate` and `report`. The repository already has tests that read `nightly.yml` (for example `.ci/case-execution.test.mjs`), so there is an existing place for such a contract.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The bot console or a project scheduled task on `定时任务与通知` starts `nightly.yml` on `main` shortly after 16:00 UTC, after checking that no run of it is queued or in progress; if one is, it starts nothing.
- [ ] `workflow_dispatch` remains available and starts the full workflow.
- [ ] The 16:00 UTC cron remains as a fallback, and the guard skips the scheduled run when a successful `workflow_dispatch` run was created since the most recent 16:00 UTC.
- [ ] The workflow has `concurrency` with `cancel-in-progress: false`, so a scheduled run does not cancel a running dispatch run.
- [ ] `stamp`, `gate` and `report` keep their current behaviour on the normal path; the guard only adds the skip condition.
- [ ] The workflow change is reviewed and merged through the repository's normal process, not through this task.

## Additional Information

### Prior recommendation search

I searched open and closed Issues in this repository before writing this. The query terms and results were:

- `nightly.yml` — 17 results; the closest are #1160 (a Nightly failure report) and #850 (a per-case execution table). Neither recommends scheduling.
- `workflow_dispatch` — 18 results; the closest are #615 (a manual-validation workflow) and #243 (a merged PR that removed a release-branch dispatch). Neither is about the late Nightly.
- `in:title schedule Nightly` — only #243, the same merged PR.
- `in:title schedule` — #1029 (an unrelated queued-run retry bug) and #243.
- `nightly delayed` — #1035 (export preview OOM) and #283 (L1–L5 test coverage); neither is about the cron delay.
- `in:title delayed`, `in:title late`, `in:title cron`, `cron delayed Nightly` — no matching Issue.
- `scheduled run late` — 30 results, but none of the items inspected is a recommendation for this workflow.
- `定时任务` and `"scheduled task" Nightly` — no scheduling recommendation for this workflow.

No earlier recommendation exists, and no maintainer closed a scheduling recommendation as not wanted. This is a new Issue rather than a comment.

### Decision and scope

This Issue is a recommendation only. I have not opened a pull request, pushed a branch, or edited `.github/workflows/nightly.yml`. Whether to adopt Part 2, and its exact implementation, is the repository's own decision; a maintainer or code owner must review and merge it through the normal process.

The workflow file at the time of writing is [`.github/workflows/nightly.yml` on `main`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/main/.github/workflows/nightly.yml). The run data above was read from `GET /repos/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/workflows/nightly.yml/runs?event=schedule` and `...?event=workflow_dispatch`.

issue:1238.body:
Actions failure classification: **external**.

Run: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44361037291 (attempt 1, `workflow_dispatch`)

Head SHA: `d57fc2693e0972b5c1040d47a4b74370eb011c3f`

Upstream failing job: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44361037291/job/135002663117 (Gate / L4/L5 real E2E / Real E2E (research-2))

## Current behavior

The only planned case in the `research-2` shard, `DRB-59 easy Swarm research integration`, was classified `PROVIDER_FAULT`. The shard reported `planned 1 / executed 1 / passed 0 / failed 0 / provider faults 1` and failed with `- e2e-real: 1 provider fault(s) — an unverified case is not a pass`. The full job log gives the case's own error:

```
Error: Main run must complete with readable, nonempty declared final artifacts; delivery_status=partial; run_status=failed; delivered_artifacts=1; run_error=[181001] model call failed, reason: openAI API async stream error: APIError: read ECONNRESET
```

The job's `stack.log` identifies the failing request as `model-8f784f89-e866-486a-88b8-9d48d6063774`: HTTP 200, 12,117 SSE records / 3,716,762 bytes over 105.9 s, then `"error":{"classification":"network"}`, with `"attempts":1,"retries":0` and `"hasText":true,"hasToolCalls":true`. The next line is:

```
[jiuwenswarm-agent] run of 670fa97d-b9d0-4410-ad9f-ac0d80e75072 failed: [181001] model call failed, reason: openAI API async stream error: APIError: read ECONNRESET
```

## Expected behavior

DRB-59 completes its declared final artifacts and the shard reports `passed 1 of 1`. A live provider keeping the response open is a precondition of that journey, not a product assertion.

## Causal chain

The gateway accepted the request (`200`), streamed the answer and tool-call deltas for about 106 s, and the upstream connection was reset while answer text had already been exposed. The model gateway's bounded mid-stream retry is deliberately disabled once answer text is visible: `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts:517` throws when `state.text` is true, so the turn was not replayed and the run failed with the original transport error. The accounting then correctly recorded `PROVIDER_FAULT` (the status-less transport classification from #1071 / #1076). Under the repository's documented policy a provider fault is not a pass, so the downstream jobs failed:

- **Account for real cases** (https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44361037291/job/135075589240) reported `Planned 21; executed 20; passed 19; provider faults 1.` and `- PROVIDER_FAULT: ...DRB-59...`.
- **Gate / merge-gate** (https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44361037291/job/135075765132) failed with `Error: CI gate failed: real-scheduled: failure`; `.ci/tier-policy.mjs:52` throws because the daily profile requires the `real-scheduled` job to succeed.
- **Report the outcome** (https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44361037291/job/135075939143) failed with `RESULT: failure`; it only asserts that the gate result is `success`.

The other 19 real cases in this run passed, so the endpoint was not globally down; the fault is confined to one model turn.

## What was checked and what it rules out

- The failed-step output of job 135002663117, its `error-context.md`, and the `real-e2e-evidence-research-2` artifact (id `14455408997`). The artifact's `stack.log` is the wire-level evidence quoted above. I read it with `gh run download`; the artifact belongs to this run and commit, but its contents and attempt association are my observation, not independently verified.
- Source at the failed SHA: `const MAX_STREAM_RETRIES = 4;` (`services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts:188`) and the `state.text` guard at `:517`. The zero retries are the documented behaviour, not a missing retry loop.
- Existing Issues: #1071 / #1076 added the status-less transport classification; #898 documented that a reset after answer text starts is not replayed; #1222 recorded the same class for DRB-58 in run 44199315530. This run is a new occurrence of that class, not a new repository defect. It is not the cause reported in #1157-#1160, which describe run 43760882196 and a different failure.

## Uncertainty

The gateway diagnostics preserve only `classification: network`; the provider's own reason for closing the connection (load, edge reset, upstream timeout) is not visible. One reset in one request does not establish how widespread the provider problem was.

## Next verification

Re-run `research-2` (or the Nightly) once when the gateway is healthy and check that DRB-59 completes; a pass would separate the outage from the commit. A rerun was not requested here because the independent J5 provisioning failure in the same run (job 135002663249) is not yet established as external; see the separate report for that job. If maintainers want a turn-level retry that discards partial text, that is the enhancement space of #898, not a fix for this incident.

Head SHA: `d57fc2693e0972b5c1040d47a4b74370eb011c3f`

Upstream failing job: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44361037291/job/135002663249 (Gate / L4/L5 real E2E / Real E2E (research-11))

## Current behavior

`research-11` planned exactly one case, J5, and executed none. The shard reported `{"status":"FAIL","planned":1,"executed":0,"passed":0,"failed":0,"skipped":1}`, `1 skipped`, and the problem line `- e2e-real: 1 skipped — a skip is not a pass`. The journey report captured in the `real-e2e-evidence-research-11` artifact (id `14460243200`) records the precondition:

```
BLOCKED: managed Python base is not ready (failed: Conda environment setup failed)
```

The environment-setup state was therefore `failed`, not `installing`. The message is the generic non-micromamba failure from `services/runner/src/environment-store.ts:1460` (`Conda environment setup failed`); the store keeps the actual provisioner transcript in `setup.error` / `components.conda.error`, but J5 prints only `setup.message`, and `real-e2e.yml` uploads `.ci-results` only. The runner's operational log at `<CI_RUNTIME_DIR>/real-standard/data/logs/runner.log` is not in the artifact, so the precise conda/provisioning error is missing.

`Account for real cases` (https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44361037291/job/135075589240) reports `- research-11: SHARD_FAILED`; `merge-gate` (https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44361037291/job/135075765132) fails with `Error: CI gate failed: real-scheduled: failure`; `Report the outcome` (https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44361037291/job/135075939143) fails with `RESULT: failure`.

## Expected behavior

The managed Python base reaches `ready` within J5's 180 s wait (the wait added by #286 / #287), J5 executes, and the shard reports planned=executed=passed=1. A setup failure must remain BLOCKED; the journey's reaction is the intended fail-closed behaviour. #286 was about the normal `installing` phase racing the first read; this run observed `failed`, so it is a different failure.

## What was checked

- The failed-step output of job 135002663249 and the `real-e2e-evidence-research-11` artifact (`14460243200`): the journey report and its blocked-step screenshot, `run.log`, `stack.log`, and `api-diagnostics`. The stack log shows three `GET /api/environment-setup 200 OK` requests and no conda/micromamba transcript. I read the artifact with `gh run download`; its origin is this run and commit, but its contents and attempt association are my observation, not independently verified.
- Source at `d57fc269`: `failSetup` (`environment-store.ts:1460`), `runManagedEnvironmentSetup` / `bootstrapStarter` / `validateStarter` (the `conda` component is entered only after micromamba is ready, so this is the Python-base create/validate phase), and `test/journey-real-request.spec.ts:73` (the BLOCKED skip).
- Previous runs: `research-11` succeeded in Nightly 44199315530 (job 134449454466) and 43984975918 (job 133711095274), both with J5 executed. In 43514552368 the job failed *after* J5 executed (a different, post-setup failure). The immediately preceding nightly, 44199315530 on `b2075e49`, ran the same provisioning path and J5 passed.
- Diff: 25 commits separate `b2075e49` from `d57fc269`; none touch `services/runner`, `packages/network`, `services/launcher`, `scripts/start-stack.sh`, `.ci/run-e2e.sh`, or `test/journey-real-request.spec.ts` / `test/helpers/environment-setup.ts`. That makes a regression from this commit in the provisioning path unlikely, but it does not identify the failing precondition.
- Not checked: the runner's operational log and the `setup.error` payload, because neither is uploaded. I did not rerun the paid Nightly to try to reproduce the state.

## Uncertainty

The inner failure is unresolved. Candidates that the missing transcript would separate: conda channel/CDN/network failure while creating the Python base, a runner disk/permission problem, or a latent race in the provisioning code. The job duration (~2 min) and the `failed` state observed before J5's 180 s deadline are consistent with a setup failure during the conda step, not with a wait timeout, but they do not choose among the candidates.

## Why report this / next verification

1. Re-run `research-11` (or the Nightly) on this commit and observe `GET /api/environment-setup`; a transition to `ready` and a J5 pass would support a transient provisioning failure, while a repeat failure would justify a code investigation.
2. Preserve the evidence next time: upload the runner's operational log for the real shard, or include `setup.state`, `setup.error` and the `components.conda` transcript in the journey report on a BLOCKED precondition. That is the one missing fact that would let the next occurrence be attributed to an external channel/network problem or to a repository defect.
3. If the transcript shows an external channel failure, this report can be closed as an environment precondition; if it shows a code error, it becomes a concrete repair issue.

issue:1241.body:
Actions failure classification: **code**.

Run: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44415877405 (attempt 2)

Upstream failing job: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44415877405/job/135282620250

Head SHA: `59d05aa70a26801e2e907ca49060329028514608`

## Current behavior

`Gate / L4/L5 real E2E / Real E2E (research-6)` failed the desktop SRBench PUCT smoke at the smoke's own bar of three expansions:

```
Error: The search must record at least 3 expansions
expect(received).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(expected)
Expected: >= 3
Received:    1
```

Its own summary step agrees that the planned case is the only failure: the shared plan reads `- e2e-real: passed 0 of 1 planned`, and the problem list names `FAIL: playwright:test/desktop-evolve-srbench-real.spec.ts::…desktop%20%2Fevolve-design%20reaches%20three%20PUCT%20expansions…`.

The job's evidence artifact `real-e2e-evidence-research-6` (artifact id 14490394792; the upload step recorded the zip digest `8e5c0c81…`) belongs to this run and this commit (`E2E_COMMIT_SHA=59d05aa7…`). In it, `real-standard/e2e-real/test-results/desktop-evolve-srbench-rea-ba575-s-on-an-LLM-SRBench-problem-real/` holds:

- `desktop-evolve-metrics.json` — `"search_status": "succeeded"`, `"expansions": 1`; the single search record is `"status": "succeeded"`, `"bestNodeIndex": 1`, `"finishedAt": "2026-11-19T02:10:53.023Z"`, and its confirmed scorecard carries `"solvedThreshold": 0.999` on a `custom_script` criterion.
- `evolve-events.json` (13 events) — the seed (node 0) scored `baselineScore: 0.194226`; the one expansion (node 1) was `"valid": true`, `"score": 1`; then a log event `"planned 24 expansions, made 1; it stopped because target_reward."` and `{"type": "search_finished", "status": "succeeded", "stopReason": "target_reward", "bestTestScore": 1, "expansionsPlanned": 24, "candidates": 2}`.

The search did not stall, lose workers or hit a token ceiling: its first candidate reached the scorecard's solved threshold (test score 1.0 vs 0.999), and the engine stopped there. This run had `E2E_LLM_THINKING_MODE=enabled`, `E2E_LLM_THINKING_EFFORT=low`, so the per-call token ceiling that #1157 described was not involved; provider faults were 0.

That stop is documented product behavior, not a defect in the search. Since #1073 (closing #948) the PUCT engine passes the scorecard threshold as the framework's target stop:

```python
# services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/puct_engine.py:399
            "target_reward": float(spec.scorecard.get("solvedThreshold") or 0.999),
```

and `services/evolve/tests/test_puct_engine.py::test_reaching_the_scorecard_s_solved_threshold_ends_the_run` asserts exactly the event shape this run produced (`stopReason == "target_reward"`, `status == "succeeded"`, fewer expansions than planned).

The smoke, however, hard-codes the count and stops polling on any terminal status, including `succeeded`:

```ts
// test/desktop-evolve-srbench-real.spec.ts:441
          || ["budget_exhausted", "failed", "stopped", "succeeded"].includes(status);
// test/desktop-evolve-srbench-real.spec.ts:449
      expect(expanded.length, `The search must record at least ${target} expansions`).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(target);
```

So the pass condition is only satisfiable when the model's first candidates do not already reach the scorecard threshold — which is model-luck, not a property of the product.

## Same test bytes passed the night before

The spec and workflows are byte-identical between the previous Nightly head and this one: `git diff b2075e4972a5af90804fdd579ee314bfa502be46 59d05aa70a26801e2e907ca49060329028514608 -- test/ .github/` is empty, and `b2075e49` is the last commit touching the spec. Nightly run 44199315530 (head `b2075e49`, final attempt 3) was green, including `Real E2E (research-6)` and `Account for real cases`. This is not a source regression on this head; the difference is whether the design's first candidate already solves the SRBench problem.

## Not the same cause as the open reports

#1157/#1158/#1159 (run 43760882196) describe a different mechanism: two expansions because 22 candidate calls were cut off at the recorded 16000-token per-call ceiling while still thinking, ending on the expansion cap. #1185 (closed, unknown) recorded 0 expansions. Here the search ended `succeeded` on `target_reward` after one expansion, with a valid candidate that scored 1.0. Those reports remain accurate for their runs; this failure needs its own fix.

## Downstream jobs

One cause explains all four failing jobs:

- `Account for real cases` (https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44415877405/job/135286552958) fails "Reconcile every planned identity" with `Planned 21; executed 21; passed 20; provider faults 0.` / `- research-6: SHARD_FAILED` — the only failed case is this one.
- `merge-gate` (https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44415877405/job/135286707014) refuses because the scheduled real layer is red: `Error: CI gate failed: real-scheduled: failure`.
- `Report the outcome` (https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44415877405/job/135286834408) runs `[[ "${RESULT}" == "success" ]]` with `RESULT: failure`, so it exits 1. It reports the gate; it does not decide it.

No rerun is requested. A rerun could pass by luck if the model's first candidate falls short of 0.999, but the assertion still contradicts the documented stop, so the same red is expected whenever the design solves the problem on its first candidate.

## Expected behavior

A search that reaches the scorecard's `solvedThreshold` on its first expansion must end `succeeded` with `stopReason: "target_reward"`, and the smoke should accept that ending as a pass while still failing a search that produced fewer than three expansions for any other reason (token ceiling, worker loss, `max_iters`/`max_calls`). Today the smoke cannot tell those apart.

## Requested code change

In `test/desktop-evolve-srbench-real.spec.ts`, step "Watch the search reach three expansions" (the block around lines 419-449): after `await save("evolve-events.json", events)`, read the `search_finished` event out of the collected events and branch before the `toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(target)` assertion:

- `expanded.length >= target` — unchanged: read each candidate back by hash as the code does today.
- otherwise, if the final event is `search_finished` with `status === "succeeded"`, `stopReason === "target_reward"` and `bestTestScore >= scorecard.solvedThreshold` — record the ending (for example `metrics.stop_reason`, `metrics.expansions_planned`) and read back the candidate(s) that were actually recorded by hash, then pass.
- otherwise — keep today's failure, with a message that names `status` and `stopReason`, so a short search that ended at the budget or on an error still fails exactly as it does now (that is the #1157 case).

Please also add a regression test for the branch itself — a small unit test over the extracted predicate is enough, since the journey needs a real model — so a later edit cannot silently drop the distinction between "goal met early" and "stopped short".

## References

- Run: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44415877405
- research-6: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44415877405/job/135282620250
- Account for real cases: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44415877405/job/135286552958
- merge-gate: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44415877405/job/135286707014
- Report the outcome: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44415877405/job/135286834408
- Earlier green Nightly with the identical spec: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44199315530

## Uncertainty and limits

I read the artifact's `desktop-evolve-metrics.json` and `evolve-events.json` (and the scorecard embedded in the former) plus the four failed-step logs; I did not open the Playwright trace or the journey report HTML, and I did not run the journey locally. The artifact metadata ties it to run 44415877405 and commit 59d05aa7 (its digest is the one job 135282620250 recorded), but I cannot separately prove which attempt every file inside it came from, nor which model endpoint state produced the 1.0 score. I make no claim about future Nightly runs beyond the assertion defect described.

This report does not approve development. Existing review gates and a development label applied by a person are still required.
