issue:1251.body:
## 🚀 Background Description

The desktop client has no way to find a Session except scrolling the sidebar. The server already serves a workbench search and the web client already consumes it, so this is a client gap rather than a new capability.

Verified on `main` `9f641cf1`:

| Piece | State |
| --- | --- |
| Search endpoint | `GET /api/search?q=&limit=&offset=` (`services/api/src/http/index.ts:1818-1824`) → `searchWorkbench` (`services/api/src/workbench/index.ts:29-93`) |
| What it matches | project **names**; Session **titles** (plus project name and Session id); artifact **names/titles** (plus their Session title and project). It does **not** look inside messages |
| Result shape | `WorkbenchSearchResult` with `kind: "project" \| "session" \| "artifact"`, project/session context, `archived` flag for Sessions, and `hasMore`/`total` paging |
| Web client | a palette in the composer (`apps/web/src/composer/WorkbenchNavigation.tsx:103` debounce, `:164` client-side filtering, `@`/`#` triggers) |
| Desktop client | **nothing**: no `/api/search` call anywhere in `apps/desktop/src`, no search field, no result list |

Two secondary gaps in the desktop list itself:

- The sidebar only ever asks for `state="active"` (`apps/desktop/src/api/sessions.ts:71-78` and its only caller `app/use-workspace.ts:763`), so nothing but the default view exists. The archive-state filter is tracked in `#1250`; this issue should not duplicate it.
- There is no filter other than "which project am I in": no by-kind, no by-time, no "has artifacts / is running".

Message-content search is a real user need, but `searchWorkbench` only reads titles today; adding it means an index and belongs to a follow-up once this UI exists.

## Design Ideas

1. **A search field at the top of the session sidebar** (and the same one reachable from the command palette if the desktop gains one): debounce ~250 ms like the web client, call `GET /api/search`, and render results grouped by kind — 项目 / 会话 / 产物 — with the project context (no `已归档` marker: archived Sessions never appear in the results — withdrawn 2026-11-27 by the repository owner, [this comment](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/1251#issuecomment-7208777074)).
2. **Keyboard first**: `Ctrl/Cmd+K` opens it, arrow keys move, `Enter` opens the result (Session → open, project → switch, artifact → open its dialog). Escape closes and restores the previous list.
3. ~~**Filters for the session list**, applied client-side over the returned page while the result set is small: 仅当前项目 / 全部项目, 仅运行中, 有产物的会话, and a time window (今天 / 最近 7 天 / 全部).~~ **Withdrawn 2026-11-26 (22:18 CST) by the repository owner** — no session-list narrowing ships with this issue; see *Withdrawn scope* under Acceptance Criteria. State (活动/已归档/全部) stays with `#1250`.
4. **Be honest about the search scope**: label the field so it does not promise message search ("搜索会话、项目、产物"), and put the content-search follow-up in the issue rather than faking it.
5. **Empty and error states**: a query with no results says so with the current scope; an API failure shows the reason and a retry instead of an empty list.

`GET /api/search` can gain additive `kind`/`projectId` params later; this issue works without them.

## Involved Public APIs

Consumed only, no changes required:

- `GET /api/search?q=&limit=&offset=` → `WorkbenchSearchResponse` (`results[]`, `total`, `hasMore`)
- `GET /api/projects/:id/sessions?state=…` for the list itself

If scoped search parameters are added later, that is a separate additive change.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

| Module | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `apps/desktop/src/api/workbench.ts` (new) | `search(q, limit, offset)` client |
| `apps/desktop/src/views/Sidebar.tsx` | Search field, result list (the filter row is withdrawn — 2026-11-26, repository owner) |
| `apps/desktop/src/app/use-workspace.ts` | Query state, selection after a result opens, refresh behaviour |
| `apps/desktop/src/text/{zh,en}.ts`, styles | Copy and layout |
| `apps/web` | Reference only (its palette is the behavioural model) |
| `services/api`, `packages/*` | Untouched |

Related, non-overlapping: `#1250` (archive/restore filter and actions).

## Test Design and Test Plan

- **Component tests**: typing debounces and issues one request per settled query; results render grouped by kind with project context (the archived marker is withdrawn — archived Sessions are not searchable, 2026-11-27); keyboard navigation opens the right target; ~~filters narrow the session list and persist for the session~~; empty result and API failure states.
- **E2E on the desktop build with the real stack**: search a term that only a Session title contains, one that only an artifact name contains, and one that only a message body contains (the last must return nothing and say why); open a result with the keyboard. ~~Filter to 仅运行中 during a run and back~~ — no session-list narrowing ships (2026-11-26, repository owner).
- Commands: `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck`, `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop test`, `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop build`, `pnpm ci:l1`.
- Screenshots (empty field, results grouped by kind, no-result state) go in the PR body for the owner's approval; the owner has approved the set delivered with #1290.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A search field in the desktop sidebar queries `/api/search` with debounce and renders results grouped by 项目 / 会话 / 产物 with their context.
- [ ] ~~Archived Sessions in the results carry an 已归档 marker, and opening one lands in the read-only view.~~ — **Withdrawn 2026-11-27 by the repository owner**: archived Sessions and their artifacts are not searchable at all, so no hit ever carries the marker — [this comment](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/1251#issuecomment-7208908315).
- [ ] `Ctrl/Cmd+K` focuses search, arrows move the selection, `Enter` opens it, Escape closes.
- [ ] ~~The session list can be narrowed by 仅当前项目 / 仅运行中 / 有产物 / 时间窗口, and the choice survives a reload.~~ — **Withdrawn 2026-11-26 (22:18 CST) by the repository owner.**
- [ ] No results and API failures are distinguishable, and both offer the next step.
- [ ] The field's copy does not imply message-content search; that gap is recorded as a follow-up in the issue.
- [ ] zh-CN and en copy; `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck|test|build` and `pnpm ci:l1` pass.
- [ ] The owner has seen the screenshots in the PR body.

### Withdrawn scope

**Criterion 4 — session-list narrowing (2026-11-26, 22:18 CST).** The **repository owner**
decided that this issue does not deliver session-list narrowing. 搜索 ships as a dialog opened
from the column's title row, and its 全部 / 项目 / 会话 / 产物 footer filters what a query
returns — not the list. Criterion 4, Design Idea 3, the narrowing lines in the test plan and the
filter row in the relevance table are withdrawn by that decision and marked so in place.

**Criterion 2 — the archived marker (2026-11-27).** The same owner decided on **2026-11-27 (CST)**
that archived Sessions and their artifacts do not appear in search results at all, so a hit never
needs an 已归档 marker. What stays: an imported read-only snapshot **is** searchable, and the line
this issue draws is archived versus live, not writable versus read-only. Criterion 2 is withdrawn
at the "archived hits are searchable and marked" layer; the decision, the card's wording and the
replacement rule are recorded in [this comment](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/1251#issuecomment-7208908315) and, with its provenance, in
[this earlier one](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/1251#issuecomment-7208777074).
What still stands, so that the whole criterion is accounted for: archived Sessions **and their
artifacts** stay out of the results; an imported read-only snapshot **is** searchable and opens
in the read-only view, so only the archived path into that view is gone; and `archived` is still
returned by `GET /api/search` on Session hits — the desktop client drops archived hits before it
builds the list, so the flag remains a fact about the API, not a requirement on this UI.

Every other criterion stands unchanged. The delivery is #1290, which closes this issue on merge.

## Additional Information

Verified on `main` `9f641cf1`: the endpoint and its matcher (`workbench/index.ts:39-83` — names/titles only, no message bodies), the web palette's debounce and client-side kinds, and the absence of any search client or UI in `apps/desktop/src`.

Out of scope here: message-content search (needs an index; follow-up), the archive-state filter (`#1250`), and any change to what `searchWorkbench` indexes.

issue:1292.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] The description below includes environment information and a minimal reproduction, so the issue can be reproduced without further questions.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary**

When the selected model has no saved API key, the run fails with the generic `semantic-error` card. In a Chinese UI the main screen only says "运行中遇到了意外问题，任务未能完成。建议重试", and the actual cause — an English sentence — appears only after expanding "技术详情":

```
semantic-error
The selected model does not have a saved API token
```

This is a user-fixable configuration problem presented as an unexplained crash: the message is not readable in the UI language, and it is one click away from the place where the user would act.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Open the desktop client (front end on 5174, API on 4410), locale `zh-CN`.
2. Settings › Models › add a custom model whose credential is left empty (any base URL, `tokenOptional` not effective for runs).
3. Select that model in the composer and send any message.
   - Observed: a failure card titled "运行异常"; expanding "技术详情" reveals `semantic-error` plus the English sentence above.
   - Expected: a readable failure that names the cause and the next step, for example "模型还没有配置 API Key / 到 设置 › 模型 补上后再试".

Reproduced 3 out of 3 times.

**Why it happens**

- The API raises a plain 400 at `services/api/src/runs/index.ts:842`:
  `throw new ApiStatusError(400, "The selected model does not have a saved API token");`
- `services/api/src/run-failure.ts:28` `classifyRunFailure()` matches only tool-call, timeout, auth-status, rate-limit, 5xx and transport wording. This 400 matches nothing and falls through to the catch-all `semantic-error`.
- `packages/schema/src/session.ts:578` `RunFailureCode` therefore has no code that describes this case.
- The desktop already has localized copy per code (`apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts:1633`, `en.ts:1582`), but with no code to look up it can only render the catch-all text. `apps/desktop/src/views/RunFailureCard.tsx:35-36` then prints the raw code and raw message inside the details block.

**Proposed fix (agreed approach)**

Give this failure its own code and its own copy, using the mechanism that already exists:

1. `packages/schema/src/session.ts` — add `model-credential-missing` to `RunFailureCode`.
2. `services/api/src/runs/index.ts:842` — raise a typed error that carries the code (do not depend on prose matching), and make `classifyRunFailure()` return it so the `run.failed` event carries `errorCode: "model-credential-missing"`.
3. `apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts` and `en.ts` — add entries to `runFailure.titles` and the per-code body:
   - zh title: 模型还没有配置 API Key
   - zh body: 这个模型在设置里没有保存 API Key，运行无法开始。到 设置 › 模型 补上后重试。
   - en title: Model has no API key
   - en body: This model has no saved API key, so the run cannot start. Add one in Settings › Models and try again.
4. `apps/desktop/src/views/RunFailureCard.tsx` — for this code, render one localized sentence above the `<pre>` in "技术详情", keeping the provider text verbatim below it for diagnostics.
5. Tests: extend `services/api/src/run-failure.test.ts` (classification) and `apps/desktop/tests/run-failure.test.ts` (title/body lookup).

**Acceptance criteria**

- With a model that has no saved key, the failure card title and body are localized and name the missing key plus the settings path.
- The raw provider message still appears in "技术详情" (diagnostics are not lost).
- A regression test covers the new code on both the API classifier and the desktop copy lookup.
- Unknown future codes keep falling back to the existing generic title and body.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Product: ScienceDiscovery desktop client (`apps/desktop`), web dev surface: front end `http://127.0.0.1:5174`, API `127.0.0.1:4410`, runner `127.0.0.1:4411`.
- Host: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS, Node.js 22.23.2, pnpm 11.1.2.
- Browser: Playwright's Chromium build 1228 (headless), viewport 1500x950, locale `zh-CN`.
- Model used for the failing run: a custom profile with an empty credential; the endpoint is never reached.

### Additional Information

- Screenshots attached: the failure card as the user sees it, and the expanded technical details.
- Found while walking a feature map over `apps/desktop` (failure-state item). A neighbouring case — a model whose base URL is unreachable — already classifies correctly as `transport-error` with actionable copy, which is why this one stands out.
- The English sentence is the provider-independent API text, so it reads the same for every model.

### Version Information

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, branch `main`

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] The description below includes environment information and a minimal reproduction, so the issue can be reproduced without further questions.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary**

In the desktop client the workspace panel's maximum width is computed as if the left task sidebar were still on screen, but opening the panel removes that sidebar (`App.tsx:1377`). The reserved width is subtracted from a window that no longer contains it, so the panel opens narrower than its own default and, at ordinary laptop widths, the splitter cannot move it at all.

**Steps to reproduce** (viewport 1500x950, `zh-CN`)

1. Open the desktop client and open any session that has artifacts (one generated `sales.csv` is enough).
2. Click the workspace panel control (`aria-label="工作区面板"`).
   - Observed: `.app-shell` becomes `sidebar-hidden panel-open` — the task sidebar is not rendered — and the panel opens at 628 px.
3. Drag the splitter to the left, or focus it and press `Shift+ArrowLeft` five times.
   - Expected: the panel widens, as it does on a wide window.
   - Observed: the panel stays at 628 px; not one pixel moves.
4. Widen the window to 1800 px and repeat step 3.
   - Observed: the panel goes 720 → 928 px and stops at 928, so the behaviour is a ceiling, not a broken splitter.

**Measured**

| viewport | panel on open | after 5x Shift+ArrowLeft | ceiling the code gives | ceiling if the hidden sidebar is not reserved |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1800x950 | 720 | 928 | 928 | 1100 (capped) |
| 1500x950 | 628 | 628 | 628 | 924 |
| 1440x950 | 568 | 568 | 568 | 864 |
| 1280x950 | 480 | 480 | 480 | 704 |

1500 px is an ordinary laptop width, and there the ceiling (628) is *below* `PANEL_DEFAULT_WIDTH` (720): `PANEL_DEFAULT_WIDTH` only applies from 1592 px up (`720 + 872`). The same happens at 1440 px (568) and 1280 px (480, the floor), which is why the splitter feels decorative rather than merely limited.

**Root cause pointer**

- `apps/desktop/src/app/panel-width.ts:81` — `clampPanelWidth` builds `ceiling = Math.min(PANEL_MAX_WIDTH, viewportWidth - PANEL_SIDEBAR_WIDTH - PANEL_MIN_CHAT_WIDTH)`, with `PANEL_SIDEBAR_WIDTH = 360` (line 44) and `PANEL_MIN_CHAT_WIDTH = 512` (line 47).
- `apps/desktop/src/App.tsx:1377` — `const taskSidebar = sidebarOpen && !panelOpen;`: while the panel is open the task sidebar is not rendered at all, so there is no sidebar column to reserve. The comment directly above it (`App.tsx:1371-1375`) states the same thing: the panel takes the sidebar's place rather than sharing the window with it.
- The constant does not match the layout either. The task column is 296 px (`apps/desktop/src/styles/design.css:184`, `--d-sidebar: 296px` in `styles/tokens.css:70`) and the rail is 64 px (`design.css:60-66`, `--d-rail`); the comment above `PANEL_SIDEBAR_WIDTH` still quotes an older grid, `256px minmax(0, 1fr) var(--panel-width)` from `styles/shell.css:26`, which `design.css` overrides because `styles/index.css` imports it last.
- `apps/desktop/tests/panel-width.test.ts:44-70` asserts the current arithmetic, so its expectations move with the fix.

**Suggested fix**

Reserve only the columns that are actually laid out. While the panel is open, that is the 64 px rail plus the 512 px conversation floor:

```ts
const ceiling = Math.min(
  PANEL_MAX_WIDTH,
  viewportWidth - PANEL_RAIL_WIDTH - (panelOpen ? 0 : PANEL_SIDEBAR_WIDTH) - PANEL_MIN_CHAT_WIDTH,
);
```

with `PANEL_SIDEBAR_WIDTH` corrected to 296. With that, 1500 px allows 924 px and 1800 px reaches the 1100 px cap.

If `clampPanelWidth` should stay a pure function of two numbers, the alternative is to pass the conversation column's real available width from `use-panel-width.ts:69` instead of `window.innerWidth`, reading `.app-shell`'s two fixed columns once per render.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Product: ScienceDiscovery desktop client (`apps/desktop`), run as the web dev surface: front end `http://127.0.0.1:5174`, API on `127.0.0.1:4410`, runner on `127.0.0.1:4411`.
- Host: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS, Node.js 22.23.2, pnpm 11.1.2.
- Browser: Playwright's Chromium build 1228 (headless), viewports 1800x950 / 1500x950 / 1440x950 / 1280x950, locale `zh-CN`.
- Reproduced by hand in the same build at all four widths, and by script on repeated runs.

### Additional Information

- Screenshots attached: the same session at 1800 and at 1500, before and after five `Shift+ArrowLeft` presses. The coloured box is the panel's measured edge, checked against the rendered border in the raw captures (x = 872 at 1500, x = 1080/872 at 1800 before/after).
- The width itself is remembered in `localStorage` (`PANEL_WIDTH_STORAGE_KEY`) and the clamp is applied to what is rendered only (`use-panel-width.ts:69`), so the stored width is not damaged — it is just never shown at these viewport widths.
- No console error is involved; this is a wrong input to one calculation.

### Version Information

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, branch `main`
- Commit: `bbdbdd5c9e7d04de3ff1d33da52eb41b87d60c9a` (2026-11-21)
- Desktop app package version: `0.0.0` (private workspace package)

![Q9-panel-width-en](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/146eeb08-ee9f-4aa4-9e03-0e654f8e2c2b)

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] The description below includes environment information and a minimal reproduction, so the issue can be reproduced without further questions.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary**

When a model connectivity test fails, the desktop client shows the API's English sentence verbatim — in a Chinese UI, with no status marker and no hint about what to fix. The localized explanations for exactly these failures already exist in `text/zh.ts`, but they are unreachable: the API always fills `message`, and the client prefers `message` over `category`.

**Steps to reproduce** (1500x950 viewport, `zh-CN`)

1. Open 设置 › 模型 and click 添加模型.
2. Keep 服务商类型 `DeepSeek`, and fill: 基础URL `http://127.0.0.1:9/v1`, API key `sk-anything`, 模型名称 `probe-model`.
3. Click 测试连接.
   - Expected: a Chinese sentence such as 「连不上这个地址，请检查网络或自定义地址是否可达。」
   - Observed: `Could not connect to model provider; support is unknown` — English, no `✕` prefix, and nothing says the base URL is the likely culprit.

The same shape appears for the other failure categories (`Compatibility check timed out; support is unknown`, `Base URL or model ID was not found`, …): every one of them is an English sentence rendered as-is.

**Why this matters**

This is the one screen where the user is expected to *fix* the problem — the address they typed. The English sentence names neither the field nor an action, and reads like an internal diagnostic, so the user is left to guess. The success path is equally unhelpful in the other direction: it renders a full technical paragraph (`✓ 基础检查通过（1132 ms） · 仅基础检查：不验证完整会话执行路径、思考或工具调用。`) inside a one-line verdict.

**Root cause pointer**

- The API builds the sentence: `services/api/src/model-connectivity.ts:58` — `message: "Could not connect to model provider; support is unknown"`; same at line 55 (`timeout`), line 61 (`invalid_response`), and in `providerFailure()` at lines 46-52 (`API key is invalid or is not authorized`, `Base URL or model ID was not found`, …).
- The client prefers that sentence over the category it already has: `apps/desktop/src/views/ModelForm.tsx:473-476`
  ```ts
  function failureMessage(test: ModelConnectivityTestResult): string {
    if (test.message.trim() !== "") return test.message;
    return TEXT.wizard.testCategories[test.category] ?? TEXT.errors.generic;
  }
  ```
- The localized text for every category is already written and translated: `text/zh.ts:746-756` and `text/en.ts:721-733` (`network` → 「连不上这个地址，请检查网络或自定义地址是否可达。」). Because the API always sends a non-empty `message`, `TEXT.wizard.testCategories` is dead code in practice.
- The verdict itself has no marker: `ModelForm.tsx:889` renders `{verdict.message}` after a bare `kind === "fail"` style, so no `✕` ever appears.

**Suggested fix**

Let the category decide the sentence, and keep the English text as the detail a developer can still reach:

```ts
function failureMessage(test: ModelConnectivityTestResult): string {
  const localized = TEXT.wizard.testCategories[test.category];
  return localized ?? (test.message.trim() !== "" ? test.message : TEXT.errors.generic);
}
```

and put `test.message` in the verdict's `title` (tooltip) — the raw sentence stays available for diagnosis without becoming the interface. Optionally add the `✕` marker so success and failure differ at a glance.

The alternative — stop sending display text from the API — was rejected: `message` is part of `ModelConnectivityTestResult` in `packages/schema`, and other consumers (the first-run wizard, review tooling) read it for logs.

If a category is genuinely new and untranslated, the fallback path keeps today's behaviour, so no failure becomes less informative than it is now.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Product: ScienceDiscovery desktop client (`apps/desktop`), run as the web dev surface: front end `http://127.0.0.1:5174`, API on `127.0.0.1:4410`, runner on `127.0.0.1:4411`.
- Host: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS, Node.js 22.23.2, pnpm 11.1.2.
- Browser: Playwright's Chromium build 1228 (headless), viewport 1500x950, locale `zh-CN`.
- Reproduced 2 times in the same build (probe run + manual check in the same dialog).

### Additional Information

- Screenshot attached: 添加模型 dialog after a failed 测试连接, with the English sentence under the model-name field.
- Found while walking the 设置 feature area (D8-04 测试模型连接); the map expected `✓ 可用（N ms）` / `✕ <reason>`, neither of which exists.
- Related but separate: #1292 covers run-time failures (`semantic-error` fallback). This one is the *configuration-time* path, with its own category enum, so it can be localized without touching run classification.

### Version Information

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, branch `main`
- Commit: `bbdbdd5c9e7d04de3ff1d33da52eb41b87d60c9a` (2026-11-21)
- Desktop app package version: `0.0.0` (private workspace package)

![d8-04-test-fail](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fb911b99-fd20-4519-80c0-60c74f61d80c)

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] The description below includes environment information and a minimal reproduction, so the report can be followed without further questions.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary**

A successful run ends with a "用时 N 秒" line. A run that fails while the model is still being reached ends with the failure card and nothing else — no duration at all. The run does know how long it took; the line just lives somewhere that never renders on this path.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Make the selected model unreachable (point its base URL at a dead port, or stop the model service) and send any message in a new session.
2. The run stops with `模型服务连接失败`, the explanation "无法连接模型服务，运行已停止。建议检查网络、代理设置及模型服务地址后重试。" and a folded "技术详情".
3. Nothing says how long the attempt took, although the same conversation's successful runs show `用时 N 秒` under the fold line.

![A failed run: title, explanation and technical details, but no elapsed time](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cd10a991-217f-4147-a660-a645f234bcb1)

**Root cause**

The duration is produced only by the fold line of a run, and the fold line only exists when the run has something to fold:

- `apps/desktop/src/views/AssistantTurn.tsx:605` — `const fold = live || hasMiddleContent(run, shown);`
- `hasMiddleContent` (`:452-465`) requires reasoning, subagents, tool calls, or prose beyond the shown answer. A run that fails before the model answers has none of them, so `fold` is `false` and the `<details>` block is skipped entirely.
- The elapsed label itself is built in `foldLabel` (`:469-482`) from `TEXT.conversation.elapsed(run.finishedAt - run.startedAt)` (`apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts:360`) and rendered only inside that `<summary>` (`:634-655`).
- The failure card is rendered separately (`:379`, `apps/desktop/src/views/RunFailureCard.tsx:31`) from `code`, `message` and `timeout` — no timing is passed to it.

So a failed run with no foldable content can never display a duration, even though `run.startedAt` and `run.finishedAt` are both known.

**Impact**

- A failure that took 4 minutes after retries looks exactly like one that failed instantly; the user cannot tell whether time was spent in the model gateway, in a retry loop, or nowhere.
- Anything that reads `用时` to recognise a finished run (a person skimming, or an automated check) sees no end marker on failed runs.
- The information is present in state, so this is a rendering gap rather than missing data.

**Suggested fix**

Render the duration for every terminal run that has both timestamps, independent of the fold:

- pass `startedAt`/`finishedAt` into `RunFailureCard` and add the same `TEXT.conversation.elapsed(...)` line there, or
- render a standalone `run-duration` line next to the failure card when `fold === false` and both timestamps exist.

A desktop unit test asserting that a terminal run with `startedAt`/`finishedAt` and no turns still shows the elapsed line would keep this from regressing.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Product: ScienceDiscovery `main` at `bbdbdd5c9e7d04de3ff1d33da52eb41b87d60c9a` (2026-11-21). API `127.0.0.1:4410`, Runner `127.0.0.1:4411`, desktop web surface `http://127.0.0.1:5174`.
- Host: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS, Node.js 22.23.2, pnpm 11.1.2.
- Client: Playwright Chromium build 1228, 1600x1000 viewport, locale `zh-CN`.
- The failing run: the selected model's base URL was unreachable, so the run stopped before producing any turn — which is exactly the case with nothing to fold.

### Additional Information

- Found while fault-injecting a broken model in scenario S-203 (fault recovery): the missing duration made it impossible to tell from the transcript whether the run had ended at all.
- Related but separate: #1292 (the failure code and detail text for this same card), #1299 (model connection test localization), #1300 (artifact version numbers).

### Version Information

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, branch `main`
- Commit: `bbdbdd5c9e7d04de3ff1d33da52eb41b87d60c9a` (2026-11-21)
- Desktop app package version: `0.0.0` (private workspace package)

issue:1306.body:
﻿### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] The description below includes environment information and a minimal reproduction, so the report can be followed without further questions.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary**

A product declared in a brand-new conversation can silently continue the version chain of an artifact created in an older conversation: the new session receives `version 4` of an artifact it never created, the older session's product is overwritten with the new content, and neither the user nor the model is told that this happened.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. In session A, ask the agent to write `report.md` in the workspace and declare it as an artifact. It becomes `v1`; publish two revisions so it reaches `v3`.
2. Start a new session B in the same project and ask the agent to write a different `report.md` (this is a separate piece of work — a run log, not a revision of A's report).
3. The agent calls `declare_artifact` with only `{"path": "report.md", ...}`.
4. B's answer says `Artifact 0635ff24…, version 4`, and B's artifact panel lists `report.md` at `v4`. Open session A: its `report.md` is now that same `v4`, carrying B's content.

**What the data shows** (`main` `bbdbdd5c`, `zh-CN`, desktop web surface)

Session B's `/api/sessions/<B>/artifact-outputs` returns exactly one entry:

```
artifact.id            0635ff24-0d7e-4eb2-a253-253d28f5e624
artifact.createdInSessionId     fca861a5-…   (session A)
artifact.createdInSessionTitle  用 Python 创建 report.md 文件
artifact.currentVersion 4
version.sessionId       e9afb9af-…   (session B)
version.version         4
version.turnId          set
```

Session A's `/api/sessions/<A>/artifacts` now reports the same artifact with `currentVersion: 4` and `updatedAt: 2026-11-22T06:41:49.242Z` — the moment session B published. So A's artifact row is visible, and its content has been replaced by another conversation's work.

**Why it happens**

- `services/api/src/store.ts:5752-5755` — when the caller does not pass an `artifactId`, the target artifact is resolved by `(projectId, name, research scope)`. A same-named artifact in the same project, created by *another session*, is a valid target.
- `services/api/src/store.ts:5797` — the new version takes `artifact.currentVersion + 1`, so the first product of a fresh conversation is `v4`.
- The publish result handed back to the model contains only `artifact_id`, `name`, `content`, `origin`, `version` and `version_id` — no `createdInSessionId`, no title, no previous version. The model therefore believes it declared a new artifact and reports "version 4" to the user without being able to explain `v1`–`v3`.
- `apps/desktop/src/views/WorkspacePanel.tsx:378-400` — the version menu labels entries `v{version}` only; there is no session or timestamp, and the picker is only rendered when a session produced more than one version (so in session B there is no picker at all, just `v4`).
- `services/api/src/store.ts:5728` already refuses cross-session rewrites with a 409 — `请在当前研究会话中创建独立产物，不能改写另一个研究副本` — but only when the owning session is a *research copy*. Two ordinary sessions of the same project are allowed to write over each other without any confirmation.
- When the caller passes no `baseVersionId`, the CAS check at `store.ts:5746` is skipped, so the write does not even need to have seen the version it overwrites.

**Impact**

- A fresh conversation's first deliverable starts at `v4`, relative to history the user cannot see in that conversation. Nothing in the panel says where `v1`–`v3` came from.
- The older conversation's product changes underneath it, silently. A user reopening it sees different content at a new version number with no record of which session wrote it.
- The model can "update" a product it has never read, and will describe a foreign version chain as its own work.
- Two sessions writing the same name interleave versions, and without `baseVersionId` the last write wins with no conflict raised. Version-number collisions are a separate defect (#1300, fixed by #1301); this one is about *which* chain a write lands in.
- Cleanup is asymmetric: `store.ts:5579` authorizes `deleteArtifact` against the *creating* session, so the session that can see and revise the artifact is not necessarily the one that may delete it.

**Suggested fix** (approved direction: make the continuation visible, and ask before the first cross-session write)

1. **Disclose the continuation.** Return the origin in the publish result, e.g. `continuedFrom: { sessionId, sessionTitle, version }` when the resolved artifact was created in another session, and let the model say so in its answer. In the panel, label the row with the creating session's title and put the per-version producer in the version menu (`v4 · 本会话 · 06:41`, `v3 · <session A> · 06:22`).
2. **Ask on the first cross-session write.** When the resolved artifact's `createdInSessionId` differs from the calling session, do not append silently: return a conflict that offers "continue this chain" (`baseVersionId` set, so CAS applies) or "publish as a new artifact" — the store already supports the latter as `forceNewArtifact` (`store.ts:5706`). The existing research-copy 409 gives the message shape to reuse.
3. Always require a base for a continuation, so a write that did not read the current version cannot overwrite it.

The project-level chain itself is intended (same path = same product inside one research scope) and should stay; what is missing is that the join is invisible and unavoidable.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Product: ScienceDiscovery `main` at `bbdbdd5c9e7d04de3ff1d33da52eb41b87d60c9a` (2026-11-21). API `127.0.0.1:4410`, Runner `127.0.0.1:4411`, desktop web surface `http://127.0.0.1:5174`.
- Host: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS, Node.js 22.23.2, pnpm 11.1.2.
- Client: Playwright Chromium build 1228, 1600x1000 viewport, locale `zh-CN`.
- Sessions: `fca861a5-…` (A, created `report.md` at 05:29), `e9afb9af-…` (B, published `v4` at 06:41). Container: `27cb6928-…`.

### Additional Information

- Found while exercising fault recovery (scenario S-203): the new session only wrote a run log named `report.md`, and was surprised by `version 4`.
- Related but separate: #1300 / #1301 (version numbers allocated without a uniqueness guard, and the stale-pointer allocation fix).
- The version picker itself (`v3`/`v2`/`v1` with no other identifier) was noted in #1300; this issue adds the missing provenance on top of it.

### Version Information

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, branch `main`
- Commit: `bbdbdd5c9e7d04de3ff1d33da52eb41b87d60c9a` (2026-11-21)
- Desktop app package version: `0.0.0` (private workspace package)

issue:1313.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**What the user sees first:** one skill file with a broken frontmatter makes the API answer **HTTP 400 to every request**, including `GET /health`. The workbench becomes unusable (nothing loads), and any health probe — the desktop's readiness check, the E2E `requireRealStack` gate, a monitoring check — reports the service as broken, although the process is running and its data is intact.

**Measured.** A skill that is actually loaded (`skills/idea-tree-team/SKILL.md`, the file shipped in the repo) had an unquoted `description` containing `: `, which is invalid YAML. With that file in the tree:

```
$ curl -sS -m 3 -w '\nHTTP=%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:4310/health
{"error":"SKILL.md frontmatter is invalid YAML: Nested mappings are not allowed in compact mappings at line 2, column 14:\n\ndescription: Use when the composer message starts with /idea-tree or /idea-tree-team, or the user explicitly asks for autonomous Idea Tree research: prepare supplied inputs for the research and explain its saved results.\n             ^\n"}
HTTP=400
```

- The same request **with** `Authorization: Bearer <token>` returns the identical body and `HTTP 400`.
- `HTTP 400`, not `503` and not a degraded payload: the failure is a refusal at the request entrance, before routing.
- The process had already logged `ScienceDiscovery listening on http://127.0.0.1:4310` and had served requests before the file was swapped in, so this is a **runtime, per-request** failure, not a startup crash.

**Negative control.** A newly added skill directory that is *not* loaded (a stray `skills/zz-bad-yaml-probe/SKILL.md` with the same kind of invalid YAML) did **not** break anything: `/health` kept answering `200`. So the trigger is "a skill the catalog actually loads", not "any YAML file under `skills/`".

**Expected.** A malformed skill file should be reported (logged, and once in the UI where skills are listed) and that **one** skill skipped; it must not take the whole API — and certainly not `/health` — down. `GET /health` should keep answering its normal payload, because a health probe must not depend on skill content.

**Reproduce**

1. Put the invalid frontmatter above into `skills/idea-tree-team/SKILL.md` (the description value unquoted, containing `: `).
2. Start the stack: `./scripts/start-stack.sh --mode local --no-node-build --no-jiuwenswarm`.
3. `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4310/health` → `HTTP 400` with the JSON error above.
4. Restore a valid file → `HTTP 200` with the normal health payload, no restart of anything else needed.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- WSL Ubuntu 24.04 on Windows 11 (Chinese locale), linux-amd64, Node v22.
- Checkout: `sciencediscovery`, working tree synced to `main` (2026-11-22); the malformed file came from a PR head under review (`667368d7`), reproduced on that head.
- Stack: `./scripts/start-stack.sh --mode local --no-node-build --no-jiuwenswarm`; API on `http://127.0.0.1:4310`, default data directory `.sciencediscovery-data`, real runner, bubblewrap 0.9.0.
- Reproduced twice: once incidentally while running a real E2E journey, once as this write-up's reproduction.
- Model endpoint is irrelevant to this defect (no model call is needed).

### Additional Information

- The error text is emitted by the skill-catalog load path; it names the offending file and the YAML line/column, so the loader already knows which file failed — the missing part is containing that failure to that one skill.
- Scope I verified directly: `GET /health`, authenticated and not. Because the refusal happens at the request entrance (the same body is returned for a route that must never read skills), I expect other routes are equally affected, but I did not probe them one by one — that part is inference, not measurement.
- Suggested acceptance: a malformed skill file is logged and skipped; `/health` still answers 200; the skills list shows that one skill as failed rather than the catalog being empty; and a test feeds the loader an invalid frontmatter and asserts the API still answers `/health`.
- This is a product defect and is independent of the PR that happened to contain the malformed file (that PR only edits prose in a skill description).

### Version Information

- Product code under test: repo `main` working tree synced 2026-11-22 (the checkout is synced by tarball, so its `.git` HEAD is stale; the working tree is what ran).
- Malformed file provenance: PR head `667368d7` (fixed later at `e4410b80`, which parses cleanly).
- No desktop build was involved: the defect reproduces over the HTTP API alone.

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] The description below includes environment information and a minimal reproduction, so the report can be followed without further questions.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary**

While a turn runs, the transcript shows one unchanging line — `正在规划下一步` — and the elapsed time appears only after the turn ends. A single request that took 77 minutes therefore looked identical to one that had hung on its first tool call.

**What happened**

One prompt (an A/B comparison task over an uploaded CSV) produced run `67330001` on the desktop surface:

- started `2026-11-22T09:14:30.770Z`, finished `2026-11-22T10:31:47.541Z` — **77 min 17 s**
- 299 model requests in that window (`model-sse-summary` lines in the API log), **7.3M tokens** charged to the session, 8 artifacts produced
- for the whole 77 minutes the conversation showed `正在规划下一步 ›` with a stop button, then `用时 1 小时 17 分` at the end

![One conversation: an interrupted run and the 77-minute run after it](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/46440f6a-036a-44f0-a82b-8cf413a1f690)

**Why it looks stuck**

- `apps/desktop/src/views/AssistantTurn.tsx:469-479` — for a run that has not reached a terminal state, `foldLabel()` returns `TEXT.conversation.thinkingNow` (`正在规划下一步`, `apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts:354`) and nothing else.
- `:480` — the elapsed string is produced only when `startedAt` and `finishedAt` both exist, i.e. only for runs that are already over.
- Tool calls and subagent cards do update, but they are inside the collapsed `<details>` body; the summary line the user sees while waiting never changes.
- `RunStatusLine` (`:362-395`) only surfaces errors, dropped events and unknown events — nothing about progress or duration.

So the only signals during a long turn are "something is happening" and a stop button. There is no stage, no step count, no last tool, no partial artifact, and no elapsed time — while the server knows all of it.

**Impact**

- The user cannot tell a working run from a stuck one. The only available action is `停止`, which throws away the work; with a 77-minute turn that is a very expensive coin flip.
- Waiting becomes unplannable: 1 minute and 80 minutes look the same, so nobody can decide whether to wait or come back.
- This is the core use case of the product — a research request that legitimately takes many tool calls — not an edge case.

**Suggested fix**

1. Show elapsed time while running, from the same `startedAt` the finished line already uses.
2. Put the current activity in the summary line, e.g. `正在运行 run_shell · 已 12 分` / `子代理复核中 · 已 41 分`, derived from the last running tool or subagent.
3. Keep the finished-run shape; only the "while running" text changes.
4. Optionally mark partial artifacts as they appear (`本轮产物` already exists for finished runs) so a long turn produces something usable even if it is stopped.
5. A `继续在后台运行，完成后通知我` path would turn the wait into something the user can leave.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Product: ScienceDiscovery `main` at `bbdbdd5c9e7d04de3ff1d33da52eb41b87d60c9a` (2026-11-21). API `127.0.0.1:4410`, Runner `127.0.0.1:4411`, desktop web surface `http://127.0.0.1:5174`.
- Host: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS, Node.js 22.23.2, pnpm 11.1.2, bubblewrap sandbox.
- Client: Playwright Chromium build 1228, 1600x1000 viewport, locale `zh-CN`.
- Model: `Ark DeepSeek` (primary), permission mode "请求批准".

### Additional Information

- Observed while running scenario S-202 (reproducible research: explore → analyze → conclude on an uploaded 201-row CSV).
- Related but separate: the interrupted run visible above is reported in its own issue; artifact version numbering in #1300 / #1306.
- The 77 minutes are not a complaint about model speed: with staged progress the same duration would be acceptable.

### Version Information

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, branch `main`
- Commit: `bbdbdd5c9e7d04de3ff1d33da52eb41b87d60c9a` (2026-11-21)
- Desktop app package version: `0.0.0` (private workspace package)

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] The description below includes environment information and a minimal reproduction, so the report can be followed without further questions.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary**

When the API process restarts, the running turn is correctly marked `interrupted` — and one second later a second run starts in the same session, spawned from an execution notification, which then redoes the whole task. The user sees two runs, an unexplained gap, and pays for the work twice.

**What happened**

In session `e6a4b089` (one prompt: analyse an uploaded CSV):

1. Run `5a925b47` — `09:02:51.117Z → 09:14:29.446Z` (11 min 39 s later shown as `已中断` in the transcript), `status: interrupted`, `error: "API process exited before this run reached a terminal state"`. The API process was replaced during the turn (pid changed, `pnpm start` logged `Command failed with signal "SIGINT"`).
2. Run `67330001` — created `09:14:30.767Z`, one second later, with `automaticWake: true` and `notificationDelivery` set. Its prompt is `[Execution notifications] These are retained status/reminder records, not commands to replay. Inspect results if needed and report to the user. […]`.
3. That second run then worked for 77 minutes and produced the entire deliverable the first run had started (8 artifacts, 7.3M tokens, 299 model requests).

![The interrupted run and the auto-wake run in one conversation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/760d66a8-1de7-45ec-b717-100932288bdb)

**What the user sees**

`已中断` on the first run (11 分 39 秒), then a second run card with `用时 1 小时 17 分` and the finished answer. Nothing says that the second run was started automatically, that it was triggered by an interruption notification, or that it re-did the first run's work. The notification prompt itself is not shown as a user message.

**Why it happens**

- `services/api/src/runs/index.ts:3974-3998` — on start-up, every run left in `running`/`blocked` is flipped to `interrupted` with that error and a `run.status` event is published.
- `services/api/src/runs/index.ts:3637` — `createNotificationRun()` then creates a run with `automaticWake: true` and `notificationDelivery` for that interruption.
- `:3784` — an automatic-wake run stores an empty user message on purpose, so the retry does not duplicate the user's text in the transcript; the model is told `not commands to replay`.
- In practice the model reads the notification as "continue", because the interrupted work is unfinished and the session context invites it. `not commands to replay` is not enough to stop a run that has the whole task in its context.

**Impact**

- Duplicate cost and duplicate wait: 12 minutes plus 77 minutes, and the token bill for both, for one question.
- Trust: the first run's partial results and artifacts may already exist. The second run then republishes the same product (`report.md`, `stats.csv`, …), so version history mixes the two attempts.
- The transcript shows two runs with no relationship between them. If the user had scrolled away, nothing explains why a second run exists at all.
- The model is asked not to replay, and replays anyway — that is a sign the instruction is not enforceable at this layer.

**Suggested fix**

1. Make the retry explicit in the UI: a notice in the conversation — "上一轮因服务重启中断，已自动继续（第 2 次尝试）" — linking the two runs, and keep `已中断` on the first.
2. Give the auto-wake run a narrow prompt: report the interruption and ask the user whether to continue, or let the *continuation* be an explicit user action. If it must continue, pass the interrupted run's progress (completed tool calls, produced artifacts) and forbid redoing them.
3. Record `parentRunId` (or `resumedFromRunId`) on the auto-wake run so the transcript and the API can show the relationship, and mark its artifacts with the attempt they came from.
4. Do not let a notification run inherit the original prompt's task framing; today the boundary is only a sentence inside the prompt.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Product: ScienceDiscovery `main` at `bbdbdd5c9e7d04de3ff1d33da52eb41b87d60c9a` (2026-11-21). API `127.0.0.1:4410`, Runner `127.0.0.1:4411`, desktop web surface `http://127.0.0.1:5174`.
- Host: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS, Node.js 22.23.2, pnpm 11.1.2.
- Client: Playwright Chromium build 1228, 1600x1000 viewport, locale `zh-CN`.
- The API restart was external to the client (`SIGINT` to the API process, pid changed from `182758` to `3793181`); the client stayed open and reconnected.
- Run records for the session: `5a925b47…` (interrupted) and `67330001…` (`automaticWake: true`, completed).

### Additional Information

- Observed while running scenario S-202 (reproducible research over an uploaded CSV).
- Complementary issue from the same run: the 77-minute turn had no staged progress (separate report).
- The interrupted run's error text is accurate; the missing part is telling the user that a second run exists and why.

### Version Information

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, branch `main`
- Commit: `bbdbdd5c9e7d04de3ff1d33da52eb41b87d60c9a` (2026-11-21)
- Desktop app package version: `0.0.0` (private workspace package)

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

With manual checkpoint confirmation turned **off**, an evolve design can end on a checkpoint without ever starting the search, and nothing in the UI says so. The session simply sits idle until the user types a reply.

Observed twice, in two shapes:

**A. Auto mode ends on checkpoint 2/4 and the run is never created** (session `665b8e96`, 2026-11-23, `a8573558`)
- New session → `/evolve-design --algorithm puct <task>` → 新建程序演进实验 → uncheck 检查点需要人工确认 → 开始设计 → 发送.
- Transcript ends with: task → 检查点 1/4 → client auto-continue message (`继续完成余下的检查点，并直接调用 create_evolve_run 启动搜索；在搜索启动前不要停下。`) → 检查点 2/4. That is the whole session (4 messages).
- No run card appears; `GET /api/evolve/runs` has no new run; the composer stays idle. No banner, badge or hint says the search was never started.
- Typing `确认检查点 2/4，继续。` continues the design and starts run `b9a8f3da`.

**B. A checkpoint that does not become a card** (session `252ca40d`, run `df752fc3`, 2026-11-22, `checkpointMode: confirm`)
- `09:51:54.709Z` checkpoint 1 renders as a card with 确认，继续; `09:55:00.530Z` confirmed.
- `09:58:27.790Z` checkpoint 2 arrives as **plain prose** (two (a)/(b) questions, no card, no buttons).
- The session sits idle until `11:03:49.635Z` — **65 minutes** — when the tester typed an answer by hand.

**Expected**: when a design's turn ends and this design has no search yet, the client should either carry the next step forward itself, or state plainly that the search has not started and what to send. The code already has the second half of that intent: `use-auto-continue.ts` renders `已停止自动续跑` (`zh.ts:1799-1800`) when the same step comes back, and its header comment says *"a record with nothing to press otherwise reads as a design that hung"* — but that badge can only be drawn **on a card** (`CheckpointCard.tsx:190-194`), so a turn that ends without a card has nowhere to say it.

**Not deterministic**: the same day, run `e344eb1b` (`252ca40d`, `checkpointMode: auto`) went from the user message at `06:25:05.088Z` to the run being created at `06:26:46.085Z` with no manual confirmation in between. So the trigger condition is still unknown; both endings do occur on the same build.

Code pointers:
- `apps/desktop/src/evolve/use-auto-continue.ts` — one push per step, `refusedStep` only surfaces through the card; explicit gates on `run.status === "completed"` and `trailingAutoStep(answer)`.
- `apps/desktop/src/views/CheckpointCard.tsx:175-194` — badge lives inside the card.
- `apps/desktop/src/Markdown.tsx:45` — checkpoint blocks are recognised by a fenced `evolve-checkpoint` block; anything else is ordinary prose.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Product: ScienceDiscovery desktop app (Electron shell around the web UI), Chinese locale `zh-CN`, window 1500×950.
- Commit: `a8573558f8c372854079a65906171b3a543b6fb7` (main, 2026-11-22), API `4410` / runner `4411` / evolve sidecar `17676`.
- Evolve runtime state: `GET /api/evolve/status` → `{"state":"ready","canInitialize":false,"sandbox":"bwrap"}`.
- Model: Ark DeepSeek (`hasApiToken=true`), permission mode 完全访问.
- Host: Ubuntu 22.04.5, Chromium 1228 driven by Playwright 1.61.1.

### Additional Information

- Evidence (desktop screenshots): `~/sd-test/evidence/s205/M1-opened.png` (the stalled session as the user sees it), `C3-checkpoint.png` (a normal manual checkpoint card), `N1-session-stopped.png` (run card after the manual continue).
- Runs involved: `84dcbd84` (puct, manual, succeeded), `17f87374` (openevolve, auto, succeeded — counter-example that auto can work), `b9a8f3da` (puct, auto, stopped by the tester), `e344eb1b` (puct, auto, succeeded — counter-example).
- The same stall shape is reproducible on the web build of the same commit; nothing in the transcript says 「搜索还没开始」.

### Version Information

- `a8573558f8c372854079a65906171b3a543b6fb7` (main branch, 2026-11-22T15:52:52Z).
- Also present in `bbdbdd5c9e7d04de3ff1d33da52eb41b87d60c9a` (2026-11-21) per the `df752fc3` observation.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

The desktop task panel for an evolve run has no **全屏 (Full screen)** and no **查看完整目标 (View full goal)** control, although the capability text for both exists in the desktop string table. A long goal can therefore only be read truncated in the run card.

Steps:
1. Start an evolve run (any algorithm), wait for the run card, click the card.
2. The right-hand panel switches to 任务 and shows the overview, the score chart, the tree and the node list.
3. Its controls are only: 停止 (`button.evolve-task-stop`), 收起面板, and the panel splitter (`调整面板宽度`).

Observed:
- No 全屏 / 退出全屏 anywhere in the panel.
- No 查看完整目标; the goal is only shown as a one-line truncated title (`写一对标准库 Python 函数 pack(text: str) -> bytes 与 unpack(blob…`), so the constraints of the task cannot be read back while the run is going.
- The panel header eyebrow 程序演进 is also absent on desktop; the panel is the generic 任务 / 产物 / 工作区 group.

Expected: the desktop task panel should expose the same two controls the web build has, or the strings should be removed so the two surfaces do not disagree.

Code pointers:
- `apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts:1902-1904` declares `fullscreen: "全屏"`, `exitFullscreen: "退出全屏"`, `fullTask: "查看完整目标"`; `apps/desktop/src/text/en.ts` mirrors them.
- `grep -rn "fullTask\|exitFullscreen" apps/desktop/src` → no matches, i.e. the strings are unused by the desktop app.
- `apps/web/src/evolve/EvolvePanel.tsx` is the surface that does render them.
- `apps/desktop/src/views/evolve/EvolveDetail.tsx:185` is where `evolve-task-stop` lives — that is the whole control row on desktop.

- Product: ScienceDiscovery desktop app (Electron shell around the web UI), Chinese locale `zh-CN`, window 1500×950.
- Commit: `a8573558f8c372854079a65906171b3a543b6fb7` (main, 2026-11-22), API `4410` / runner `4411` / evolve sidecar `17676`.
- Evolve runtime: `{"state":"ready","canInitialize":false,"sandbox":"bwrap"}`; model Ark DeepSeek, permission 完全访问.
- Host: Ubuntu 22.04.5, Chromium 1228 + Playwright 1.61.1.

### Additional Information

- Screenshot: `~/sd-test/evidence/s205/E4-panel-full.png` — a running puct run with the panel open (overview 最优解 0.5930 / 有效节点 11/11 / 层数 3 / puct / Token 81,415, score chart and tree present, controls only 停止 + 收起面板).

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

While a turn is running the permission pill is disabled, so its mode cannot be changed. An evolve design started in 请求批准 (`ask_for_dangerous`) mode therefore stops at its first shell command, and the UI gives no sign that it is waiting for an approval — it keeps showing 正在规划下一步. In my run the design sat like that for **3 hours 31 minutes** until I cancelled the turn.

Steps:
1. New session in the desktop app; leave the permission pill at 请求批准.
2. Type `/evolve-design --algorithm openevolve <task>` and send.
3. The design writes an evaluator, then asks for `Run a shell script in the Session workspace`.
4. Try to switch to 完全访问 while it waits: the pill is `disabled`, `title="这一轮跑完才能切换权限"`.

Observed:
- `GET /api/permission-requests?status=pending` shows the request (`createdAt 2026-11-23T02:11:52.696Z`, summary `Run a shell script in the Session workspace`), still `pending` after 3.5 h.
- The composer shows only 正在规划下一步 and the disabled pill; nothing points at the pending approval, and there is no link or badge to open it.
- Cancelling the turn (`POST /api/sessions/<id>/run/cancel` → 202) then loses the half-written design; the only way forward is to start over with 完全访问.

Expected, any of:
- allow switching the permission mode for subsequent tool calls of the running turn (or offer "allow and switch to 完全访问" on the approval itself), or
- at minimum surface the pending approval prominently (badge/HUD with a link) instead of a passive 正在规划下一步, and keep the request reachable after the turn is cancelled.

Code pointers:
- `apps/desktop/src/views/Composer.tsx:1113` — `title={running ? TEXT.composer.permissionLocked : TEXT.composer.permissionMode}` and the same `running` flag disables the button.
- `apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts:259` — `permissionLocked: "这一轮跑完才能切换权限"`.

Note: the same lock makes the *documented* evolve workflow fragile, because evolve needs shell runs and the documented setup is to switch to 完全访问 **before** starting the design; if the user forgets, the only feedback is a silent stall.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Product: ScienceDiscovery desktop app (Electron shell around the web UI), Chinese locale `zh-CN`, 1500×950.
- Commit: `a8573558f8c372854079a65906171b3a543b6fb7` (main, 2026-11-22), API `4410` / runner `4411` / evolve sidecar `17676`.
- Session: `fb32e61f-59e3-46d9-a325-2083b3ed3bc2` (the stalled design), pending request id `27b4ceee-b80f-4bd1-9734-f779b24094b3`.
- Evolve runtime `{"state":"ready","canInitialize":false,"sandbox":"bwrap"}`; model Ark DeepSeek.
- Host: Ubuntu 22.04.5, Chromium 1228 + Playwright 1.61.1.

### Additional Information

- Evidence: `~/sd-test/evidence/s205/H1-dialog-auto.png` (the dialog before sending), `J1-dialog.png` (the same dialog after switching to 完全访问 — this path works), plus the pending-request JSON quoted above.
- Workaround used: approve via `POST /api/permission-requests/<id>/decision {"decision":"allow_matching"}` — that resolves it, but the UI never offered it.
- The same applies to any long tool-using turn, not only evolve: the turn cannot be re-scoped mid-flight, so the user must cancel and restart.

### Version Information

- `a8573558f8c372854079a65906171b3a543b6fb7` (main branch, 2026-11-22T15:52:52Z).

issue:1334.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary.** In a report, an `[evidenceN]` chip opens the 科学记忆 card. When the cited Evidence node was created in a *different Session of the same project*, the card always says **"This memory was not found"**, although the node exists in the memory graph and can be read by an unscoped query. Only citations whose node lives in the report's own Session can be opened.

This is the normal case for project memory: a later Session writes a report that cites literature gathered earlier in the project.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. In the desktop client, in Session A (`789fd699-f16a-4248-a59c-4fd6e8fa10d7`), retrieve literature so that Evidence nodes are recorded — e.g. PMID 42888260, 43044265, 40242216.
2. In Session B (`94d52ab1-1718-416f-9675-85d2117e7bb0`), same project, let the agent produce `report.md` that cites those nodes. The report version persists the alias → node map:

```json
[{"id":"4c6f51fa-0c87-46ca-b7aa-cd73f2844207","kind":"evidence","label":"evidence1"},
 {"id":"73392b92-10e9-4963-99d3-9068de05cd64","kind":"evidence","label":"evidence2"},
 {"id":"978921ef-ac48-4bd2-90c8-fb74d7537da9","kind":"evidence","label":"evidence3"}]
```

3. Open that report and press `[evidence1]` (or `[evidence3]`).

**Actual**

```text
证据
科学记忆
没有找到这条记忆
记忆里没有这条记录。它可能已被删除，或记忆服务当前不可用。
```

**Expected.** The card shows the evidence content and its 溯源 (provenance) chain, exactly as it does for evidence created inside the report's own Session.

**Proof that the node exists.** The card's lookup is the node-type query, scoped to the report's Session:

```text
POST /api/memory/query/by-node-type
{"node_types":["Evidence"],"session_id":"94d52ab1-1718-416f-9675-85d2117e7bb0"}
-> {"hits":[],"total":0,"truncated":false}

POST /api/memory/query/by-node-type
{"node_types":["Evidence"]}
-> {"hits":[{"id":"978921ef-...","sessionId":"789fd699-...",...},
            {"id":"73392b92-...","sessionId":"789fd699-...",...},
            {"id":"4c6f51fa-...","sessionId":"789fd699-...",...}], "total":5}
```

Same ids, same graph; only the Session scope differs.

**Root cause**

- `apps/desktop/src/views/MemoryCardDialog.tsx:161`:

  ```ts
  const targetSession = reference.sessionId ?? sessionId;
  ```

  The dialog then calls `listMemoryNodes(client, [label], targetSession)` and matches the reference by node id (`matchReferenceHit`, `apps/desktop/src/app/memory.ts:159`). No match → `missing` → "This memory was not found".
- The persisted reference carries **no** `sessionId`. The alias → node map is built by `toChipMap()` in `packages/memory/src/memory-graph.ts`, which copies only `id`, `kind`, `label` (and `version` for artifacts) out of the sidecar's `chip_map`. `ComposerReference.sessionId` exists in the schema (`packages/schema/src/session.ts:168`) and the card already honours it — nothing ever writes it.
- So the lookup is scoped to the Session that wrote the report, where a node created elsewhere does not exist.

**Impact if not fixed**

- Every citation that points at project memory from another Session is unreadable in the desktop client: the reader sees "not found" for a record that is there. The citation trail — the whole point of 科学记忆 — is broken exactly in the workflow it exists for (gather once, cite in later Sessions).
- The message says "*It may have been deleted*", which actively implies data loss. An unavailable service already has its own message (`unreachableTitle`/`unreachableBody`, selected in `MemoryCardDialog.tsx:183-190` via `graphTemporarilyUnavailable`), so the "unavailable" half of that sentence never applies — a genuinely missing record and a record outside the Session look identical to the user, and both look like deletion.
- It also corrupts downstream judgement: in the same run a Reviewer specialist reported two numeric claims as unsupported because it saw no `[evidenceN]` mapping, while the mapping existed — it simply cannot be opened.

**Suggested fix**

A. Card-side fallback (smallest, fixes existing reports): when the scoped lookup returns no match and the reference has no `sessionId`, retry once with `session_id` omitted — node ids are globally unique — and use that hit, including its `sessionId` for the provenance chain. A budget refusal (`memory_graph_query_limit`) or an unreachable sidecar must keep rendering as "unavailable", not as "missing".

B. Persist the owning Session: add `session_id` to the sidecar's `chip_map`, copy it in `toChipMap()`, and the card's existing `reference.sessionId` path works with no further UI change. More correct long-term, but references already stored need a backfill, so A is still worth having.

C. Fix the copy in the same change: `memory.notFoundBody` should not claim the record may have been deleted or that the service may be unavailable; say that the record is not in this Session's memory (or drop the sentence in favour of the honest "not found"), and keep the unavailable case on its own message.

A + C is enough to make every already-stored report readable; B can follow as data work.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- ScienceDiscovery desktop client (Electron shell driving the desktop web UI), viewport 1500x950, `zh-CN`.
- Linux (Ubuntu 22.04.5), Chromium 1228 driven by Playwright 1.x from the repo's `.e2e` install.

issue:1340.body:
Run: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/45212568993 (Nightly #105, attempt 1, `workflow_dispatch`, profile `daily`, backend `jiuwenswarm`)

Head SHA: `9da58ad619f972e44eb674c5d4cc9118813f7222`

## Summary

Two independent external causes made this nightly red. Neither is a product defect, but one of them is recorded wrongly, and the recovery path the run needs does not exist in the failed-jobs rerun.

| Job | Result | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Gate / L4/L5 real E2E / Real E2E (research-11)` | failure | external: model gateway answered 502 / `read ECONNRESET` on both attempts |
| `Gate / L4/L5 real E2E / Account for real cases` | failure | downstream accounting: `- research-11: SHARD_FAILED` |
| `Gate / merge-gate` | failure | downstream: `CI gate failed: real-scheduled: failure; macos-desktop: abandoned` |
| `Report the outcome` | failure | downstream: `RESULT: abandoned` |
| `Gate / macOS desktop installer (arm64)` | cancelled | external: no macOS runner was ever assigned; no step ran |

Everything else passed on this SHA: L1, UT, ST, Docker, both binary releases, the Windows installer, Coverage, all five mocked workers (`Planned 189; executed 189; passed 189`) and 13 of the 14 real workers, so `Account for real cases` counted `Planned 22; executed 22; passed 21`.

## 1. research-11: a provider outage is scored as the product's failure

Job https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/45212568993/job/137825635928, step `Run the frozen real E2E shard`.

The frozen shard held one identity, `test/journey-idea-tree-real.spec.ts › Idea Tree real research › real Idea Tree research completes and its result survives a reload` (plan digest `cc111227c7d7`). First attempt:

```
18:22:32.4688386Z   Error: research settled as "interrupted": Model HTTP 502: {"error":"Model stream failed after response headers: read ECONNRESET"}
18:22:34.0581408Z   ✘  1 [real] › ../test/journey-idea-tree-real.spec.ts:26:3 › … (2.9m)
```

The harness retried the case once in the same job (`18:22:36.7162821Z Repeating 1 failed case(s): …`) and got the identical gateway answer:

```
18:28:46.9978838Z   Error: research settled as "interrupted": Model HTTP 502: {"error":"Model stream failed after response headers: read ECONNRESET"}
18:28:48.8493928Z   ✘  1 [real] › ../test/journey-idea-tree-real.spec.ts:26:3 › … (5.8m)
```

The shard summary then recorded no provider fault at all:

```
| e2e-real | `cc111227c7d7` | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 |   (planned/executed/passed/passed-after-retry/failed/provider faults/skipped)
- e2e-real: PROVIDER_FAULT_RETRY_FAILED: 1
- e2e-real: PLAYWRIGHT_WORKER_FAILED: 1
- e2e-real: FAIL: playwright:test/journey-idea-tree-real.spec.ts::…/Idea%20Tree%20real%20research/…@linux/amd64/jiuwenswarm
```

That is the gateway's own 502 body, not a product verdict, but the harness files it as `FAIL` with `provider faults 0`, and `Account for real cases` repeats it that way (`- FAIL: playwright:test/journey-idea-tree-real.spec.ts::…`). The classifier only recognises a gateway fault when the text carries the gateway's own vocabulary (`181001`, `model call failed`, `openai api`, `chat/completions`) — see `GATEWAY_CONTEXT` in `test/support/tagged/provider-fault.mjs`. Idea Tree's transport raises its own wording instead, `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/vendor/idea_tree/research.py:250`:

```python
raise RuntimeError(f"Model HTTP {error.code}: {detail}") from error
```

which matches no gateway context, so the fault is dropped. Reproduced at this SHA against the exact recorded message:

```
$ node --input-type=module -e '
import { detectProviderFaultFromErrors } from "./test/support/tagged/provider-fault.mjs";
const msg = `research settled as "interrupted": Model HTTP 502: {"error":"Model stream failed after response headers: read ECONNRESET"}

expect(received).toBe(expected) // Object.is equality

Expected: "completed"
Received: "interrupted"`;
console.log("observed  =>", JSON.stringify(detectProviderFaultFromErrors([msg])));
console.log("181001    =>", JSON.stringify(detectProviderFaultFromErrors([msg.replace("Model HTTP 502", "[181001] model call failed, Model HTTP 502")])));
'
observed  => null
181001    => {"code":"provider-transport","status":null}
```

So the same text is a `provider-transport` fault once the gateway's `181001 model call failed` wording is present, and the product's failure when Idea Tree is the one reporting it. `.ci/provider-fault.test.mjs` pins only the gateway vocabulary (`GATEWAY_500`, `GATEWAY_503`), so nothing covers this second reporter.

That matters beyond cosmetics: the failure is attributed to the product in the run summary and in this report's own accounting, while #1238 (the same class of outage, reported by the gateway itself) was classified `external` / `PROVIDER_FAULT`. The product did retry — `research.py` retries 429/5xx up to `MAX_ATTEMPTS = 2` with ≤4 s backoff before raising — and the shard retried the whole case once, so the fault was seen three times over ~10 minutes.

Transient or not: the gateway was healthy again immediately afterwards on the same endpoint. `Real E2E (research-12)` ran 18:29:28–18:32:55 and `Real E2E (research-13)` ran 18:33:27–19:04:23, and both passed, so this is not a configuration or product problem for this SHA.

## 2. macOS desktop installer (arm64): the runner was never assigned

Job https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/45212568993/job/137825643357 (`needs: [policy, l1]`, both succeeded at 16:06:41Z), label `macos-15`.

```
$ gh api /repos/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/jobs/137825643357
{"completed_at":"2026-11-23T16:21:43Z","conclusion":"cancelled","created_at":"2026-11-23T16:06:41Z",
 "labels":["macos-15"],"name":"Gate / macOS desktop installer (arm64)","runner_id":0,"runner_name":"",
 "started_at":"2026-11-23T16:06:41Z","status":"completed","steps":[]}
```

No step ever started, no runner was assigned (`runner_id: 0`), and nothing in the repository can explain it: the same job on the previous run's runner was healthy (`45073284028`, `macos-15`, 18 steps, success 21:40–22:02Z), the workflow's `timeout-minutes: 120` does not apply while queued, and GitHub recorded no incident on 2026-11-23 (`https://www.githubstatus.com/api/v2/incidents.json` has no entry that day). The `needs` context inside `merge-gate` reports the job as `abandoned`, and `tier-policy.mjs gate` correctly refuses to treat that as a pass.

The recovery gap is that a cancelled job is not a failed job. `merge-gate` raised:

```
Error: CI gate failed: real-scheduled: failure; macos-desktop: abandoned
```

and the only offered bulk operation, `POST /actions/runs/45212568993/rerun-failed-jobs`, is documented as "re-run all of the failed jobs and their dependent jobs" — nothing in it recreates a job that never started, so `macos-desktop` would still be `abandoned` in the rerun's `needs` and the gate would fail again with the same message. The specific-job endpoint (`POST /actions/jobs/137825643357/rerun`) is the only thing that can re-run that job, and even that alone cannot pass the gate while `real-scheduled` is still a failure from attempt 1 — recovering this run needs both, or a fresh run.

## 3. Downstream jobs fail as designed

- `Account for real cases` (job 137939547826): `### Real E2E: FAIL`, `Planned 22; executed 22; passed 21; provider faults 0`, `- research-11: SHARD_FAILED`. It runs no model call; it reconciled 14 shard artifacts, including `real-e2e-results-research-11`, and the missing pass is real evidence, not an accounting bug.
- `merge-gate` (job 137939753365): declared `"real-scheduled": {"result": "failure"}` and `"macos-desktop": {"result": "abandoned"}` itself, so the gate message names its own inputs.
- `Report the outcome` (job 137939983308): `RESULT: abandoned` fails the `[[ "${RESULT}" == "success" ]]` step. Expected: "a skipped or cancelled gate is not a pass either".

## What was checked / how a rerun behaves here

- All five job records of this run through `/actions/runs/45212568993/jobs` and each failed job's own log; the `needs` JSON printed by `merge-gate`; the accounting output of `Account for real cases`.
- Whether a failed-jobs rerun re-uses attempt-1 artifacts: it does. In run 45073284028 attempt 2 the identical four jobs were re-run after `Real E2E (research-8)` failed and the run went green, consuming the other shards' attempt-1 artifacts, and re-uploading the same artifact names (`real-e2e-results`, `e2e-results`, `real-e2e-verdict`, `case-execution-details.md`) produced a second artifact per name rather than a conflict.
- Why no failed-jobs rerun was made here: every failed job is downstream of one of the two external causes above, but the resulting rerun cannot turn the run green, for the reason in section 2. A rerun would spend another paid research-11 shard to reproduce a red `macos-desktop` gate. A full re-run (`POST /actions/runs/45212568993/rerun`) or a fresh `Nightly` dispatch re-runs ~14 real workers and ~2 h of gate time, and is a scheduling decision for the repository, not a repair.

## Related work

- #1238 — same class of gateway fault (stream reset mid-answer), but reported by the gateway, so it was classified `external`/`PROVIDER_FAULT`. That is the attribution this run did not get.
- #1239 — an earlier research-11 nightly report; different root cause (managed Python base setup `failed`, case `BLOCKED`, nothing executed). This run executed the case and lost it at the gateway.
- #1327 — Idea Tree ends the whole research as `interrupted` on one unusable model answer. This run's `interrupted` came from a transport 502, not from answer validation, so it is a different entry into the same terminal state.
- #1339 (open) — isolate tagged case retries. It does not change this outcome: the retry ran, and the provider was still returning 502.
- #813 — the earlier L3 version of "one gateway outage fails the gate"; the accounting and retry handling in this run are the later form of that work.

## What would close this

1. Let the provider-fault classifier recognise Idea Tree's own reporter, e.g. a `Model HTTP <5xx>:` raised by `research.py`'s transport beside the body that follows it, so this outage is reported as `PROVIDER_FAULT` (status 502) instead of `FAIL`, and add a regression case for the exact text above to `.ci/provider-fault.test.mjs`.
2. Decide the recovery route for a distribution job that was never started: the gate must keep failing on it, but "re-run failed jobs" cannot fix it, so the documented remedy has to be a specific-job re-run or a fresh run. A person with Actions write decides which.

Environment: `ubuntu-26.04` hosted runners for the Linux jobs, `macos-15` for the desktop job, Windows runner for the installer; CI Node 22.19.0; profile `daily`, backend `jiuwenswarm`, model `deepseek-flash` through the CI gateway; version stamp `nightly-20261124-9da58ad`.
