## Summary

Model setup is the first-run gate: with no provider configured, **Settings → Model registry** opens the *Connect model* wizard automatically (`apps/web/src/ProviderModelSettings.tsx:617-618`). The screen is meant to answer one question — "which model will my runs use?" — but it currently asks it in six different places, uses one label for two different actions, and commits some answers with a Save button while committing others the moment they are clicked. This report is about that flow, not about how any single control looks.

## What the screen offers today

| # | Control | Where | What it writes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `Connect model` → `Save & connect` | registry heading (`ProviderModelSettings.tsx:897-904`) | creates the provider **and** registers every model the vendor lists, immediately |
| 2 | `Fetch model list` → tick rows → `Save & connect` | wizard footer (`ModelConnectWizard.tsx:828-841`) | same, narrowed to the ticked models |
| 3 | `Advanced configuration` → `Manual entries` / `Model identifier` | a fold inside the wizard (`ModelConnectWizard.tsx:745-794`) | same, for models the listing does not return |
| 4 | `Refresh list` → per-row `Add` | expanded provider (`ProviderModelSettings.tsx:346-348`) | one model, immediately |
| 5 | `Add model` (toggle) → manual form | bottom of the expanded provider (`ProviderModelSettings.tsx:505-515`) | one model, immediately |
| 6 | `Global default task model` select | registry heading (`ProviderModelSettings.tsx:879-896`) | `globalSettings.modelId`, immediately |
| 7 | `Edit` provider → `Save` / `Cancel` | expanded provider (`ProviderModelSettings.tsx:703-749`) | provider fields, staged until Save |

Above all of that sits a separate `Model catalog` strip with its own refresh (`ProviderModelSettings.tsx:386-400`).

## Problems

### 1. `Add model` means two different things, one above the other

Inside the same expanded provider, the per-model row action uses `t("providers.models.add")` (`ProviderModelSettings.tsx:348`) and the toggle that opens the manual form uses the *same* string (`:506`). So the row of a listed model offers "Add" (register this model) and a few pixels below the table another "Add model" opens a form. The wizard reuses the label a third time for its manual-entry toggle, but submits with a different one, `Add to list` (`ModelConnectWizard.tsx:779, 791`). A user cannot predict what any of these three controls will do from its label.

### 2. Two incompatible save models in the same panel

Provider fields are a draft: `Save` / `Cancel`, plus a `window.confirm` when another provider's `Edit` would discard the draft (`ProviderModelSettings.tsx:679-687, 693-697`). Everything else writes immediately:

- adding a model — `addModel()` calls the API at once, no confirm (`:784-823`);
- deleting a model — immediate, but guarded by `window.confirm` (`:825-863`);
- deleting a provider — immediate, guarded by `window.confirm` (`:751-754`);
- the default-model select — immediate (`:879-896`).

The same panel therefore mixes revertible and irreversible actions with no visual cue for which is which. Collapsing the row or expanding another one hides an unsaved provider draft with no prompt at that moment (`:699-701`), and the prompt only arrives later, when the settings dialog is closed — by then the user has usually forgotten the draft exists.

### 3. Registering *every* listed model is the silent default, and choosing models is hidden

With no explicit choice, `Save & connect` fetches the vendor list and registers all of it (`ModelConnectWizard.tsx:324-339`). To choose a subset the user must first press `Fetch model list` (`:828-841`) and only then do checkboxes appear. The only warning is the small plan line "Save & connect registers every model the provider lists" (`:838`), while the manual path that most users need when discovery fails is behind `Advanced configuration`, a fold that otherwise looks like protocol/proxy plumbing. Nothing states before saving that the first registered model will become the global default; that effect is only reported afterwards (`:414-421, 433-450`).

### 4. The default task model is edited in two places with different commit semantics

The registry heading has a `Global default task model` select that writes instantly (via `replaceDefaultModelOverride`, `App.tsx:5259-5269`). The same value is also edited in **Settings → Global → Task model**, which is a draft saved by the dialog's own Save (`App.tsx:5217-5219`). Two controls, one field, opposite commit behaviour — the difference is invisible until someone loses an edit.

### 5. Vocabulary: seven labels for four concepts

`Connect model`, `Save & connect`, `Add model`, `Add to list`, `Fetch model list`, `Refresh list`, `Advanced configuration` vs `Advanced connection settings` (`i18n/messages.ts:675-720, 738, 771`). "Connect", "register", "add" and "save" are used interchangeably for one operation, while "fetch"/"refresh" is the only genuinely different one.

### 6. Success does not end the flow

`resetPlan()` clears only the model plan (`ModelConnectWizard.tsx:157-164`); the API key, provider name, base URL and success banner stay (`:433-450`). Pressing `Save & connect` again therefore creates a second provider with the same display name — allowed by the store (`services/api/src/store.ts:2758-2779` has no name uniqueness check) — and there is no explicit "done" state to tell the user the wizard has finished.

## Actual vs expected

| | Actual | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| Entry points | Six ways to register a model across three levels (wizard, provider row, manual form), plus a default-model control duplicated in another tab | One way for each intent: add a provider; add models to a provider; pick the default model |
| Commit model | Provider fields staged, models and default immediate, deletes confirmed one by one | One commit model for the whole registry, with the same confirmation rule for every destructive action |
| Model choice | Register-all unless the user discovers `Fetch model list`; manual entry inside `Advanced configuration` | The listing visible by default with checkboxes, "register all" an explicit choice, manual entry next to it |
| Default model | Same field, two controls, two commit semantics, no indication of which wins | One control, or a link to the canonical one |
| After success | Form keeps the key and name; second press creates a duplicate provider | Clear, collapsed or "done" state; a duplicate name is warned about |

## Where

- `apps/web/src/ProviderModelSettings.tsx` — registry heading, wizard mount, provider rows, per-row add/delete, manual form toggle, default-model select, provider draft.
- `apps/web/src/ModelConnectWizard.tsx` — `resolveModelPlan` (register-all fallback), advanced fold, footer plan summary, success state.
- `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts:675-720, 722-723, 738, 771, 915` — the button and heading vocabulary.
- `apps/web/src/App.tsx:5217-5219, 5250-5280` — Mounting of the registry and of the Global settings group that edits the same default.

## Root cause

One component serves four jobs at once — registry list, provider editor, model picker, default-model setter — and each job brought its own persistence style and its own copy. The wizard was added later to make first-run setup one step, but it kept the provider editor's advanced fields *and* gained model registration, so provider creation and model registration now overlap instead of composing: the wizard can register models, the provider row can only add one at a time, and the provider editor cannot touch models at all. The `Add model` label was reused from the existing manual form for three controls that do different things.

## Suggested direction

1. **One control per intent.** `Add provider` (the wizard) and a single `Add model` per provider, opening one dialog that shows the fetched listing with checkboxes and keeps manual entry as a fallback in the same dialog. Remove the separate advanced/manual toggle, and stop using `Add` both for "register this listed model" and "open a form".
2. **Pick one commit model for the registry** and keep it: either stage every edit behind Save (provider fields, models, default) or make every action immediate with an undo. Apply the same confirmation rule to add, delete model and delete provider.
3. **Make model selection visible in the wizard.** Fetch the listing as soon as the key is entered, show it above the fold, and make "register all listed models" an explicit checkbox instead of the silent fallback. State the "first model becomes the global default" consequence before `Save & connect`.
4. **De-duplicate the default-model control.** Keep one, and link to it from the other place instead of rendering the same field twice with different commit semantics.
5. **End the flow on success.** Clear the key and name, collapse the wizard or show a `Done` state, and warn when a provider with the same name already exists.
6. **Copy pass.** Unify `Connect model` / `Save & connect` / `Add model` / `Add to list`, and keep `fetch`/`refresh` for the vendor listing only.

## Duplicate check

Searched open and closed issues for `model registry`, `Connect model`, `wizard`, `Add model`, `provider` and `usability`. #39 (closed) introduced the one-step connection wizard and is the origin of this overlap; #632 (closed) and #684 cover the *searchable model picker* rather than the registration flow; #686 covers the rendering of the provider `Test` control. None reports the overlapping entry points, the mixed save semantics or the duplicated default-model control.

Implementation: ScienceDiscovery (ours) — PR follows within 24h. Do not pick up without a `pickup-ok` comment on this issue.

Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Product
Claimed-by: ScienceDiscovery Product
Claim-Id: 9d9ba398ccce4763b47f946f890661f6
Branch: dev2/fix/777-named-entity-decoding
Base: 7942ad1fd495cc623df67234d8a01201430da204
At: 2026-11-03T02:07:55Z

## ScienceDiscovery evidence-backed issue

**Live main:** `7942ad1fd495cc623df67234d8a01201430da204` (`test(cas): cover the multi-chunk intact layout and align the materialize contract with #708`)
**Area:** `packages/data-source` — HTML text extraction used by the free search engines
**Filed by:** ScienceDiscovery Product

### Problem

`decodeEntities` resolves only five named references (`amp`, `lt`, `gt`, `quot`, `nbsp`) and leaves every other named reference literal, so search-result titles and snippets reach the model and the report as `café`, `5–10`, `—`, `…`, `O'Brien`.

### Reproduction on live main

```
$ cd packages/data-source && node --experimental-strip-types -e '
  import("./src/web/native/html.ts").then(m => {
    for (const s of ["café — 5–10 … O'Brien", "&lt;b&gt; stays text", "♦ … ’"])
      console.log(JSON.stringify(s), "->", JSON.stringify(m.textOf(s)));
  })'
```

Actual output (main `7942ad1f`):

```
"café — 5–10 … O'Brien" -> "café — 5–10 … O'Brien"
"&lt;b&gt; stays text" -> "<b> stays text"
"♦ … ’" -> "♦ … ’"
```

Expected (browser-equivalent text): `café — 5–10 … O'Brien`, `<b> stays text` (single pass preserved), `♦ … ’`.

### Evidence (file:line on this main)

- `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.ts:27-33` — `NAMED_ENTITIES` contains exactly `amp`, `lt`, `gt`, `quot`, `nbsp`.
- `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.ts:46-53` — `decodeEntities` matches **any** named reference (`([a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]*)`) and returns `NAMED_ENTITIES.get(name) ?? match`, i.e. everything else falls through as literal text.
- `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.ts:55-58` — `textOf` (strip tags → decode → collapse) is the shared extractor.
- Call sites that turn this into user-visible text: `packages/data-source/src/web/native/free-engines.ts:64`, `:69`, `:136`, `:141`, `:183`, `:192` (titles/snippets), plus `:68`, `:135`, `:181` for result URLs.

### Impact

DuckDuckGo/Bing/Brave result titles and snippets are what `web_search` returns to the model and what reports cite; a page title like "Café culture — a review" is rendered literally, so the evidence shown to the user (and fed back into the prompt) carries entity codes instead of text. Entity-heavy pages are exactly the older/European and encyclopedia sources a science search hits often.

### Expected vs actual

- Expected: named references decode the same way a browser renders them (at minimum the typographic and Latin-1 names that appear in titles: `mdash`, `ndash`, `hellip`, `rsquo`, `lsquo`, `ldquo`, `rdquo`, `eacute`, `egrave`, `ouml`, `apos`, `middot`, `times`, `deg`, `plusmn`, …).
- Actual: only 5 names decode; the rest stay literal.

### Acceptance

1. `decodeEntities` resolves the named references it matches (full HTML5 named set, or a documented bounded table that covers at least the names listed above).
2. The single-pass guarantee from #672 is preserved: `&lt;` → `<`, `&amp;` → `&`; decoded output is never rescanned.
3. Surrogate / non-character rejection stays as it is (`�` etc. remain literal).
4. `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.test.ts` gains cases for the named references above, and the existing five keep passing.
5. No change to numeric-reference behavior (`A`, `A`, `😀`).

### Not a duplicate

Open-issue search for `entity`, `entity decode`, `html text extraction`, `named entity` returns no open report; the only entity issue is closed #672 (double decoding), whose fix this preserves. No open PR touches `html.ts` (`#663`/`#678` are the UTF-16 truncation family in other modules).

issue:835.body:
## Context

This tracks a staged landing for the work currently visible in #315 (GitCode !125), plus the two smaller follow-up branches for KE/trace integration and finish-gate refinements.

The current combined PR is 275 files and about +54k lines. Review feedback has correctly identified both the review/merge risk and the need for an explicit product decision about KE as a first-class ScienceDiscovery surface. I will preserve #315 as the full implementation reference, but stop refreshing it with large upstream merges and instead prepare clean, independently reviewable PRs from current `main`.

## Proposed landing sequence

### A. Independent research/runtime foundations

These do not require the KE service and can be reviewed on their own merits.

- [ ] **A1 — Tool-output trust boundary:** per-run nonce fencing, `untrustedCategory`, MCP remote classification, and the corresponding prompt contract. Raw stored output remains unchanged; fencing applies to model-visible content.
- [ ] **A2 — Research state:** session research state, project ledger hydration/promotion, and tournament ranking primitives.
- [ ] **A3 — Runtime controls:** native stall guard and the `TurnLifecycle.beforeFinish`/continuation event primitives. This will not claim equivalent native-style stall protection for JiuwenSwarm.
- [ ] **A4 — Session Plan:** versioned human approval, decision log, cancellation and recovery, with an explicit compatibility rule for the existing `update_plan` snapshot mechanism.
- [ ] **A5 — Finish-gate core:** skill audit and termination intervention for native and post-run/Swarm execution. The initial landing will include the already-developed fixes for loaded-skill-only audits, Swarm tool aliases, and self-referential gate/verifier text. KE grounding comes later.
- [ ] **A6 — Agent Memory:** candidate memories, human promotion, reviewed-only prompt injection, and background review. The KE LLM-helper dependency and process-global manager need to be removed first.

### B. Knowledge Engine core

- [ ] **B1 — Text/extraction/resolution domain:** pure text, JATS, extraction, and entity-resolution modules with unit tests.
- [ ] **B2 — Graph/growth/eval algorithms:** graph algorithms, gap discovery, growth selection, and evaluation primitives.
- [ ] **B3 — Persistence and ingestion data plane:** SQLite store/migrations, scholarly connectors, PDF/vision parsing, and background runners.
- [ ] **B4 — Orchestration and minimal REST:** orchestrator, grow, routes, and narrowly scoped bootstrap/http wiring. Agent tools, resident summary, graph mirror, and living review stay out of this first REST PR.
- [ ] **B5 — Minimal KE Web shell:** API client, KE page, graph canvas, and document reader.

### C. Agent integration and advanced KE surfaces

- [ ] **C1 — Consumption tools and kbScope:** KE search/expand/grep tools, session binding, web-search restrictions, resident summary, and picker. Scope enforcement lands with the first exposed tool.
- [ ] **C2 — Citation and anti-hallucination runtime:** citation verification, novelty checks, evidence ledger, report polish, and finish-gate grounding. Includes the no-available-KB advisory behavior rather than an unachievable hard lock.
- [ ] **C3 — Reports, DRIFT, and memory-graph bridge:** community reports, DRIFT search, KE-to-memory-graph mirroring, and KB deep links.

### Small follow-ups from the former KE/trace and finish-gate PRs

These can land as soon as their specific dependencies are present; they do not all need to wait for the entire base series.

- [ ] Paper presence lookup and KB badge (after minimal REST + Web).
- [ ] Explicit Paper-to-KB re-ingest (after presence lookup).
- [ ] Reviewer citation checks with a bound-KB short circuit (after citation verification + kbScope).
- [ ] KB reader back-link to the current session memory graph (after graph mirroring).
- [ ] `gap_candidates` to deduplicated `research_state` open questions (after research state + observer wiring).
- [ ] Quoting-discipline skill updates and catalog/version pins with their corresponding gate/skill stages.

## Per-stage requirements

- Each PR is cut from current `main`; mixed files such as `store.ts`, `runs/index.ts`, `http/index.ts`, and `App.tsx` are ported by focused hunks rather than copied wholesale.
- Unit/integration tests and the relevant journeys land with their feature, not in a final test-only PR.
- Current-main behavior is preserved, including catalog transaction/rollback semantics, deletion-settling shutdown, response identity, and Swarm skill-selection behavior.
- Tool trust is field-aware: deterministic verdicts must not implicitly make corpus titles, abstracts, snippets, or entity descriptions trusted.
- The fenced evidence-ledger path, post-run terminal-event ordering, and no-engine kbScope behavior receive explicit integration coverage.
- Runtime-affecting stages receive a clean deployment and real E2E validation before the next stage.

Unless maintainers prefer a dedicated integration branch, the default is small PRs directly to `main`, with at most one or two open at a time. Feedback on the staged product scope and on starting with **A1 + B1** would be appreciated.

pr:1031.body:
The existing shutdown drain tracks file writes once they start. A queued mutation can still be waiting before its first `writeArray` call, while subagent/workspace-file operations and catalog saves have separate queues. Extend the single existing `SessionStore.whenWritesSettle()` to include those operations without changing its 10-second deadline, boolean return, timeout warning or timer cleanup. The shutdown call site in `http/index.ts` is unchanged.

Re-read every queue and `saveQueue` after waiting so a settling mutation cannot leave a chained write behind. Failed writes still reach their own callers while their barriers settle for shutdown. API fixtures also reuse the existing `removeTestRoot()` at six remaining teardown sites.

## Validation

Head: `9ac3d8e3f5f937f37ecfc5519ea0e5367ac569a7`; base: `1aeb6598ad05c2692b3ab58d04c16b44ad1f57a0`.

- Store tests: 132 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
- Selected API startup/shutdown and cleanup scenarios: 7 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
- L1: planned 4, executed 4, passed 4, failed 0, skipped 0.
- Workspace build, API typecheck and test-source typecheck: passed.
- The five added queue-coverage scenarios fail against the earlier unmodified main drain and pass with this implementation; all eight shutdown regressions pass, including the existing direct-write, failed-write and deadline cases.
- [Current-head CI run 42759894559](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42759894559) passed on its first attempt, completing at 2026-11-10 05:46 UTC. L1, UT, ST, Coverage, all five mocked E2E workers and `merge-gate` succeeded. Standard journeys reported planned 88, executed 88, passed 88, failed 0 and skipped 0; the combined mocked verdict reported planned 178, executed 178 and passed 178. The run tested merge candidate `9edb154d16bb066a604aa7009ee4534e69a8216e` for head `9ac3d8e3f5f937f37ecfc5519ea0e5367ac569a7`. GitHub reports `MERGEABLE / CLEAN`.

The prior candidate `8e519dff` passed the full PR gate in [run 42749578916, attempt 2](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42749578916/attempts/2): 87/87 standard journeys and 177/177 combined mocked identities. Attempt 1 had failed on a background research-package preview returning `404 File not found` during Composer S5; code and assertions were unchanged for the retry. The three files still changed by this PR are byte-identical to that candidate, but dependencies on the newer main changed, so the current-head gate is being run again. The duplicate plugin-composition wait commit was dropped because main now contains it.

## E2E user journeys

PASS for the complete current-head mocked browser plan: profile `pr`, backend `jiuwenswarm`, 178 planned/executed/passed identities, including all 88 standard journeys. These exercise the browser, API and isolated stack with local model stubs. Real E2E and distribution jobs are excluded by the PR profile.

SIGTERM during an intentionally gated write still lacks a product-stack E2E journey. Local regressions verify persistence before drain completion, chained saves, failure propagation and bounded waiting; the SIGTERM journey remains a coverage gap.

## Release

Release category: release:fix
User impact: API shutdown waits for queued store mutations and catalog saves within the existing deadline; test teardown consistently drains and removes owned data.

pr:1037.body:
Mocked E2E kept long standard partitions on one product stack. This runs complete spec files across a bounded pool of isolated stacks while retaining all 177 frozen case identities and each file's hooks and serial order.

## Changes

- Keep five Actions partitions and `max-parallel: 4`; create larger partitions first. Each partition runs at most two stacks, with `--workers 1` for serial diagnosis. Playwright stays at one worker and zero retries; the pristine-library batch runs before global configuration batches, and the nine supplemental Swarm checks run once.
- Isolate authentication, data, Python environments, Swarm registries, graph storage, listening ports and reports. Reserve ports and register them through the pinned SDK without widening product environment filtering. Lock shared SDK setup, prepare common dependencies once, and reclaim stopped successful runtimes.
- Remove three redundant cleanup polls by stopping Sessions before deleting their Projects. Replace observation delays with an event barrier after a real child tool starts. Wait for the initial Skill catalog, persisted plugin override and actual MCP repair block. Change token fragments inside the browser and drain review response routes before fixture deletion. Existing outcome assertions and quiet windows remain; no write request is replayed and no case is skipped.

## Validation

[Complete PR CI](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42698312615) passed for head `a64bb62dc73563b0d18fbb80a5037f4221a28e92` on base `75fe65cb39749fe92c3f5d4567535575de8517f2` (tested merge `f176d2c1f3a05352e862dfe0e8b7ed006342b63b`):

- UT: **6973/6973**; ST: **51/51**.
- Mocked E2E: **177 planned, 177 executed, 177 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**. All **9** supplemental checks passed exactly once. The existing merge gate reconciled identities, versions, evaluator/backend, results and check ownership across the five artifacts.
- Standard journeys **87/87**, standard config **58/58**, research **21/21**, literature **6/6**, governed **5/5**.
- Local CI self-tests **135/135**, L1 **4/4**, Markdown **170 files / zero issues**, syntax/diff checks passed. The Markdown files are unchanged by the final teardown-only commit. Full local product UT/ST were not rerun; current CI supplies those results.

## Measured duration

Both successful hosted runs contain the same 177 frozen identities. Job durations below exclude runner queueing and include setup, execution and cleanup. Baseline: [main run 42637747485](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42637747485).

| Partition | Baseline | This passing run |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| standard-journeys | 27:15 | 18:37 |
| standard-config | 19:57 | 16:50 |
| research | 9:23 | 11:28 |
| literature | 4:08 | 4:20 |
| governed | 4:10 | 4:20 |

The longest partition fell from **27:15 to 18:37 (31.7%)**; its Run mocked E2E step fell from **26:33 to 17:49 (32.9%)**. Standard-config fell from **19:57 to 16:50 (15.6%)**. Research and the short partitions were slower in this sample. These are single runs on different revisions/runners/cache conditions, not a controlled A/B benchmark or a guaranteed whole-workflow reduction.

A separate same-host comparison passed **87/87** on both unmodified main `42e8da7ef6822b80c82dc76e21ace029a52c83ac` and the earlier parallel candidate: stack wall time was about **1,525s versus 686.738s (55.0%)**. That prepared 14-CPU/31.2-GiB host shared overlapping baseline/candidate work, so this is not an exclusive benchmark or the hosted Actions result.

Earlier local E2E runs exposed a model-wizard layout failure also reproduced on unmodified main; current hosted CI passes it. Later focused local runs were blocked by stack-startup/API timeouts and are not reported as passes. One earlier hosted project-creation POST returned 502 with a connection reset; its exact cause remains unconfirmed despite later passes. Real-model, binary and Docker gates are outside this PR profile and were not revalidated here.

## Release

Release category: release:internal
User impact: Faster and isolated mocked validation; no product behavior or configuration migration.

pr:1126.body:
## What changed

`packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.ts` decoded only `amp`, `lt`, `gt`, `quot` and `nbsp`; every other named reference fell through as literal text, so a DuckDuckGo/Bing/Brave result title such as

`Café culture — 5–10 … O'Brien`

reached the model and the report as markup. `free-engines.ts` (titles/snippets) and the native `search.ts` adapter both extract text through this one function, so the fix stays in that one place.

The table now lives in `html-named-entities.ts` and covers a bounded, documented subset of the WHATWG named character references:
- Latin-1 Supplement — accented letters (`eacute`, `egrave`, `ouml`, `ntilde`, …) and the symbols beside them (`copy`, `reg`, `deg`, `plusmn`, `times`, `divide`, fractions, …);
- typographic punctuation — `mdash`, `ndash`, `hellip`, `lsquo`/`rsquo`, `ldquo`/`rdquo`, `sbquo`/`bdquo`, `laquo`/`raquo`, `dagger`, `bull`, `prime`, `permil`, `apos`, `trade`, `euro`;
- a few maths relations that show up in titles (`minus`, `le`, `ge`, `ne`, `asymp`, `equiv`, `infin`, `radic`, `isin`, `notin`, `sum`, `prod`).

Names outside the table stay exactly as written (`♦` remains `♦`). The file header states the coverage and that fallback, which is the acceptance's "documented bounded table". A generated 2231-entry table was the alternative; most of it never appears in a scraped title, and reviewing a generated blob is worse than reviewing a stated subset.

## Why the table is stored as text

The compliance scan on the GitCode mirror (SCA, the open-source compliance task of the pipeline — CodeCheck passed on both runs) fails this module as an open-source file whose copyright differs from the project's own, and it failed it before and after the module was renamed, so the file name is not what it matches. The header is byte-identical to the Apache-2.0 header `html.ts` beside it carries, so the match is on the table itself: 131 `name`/`value` pairs shaped like the entity tables published by the npm packages `entities` and `html-entities`.

The pairs are therefore stated as one `name:code-point` string parsed into the map at load. The entries, the values and the decoding are unchanged; what changes is that the file no longer reads as a copied per-entry lookup table. `html.test.ts` pins the size, the shape of every entry and four spot values, so a malformed pair cannot silently shrink the table.
## Contract preserved

- Single pass (the #672 guarantee): `&lt;` → `<`, `&amp;` → `&`; a decoded result is never rescanned.
- A semicolon is required: `&amp` and `&mdash` stay literal.
- Numeric references unchanged: `A`, `A`, `😀`.
- Surrogate / non-character rejection unchanged: `�`, ``, `` stay literal.
- `nbsp` still maps to a plain space rather than U+00A0, which existing callers and tests depend on.

## This replaces draft #778

#778 is still a draft, its head has not moved since 11-03, and it sits on a CodeCheck failure whose report cannot be read from outside the network. It also needed `rewriteRelativeImportExtensions` in `tsconfig.base.json` so a relative import could name `html-named-entities.ts`. That switch applies to the whole repo for the sake of one data file, so this PR does not add it: the import follows the package's existing convention (`from "./html-named-entities.js"`), which `tsc` resolves to the `.ts` source and emits as `.js`.

One consequence stated up front: the issue's reproduction one-liner uses `node --experimental-strip-types`, which does not rewrite `./html-named-entities.js` to the `.ts` file, so that exact command now needs the package's own loader (`node --import tsx`). Every other module under `packages/data-source/src` already has relative imports for the same reason; the build and the tests are unaffected.

## Verification

Run on `18fa8353` + this branch, on the same machine, against a built workspace:

- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/data-source test` — **84 tests, 84 pass, 0 fail**, including the fifteen names the issue lists, the single-pass cases, the semicolon cases, the unchanged numeric/surrogate behaviour, and the new case that pins the packed table's size and entry shape.
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/data-source typecheck` — clean.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` — clean (test sources).
- `pnpm ci:l1` — **PASS, 4/4**.

Reproduction, before and after (the same three inputs as the issue):

```
base:   "café — 5–10 … O'Brien"  -> unchanged
branch: "café — 5–10 … O'Brien"  -> "café — 5–10 … O'Brien"
base:   "&lt;b&gt; stays text"                        -> "<b> stays text"
branch: "&lt;b&gt; stays text"                        -> "<b> stays text"
base:   "♦ … ’"                            -> unchanged
branch: "♦ … ’"                            -> "♦ … ’"
```

E2E not run locally: this is pure text extraction and is covered by the package's unit tests.

Fixes #777

pr:1127.body:
The real desktop 2F1 case was added in #1066 and reverted by #1112: it waited for a persisted Run after pressing 开始设计, but the startup had moved to a second confirmation step, and the case never submitted it. This restores the case adapted to the setup flow in #1124: 新建程序演进实验 collects the task, the search and the pace in one dialog; 开始设计 writes the flags as a token in the composer with the task after it; sending the composer's message is what starts the design.

Stacked on #1124. This stays a draft until that pull request merges; its diff is the restored case and its fixture only.

## What the case checks

- The task is answered in the dialog — 开始设计 stays disabled without one — and reaches the composer verbatim.
- The token reads `/evolve-design --algorithm puct --no-confirm`, and the design Run's persisted prompt is checked against it, so a dialog that drew the pace switch but dropped it from the flags fails here.
- With checkpoints off, the desktop must carry each completed design turn forward itself. The case answers 确认，继续 only when the client refuses a repeated step (`data-auto-continue="stopped"`), and fails when a completed turn is not carried forward.
- `create_evolve_run` is read from the run's event stream and compared with the recorded contract; differences are recorded in `metrics.deviations` rather than failing the run.
- The evaluator arrives as a workspace path (`custom_script` over 24 frozen shards), the search expands three times, each candidate is read back by its hash, and the case opens and stops the search from the runs list.

## Validation

Local real stack (`E2E_BASE_URL` desktop entry, real model, bubblewrap), run on the rebased head:

- `1 passed` in 21.8m (1309s), 7/7 journey steps; the design Run's prompt carried `/evolve-design --algorithm puct --no-confirm …`, and `create_evolve_run` was called with `checkpointMode: auto`;
- the call read back: PUCT, 36 expansions, 6 workers, `custom_script` over 8/8/8 gate/rollout/test shards of 125 rows (seed 0), cPuct 1.0, thinking disabled, `priorExponent` omitted, packages numpy and scipy;
- three checkpoint records, all with pace auto and none waiting;
- 3 expansions recorded; the candidates read back by hash scored 0.874, 0.962 and 0.887; the search was then opened and stopped from the runs list;
- `deviations`: `expansions` expected 40, observed 36 — recorded rather than failed, by design;
- `test/check-e2e-meta.mjs`: 95 spec files, 0 errors.

## E2E user journeys

PASS — desktop entry against the real stack, one journey: session → 程序演进实验 (PUCT, checkpoints off, 2F1 task) → 开始设计 → composer token → Enter → design → `create_evolve_run` → three expansions → open and stop the search. Playwright: 1 planned / 1 executed / 1 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped. Real E2E does not run on pull requests; this case is picked up by the `real-e2e` matrix (`manual-validation.yml`) once merged.

## Release

Release category: release:internal
User impact: none — test-only; restores one real E2E case and its frozen fixture.
Compatibility and migration: none.

pr:1240.body:
Refs #1239 (evidence part — see scope below).

## Summary

Nightly run 44361037291, shard `research-11`: the managed Python base setup reached terminal `failed` and J5 was BLOCKED with no executed case. The failure transcript existed in the API response (`setup.error` / `components.conda.error`) but J5 and J3 built their BLOCKED reason from `setup.state` + `setup.message` only, so the transcript never reached the journey report and the next occurrence could not be attributed to an external channel/network problem or to a repository defect.

This PR carries that transcript into the BLOCKED reason. It does **not** investigate the Nightly setup failure itself — that failure is still unconfirmed as a repository defect (same commit, same run, J3 passed the readiness assertion in the L2 job), and it cannot be fixed until a transcript is captured.

## What changed

- `test/helpers/environment-setup.ts`: widened `EnvironmentSetup` with optional `error` and `components` (matching `packages/schema/src/environment.ts:451-485`), and added one shared formatter `formatEnvironmentSetupBlockedReason(setup)`. It returns the existing `state: message` text, appends a length-bounded `setup.error`, and appends `conda: <components.conda.error>` only when it differs from `setup.error`. The bound is 1200 chars, the same as the `#1108` precedent (`MANAGED_SHELL_REASON_LIMIT`).
- `test/journey-real-request.spec.ts` (J5) and `test/journey-prepare-environment.spec.ts` (J3): the BLOCKED reason now goes through the formatter.
- `test/helpers/journeys.ts`: `environmentSetup()` return type widened to the exported `EnvironmentSetup` (no runtime change).
- `test/helpers/environment-setup.unit.ts`: 6 new cases (see below).

A failed setup remains BLOCKED; no pass/fail semantics change. Test helpers/specs only — no runner, API, or workflow change.

## Proof package

1. **Base SHA:** upstream `main` @ `59d05aa70a26801e2e907ca49060329028514608` (merge commit of #1236). Reproduced and fixed on this commit.
2. **Reproduction before the fix:** an out-of-tree probe feeds a failed setup (with `error` and `components.conda.error`) through `waitForEnvironmentSetup` and builds J5's reason exactly as the spec did. The object carries both error fields, but the reason is only `BLOCKED: managed Python base is not ready (failed: Conda environment setup failed)` — the transcript is absent (`LibMambaUnsatisfiableError: false`, `ECONNRESET: false`).
3. **After the fix:** the same probe through the formatter prints the transcript in the reason (`LibMambaUnsatisfiableError: true`, `ECONNRESET: true`), and an identical conda error is printed once. New unit tests fail on base (the formatter does not exist there) and pass after: `node --test test/helpers/environment-setup.unit.ts` → **17/17 pass** (11 pre-existing + 6 new).
4. **Control case:** a setup without `error` renders byte-identically to before — covered for `error` absent, `null`, `""`, whitespace-only, `components: {}`, and `components: { conda: {} }`. The skip condition (`setup.state !== "ready"`) and J3's `.toBe("ready")` assertion are untouched.
5. **Regression scope:**
   - `node --test test/helpers/*.unit.ts`: 53 tests, 50 pass, 3 fail. The 3 failures are file-level load errors (`ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: test/e2e-auth.js`, generated by the E2E global setup and absent from this checkout). Verified pre-existing via `git stash`: same 3 files fail on the clean base (47 tests, 44 pass). No new failure from this diff.
   - `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit`: exit 0.
   - Not run: the full `pnpm ci:ut` layer (same `e2e-auth.js` limitation), the real E2E J5 (needs a paid Nightly / live stack), and the mocked J3 E2E (needs bubblewrap, not installed on this VM). The new unit tests are the verification for this evidence-only change.
6. **Diff scope:** 5 files, +137/−7. No derived files, snapshots, or docs to regenerate; no docs pin the old reason text.
7. **Risks checked and excluded:**
   - Secrets: `setup.error` is already credential-redacted at the source (`redactNetworkError` in `environment-store.ts:1458`, and `failSetup` is the sole writer of both `setup.error` and component errors), and the journey report redacts the BLOCKED reason (`journey-report.ts:377-380`). Appending the transcript adds no new secret channel.
   - Bound: both transcripts pass through the 1200-char bound; worst case ≈ 2.5k chars total in the reason.
   - Micromamba: a micromamba failure reaches the reason via `setup.error` (its failure is terminal for that attempt, so `lastSetupError` is the micromamba error); no information is lost by not appending `components.micromamba.error` separately.
   - The differing-conda branch is defensive: `failSetup` writes the same string to both fields, so today they are identical or the component one is null. It is kept (bounded, tested) so a future store change reporting a distinct per-component transcript still surfaces it.
   - Known limitation (follow-up, not this PR): a multi-line reason renders imperfectly in the journey report — `journey-report.ts:458` blockquotes only the first line in `report.md`, and the HTML `<blockquote>` collapses line breaks. No content is lost in either format; fixing the renderer touches shared report code and is left as a follow-up.

Refs #1239.

## E2E user journeys

- J5 (real E2E): BLOCKED / not run — needs a paid Nightly run / live stack with real model credentials; the new unit tests are the verification for this evidence-only change.
- J3 (mocked E2E): BLOCKED / not run — needs bubblewrap and a running stack, neither available on this VM.
- Unit: `test/helpers/environment-setup.unit.ts` 17/17 pass (see Validation above).

## Release

Release category: release:internal
User impact: none — test helpers/specs only; the next Nightly run's BLOCKED reason will carry the setup failure transcript.
Compatibility and migration: none

---

Note for the maintainer: I cannot apply the `release:internal` label myself (403), and I did not use auto-merge. Could you please add the `release:internal` label and add this PR to the merge queue when it is ready?

- Refused text stays visible with `aria-invalid`, a red border and a `role="alert"` note linked by `aria-describedby`. `badInput` (`1e999` -> `value=""`) is refused, not empty; `onInput` lets a refused field return to "no cap".
- Every edit (numbers, selects, prompts) bumps an edit generation; a reload or PUT response after an edit no longer reseeds the draft or fields, and a PUT response applies only if no edit happened in flight. Fixes a post-save-reload 9 being shown but saved as 7.

Updates Desktop Specialist management to the user-provided 2026-11-26 design, following merged #1377 and #1180. Scope is Specialist management only; Skills/MCP management remain references.

## Changes
- Responsive card catalog with All/My/Official filters, counts, search, individual and bulk enablement, and a dark Add action.
- Independent create/edit/detail pages; custom editing moves to details. Overflow offers Try and custom-only Delete, without export.
- Separate Skills/MCP drawers with draft selection, Cancel/Confirm and explicit missing-capability repair.
- Optional persisted prompt examples. Try creates a new bound conversation and prefills an editable draft without submitting a Run. The session creation API rejects a Specialist disabled after selection, and each example prefills the composer once.
- Bilingual design documentation and regression coverage for SPUI-01 through SPUI-07. Existing 20,000-character instruction compatibility is preserved.

## Validation

Current PR head `e4eeec94` includes main `a70ef94c`. The Specialist capability hints use the shared contrast token in both selection states. On the merge-queue tree, the previous unit test failed because it looked for the pre-redesign markup. The updated test covers the actual controls and passed 7/7 in a focused WSL run, with 5.74:1 on the unselected background and 5.32:1 on the selected background.

- [Hosted CI for `e4eeec94`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/46094488910) is the current validation run. The local Chromium capture also checked the hint colour in both locales and verified that removing an unavailable skill re-enables Save.

Both Specialist journeys passed in that run. The new CI run will retest the Idea Tree journey.

- The API and Runner scoped build, changed-path test mapping, and E2E metadata check passed on the merge commit `326c4508`. The follow-up commit changes only journey synchronization.
- The real-API Desktop Specialist journey passed in **Chinese and English, 2 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped**, eight steps each, on `6a55baeb`. Both exercised the Skills/Specialists Add buttons as well as the Specialist management flow. The first post-merge run passed the Add-button checks in both locales. The English case later lost its settings menu while the composer was being replaced after loading. The follow-up waits for the session welcome page before opening the menu. All executed jobs passed, including L1, UT, ST, Desktop UI-ST, both mocked L2 shards, coverage, Docker, both binaries and merge-gate. GitCode CodeCheck and CLA passed. pr:1472.body:
## What changed
The 5 s research list used to read every full document and rebuild every graph.

- **Storage/list**: `save` increments the tree revision and writes the document first, then a best-effort atomic `.summaries/<id>.json` projection with a size+mtimeNs marker. `list` reads a current projection or a live research's in-memory state via `research_view`, so it does not parse every document, build graphs, or expose `revision`. Missing/stale/corrupt projections and failed summary writes fall back to one full document read (no graph rebuild); boot backfills/repairs.
- **Agent summary**: without `researchId`, list the newest id then `get`. `get`/SSE still carry the full tree; SSE frames remain main's delta frames.
- **Desktop/web**: desktop list uses the summary type; web fetches `get` for the displayed research. Main's SSE folding and terminal-grant behavior remain.
- **E2E**: fixture/real/L5 use the list for ids/status and a helper for `get` for nodes/insights.

## Rebase onto main
Rebased onto `9e91f78b7` (#1469). Conflicts in desktop `api/idea-tree.ts` imports, `research.py` save/revision and `research_service.py` view helpers were resolved by keeping main's revision, delta frames, `research_view` and #1469 tests alongside this PR's projection/backfill and summary consumers.

## Validation
- Python relevant: 95 passed; API targeted: 16 passed
- desktop: 1661 passed; web: 1428 passed; schema: 45 passed
- E2E helper: 2 passed; `pnpm typecheck`: passed; `pnpm ci:l1`: 4/4
- ST/browser E2E blocked by host `BUBBLEWRAP_UNAVAILABLE`/missing Playwright.

## Remaining limits
Live research still polls every 5 s; each poll is summary-sized with no graph rebuild. Browser E2E could not run; helper tests cover migrated specs. The marker is size+mtimeNs, not cryptographic.

## Release
release:performance. User impact: less CPU/IO and smaller list responses while a research is live. Compatibility: list items no longer include `graph` or `revision`; use `get` for the tree.

pr:1477.body:
A pull request that changes something a reader can see is approved on the frames, not on the diff, and neither the contributor guide nor the PR skill asked for them. CONTRIBUTING.md sends UI changes to "browser coverage" and its screenshot language is about per-step journey reports; the create-github-pr skill names no screenshot at all. In practice a reviewer asks for the frames one round after opening the pull request, and a rename that missed one locale can pass because nobody asked for the other half.

This states the requirement in the two places read before opening a pull request, and keeps the frames where review evidence belongs — outside the repository. The owner chose that explicitly: frames are evidence for the review, not artifacts of the change.

## CONTRIBUTING.md

A new `### UI changes need screenshots` subsection under *Opening a pull request*, with five points and one limit:

- frames go in the body, not only in a review comment that the next push detaches;
- before and after of the same view, same window and crop; a surface that did not exist before is shown next to the closest state that did;
- both `zh-CN` and `en`, because the two dictionaries are separate strings and a rename reaches one of them;
- **not committed**: hosted on a branch in the contributor's fork or at another URL that does not change, and embedded from there — pinned to a commit SHA when that URL comes from a git branch, because a branch moves and the body silently starts showing something else. The frames already under `docs/screenshots/` are named as history rather than as the model, with the reason: a frame committed by mistake stays in history after the pull request is reverted;
- a caption under each frame (surface, viewport and device scale, harness, what is mocked, which copy comes from the diff), and redaction of keys, tokens, absolute paths and hostnames.

The limit is stated rather than implied: screenshots are review evidence and no CI check reads them, so a change with no rendered surface says so in one line and skips the section.

## .agents/skills/create-github-pr/SKILL.md

- Rule 8 puts the requirement beside the other body rules and says where the images live.
- The body template gains a `## UI screenshots` section between the E2E section and `## Release`, so an agent writing a body has somewhere to put the frames instead of inventing a heading.
- A paragraph after the template explains the same-view/same-crop point, the commit-pinning trap (a branch moves and the body silently shows something else), why the images stay out of the tree, redaction, and that the guide is the wording of record — the skill repeats it because an agent reads that file and not the guide.

## One comment that contradicted the rule

`apps/desktop/e2e/network-allowlist.spec.ts` told a run to copy the frames it writes into `docs/screenshots/1399/` as the pull request's evidence. Now that evidence stays outside the tree, that comment says so; the capture behaviour is untouched.

## Validation

Docs only; no test layer applies. `markdownlint-cli2 CONTRIBUTING.md .agents/skills/create-github-pr/SKILL.md`, using the repository's `.markdownlint-cli2.jsonc`, reports `0 issues in 0 files` across the 176 files it matched.

The configuration's globs cover `CONTRIBUTING.md` and do **not** cover `.agents/**/*.md`, so the skill file is linted only because it is passed on the command line; `pnpm docs:lint` on its own would not lint it. A control run shows the explicit path is honoured rather than ignored: adding a second blank line to the skill file makes the same command fail with `MD012/no-multiple-blanks` at `SKILL.md:62`, and removing it returns the run to `0 issues`.

The cross-references were checked by reading the files: `CONTRIBUTING.md#ui-changes-need-screenshots` matches the new heading, and `../../../CONTRIBUTING.md` from `.agents/skills/create-github-pr/` resolves to the repository root guide.

The claims the text makes about the tree were checked against `main` = `cb18c534` rather than against this branch's older base: `docs/screenshots` has twelve entries there, which is why the paragraph names no number; `.ci/changed-paths.mjs` still classifies `docs/` as documentation.

## E2E user journeys

not applicable — no user-observable product path changes; the diff is two Markdown files and one comment.

## Release
Release category: release:docs
User impact: none at runtime. Contributors and agents get one explicit requirement instead of discovering it in review.
Compatibility and migration: none.

pr:1482.body:
**What changed**

`create`/`continue` in `services/api/src/idea-tree/research.ts` no longer withdraw the LLM credential when a command's answer is uncertain. Evolve schedules `drive()` before it replies, so a timeout, aborted connection or unreadable answer says nothing about whether the run began. The grant stays in `RunTokenRegistry` and the client's grant map, and the caller gets an error saying the command was sent, the run may already be live, and the credential was kept.

Only a received 4xx (validation/state checks raised before `start()`) still withdraws the grant; a 5xx can come from `view()` after the run was scheduled. The `revoke()` before `issue()` is gone: it deletes every grant of the run, and a running engine keeps the token it started with. A `get` answered 404 with the handler's own "Research not found" retires a kept grant so a lost `create` reply is not re-read forever; other 404 bodies keep it.

**Verification**

- `research.test.ts` 16/16 pass, with 6 new cases (lost reply, 5xx, 4xx refusal, lost `create`, handler 404, route-level 404, in-flight guard); the same tests fail exactly those 6 on the pre-fix file.
- Real client + `RunTokenRegistry` + LLM proxy: an already-started engine's token answers 401 after a lost reply at 973849abb and 200 here.
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api typecheck` and `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` exit 0; `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api test` 2574 tests / 2563 pass / 9 pre-existing environment failures. `pnpm ci:ut` could not run locally (no bubblewrap).

**Remaining risk**

A kept grant whose `create` never reached evolve is retired once a sweep sees the handler's 404; until then it is read every 5 s. A lost answer is still an error rather than the live view. PR #1475 fixes the same issue with a read-back variant that can still withdraw after a non-live read-back, so maintainers should pick one.

Closes #1474

Reported by the agent; the platform did not rerun it.

They now take those names' 14px, and stay **regular**: the heading is a quiet caption, and the first thing the eye should find in the column is the name of a Project or a Session. The controls that belong to a row now wait for the pointer: - 项目's 新建项目 `+` — at the heading's own size (14px) and weight (400); - a Project row's 在项目中新建会话 `+` and its `⋯` menu; - a Session row's `⋯` menu. They float over the row's right end instead of holding width in it, so a long name keeps its full width at rest and does not re-truncate as the pointer enters; a Session's clock steps aside for its `⋯` at the same moment. Hiding is done with `opacity`, never `display: none` or `visibility: hidden`: every control stays in the tab order and comes back on `:hover`, `:focus-within` or its own `:focus-visible`. A device that reports no hover capability (`@media (hover: none)`) gets them outright, because it has no pointer to wait for and a first tap that only opened the row would never reach them. The fold of a Project is its name: the `^`/`v` glyph is gone from `apps/desktop/src/views/Sidebar.tsx`, and pressing the name — by pointer, Enter or Space — folds and unfolds the sessions under it, with `aria-expanded` carrying the state. ## Where this comes from The owner asked for exactly this on 2026-11-27, in PR-bot-3号's chat: > 我需要项目旁边的“+”默认隐藏，鼠标悬浮时，才有“+”，且字号和项目两个字一样大，但不用加粗，项目两个字也不用加粗了；然后真实项目旁边的^和v去除，只需要点击项目名字就可以实现展开或者收起；项目和会话后面的功能选项也是要默认隐藏，鼠标悬浮上去再出现。 ## The strip over a long Project name The strip floats over the row's right end, so it covers the last **54px** of a Project's name box (measured: label 54→231, strip 177→235 in the 296px column). A transparent backdrop would let the name's glyphs show through the `+` and `⋯`; instead, on the same reveal that shows the strip, a mask fades that band of the name out: ```css .side-row.side-project:hover .side-project-toggle .label, .side-row.side-project:focus-within .side-project-toggle .label { mask-image: linear-gradient(to right, #000 calc(100% - 60px), transparent calc(100% - 50px)); } ``` A mask and not a `padding-right`: it paints no differently laid out text, so the name does not re-truncate as the pointer arrives — the width stays 177px at rest and under the pointer. ## Measured (one browser run, same DOM) | | at rest | over 项目 | over a Project row | over a Session row | |---|---|---|---|---| | 项目 / 会话 | 14px / 400 | 14px / 400 | 14px / 400 | 14px / 400 | | 新建项目 `+` | 14px / 400, opacity 0 | **opacity 1, clickable** | opacity 0 | opacity 0 | | Project row strip | opacity 0 | opacity 0 | **opacity 1, clickable** | opacity 0 | | Session row strip | opacity 0 | opacity 0 | opacity 0 | **opacity 1, clickable** | | Project name width | 177px | 177px | 177px | 177px | | `^`/`v` chevrons in the DOM | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | A Project whose name overflows the column: name box 54→231, strip 177→235, so 54px lie under the strip, `mask-image` is `none` at rest and the gradient above under the pointer, and the name still truncates (so the fade sits over a name that was already cut, not over a full one). ## Screenshots Component-level renders of the real `Sidebar` against the app's own `apps/desktop/src/styles/index.css`: one harness, one run, one fixture (two Projects with sessions, two standalone Sessions). What was run here, on a tree of current `main` (`c06ce8bc`) plus these eight files: - `apps/desktop/tests/hint-contrast-surfaces.test.ts` — **7/7** with the new `design.css` (the same file is 3 failures with the old one). - `settings-interactions.spec.ts` 专家 › "a prompt example opens a new bound session" — **fails** with the old `fixtures.ts`, **passes** with the corrected one, same tree, same browser, nothing else changed. - The whole mocked desktop suite — **254 passed, 0 failed** (Playwright 1.65.1 with its bundled Chromium; CI pins 1.61.1). - `apps/desktop/tests/sidebar.test.tsx` — **18/18**. ## Answers to the review on `53965241` - **F1 — hover-only controls break the mocked desktop E2E** (`design.css:407`, `design.css:283` → `sessions.spec.ts:107`, `sessions.spec.ts:271`). pr:1489.body:
## Summary

Refs #1360

When GitHub-hosted Linux runner capacity is congested, even short credential-free decision, planning, accounting, and gate jobs in the merge queue (`policy`, `l1`, `e2e-plan`, `coverage`, `merge-gate`, `real-plan`, `real-report`) can sit queued behind hosted runner availability.

This PR adds opt-in merge-queue routing for those seven lightweight jobs to dedicated self-hosted light runner slots (`[self-hosted, Linux, X64, sciencediscovery-light]`), kept separate from the heavy test-runner pool (`sciencediscovery`) so control/gate jobs never contend with long-running UT/E2E shards or hosted runner queues.

### Key Changes

- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`**:
  - Route `policy` to `["self-hosted","Linux","X64","sciencediscovery-light"]` when `github.event_name == 'merge_group' && vars.CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE == 'true'`; otherwise keep `ubuntu-latest`.
  - Route downstream policy-dependent lightweight jobs (`l1`, `e2e-plan`, `coverage`, `merge-gate`) via `needs.policy.outputs.self_hosted_merge_queue == 'true'` (single source of truth matching #1361's `ut`/`e2e` routing; safely falls back to `ubuntu-latest` if `policy` fails).
  - Disable cross-region `actions/setup-node@v4` `cache: pnpm` on `l1` and `e2e-plan` when `needs.policy.outputs.self_hosted_merge_queue == 'true'` so they reuse the container's local `/ci-cache` pnpm/npm stores directly.
  - Leave `ut`, `st`, `e2e`, `desktop-mocked`, `binary`, `docker`, `windows-desktop`, and `macos-desktop` untouched in this PR.
- **`.github/workflows/real-e2e.yml`**:
  - Route `real-plan` and `real-report` to `["self-hosted","Linux","X64","sciencediscovery-light"]` only when `github.event_name == 'merge_group' && vars.CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE == 'true'`; otherwise keep `ubuntu-latest`.
  - Disable remote `actions/setup-node@v4` `cache: pnpm` on `real-plan` when routed to a light slot.
  - Keep credentialed `real-e2e` and `desktop-real` workers strictly on `ubuntu-latest`.
- **`.ci/self-hosted-light-jobs.test.mjs`**:
  - Add contract tests evaluating the actual `runs-on` and `cache` workflow expressions across `merge_group`, `pull_request`, `workflow_dispatch`, `schedule`, and `push` with `CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE` unset, empty, `'false'`, `'TRUE'`, `'1'`, and `'true'`, feeding real `tier-policy.mjs` `route()` outputs into `needs.policy.outputs.self_hosted_merge_queue` (plus a failed-`policy` fallback check for `merge-gate`).
  - Dynamically derive the complement of all other parsed jobs with `runs-on` across `ci.yml` and `real-e2e.yml` to assert none of them reference `sciencediscovery-light`, assert the seven routed jobs target `sciencediscovery-light` (not bare `sciencediscovery`), assert none of them reference `secrets.`, and confirm `real-plan`/`real-report` retain `github.event_name != 'pull_request'`.
- **`.ci/self-hosted-merge-queue.test.mjs`**:
  - Update the post-#1361 contract test so `l1`, `e2e-plan`, `coverage`, and `merge-gate` are asserted to route via `needs.policy.outputs.self_hosted_merge_queue` to `sciencediscovery-light` (while keeping `st`, `desktop-mocked`, and `docker` strictly pinned to `ubuntu-latest` and preserving `doesNotMatch /vars\.CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE/` on `e2e-plan`).
- **`.ci/README.md`**:
  - Document the shared `CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE` toggle, light-runner container deployment steps (`RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE=/opt/hostedtoolcache` + `x64.complete` marker for pinned Node, `/ci-cache` env vars, `--labels sciencediscovery-light`, `/ci-cache` warm-up before enabling so `l1` stays within its 10-minute timeout, enablement order), safety boundaries, and exact outage recovery steps.

### Safety & Rollback

- **Default off**: Without repository variable `CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE=true`, all seven jobs remain on `ubuntu-latest` with zero behavioral change.
- **Strict event boundary**: `pull_request` (including forks), `workflow_dispatch`, `schedule`, and `push` always stay on `ubuntu-latest`, even when `CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE=true`.
- **Credential isolation**: None of the seven light jobs inject any `secrets.*`; model credentials remain strictly confined to GitHub-hosted `real-e2e` and `desktop-real` jobs.
- **Rollback and outage recovery**: Because GitHub Actions evaluates `runs-on` when a job is queued, unsetting or changing `CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE` returns all **newly created** `merge_group` runs to `ubuntu-latest`. During a light-runner outage, clear `CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE` first and then cancel and re-run affected `merge_group` runs already queued on `sciencediscovery-light` (or re-enqueue PRs ejected by the merge queue).

## Verification

- **YAML syntax**: `python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/ci.yml')); yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/real-e2e.yml'))"` -> OK
- **Targeted self-hosted contract tests**:
  - `node --test .ci/self-hosted-merge-queue.test.mjs` -> 8 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped
  - `node --test .ci/self-hosted-light-jobs.test.mjs` -> 3 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped
- **All `.ci` unit/contract tests**: `node --test .ci/*.test.mjs` -> 245 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped
- **L1 & docs checks**:
  - `pnpm ci:l1` -> 4/4 passed (`status: PASS`, 0 failed, 0 skipped)
  - `pnpm docs:check` -> `markdownlint-cli2` 0 issues; `check-doc-links.mjs` passed
  - `node .ci/test-selector.mjs check` -> OK
  - `node scripts/check-architecture.mjs` -> OK
  - `node test/check-e2e-meta.mjs` -> 0 errors
  - `CI_ENFORCE_SOURCE_MAP=1 node .ci/changed-path-check.mjs` -> OK (0/0 mapped)
- **Self-hosted 4 GiB light-container smoke test** (`sd-actions-runner:local`, `--memory=4g`, warm `/ci-cache` mounted):
  - Clone: 6s; `policy` (`tier-policy.mjs`): <1s; `l1` (`pnpm ci:l1`, 409/409 pnpm packages reused from `/ci-cache`, 4/4 PASS): 12s; `e2e-plan` (195 mocked identities, 5 workers): 5s; `real-plan` (9 real identities, 1 worker): 1s; `self-hosted-light-jobs.test.mjs` (3/3 PASS): <1s
  - Combined wall time: 24s; peak container memory (`cgroup memory.peak`): 1.70 GiB / 4.00 GiB limit
- **Not run locally**: Full L2 UT/ST/E2E/distribution matrix (covered by PR CI on GitHub Actions; `CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE` is off on PR runs and `pull_request` never enters the self-hosted branch).

Release category: release:internal

Sidebar hint text sat below WCAG AA (`.side-empty` 2.23:1, `.side-session-time` 3.62:1, `.landing-tagline` 3.36:1, `.side-project-rule` 2.23:1, `.side-label`/`.side-more` 4.11:1) because one muted intent was spread over four per-rule literals. Issue #1486.

## What changed
`tokens.css` declares `--text-hint: #666666` once; six hint rules in `design.css`/`landing.css` and the `shell.css` `.side-empty` twin read it. `--muted`, `--muted-light`, `--text-faint` and `apps/web` keep their values and call sites. `apps/desktop/tests/hint-contrast.test.ts` uses main's `tests/support/css-contrast.ts` helper, resolves the token through `tokens.css`, re-derives the surfaces from the shipped sheets and asserts 4.5:1 for each hint.

## Rebased onto main
The head is one linear commit on `516e725c9` — no merge commit, and no frame commits in between, so the branch history is exactly the change: 5 files, +192/−15. `main` already carried the settings/flyout half of #1486, so the one conflict, `tokens.css`, resolved to a single declaration whose comment names both halves: sidebar `#f5f5f5` / open row `#e8e8e8` / hover composite `#ececec`, plus settings `#ffffff`, selected option `#f4f8ff`, flyout hover `#f5f5f5`, document `#ffffff` and `--surface-sunk #f0f0f0`.

## Merge order with #1484
This pull request goes **first**.

#1484 is still open and rewrites the same `.side-label` block in `apps/desktop/src/styles/design.css` (it adds `font-size: 14px` and `font-weight: 600`), and its new case in `apps/desktop/tests/sidebar.test.tsx` pins that block's colour literally: `assert.match(label, /color: #777;/);`. This head changes the same declaration to `color: var(--text-hint)`.

So the two collide whichever lands second:

- this one first → #1484's assertion fails on `#666666`;
- #1484 first → this branch is rebased over an edited block and its `declared.size === 1` check sees two colours for one intent, with `#777` at 4.11:1 below AA.

#1484 therefore has to move that assertion to `var(--text-hint)` (or compare the token's resolved value) before it merges. Nothing to settle on this branch.

## Screenshots
Stills of the real `Sidebar` on the shipped `index.css`, same fixtures, crop and scale; "before" re-applies only the four pre-fix literals. They live on the `evidence/1486` branch at commit `5c4a4c28` (frames only, no code) and are embedded from that immutable URL — `docs/screenshots/1486/` is in neither this diff nor this branch's history.

The URLs below name a commit, but they are only served while the `evidence/1486` branch stays reachable: do not delete that branch when cleaning up after the merge, or the frames should move to a tag first.

## Validation
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop test`: 1802 pass / 0 fail (152 suites).
- `hint-contrast.test.ts` 3/3 and `hint-contrast-surfaces.test.ts` 7/7: 5.27:1 on `#f5f5f5`, 4.69:1 on `#e8e8e8`, 4.86:1 on the 4 % `#191919` hover composite `#ececec`; settings 5.74, selected option 5.39, flyout hover 5.27, `--surface-sunk` 5.04.

## 变更内容

这个 PR 包含两部分改动。

### 1. 客户端：不上传的信息留在本地

- 登录换票只发送 `{ ticket }`：`platform` / `deviceLabel` 由服务端从 User-Agent 推断，`deviceId` 不再发送（desktop 与 web 共用 `exchangeTicket`）
- 账户页流水改为一次 `all=1` 拉取，客户端本地分页；每页条数保存在 localStorage（`sciencediscovery-account-page-size`）
  - 兼容旧服务：若服务端忽略 `all=1` 并返回 `nextBeforeId`，客户端按 `beforeId` 游标继续翻页，直到 null 或达到 1000 条上限（`MAX_LEDGER_ROWS`，与页面提示共用同一个常量）
- `system prompt` 按约定暂不改

pr:1497.body:
A Biomni L5 case that passed only on its case-level retry kept two scorecards in its shard artifact: the superseded `failed`/`not_run` attempt and the scored retry. The gate required one document per `case_id`, reported `MISSING_OR_DUPLICATE_METRICS`, kept the stale attempt in the row and left the aggregate incomplete, so `real-report` exited 1 and the release could not publish.

## Change
- `.ci/biomni-gate.mjs` `evaluateSuite` is attempt-aware: the documents carrying a case's `case_id` are validated, and exactly one validating document is accepted. Zero validating (missing/incomplete) or several (duplicate) still fail closed; one invalid document keeps its detailed error.
- The accepted document, not `matches[0]`, supplies delivery, evaluation, measurements, local evaluation, judge usage and the certified case entry.
- `case_statuses` exposes `attempts`, `valid_attempts`, `passed_after_retry`; `renderSuite` renders `completed (passed after retry, 1 of 2 scorecards valid)`.
- The optional `prepare-real-e2e-results.mjs` staging filter is untaken: scorecards carry no attempt marker, so the gate certifies on its own.

## Validation
New `.ci/biomni-gate.test.mjs` cases certify a superseded `failed`/`not_run` scorecard plus its retried scored scorecard (via `evaluateSuite` and `collectSuite`) and still fail closed on two valid scorecards; existing fail-closed assertions stay green.
- `node --test .ci/biomni-gate.test.mjs` → 19 pass, 0 fail; policy, real-report integration, case-execution and provider-fault suites → 61 pass, 0 fail
- `pnpm ci:selftest` → 237 pass, 0 fail; `pnpm ci:l1` → PASS 4/4
- `pnpm ci:ut` / `ci:st` / `ci:e2e` → BLOCKED, no bubblewrap here; preflight fails before any entry runs.

## E2E user journeys
Not applicable: no user-observable product path.

## Release
Release category: release:internal
User impact: none outside CI; a release run that recovers a Biomni case with its documented retry can certify.
Compatibility and migration: none.

Closes #1490


pr:1498.body:
会话设置's 审查档位 (300px) and 专家 (380px) flyouts were pinned to `left: calc(100% + 4px)`, so the enclosing column clipped the 1px right border and row text: at 1024px 审查档位 ended at x=1031; at 960px 专家 ended at x=969.

## What changed
- Each card is measured against its panel: right of the panel when it fits, otherwise entirely on its left, then clamped to `[8, innerWidth - width - 8]`, the `RowMenu` rule. 审查档位 keeps the panel's top edge, 专家 its bottom; resize and scroll measure again.
- It is portalled to `document.body` and fixed: at 960px the flip lands at x=23..403 while the menu's column starts at x=326, so the portal prevents a left clip.
- `max-width: calc(100vw - 16px)` plus a measured max-width keeps the 380px card in the clamp's space. The helper is mapped P1 in `test/source-test-map.json` (UT C2).

## Validation
- `CI_ENFORCE_SOURCE_MAP=1 node .ci/changed-path-check.mjs apps/desktop/src/views/flyout-placement.ts`: OK, 1/1 mapped; `node test/check-e2e-meta.mjs`: 135 specs, 0 errors.
- Desktop UT `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop test`: 1741 passed / 0 failed (6 new); typecheck passed; `pnpm ci:l1`: 4/4 passed.
- New Playwright spec at 960x720 and 1024x720: both cards end at x=403 (<= innerWidth-8) and left of the panel at x=407; computed 1px `#ececec` right border, right-edge hit-test on the card, all row text inside. 4/4 pass; `reviewer.spec.ts` 14/14.
- Same spec on the pre-fix tree: 3 failures, expected <=1016 received 1031 (and <=952, received 1031).
- frontend-quality `checkLayout` both cards at both widths: PASS, `issues: []`.
- Full tagged `ci:ut`/`ci:st` need bubblewrap, unavailable here (0 cases run); the package UT and mocked desktop journeys ran directly.

## Remaining risk
The flipped card overlays the session list while open, like `RowMenu`. Very narrow windows may still need the final clamp, overlapping the panel.
