pr:1499.body: The desktop idea tree had exactly one scale: the one `fit()` computed from the column width. No wheel, no button and no drag changed it, so a drawing wider than the column could only be read by scrolling at whatever size the column imposed — a wide branch could not be shrunk to see its shape, and a hypothesis could not be enlarged to read it. ## What changed - **`apps/desktop/src/views/idea/IdeaTree.tsx`** - **Zoom.** The wheel zooms the drawing, and a small bar adds `−` / percentage / `＋` / `适应宽度`, both sharing one range (0.4–2). The buttons are ordinary buttons with `aria-label` and `title`, the percentage is an ``, and each button is disabled at the end of the range. The wheel listener is native and non-passive: React's wheel handler is passive, so it could not keep the panel behind the tree from scrolling while the drawing zoomed. The scale is computed first and the event only claimed when it can actually move: at either end of the range, or with no vertical delta, the box keeps the gesture and scrolls. - **Pan.** Dragging the background moves the drawing by scrolling it, so nothing — not a zoom step, not a drag, not a resize — moves the reader's view away from what they were reading. The grab cursor appears only when the drawing is actually bigger than the column. A press that lands on a node button, or on the zoom bar, is that control's press and does not start a pan. - **Double click.** On the background: one step in (×1.5), and a second double click back to the column's fit. - **Keyboard.** With the tree focused, `+` / `-` zoom and `0` fits; the region is focusable and shows a focus ring (`aria-keyshortcuts="+ - 0"`). - A scale set by hand survives new nodes arriving and a resize. Before this, `ResizeObserver` re-fitted on every layout change, which is exactly the state a running research is in; a new tree, or the fit control, still starts from the column's own fit. - **`apps/desktop/src/styles/idea-tree.css`** — the tree gets a positioned wrapper (`.idea-tree-shell`) and the bar is its child, absolutely placed at the wrapper's top-right; the grab / grabbing cursors; the focus ring. The bar is **not** inside the scroller. - **`apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/text/en.ts`** — four labels (canvas zoom, zoom in, zoom out, fit width). - **`apps/desktop/tests/idea-tree-view.test.tsx`** — eight cases: the fit never magnifies and stops at the readable floor; the hand range clamps; a wheel asks for a scale and reports when it cannot move the one it has (pixels, lines, pages, both ends, a zero delta); zooming keeps the viewport's middle over the same drawing; an automatic fit leaves a hand-set scale alone; the component's own buttons take 100% → 120% → 144% while a new graph keeps 144%; the keyboard zooms and `0` fits; and a double click zooms one step and then returns to the fit. - **`apps/desktop/tests/idea-tree-legacy.test.tsx`, `apps/desktop/tests/idea-tree-stale-node.test.tsx`** — select a node by `idea-tree-node-button` instead of "the first button", so the new controls are not counted as node buttons. This is the **desktop** implementation. The browser workbench draws its own tree (`apps/web/src/IdeaTreeCanvas.tsx`, whose wheel zoom is reset by each graph update); that is a separate component with its own tests and is not touched here. ## Behaviour, measured Same component, same 360px column, same graph. Real wheel, real drag, real click, real double click and real key presses, read back from the DOM: | | result | |---|---| | wheel, one step | fit **60%** → **75.1%** | | next graph update | still **75.1%** | | `适应宽度` | back to **60%** | | a real click on `＋` | **60% → 72%** | | a real click on `−` | **72% → 60%** | | drag 50px left on the background | `scrollLeft` **78 → 128** | | a drag that starts on the bar | pan did not move (`scrollLeft` unchanged) | | double click on the background | **60% → 90%** (×1.5) | | second double click | **90% → 60%** (the fit) | | `+` with the tree focused | **60% → 72%** | | `0` with the tree focused | **72% → 60%** | | at 149%, scrolled fully right | bar at x **165–322** inside the tree's **12–348** | | at 200%, one wheel notch further in | scale held at **200%**, `scrollTop` **80 → 0** (the box got the gesture) | On `main`, the same wheel leaves the scale at 60% and the bar does not exist: there is no zoom at all, which is what the report was about. ## Screenshots Component-level renders of the real `IdeaTreeView` against the app's own `apps/desktop/src/styles/index.css`, in a 360px column. This is not a recording of the whole app; the Electron window is not automated in this environment. Pinned to the storage commit `3a127cf870606f42384a28526a617a7a8aea35ff` (`shots/desktop-idea-tree-zoom/`), from one run of the current head: ![the four states, zh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/3a127cf870606f42384a28526a617a7a8aea35ff/shots/desktop-idea-tree-zoom/states-zh.png) ![the four states, en](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/3a127cf870606f42384a28526a617a7a8aea35ff/shots/desktop-idea-tree-zoom/states-en.png) The four panels are: this branch at the column's fit, one wheel step in, after the next graph update, and back at the fit after `适应宽度`. Both languages, because the bar carries visible copy and the two are not the same width. At 149%, panned to the far right — the state that used to carry the controls out of view: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/3a127cf870606f42384a28526a617a7a8aea35ff/shots/desktop-idea-tree-zoom/zoomed-scrolled-zh.png After a drag, the same drawing at the same scale, moved: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/3a127cf870606f42384a28526a617a7a8aea35ff/shots/desktop-idea-tree-zoom/panned-zh.png For comparison, `main` at the same column and the same graph: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/3a127cf870606f42384a28526a617a7a8aea35ff/shots/desktop-idea-tree-zoom/main-zh.png ## Fixes in this head (`9c3fc16a`) - **Clicks on the zoom bar did nothing.** A press on the bar started a pan: `onPointerDown` captured the pointer on the scroller, `pointerup` was retargeted to the scroller, and the browser sent the click there instead of to the button. Now a press inside `.idea-tree-zoom` is left to the bar (as a press on a node already was), and a double click on the bar no longer bubbles into the canvas gesture. Verified with real clicks, not `props.onClick`: see the two click rows above. - **The bar scrolled out of the viewport horizontally.** `position: sticky; top: 0` pins one axis only, and the zoom itself re-centres the drawing. The bar now lives in a non-scrolling wrapper beside the scroller and is positioned against it, so it keeps the tree's corner on both axes — measured at 149% with the drawing scrolled fully right, and in the `zoomed-scrolled-zh` frame. - **The wheel swallowed every gesture.** It now computes the clamped scale first and only claims the event when the scale actually changes; at the 40% / 200% ends, or with no vertical delta, the box scrolls instead of going dead. Measured above at 200%. - **Two existing desktop tests were red** (`idea-tree-legacy.test.tsx:87` counted 5 buttons, `idea-tree-stale-node.test.tsx:49` took the zoom-out button as the node). Both now select `.idea-tree-node-button`, like `idea-tree-view.test.tsx` already did. ## Tests - `apps/desktop/tests/idea-tree-view.test.tsx`, `idea-tree-legacy.test.tsx`, `idea-tree-stale-node.test.tsx`: **21 pass / 0 fail**. The files are tagged `os:linux`; on this Windows host they were run as copies with only the platform tag changed to `os:windows`, deleted afterwards. - The whole `apps/desktop` suite on this host: **163 pass / 0 fail**, 139 skipped because they are tagged `os:linux`; CI runs those on Linux. - `tsc -p apps/desktop/tsconfig.json --noEmit` — clean on the pre-rebase worktree (main `940ea4f0` plus these files). The pushed head is main `a19476ae` plus the same seven files, and CI typechecks that tree; this host cannot install main's workspace packages to repeat the check locally. - Mutation: removing the guard that lets a hand-set scale survive an automatic fit turns that case red. - The frames were taken behind two gates: every `` fully loaded (`complete` and `naturalWidth > 0`) and no request answered 4xx, or the run aborts and writes nothing. The gestures above were exercised with real browser input events, not by writing the state directly. ## Optional notes from the review, not taken - **Zoom about the pointer** (`EvolveTree` does): this zooms about the viewport centre. Centring is what keeps `ideaTreeScrollAfterZoom` a pure ratio of the middle and testable as "the same drawing column under the middle"; pointer-anchored zoom is a different contract and a different gesture for `EvolveTree` to converge on, not something to slot in here. - **Composing the pending scroll across a burst of wheel events**: a flick can still compute each step from the scroll that has not been applied yet. Left as is — the target is overwritten, not composed, and a burst lands within a few pixels. - **`IDEA_TREE_ZOOM_MIN = 0.4` below the fit's readable 0.6**: deliberate, as the review says. The comment on the constant says the hand range is the reader's choice; the fit stays readable. ## Scope Only the tree view. `IdeaNodeDetail`, the research card, the panel and the create dialog are untouched; no product text is removed, and the node list keeps its own controls.

pr:1500.body:
## What this fixes

The rail paints `apps/desktop/src/assets/brand/app-mark.png` at 32x32 on a `#f5f5f5` surface. Since `6614a0c4` ("switch logo, app mark and Windows icon to the rounded light variant") that PNG fills its whole 128x128 canvas with a white rounded square - 93.6% of its pixels are fully opaque and 60.3% are pure white - so the rail shows a white tile with the mark inside it instead of the mark itself.

This replaces the asset with the transparent cut of the official light artwork, corrects the stylesheet comment that described a tile, and gives the shell's first-run pages the same cut so one launch does not change the mark halfway through. Three files: the PNG, `design.css` (comment), `application/scripts/build.mjs` (the copy source).

## How the asset was made

- Source: the official vertical light logo, rendered at 8x on a transparent page.
- The wordmark is everything below the fully transparent band at y=471-564 of that render; the mark above it is 320x372 px there.
- Crop: a square canvas sized on the mark's long side (394 px at 8x, ~6% above and below), resized to 128x128 with Lanczos, RGBA.
- Measured on the file that ships, with explicit thresholds: ink box (`alpha > 0`) 109x126 px inside 128, margins 10 px left, 9 px right, 1 px above and below; `alpha = 255` on 29.6% of the canvas, `alpha = 0` on 55.1%, and the remaining 15.3% partial. At `background-size: 32px` that draws the mark at about 27x31.5 px - it is a tall mark, so it fills the box vertically and keeps its air on the sides.
- The file keeps the 128 px size the stylesheet asks for, so `background-size: 32px 32px` and `border-radius: 8px` are untouched.

## Where the mark is painted

Six surfaces paint it, all on a light background:

| surface | rule / file | background |
| --- | --- | --- |
| rail | `apps/desktop/src/styles/design.css:90` | `#f5f5f5` (`.rail`) |
| sign-in page header | `apps/desktop/src/styles/login.css:36` | `#fff` (`.login-page`) |
| setup-wizard header | `apps/desktop/src/styles/wizard.css:59` | `#fff` (`.wizard-page`) |
| 技能 › 从 GitHub 导入 | `apps/desktop/src/styles/settings.css:1807` | `#fff` (settings dialog) |
| shell loading page | `application/src/loading.html` (`.wizard-brand-mark`) | `#fff` |
| shell first-run page | `application/src/wizard.html` (same rule) | `#fff` |

The last two load `app-mark.png` from `dist/`, which `application/scripts/build.mjs` writes - now from the renderer's asset, so they paint this file too.

The remaining three mentions do not paint anything themselves: `apps/desktop/src/views/Rail.tsx:76` and `apps/desktop/src/views/settings/SkillGitImportView.tsx:259` name it in a comment and a class name, and `application/scripts/build.mjs` is the copy step.

## The shell pages paint the same cut

Before this branch `build.mjs` copied `application/build/icon-256.png` to `dist/app-mark.png`, so the pages that load before React painted the old tile at 24x26 px inside the 32 px box while the rail painted 28x30 px - the mark changed as the loading page handed over to the SPA.

The fix is not to make `icon-256.png` transparent. That one file has three jobs:

- `dist/icon.png` - the tray image (`application/src/main.ts:1601`), which sits on unknown desktop backgrounds and needs its tile;
- the OLD source of `dist/app-mark.png`, the shell brand row, until this branch;
- the 256 frame `application/scripts/make-icon.ps1` wraps into `build/icon.ico` for the installer and taskbar.

So `build.mjs` now copies the renderer's transparent asset to `dist/app-mark.png` and leaves `dist/icon.png` exactly where it was: the UI gets the transparent cut, the system icons keep the opaque one.

Verified by running those two copy statements as written (same `join`/`cpSync` expressions) in the shell package: `dist/app-mark.png` comes out byte-identical to `apps/desktop/src/assets/brand/app-mark.png` (md5 `9263f9c9...`) and `dist/icon.png` byte-identical to `build/icon-256.png` (md5 `5081a365...`), so the tray image did not move. `node --check application/scripts/build.mjs` exits 0. The whole script could not be run here - the shell package's `node_modules` are not installed in this checkout and esbuild stops on `electron-updater` - so the esbuild half was not executed; the copy half is what this diff changes, and that is what I ran.

## Frames

Pinned to commit `97142e04` on `yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery:screenshots-appmark`, not to a branch name. Harness: `apps/desktop/e2e` - Vite on its own port, `fixtures.ts` answers every `/api/**` request; viewport 1280x820, DPR 1, zh-CN. The only difference between a "before" and its "after" is `app-mark.png`.

**Frames for the two shell pages.** `application/src/loading.html` and `application/src/wizard.html` are plain HTML with inline CSS, so both were rendered directly at `e969931e`: the shipped markup and stylesheet, the same 1440x900 viewport at DPR 2, and only `app-mark.png` swapped between the two copies (`application/build/icon-256.png`, md5 `5081a365…`, which is what the old `build.mjs` copied, versus `apps/desktop/src/assets/brand/app-mark.png`, md5 `9263f9c9…`). `wizard.html` replaces its body when `window.sdShell.wizard` is absent, so its preload bridge was stubbed; no markup, style or asset was altered, and the loading page needed no stub because its bridge calls are guarded.

pr:1508.body:
Closes #1485.

The settings surface was modal for the pointer and not for the keyboard: opening it left `document.activeElement` on the 设置 button in the rail, the first Tab walked the page behind the backdrop, and Escape closed the panel without returning focus anywhere useful (#1485 measured 23 Tabs before the dialog was reached and 47 before the focus loop fell out to `BODY`).

**What changed** (four files: `SystemSettingsDialog.tsx`, `SettingsModal.tsx`, the new `settings-keyboard.spec.ts` and the map registration; +324/−3 across the pull request)

- the panel is now `<section role="dialog" tabIndex={-1} ref>` and an effect moves focus into it on open, remembering the element that opened it;
- a keydown trap keeps Tab inside the panel: at the last stop Tab wraps to the first, at the first Shift+Tab wraps to the last, and the panel itself counts as one end so the very first Tab enters the content instead of leaving;
- the focusable list is filtered with `getClientRects()` so hidden items are skipped, and it includes `summary`, which this panel really has (`McpServers.tsx:533`, `SandboxDirectSettings.tsx:147`, `SkillGitImportView.tsx:316`);
- Escape still closes through the existing window listener and `claimsEscape`; the trap's cleanup returns focus to the opener when that element is still connected (the skill-import and MCP-trial paths navigate away instead, so they are left alone);
- the panel keeps holding the boundary for the surfaces that trap nothing (添加模型 and the two skill dialogs), while a nested surface that does trap Tab claims the key first and the panel leaves it alone through `event.defaultPrevented` — that is `McpModal`, and also the skill drawer inside `SettingsModal` (`SettingsModal.tsx:58-72`), whose listener now sits on the drawer surface instead of on `document`. Without that move the panel handler, being closer to the target, ran first and swallowed the drawer's wrap: from 设置 › 专家 › 新增专家 › 指定可用能力 › 配置技能, Tab off the drawer's 确定 walked the form behind it instead of wrapping. The 新增专家 / 编辑专家 screens themselves are panel pages (`specialist-subpage`), not dialogs, so nothing there traps.

**Where focus lands, and why** — on the panel container, not on its first control. That is what `McpModal.tsx:89-109` and `SkillDialog.tsx:49` already do, and this surface should behave like those two rather than like a fourth variant. Two alternatives were built and photographed before choosing: the first focusable control here is the 收起侧栏 button (Enter collapses the navigation), and focusing the selected navigation item (`aria-current="page"`, 「通用」) would add a rule neither existing modal has. Switching to that second option later is a one-line change in the same effect, if it is wanted after seeing the frames.

**Evidence** — `apps/desktop/e2e/settings-keyboard.spec.ts`, six mocked desktop cases on real Tab presses:

1. opening the panel puts focus inside it, and the first Tab lands on a control inside it;
2. Shift+Tab from the panel goes to the last stop, Tab from the last wraps to the first, and 60 consecutive Tabs never leave the panel;
3. keyboard open, focus inside, Escape: focus is back on the 设置 button (`data-guide="settings"`);
4. with 添加模型 open over the panel, twenty Tabs stay inside the panel and reach the nested dialog's own controls;
5. the backdrop starts at the rail's right edge, the rail is still clickable, and the page behind accepts no pointer;
6. with the skill drawer open, twelve Tabs from its 确定 stay inside `.specialist-drawer` instead of walking the form behind it.

On the pre-fix source the first three fail and the backdrop case passes. Mutation runs, each reverting one mechanism only: dropping `node.focus()` fails case 1; dropping the keydown listener fails case 2; dropping `previous.focus()` fails case 3; dropping the "panel holds focus" Shift+Tab branch fails case 2; putting the nested stand-aside back fails the 添加模型 case (that run was filtered to the single case, so it shows 1 failed and says nothing about the other four). The source was restored between runs and matched the committed bytes.

**Frames** — 1440×900 at 2×, mocked desktop harness, the same steps in every frame: Tab to 设置 in the rail, Enter to open, and the focus ring is the browser's own (no styling or annotation added). Before is `a70ef94c` (main, no fix), after is `ff611c9c`. These twelve frames are byte-identical (SHA-256, 12 of 12) to the set rendered before the nested-dialog fix landed, and the only later commit (`6ee27008`) touches `settings-keyboard.spec.ts` alone, so no pixel in these three states moved across the review round.

The plain statement of what each pair shows: on open the ring sits on the rail's 设置 before and there is no ring on the page after (focus is on the panel, which draws none — that is the chosen behaviour, not a lost state); after one Tab the ring is on the account button behind the backdrop before and on the panel's own 收起侧栏 after; after Escape the ring stays on the account button before and returns to 设置 after.

pr:1512.body: ## Summary The desktop shell no longer opens an in-app web page for HUAWEI sign-in: it opens the account service in the **system default browser**, receives the one-shot ticket over a loopback callback, and forwards it to the renderer. - **Install-phase entry page** — after a successful sign-in the page shows the success panel (登录成功 / welcome / credits) with an 「进入工作台」 button. - **Account page (用户详情页)** — a settled sign-in swaps straight to the account details; the success summary belongs to the install phase only. - **Failure handling** — the install phase offers 「继续配置自定义模型」 or 「重试」; the account page keeps its signed-out state and offers 重试. - **No frozen page** — an in-flight sign-in can be cancelled while the browser leg is in flight (once the ticket is being exchanged there is nothing left to cancel) and times out after 5 minutes (Microsoft Entra allows 5 minutes per interactive step, Okta/Auth0 document 5-minute browser redirects, RFC 8628 device flows use 5–30 minutes). - Plain browsers (web build, SPA dev server, Playwright) keep the existing same-window fragment redirect. ## Changes | Area | File | What | |---|---|---| | Shell | `application/src/signin-callback.ts` | one-shot loopback callback server bound to a per-flow nonce (same-origin and JSON body only, single use, 16 KB body cap, 10-minute safety timeout) | | Shell | `application/src/main.ts`, `application/src/preload.ts` | `sd-shell:account-signin-*` IPC plus `shell.openExternal` for the built sign-in URL | | Renderer | `apps/desktop/src/auth/browser-signin.ts` | bridge wrapper, 5-minute deadline, cancel | | Renderer | `apps/desktop/src/views/LoginPage.tsx` | success panel, failure panel with the two ways forward, waiting hint and cancel | | Renderer | `apps/desktop/src/views/AccountPage.tsx` | system-browser sign-in from the account panel, details directly after success, retry after failure | | Copy | `apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/text/en.ts` | new strings | | Tests | `application/test/signin-callback.test.ts`, `apps/desktop/tests/browser-signin.test.ts` | callback, cancel and timeout coverage | ## Validation Local run on Windows 10 22H2, Node 24.22.3, pnpm workspace: | Check | Result | |---|---| | `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck` | pass | | `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop build` | pass | | `node scripts/build.mjs` (shell bundle) | `shell build ok` | | `apps/desktop` targeted unit tests (browser-signin, shell-bridge, boot-screens, setup-wizard, account-gate, accounts-signin-notice) | 8 pass, 4 skipped (other platforms), 0 fail | | `apps/desktop` browser-signin unit tests (incl. cancel during `begin()`) | 6/6 pass | | `application` loopback callback tests (incl. wrong-flow, cross-site and foreign-origin posts) | 7/7 pass | | `apps/desktop` `onboarding-account.spec.ts` (desktop-chromium, after the rebase) | 7/7 pass | The screenshots below come from the built desktop UI served by the local stack, driven through a mocked shell bridge and a mocked account service so every state is deterministic and repeatable. Both languages were captured. ### 中文 | State | Screenshot | |---|---| | 01 安装配置页（入口） | | | 02 等待系统浏览器登录（5 分钟提示 + 取消登录） | | | 03 登录失败（继续配置自定义模型 / 重试） | | | 04 登录成功（欢迎 / 积分 / 进入工作台） | | | 05 用户详情页（未登录） | | | 06 用户详情页（登录成功后直接显示详情） | | ### English | State | Screenshot | |---|---| | 01 Install-phase entry page | | | 02 Waiting for the system browser (5-minute hint + cancel) | | | 03 Sign-in failed (custom model / try again) | | | 04 Signed in (welcome / credits / enter workspace) | | | 05 Account page (signed out) | | | 06 Account page (details shown right after sign-in) | | ### Notes - The screenshots are not committed to this branch: they live on the temporary `pr-1512-assets` branch, and the tables above pin them to commit `12a70738`, so the pixels this description shows cannot drift. They are review evidence, not part of the build. - The real end-to-end round-trip (system browser -> HUAWEI -> loopback callback -> desktop) was also exercised manually before these captures, with the shell's `SCIENCE_AGENT_ACCOUNTS_URL` set to `https://sciencediscovery.openjiuwen.com/accounts`. ### Review follow-up (commit `f7c68f66`) - **F1** — `test/source-test-map.json` maps `apps/desktop/src/auth/browser-signin.ts` to its unit test, so the changed-path gate can pass. - **F2** — the loopback callback is bound to a per-flow nonce (`/callback/` serves the page, `/result/` accepts the post; anything else is 404). A foreign `Origin`, a non-`same-origin` `Sec-Fetch-Site` and a non-`application/json` body are refused, and the page sends `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` and a CSP. - **F3** — a flow cancelled while `begin()` is still in flight (or whose `open()` fails) now closes the just-created server instead of leaving it until its own timeout. - **F4** — the account panel awaits `onSignedIn` before leaving its pending state, and a rejection reaches the failure state. - **F5** — cancel is offered only while the browser leg is in flight, in both the install page and the account panel. - **F6** — the accounts deploy template moved out of this repository with #1492, so the `WEB_ORIGINS=http://127.0.0.1:*` line now belongs to the extracted accounts service's deployment template; the rebase dropped this branch's edit of that file. - **F7** — the system-browser page is bilingual; that browser's language is not readable from the app. - The screenshots are no longer committed to this branch; they moved to the temporary `pr-1512-assets` branch, pinned to commit `12a70738`, and the 02 frames were refreshed for the narrower, left-aligned cancel action. Rebased onto `main` (`4f3d75ed`, which includes #1492's merge `90e736bc`): `settleAuthTicket` now calls #1492's `exchangeTicket(ticket)` signature, and the deleted accounts deploy template is no longer edited here.

## What

Deletes `docs/screenshots/` from the tree: **14 directories, 95 files, 8,327,474 bytes (about 7.9 MiB)** at `main` = `e374837d`. Deletions only; no file is added, edited or moved.

| directory | files | bytes |

| `setup-wizard-button-radius` | 6 | 384,930 |

Of the 95 files, 79 are `.png`, 6 are `.jpg` and 10 are the `README.md` files that describe the older sets. This includes `1440`, added on 2026-11-27 (18:04:07Z) — the most recent committed set.

## Why

#1477 records the convention that UI frames are review evidence, not repository artifacts: they are hosted outside the tree at a URL that does not change, embedded in the pull request body, and pinned to a commit SHA when that URL comes from a branch. Those directories are history rather than the rule, and the tree still carries that history. Git keeps every one of them: each blob stays reachable from the commit that added it, so this change removes them from the current tree without losing them.

## What this does not break, checked rather than assumed

- **In-tree references: exactly one.** `apps/desktop/e2e/network-allowlist.spec.ts:48` is the only file on `main` that names a path under `docs/screenshots/`, in the comment "The screenshots each run writes are copied unchanged into `docs/screenshots/1399/`…". I downloaded and grepped the contents of all 1,034 text files on `main` (`.md`, `.mjs`, `.json`, `.yml`, `.yaml`, `.sh`, `.py`, `.txt`, `.html`, `.spec.ts`, and `.ts`/`.tsx` under `scripts/` or `e2e/`). Several files discuss screenshots in general — `.ci/README.md`, `.agents/skills/frontend-quality/{SKILL.md,references/*}`, `docs/en/design/desktop-mcp-controls.v2.md`, `docs/en/developer-docs/frontend-quality.md` among them — and every one of those mentions the word, not this path: no link, no path, nothing that resolves into the directory. There is also no index `README.md` at `docs/screenshots/`.
- **The one comment is comment-only and does not read this directory.** It says a run copies its captures there for review evidence; no test reads or writes those files, so the capture behaviour is unchanged by deleting them. #1477 already rewrites that same comment (`:47-49`) to say the frames are attached to the pull request.
- **Pull request bodies: none point into `main`.** Of the 116 pull requests that mention `docs/screenshots`, I read every body: no body links or embeds a path on `main`/`master`. Recent ones embed frames from a fork branch or from an upstream commit SHA (for example `…/3df4eb11…/docs/screenshots/1503/…`), and those keep resolving because the commits still exist.

## The guide's wording is a follow-up, not part of this change

#1477 adds a `### UI changes need screenshots` section to `CONTRIBUTING.md` whose two sentences describe these directories as still present:

> Some directories under `docs/screenshots/` still hold frames committed by earlier changes; that is history, not the rule…

> Some of the committed directories kept that in a `README.md`; the rest left it in the pull request that added them…

After this change both clauses describe directories that no longer exist. Those lines are **not on `main` yet** — #1477 introduces them — so editing them here would race that pull request on the same file for no benefit. So this PR deliberately does not touch `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and the wording correction follows in a separate change once #1477 has landed: both sentences move to the past tense (planned: "…held frames committed by earlier changes…" and "The directories that held committed frames kept that in a `README.md`…"). Until then the guide is no more wrong than it is today, and after this change it is wrong only about the tense.

## Verification for this head

- Merge base is `main` = `e374837d`; the branch is one commit that changes no file except the 95 deletions.
- The tree I built was diffed against `main` before pushing: `docs/screenshots/` has no remaining entry, and no other path changed (the `docs` tree node's own sha moves, which is the consequence of its child changing).
- No test suite applies to deleting documentation image files; the reference audit above is the evidence, and its inputs are named so it can be repeated.

`decodeEntities` decoded only five named references, so search titles and snippets reached the model and report as `café — 5–10 … O'Brien`. It now decodes the names a browser renders, keeping the single-pass contract.

## Changes

Ask-mode recovery after a sandbox network block no longer asks for a third shell approval when the token re-run is the same execution. pr:1517.body:
`web_fetch`'s public-URL guard decoded only mapped/compatible IPv6 literals, so a URL could still reach loopback, RFC1918, metadata or CGNAT through NAT64 (`64:ff9b::/96`, `64:ff9b:1::/96`), 6to4 (`2002::/16`), IPv4-translated (`::ffff:0:0:0/96`) or Teredo (`2001:0::/32`), and site-local `fec0::/10` was public. This was missing on main when this PR opened; #922 implemented this class but was closed unmerged; #664 closed only mapped/compatible.

## Change
- `url-guard.ts`: `ipv6Blocked()` strips a zone id, decodes the embedded IPv4 for those families into the unchanged `ipv4Blocked()` table, inverts Teredo first, rewrites a trailing dotted quad to hex so all spellings agree, and rejects `fec0::/10` by prefix.
- Addresses review comment 7233514884: non-canonical suffixes of the local-use `64:ff9b:1::/48` are default-denied, since RFC 8215 lets a deployment choose that prefix's length, so the embedded-IPv4 position is unknown and a public verdict could hide a private address; canonical `/96` still decodes, so public NAT64 egress works.
- `providers.test.ts`: per-family blocked rows (loopback, RFC1918, 169.254.169.254, CGNAT), allowed canonical/public rows, dotted/hex pairs, zone+dotted rows and non-canonical suffix rows, on literal and resolver paths.

## Validation
- Red: 18 pass / 1 fail for the zone+dotted rows (`::ffff:127.0.0.1%eth0 false !== true`).
- Green: 19/19 focused; 99/99 package; root `pnpm typecheck` exit 0.
- UT/ST/E2E could not run locally: preflight stops with `BUBBLEWRAP_UNAVAILABLE` (no bwrap or user namespaces). CI runs them on this PR.

## E2E user journeys
No UI changes; the guard's rows above cover it. Mocked E2E: BLOCKED on the same preflight.

## Release
Release category: release:fix
User impact: private/metadata/CGNAT targets in these forms are refused; public NAT64/6to4/Teredo egress keeps working.
Compatibility: canonical NAT64 is unchanged; non-canonical local-use suffixes are refused rather than guessed.

pr:1521.body:
Closes #1520

Two independent assumptions in the import path made a freshly exported package fail to import. #1520 reproduced both against real packages; this fixes each where it breaks and pins it with a test that fails when the fix is reverted.

## Root cause 1 — a version object the package does not carry killed the restore (`404 File not found`)

`records.versionObjects` names every version the session's records point at, including the ones the exporter could not read. One real package carries **271** `version:…:unavailable source object` lines in `manifest.omissions`, the same **271** refs still in `records.versionObjects`, and **none** of their objects in `archive/objects` — the package is honest, and the import died on the first one.

The two import paths disagreed about their own interface:

- `importResearchPackage` builds a `Map`, so a missing object is `undefined` and the existing `if (object)` guards skip it;
- `importResearchPackageStreamed` builds `DirectoryObjects` (`packages/research-package/src/index.ts`), which is declared as a `PackageObjectDirectory extends ReadonlyMap<string, Uint8Array>` but whose `get` was `readFileSync` — a miss threw `ENOENT`, and the server turned that into `404 {"error":"File not found"}`.

**Fix.** `DirectoryObjects.get` answers a miss with `undefined`, exactly like the map it claims to be; the read that iterates its own listing keeps using a private `read`. Every existing guard in `restorePackage` then works for both import paths, and nothing else changes.

The version restore no longer stays silent when a package does *not* declare the loss: it records `version:<pool>:<digest>:missing object`, but only when the package has not already said so — so the 271 declared ones are still reported once, not twice.

## Root cause 2 — a tool record's citation list was rewritten as a composer reference (`400 Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'match')`)

`remapRunEvent` decided by **key name only**: anything reached under a key called `references` was cast to `ComposerReference` and had its `id` rewritten. A tool call keeps its own citation list under that same name —

```json
{ "refsource": "Water Res. 2015 Nov 1;84():378", "reftype": "Erratum in", "pmid": "", "note": "" }
```

— with no `kind` and no `id`. The rewrite called `ids.id(undefined)`, `source.match` threw, and a valid import answered `400` with that raw JavaScript message, which the dialog shows verbatim. One package carried eight of them.

**Fix.** A reference is rewritten only when it actually carries a string `id`; anything else is walked and left exactly as it is. The composer's own references still get the new namespace, so this is a shape test rather than switching the rewrite off.

## Evidence

`packages/research-package/src/stream-import.test.ts` — a streamed package's object map answers `undefined` for a path it does not carry, the same as the in-memory map (previously threw `ENOENT`).

`services/api/src/research-package-http.test.ts` — two HTTP cases over the real `inspect`/`import` route with the streamed path:

1. a package whose `records.versionObjects` names an object the archive does not carry imports with `201` and reports `version:agent-state:<digest>:missing object`;
2. a version the package already declared unreadable is reported **once**, not twice.

`services/api/src/research-package-history.test.ts` (new) — a run event whose only `references` entry is such a citation comes back deep-equal, while a composer reference is still remapped.

**Mutation runs**, each reverting one mechanism:

| mutation | result |
| --- | --- |
| `DirectoryObjects.get` throws again | `stream-import.test.ts` 9/10 (the new parity case red) |
| the same, with `packages/research-package` rebuilt so the API sees it | `research-package-http.test.ts` 29/31 (both new cases red) |
| the shape guard removed | `research-package-history.test.ts` 0/1 |
| the `missing object` line removed (back to silent skip) | `research-package-http.test.ts` 30/31 — the "says so" case red; the once-only case still passes there, because the package's own declared line is what it counts |

**Suites run**, on the exact bytes pushed: `research-package/src/{index,stream-import,json}.test.ts` 18 + 10 + 3, `research-package-http` 31, `research-package-history` 1, `research-package-preflight` 11, `research-package-necessary` 4, `research-snapshot-integrity` 21, `shell-executions` 62 — **161 passed, 0 failed**. `tsc -p services/api`, `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` and `tsc -p packages/research-package` all exit 0.

## Not verified here

- The four `.sdresearch` files from the report are on the reporter's machine; both failing shapes are pinned with packages built in the tests rather than with those exact files.
- The full UT/ST layers, L1/L2, `merge-gate` and a real backend were not run locally; CI is their evidence.
- No user-visible surface changes: the import dialog already renders the receipt's omission list, and this only changes what reaches it (`201` plus an omission instead of `404`/`400`).

pr:1530.body:
Closes #1515

## What changes

`GET /api/search` matched Project names, Session titles (plus project name and Session id) and artifact names/titles — never a message body — so a phrase that exists only inside a conversation found nothing. `searchWorkbench` now also matches message bodies for a non-empty query, and returns the conversation as the **same** `kind: "session"` hit it already returns, carrying:

- `snippet` — the latest line of the transcript that contains the query, clipped around the match with `…` on the cut side, at most 200 characters. Cuts land on code points, so a clipped line never ends in half an emoji. New optional field on `WorkbenchSearchResult`; `detail` stays the Project line it was.

No new result kind, so `limit`/`offset`/`hasMore`/`total`, ordering and the project/session/artifact filters keep their meaning, and both clients keep their existing result list.

## The scan is bounded, not exhaustive

A transcript is one JSON file read whole (`services/api/src/store.ts:7319`), and nothing indexes it, so this is deliberately a bounded scan rather than "search everything":

| bound | value |
| --- | --- |
| Sessions read per query | the 200 most recently updated live Sessions outside the inbox |
| Messages scanned per Session | the newest 500, counting back from the last turn |
| Message-body characters scanned per Session | the newest 2,000,000, spent from the last turn backwards |
| Serialized transcript bytes charged per query | 8,000,000 |

Both per-Session bounds are spent from the newest turn backwards: a transcript is stored oldest-first, so a long Session loses its oldest text to the budget rather than its newest, and the matching line reported for a Session is its latest one. Each Session is charged the size of the transcript `readMessages` actually parsed (including `modelContext` and keys outside the body), not the text up to the first hit, so a hit cannot under-count the budget. A title hit is never re-read and never appears twice; an exact Session id is a lookup that reads no transcript; archived and inbox Sessions are never content-searched.

**Residual, stated rather than hidden:** one unusually large transcript is still read whole before it is charged, so a query can cost one full parse of such a file. That is the price of having no index; a real index is a separate change.

## Both clients

- Desktop search dialog: the matching line is a third row under the Project line (`search-hit-snippet`), so a long Project name cannot ellipsize the reason the row is there. `searchSnippet` refuses a snippet on a non-session hit.
- Web composer palette: it draws the same row and keeps a content hit when its client-side filter matches only the snippet.
- `zh-CN` and `en` hint and empty state no longer claim that message text is not searched.

## Relation to the closed #1519

#1519 was closed by the maintainer's decision that this account lands the change, on the same shape. This branch starts from that implementation: I re-read it against the route, the store read path, the shared schema and both clients, ran every gate below myself, and fixed the one thing its review flagged as non-blocking — the `MockOptions.search` doc comment in `apps/desktop/e2e/fixtures.ts` still said the mock matches `label` only, while it also matches `snippet`. No behavioural divergence.

## What I ran

- `pnpm ci:l1` — `{"status":"PASS","planned":4,"collected":4,"executed":4,"passed":4,"failed":0}`
- `node --import tsx --test src/workbench/index.test.ts` (api) — **19/19 pass**, including three tests added with the newest-first fix: the newest turn of a 600-message transcript is found, the character budget is spent from the newest message when the two older turns hold 6 MB, and a clipped snippet keeps surrogate pairs whole
- desktop `search-dialog.test.tsx` + `session-search.test.tsx` — **19/19 pass**
- web `WorkbenchNavigation.test.tsx` — **10/10 pass**
- typecheck clean: `packages/schema`, `services/api`, `apps/desktop`, `apps/web`
- mutation: with the content scan disabled (`snippets` forced empty) the workbench suite goes **11 fail / 5 pass**; restored, **16/16 pass**. So the new tests fail without the behaviour. With the scan put back to oldest-first (`slice(0, cap)` walking forward), the three new tests fail — `# pass 15 / # fail 4` — and restoring the fix brings it back to **19/19**.
- latency at the documented ceiling, measured here on a real `SessionStore` (throwaway data directory): 200 Sessions × 9 messages × ~4 KB of body each (~7.5M characters), warm runs — **hit 63–84 ms (median 69 ms), miss 60–71 ms (median 66 ms)**. WSL2, Node v22.23.4, `searchWorkbench` timed with `performance.now()` over 9 hit runs and 6 miss runs after one warm-up each. That is this machine, not a CI runner.

Every message is unchanged.
- `http/index.ts`: the catch-all maps that code to `400` with the store's own sentence, beside `INVALID_WEB_SETTINGS`. Only validation is tagged: a catalog write failure in the same save still answers 500 and still logs `unclassified_request_error`.

pr:1536.body:
## Summary

When `CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE` is on, `merge_group` runs already send `UT` and the three heavy mocked shards to the self-hosted pool `[self-hosted, Linux, X64, sciencediscovery]`. This PR routes the remaining credential-free Linux L2 jobs there too:

- `ST`
- `L2 E2E (mocked, governed)` and `L2 E2E (mocked, literature)`
- `Desktop UI-ST and mocked E2E`

Pull requests, every other event, hosted runs, credentialed real E2E jobs and distribution jobs are unchanged.

## Why

Merge-queue runs between 05:15 and 07:22 UTC on 2026-11-28 (423 jobs):

| Pool | Average utilisation | Peak concurrency | Queue time |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Self-hosted heavy | 28% of 36 runners | 28 | ≈0 (max 0.1 min) |
| Hosted, for the jobs moved here | — | — | median 3.9–6.0 min, max 15.6–20.2 min |

| Job (hosted) | Run (median) | Queue (median / max) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Desktop UI-ST and mocked E2E | 8.7 min | 3.9 / 18.1 min |
| ST | 4.7 min | 5.1 / 15.6 min |
| L2 mocked governed | 3.5 min | 5.4 / 20.2 min |
| L2 mocked literature | 3.2 min | 6.0 / 18.0 min |

The slowest self-hosted L2 job (`standard-config`) takes about 12.7 min. The L2 stage as a whole had a median of 17.7 min and a maximum of 26.3 min. In 5 of the 11 fully green runs, the job that finished L2 last was one of these hosted jobs. The self-hosted pool has since grown to 52 heavy runners across three hosts, so moving these four jobs should bring L2 close to the `standard-config` bound.

## Changes

- `.ci/mocked-matrix.mjs`: `HEAVY_MOCKED_SHARDS` becomes `SELF_HOSTED_MOCKED_SHARDS` and lists all five mocked shards. A newly added shard stays hosted until someone lists it.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:
  - `st` and `desktop-mocked` use `runs-on: ${{ fromJSON(needs.policy.outputs.ut_runner) }}`, the same policy output and pool as UT.
  - Both drop the remote `cache: pnpm` on the self-hosted path; `st` also drops the uv cache.
  - `st` provisions bubblewrap with `sudo` only when `bwrap` does not already work, using the same check as UT and the mocked E2E job.
  - On self-hosted, `st` skips `actions/cache` for the verified CPython archive and points `BINARY_CACHE_DIR` at the persistent `/ci-cache/binary-cache`. `fetch-runtime.mjs` already creates that directory and stages each write before renaming it into place.
  - On self-hosted, `desktop-mocked` runs `playwright install chromium` without `--with-deps`. The runner image already carries Chromium's system libraries and grants no `sudo`.
- `.ci/self-hosted-merge-queue.test.mjs`: the contract now expects all five shards to be routed, and checks the new routing, cache and no-sudo wiring for `st` and `desktop-mocked`. `docker` and the binary jobs must stay hosted.
- `.ci/README.md`: the self-hosted routing section lists the new jobs and what stays hosted.

## Validation

- `node --test .ci/*.test.mjs`: 246 tests, 246 passed, 0 failed.
- `pnpm ci:l1`: PASS, planned 4, executed 4, passed 4.
- `pnpm ci:selftest`: passed.
- `pnpm docs:check`: passed (148 Markdown files).
- The four moved jobs, reproduced at `main` `a19476ae2` inside temporary containers. Each container used the self-hosted runner image and the same container options as the registered runners, was not registered with GitHub, and ran the steps as this workflow now runs them on self-hosted (no `sudo`, no remote caches, local `/ci-cache`):

  | Job | Result | Wall time incl. clone and install |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | ST (`pnpm ci:st -- --profile merge --coverage`) | PASS 69/69 | 4.2 min |
  | mocked `governed` (`pnpm ci:e2e -- --profile merge --shard governed`) | PASS 5/5 | 2.1 min |
  | mocked `literature` (`--shard literature`) | PASS 6/6 | 2.0 min |
  | Desktop: `run-desktop-e2e.mjs ui-st` and `mocked` with `CI_DESKTOP_SPECS=all`, `CI_DESKTOP_PROFILE=merge` | 14 passed + 254 passed, 0 failed | 4.9 min |

- UT and the other mocked shards were not re-run on this commit: the change only touches CI orchestration, and those jobs keep their existing routing.

## E2E user journeys

Not applicable as a product change. No user-observable behaviour changes. The journeys these jobs run were executed unchanged on the self-hosted image as listed above.

## Risk and rollout

- This changes the CI contract (workflow routing), so it needs maintainer confirmation.
- Self-hosted runners only receive trusted `merge_group` runs. The policy fails closed to `ubuntu-latest` for `pull_request`, forks and every other event.
- Rollback: unset or change `CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE`. Newly created merge-queue runs then go back to `ubuntu-latest`; runs that were already queued for self-hosted labels need to be cancelled and re-queued.

## Release

Release category: release:internal

User impact: none; merge-queue validation runs on different runners.

Compatibility and migration: no migration. The self-hosted runners already provide `/ci-cache`, bubblewrap and Chromium's system libraries.

pr:1537.body:
## Problem

Nightly L4 run 44361037291 (head `d57fc269`) failed on `research-2` / DRB-59 with `[181001] model call failed ... read ECONNRESET` and delivered partial. `stack.log` shows the request `model-8f784f89` was HTTP 200 with 12,117 SSE records / 3,716,762 bytes / 105,894 ms, `hasText` and `hasToolCalls` true, `finishReason: "tool_calls"` — and then `error.classification: "network"`, `attempts: 1`, `retries: 0`. The provider had declared the turn complete; the gateway reset the connection before `[DONE]`, and the turn was discarded.

## Root cause

All three protocols read through the shared `sseData` reader (`packages/model/src/client.ts`), but only the chat reader wraps it with `canRecoverAfterCompletion`. The Responses and Anthropic readers iterate `sseData` without that guard, so a transport failure after their terminal record (`response.completed` / `message_delta`) propagates and the parsed turn is lost.

On this base the chat reader already carries the guard, so DRB-59's exact protocol no longer reproduces there — the same defect is still live for the other two protocols that share the reader, and there was no transport-level test at all (only gateway-level tests that inject a fake streamer).

## Change

- Adds `sseDataWithRecovery`, a thin wrapper around `sseData` that takes the caller's live completion state and ends the iteration normally when the transport fails after a terminal record was seen; a failure before that still propagates.
- The Responses reader passes `response.completed` / `response.incomplete` as its terminal state, the Anthropic reader maps `stop_reason` to the canonical finish reasons (`tool_use` → `tool_calls`, `max_tokens` → `length`, otherwise `stop`).
- Both readers keep the chat path's post-recovery guard: a recovered turn with incomplete tool arguments still throws.
- `jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts` is untouched, as are `MAX_STREAM_RETRIES` and the "do not replay once text was sent" policy — that policy is by design and out of scope here.

## Red / green evidence

New file `packages/model/src/client-transport.test.ts` drives a real HTTP server, writes the frames, and destroys the socket without `[DONE]`.

Before (`client.ts` at `4f3d75ed`, new tests only):

```
ok 1 - a chat stream reset after finish_reason still returns the completed turn
not ok 2 - a Responses stream reset after response.completed still returns the completed turn
not ok 3 - an Anthropic stream reset after message_delta still returns the completed turn
not ok 4 - a recovered Responses turn with truncated tool arguments is still rejected
ok 5 - a stream reset before finish_reason still fails
# tests 5
# pass 2
# fail 3
```

After (this PR):

```
ok 1 - a chat stream reset after finish_reason still returns the completed turn
ok 2 - a Responses stream reset after response.completed still returns the completed turn
ok 3 - an Anthropic stream reset after message_delta still returns the completed turn
ok 4 - a recovered Responses turn with truncated tool arguments is still rejected
ok 5 - a stream reset before finish_reason still fails
# tests 5
# pass 5
# fail 0
```

Case 1 is a regression guard for the protocol DRB-59 used; cases 2 and 3 are the defect this PR fixes; case 4 covers the post-recovery tool-argument guard on the new path; case 5 pins that a stream reset before any terminal record is still an error.

## Test collection

The tagged node audit requires each `test(...)` callback to be a static arrow or function expression, so every case is registered as `test("…", async () => { await runAfterCompletionCase(...); })`. `node --import tsx test/support/tagged/node-collect.mjs` with this file collects 5 identities, and `node test/support/tagged/shared.mjs list --profile pr --slice ut` now gets past the node phase. That slice then stops at its *python* collection phase in this worktree (no `uv` environment built here), so the UT job on CI is the real confirmation of the whole slice.

## Verification

- `node --import tsx --test "src/**/*.test.ts"` in `packages/model` — 173 tests, 173 pass, 0 fail
- `tsc -p packages/model` — clean
- `pnpm ci:l1` — PASS, planned 4 / passed 4 / failed 0
- Real L4/L5 E2E was not run locally: it needs `E2E_LLM_BASE_URL`, `E2E_LLM_MODEL`, `E2E_LLM_TOKEN` and quota, which this environment does not have; the nightly run is the real-layer check.

## Reproduction

1. Start an HTTP SSE endpoint that writes a chat/Responses/Anthropic stream with its terminal record and then destroys the socket without `[DONE]`.
2. Call `streamModelTurn` against it.
3. Before this PR the Responses and Anthropic calls reject with a network-classified error; with this PR they return the parsed turn, while the same reset before the terminal record still rejects.

## Files

- `packages/model/src/client.ts` — `sseDataWithRecovery`, the two reader call sites, the post-recovery tool-argument guard.
- `packages/model/src/client-transport.test.ts` — new transport-level cases.

Fixes #1238

- The gateway's `streamTurn` uses the same helper; its constants, log line, backoff and failure text are unchanged, and its 70 tests pass untouched.
- `EmptyModelTurnError` keeps its wire record readable from the exhausted failure; `run-failure.ts` keeps the same `server-error` mapping (only its stale comment is updated).

Extra to the plan: the `packages/model` export, wire-record registration, a unit test and a `test/source-test-map.json` entry.

pr:1545.body:
Closes #1540

## What changes

A corrupt, truncated or simply wrong file uploaded to `POST /api/projects/<id>/research-package/inspect` or `.../import` answered `500 {"error":"Internal server error"}`: the decompressor's `Z_DATA_ERROR` / `Z_BUF_ERROR` and the archive parser's own refusal sentences were never classified, so the log line was `unclassified_request_error` and the dialog showed an internal error for the caller's own file.

`services/api/src/http/research-package-refusal.ts` maps them, and the global handler asks it before the generic branch:

| input | answer |
| --- | --- |
| random bytes / a file that is not gzip (`Z_DATA_ERROR`, `incorrect header check`, `not in gzip format`) | `400` `RESEARCH_PACKAGE_INVALID` |
| a truncated archive (`Z_BUF_ERROR`, `unexpected end of file`) | `400` `RESEARCH_PACKAGE_TRUNCATED` |
| a package the parser refused (bad manifest, checksum mismatch, unlisted entry, unsafe path, ...) | `400` `RESEARCH_PACKAGE_INVALID`, with the parser's sentence in parentheses |
| a metadata entry over its bound | `413` `RESEARCH_PACKAGE_TOO_LARGE` |

Each answer carries an `error` sentence the import dialog can show — "This file is not a valid research package: it ends before the archive does." — instead of an internal-error string, so the two endpoints now behave like the refusals that already work (`507` capacity, `409 SESSION_EVIDENCE_LOCKED`).

**The exception list is deliberate.** The refusal sentences are named one by one rather than "any error from the parser is the caller's fault": exporter-side faults (`A synchronous export cannot stream package objects`, `Package object size changed while hashing`), filesystem failures (`ENOSPC`, `EACCES`, ...) and every failure outside the two upload paths keep their `500`. The direction of the trade is written in the module: a refusal the parser adds later keeps its `500` until it is classified here, which is the safe way to be wrong.

## What I ran

- `node --import tsx --test src/research-package-invalid.test.ts` (new, api) — **4/4 pass**. The endpoint test posts the four payloads #1540 measured — 64 KiB of random bytes, an archive truncated to half, a 12-byte gzip header, `{"hello":"world"}` — to **both** endpoints (8 requests) and asserts `400`, a stable `code`, an `error` sentence containing "not a valid research package", and that the body is not `Internal server error`.
- `node --import tsx --test src/research-package-http.test.ts` (existing, api) — **29/29 pass**, so the `413` / `507` / `409` answers that already existed are unaffected.
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api typecheck` — clean.
- Mutation: deleting the new branch from the global handler turns the endpoint test red with exactly the reported symptom — `inspect: 64 KiB of random bytes answered 500 {"error":"Internal server error"}` — and restoring it brings the suite back to 4/4.
- Classifier unit tests pin both directions: the parser's refusals map to 4xx, and an exporter fault, `ENOSPC` and a non-upload path stay `undefined` (500).

## Scope

Backend only: no client change and no visual change, so no screenshots. The dialog already renders `error` from a 4xx package refusal.

Files: `services/api/src/http/index.ts` (the branch, 7 lines), `services/api/src/http/research-package-refusal.ts` (new), `services/api/src/research-package-invalid.test.ts` (new). None of them is in #1521, whose change is in `packages/research-package/src/index.ts` and `services/api/src/research-snapshots.ts`, so the two PRs do not collide.

pr:1548.body:
A server fault was answered as `400` whenever its message contained words like "cannot" or "invalid", so an internal `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'match')` reached clients as raw JavaScript text. The catch-all now decides internal faults before reading that prose list.

## Changes
- `error-classification.ts`: `isInternalFault` is true for `TypeError`/`RangeError`/`ReferenceError` and for any error with a string `code`; `isKnownClientInputError` asks it first, keeps `SyntaxError` true, and leaves the legacy list untouched for plain `Error`.
- `http/index.ts`: the 400 fallback is `!isInternalFault(error) && isKnownClientInputError(error)`, so those exceptions keep the generic 500 body and the `unclassified_request_error` line. `ApiStatusError`, `SessionStoreHttpError`, ENOENT, CONFLICT, SKILL_*, MALFORMED_PATH_PARAM and RunnerHttpError branches are unchanged.
- `store.ts`: `applyWebSettingsSync` rejects a non-object settings body explicitly; its destructuring used to throw a `TypeError` that only the prose fallback turned into a 400.

## Scope of the fix
Runtime exceptions (`TypeError`/`RangeError`/`ReferenceError`) and errors carrying a string `code` now always keep the generic 500. A plain `Error` is still decided by the legacy prose list, so a hand-written internal `throw new Error("… must …")` outside a validator still answers `400` — that residual is deliberate (the list is what keeps the established validator 400s) and disappearing it would need every such thrower migrated to `ApiStatusError` or a stable code.

## Validation
- New real-socket tests: with the fix stashed, 3/6 fail (`400 !== 500`); after it, 10/10 pass (HTTP + helper).
- Still 400 with their own sentence and no fault line: "modelId is required", malformed JSON. `ApiStatusError` keeps its status, code and message.
- `pnpm ci:l1` PASS 4/4; `pnpm typecheck` and the api package typecheck pass.
- Full api suite: 2626 tests, 2614 pass, 2 skipped, 10 fail. Two subagent timeline tests fail identically at baseline (fix stashed); runner/ACP/specialist-transport cases lack host prerequisites; one deadline case is a load flake (3/3 alone). `pnpm ci:ut` cannot run here (`BUBBLEWRAP_UNAVAILABLE`, 0/8889).

## E2E
API-level: the new tests drive the running server over a socket; no browser surface changed.

## Release
Release category: release:fix
User impact: internal faults no longer surface as 400s carrying JavaScript text.
Compatibility and migration: none.

Closes #1533

### Tests

```
cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/http/error-classification-http.test.ts src/http/error-classification.test.ts src/web-settings-api.test.ts src/http/malformed-path.test.ts src/http/sandbox-network-settings-validation.test.ts src/specialists-http.test.ts
```

Reported by the agent; the platform did not rerun it.

J5 keeps the real layer from regressing and was accepted as necessary in review.
- Tests use captured libmamba transcripts, assert a marker in the failed prefix is removed, cover 503/timeout/DNS/reset and the per-attempt kill, and drive `installManagedMicromamba` itself through one transient timeout. The CI skill and `.ci/README.md` now describe lane-scoped provisioning.

pr:1551.body:
Closes #1533.

The request catch-all decides whether a failure was the caller's mistake by matching words in the error message, and answers `400` with that message as the body (`services/api/src/http/index.ts`: `isKnownClientInputError(error)` → `sendError(response, 400, message)`). An internal fault whose text happens to say "cannot", "invalid" or "must" therefore reaches the client as a client error, carrying JavaScript that was never written for a reader. #1520's import did exactly that:

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'match')
```

matched /cannot/, so the dialog showed that sentence and the status said the caller was wrong while the server was.

## What changed — one file, no change to the catch-all

`services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts` gains two gates, both consulted before the wording list:

- `isRuntimeFault` answers `false` for `TypeError`, `RangeError`, `ReferenceError`, `EvalError`. They are the interpreter reporting a defect in this server, so their message is not evidence about the caller. The three shapes #1533 names (`Cannot read properties of undefined`, `Invalid array length`, `Cannot convert undefined or null to object`) are pinned by a test.
- `quotesInterpreterFault` answers `false` for any `Error` whose message is one of the engine's own sentences, because a handler that re-wraps `cause.message` keeps the text and loses the class. It covers the `Cannot read|set properties of undefined|null` family, `Cannot convert undefined or null to object` / `a BigInt value to a number` / `object to primitive value`, `Cannot create property … on string|number|symbol`, `Cannot destructure …`, `Cannot use 'in' operator …`, `is not a function` / `is not iterable` / `is not defined`, `Invalid array length|string length`, `Maximum call stack size exceeded`, `Assignment to constant variable`. One representative sentence per pattern is pinned by a test; the patterns keep the part that makes the wording unmistakable, so a validator sentence (`after_ms must be a positive integer`) does not match.
- `SyntaxError` stays a client error: a body that does not parse is the caller's own bytes.
- A plain `Error` whose text is ordinary prose keeps the existing wording rules, because that list is a record of what the legacy validators say — deleting it would turn every one of their `400`s into a `500`, which is the opposite failure.

**There is no edit to `services/api/src/http/index.ts`.** That matters for two open pull requests: #1545 adds a branch to the same `else if` chain (`researchPackageRefusal`), and #1548 rewrites the same chain for its own version of this issue. Keeping the fix in the classifier means this one cannot conflict with either, and it is also the narrowest place that holds the rule. #1548 is not touched, closed or commented on here.

## Honest boundary

The guarantee this change makes is: **no interpreter-raised fault, and no error carrying an interpreter sentence, is answered `400` or echoed.** Those get `500` with `{"error":"Internal server error"}`, and the original text goes to the `unclassified_request_error` log line.

What is still not covered: an `Error` thrown by our own code whose message is ordinary prose containing "cannot", "must" or "invalid" but does not look like engine text — `cannot open the catalog database`, say — is still answered `400` with that text. A prose list cannot tell an internal sentence from a validator's; closing that residue means giving the legacy validators typed errors (`ApiStatusError`) instead of prose, across the stores. The `specialists` routes already do this with their own exact-wording table; the shared catch-all does not.

## Evidence

`services/api/src/http/error-classification.test.ts` — three cases, one added here: "a plain Error quoting the engine's own sentence is not client input either". Sixteen engine sentences (including a prefixed one, `Research package import failed: Cannot read properties of undefined …`) are `false` on a plain `Error`; five legacy sentences that do match the old list (`after_ms must be a positive integer`, `… cannot be deleted`, `… does not match …`, `Unsafe skill package path: …`) stay `true`; `SyntaxError` stays `true`.

`services/api/src/http/internal-error-http.test.ts` — drives the route with a fault thrown once from inside the request handler, the way a store failure surfaces. Two cases: a `TypeError` and a plain `Error` carrying the same sentence. Each must answer

1. `500` with the body `{"error":"Internal server error"}`,
2. free of the interpreter's sentence (`reading 'match'`, `Cannot read properties`), and
3. accompanied by an `unclassified_request_error` line, asserted against the real `apiLog`.

The same file keeps a legacy validator rejection (`Specialist name is required`) at `400` with its own wording, so a future change cannot quiet the whole path instead of narrowing it.

**Mutation:** removing `if (quotesInterpreterFault(error.message)) return false;` and nothing else makes the new unit case fail (`expected false, actual true`, on the first engine sentence) and the plain-`Error` route case fail (`# pass 2 / # fail 1`); restored, the file bytes match the commit and both files pass. The mutated run was filtered to these two files, so it says nothing about other suites.

**No validator's `400` turns into a 500:** every string literal in `services/api/src` and `packages/*/src` (461 files, 59,286 literals without expressions, `*.test.ts`/`*.spec.ts` excluded) was classified by the previous and the current classifier; the number whose answer changed is **0**. That is the check behind keeping the prose list: the repository does not contain a message that the new shapes swallow.

## Checks on this head (`f9da0b2b`)

- `pnpm exec tsc -p services/api --noEmit` → exit 0
- `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` → exit 0
- `error-classification.test.ts` → 4 passed
- `internal-error-http.test.ts` → 3 passed
- neighbour suite `specialists-http.test.ts` (same classifier, 400 wording and a coded `node:sqlite` fault) → 17 passed
- `test/source-test-map.json` is unchanged: the new file is a route test beside its source, and the classifier already has its unit test.

Not verified here: the full `UT`/`ST` layers, `L1`/`L2`, `merge-gate` and a real backend — CI is their evidence. The repository's tests declare `os:linux`; the runs above were on this host with the declarations honoured.

No user-visible surface changes: this is the status code and body of a failure path, and no stylesheet or component is touched.

pr:1552.body:
Closes #1543

## What changes

A workspace file whose current provenance revision has no `contentHash` has no address a preview could name: its size is booked in `unpinnedObjectBytes`, and the export hashes it while it copies. But `needed` collected every `record.workspace.map((file) => file.objectPath)`, so `""` entered the CAS work set, `cas.storedSize("")` threw, and the catch recorded

```
cas::unavailable source object
```

— a limitation the dialog renders verbatim (`apps/web/src/research-package/ResearchPackageActions.tsx:345`), five entries for a package that declares four, and the extra one names an internal concept with an empty address.

`needed` now skips an entry that has no address, with the reason in a comment beside it. Nothing else moves: the file still counts once towards the estimate through `unpinnedObjectBytes`, and the export still writes it with a real address and lists it in the inventory. The two `cas:`-pushing sites (`research-snapshots.ts:468` for a streamed export, `:874` in the sizing loop) are both fed from that set, so the filter covers both.

## The assertion the issue asks for

The new test builds a Session with exactly one hash-less workspace file, then previews and exports it:

- the preview's limitations **equal in number** the export's `omissions` — this is the “预览 5 条 = 实际 4 条” difference in the report;
- no limitation starts with `cas:`;
- the file's size is still in `unpinnedObjectBytes`, so the estimate did not lose bytes;
- the export still carries the file, addressed with a 64-hex `objectPath`.

Without the fix the same test shows the issue's line verbatim —
`cas::unavailable source object` — and with it the preview and the export agree.

## What I ran

- `node --import tsx --test src/research-package-preview-omissions.test.ts` (new) — **1/1 pass**.
- Mutation: putting `record.workspace.map((file) => file.objectPath)` back turns it red with the reported line; restoring the fix is green.
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` and `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api typecheck` — both clean.
- `changed-path-check` — `research-snapshots.ts` is an existing file, so the policy reports it as a warning rather than a blocking “added source has no test mapping”.

## Scope

Backend only; no client change and no visual change, so no frames. `#1521` merged as `c06ce8bc` before this branch was cut, which is the file this one touches.

pr:168.body:
This PR adds an opt-in, user-perspective JiuwenSwarm → `antibody-design` Skill → Ascend NPU journey, alongside the lower-level mocked NPU binding test. It depends on Skill backport PR #159; duplicate Skill PR #167 was closed.

## User journey

A fresh Project/Session is created with a live model and selected 131 Runner. The driver uploads the user's two PDBs and sends a high-level request through the public Session Runs API. It does not invoke any model script, choose a Python environment, or preseed model assets. The real Agent must load the Skill, inspect/select a managed environment, push inputs, perform first-use preparation and validation, run RFdiffusion → ProteinMPNN → Protenix → screening on NPU, pull results, declare report/CSV/CIF Artifacts, and explain the result. The test observes automatic wake Runs, committed execution receipts, nonempty remote and local stage files, completed transfers, and final Artifacts. It never resubmits an accepted user Run; a pipeline retry is accepted only after the preceding execution has a confirmed, committed failure. Any `unknown`/unconfirmed execution fails the test.

The real case is tagged `npu:required`, `model:real`, `status:external`, collected but deselected by ordinary PR CI until gated NPU hardware exists. The mocked binding/ST case remains for CI.

## Real-hardware verification (2026-09-24)

- **Full-Agent E2E: PASS (1/1)** on a fresh Project `9df41ef6-e2ea-4096-8e3a-6f8f5783e546`, Session `fb3dbdac-e218-40d5-a50c-565167421e4e`, initial user Run `a62cd447-a1e6-4570-8ddc-de3937edb97d`. The Agent loaded `antibody-design` itself, selected a managed environment, pushed inputs, and completed first-use preparation `74864a72-89e7-475d-af6e-ebf34495deaf` and validation with committed zero-exit receipts. One NPU pipeline Execution `a91eb590-1457-491a-977e-be73e98ba73c` finished `completed / committed / exitCode=0` on the selected remote Runner. RFdiffusion, ProteinMPNN, Protenix, and screening each produced files. Report, CSV, and CIF were transferred to the Session, declared as Artifacts, and explained by the Agent across the original and an automatic wake Run.
- The full live submission used the test driver at `9afed0fa`; the final `ae556055` driver passed by **read-only observation of the same Run**, after fixing a test-only assertion that had incorrectly required three `declare_artifact` tool calls even though the Agent legitimately declares multiple Artifacts in one call. No extra NPU job was submitted for that verification. The final Agent response also names the report, CSV, and CIF. The WSL product source snapshot was labelled `89a3ac7c` and included the Skill backport.
- Earlier fresh full-Agent Run `8d3814fa-f681-4957-a647-a55c81ac06e8` is **not a pass**: first-use preparation `4eb49ef9-8c60-4708-8996-9db8fec44500` became `unknown/unconfirmed` after `fetch failed`. A first pipeline attempt then had a confirmed Runner workspace-snapshot `ENOENT` on a transient MindScience `__pycache__` file; the Agent recovered and its later NPU pipeline/output delivery succeeded, but the preparation receipt remained unconfirmed. This is a real stability risk to address separately, not a result hidden by the passing rerun.
- The older prepared-environment NPU Run `c1ba1acc-2968-417f-8714-7947ee3e1b32` is lower-level evidence only, not the full-Agent E2E result.
- `node --check`, CI contract, E2E metadata (0 errors, 11 pre-existing legacy warnings), and diff whitespace checks passed locally. The previous CI run had ST, UT, Docker, both binary builds and CLA passing; the latest push starts a fresh CI run, so its final state is not yet claimed. The hardware case is intentionally deselected in CI.

## Release

Release category: `release:internal`
User impact: no runtime code change; adds regression coverage for the complete Agent-to-NPU workflow.
Compatibility: merge Skill backport PR #159 before this PR.

pr:196.body:
Users who route through Requesty currently have to set it up as a custom OpenAI compatible provider by hand. This adds it as a built-in preset alongside OpenRouter, with the same shape: OpenAI chat completions, `GET /models` discovery, and a models.dev mapping for catalog facts and prices.

## Preset
`packages/schema/src/model-provider-presets.ts` gets a `requesty` entry right after OpenRouter: base URL `https://router.requesty.ai/v1`, `apiVariant: "openai"`, `modelDiscovery: "openai-models"`, docs `https://docs.requesty.ai`, key page `https://app.requesty.ai/api-keys`. `ModelProviderPresetId` in `model-provider.ts` gains `"requesty"`. The wizard and settings UI read the preset list, so nothing else changes there. Requesty is not made a default anywhere.

## models.dev mapping
models.dev publishes a `requesty` provider whose `api` is `https://router.requesty.ai/v1`, so the host check in `pricesApplyToPreset` accepts its prices for this preset. It is mapped after OpenRouter, in the aggregator block, so first publish wins still hands capability facts to the vendor listings. The ordering test in `packages/model/src/models-dev.test.ts` now counts `requesty` as an aggregator so a misplaced insert would fail it.

## How to test
Pick Requesty in the connect wizard, paste a key from https://app.requesty.ai/api-keys, and choose a listed model such as `openai/gpt-4o-mini` or `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5`. For EU routing, edit the base URL to `https://router.eu.requesty.ai/v1`.

## Validation
Run on macOS arm64 at ae150eb, with deps installed only for `@sciencediscovery/model` and its workspace dependencies.
- `pnpm typecheck` in `packages/schema` and `packages/model`: clean.
- `node scripts/check-architecture.mjs`: OK, 276 package source files checked.
- Package unit tests with `node --test "src/**/*.test.ts"`: schema 12 passed / 0 failed, model 45 passed / 0 failed (including "every aggregator mapping sits after every vendor mapping"). These files are tagged `os:linux`, so on macOS I ran them with `process.platform` reported as linux; nothing else was changed.
- Live check through the package's own code: `listProviderModels` with the preset's `baseUrl` and discovery strategy returned 762 models including `openai/gpt-4o-mini`, and `streamModelTurn` with the preset's protocol and variant streamed a reply from `openai/gpt-4o-mini` with usage reported.
- Not run: `pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, `pnpm ci:e2e` and `apps/web` tests. The UT and E2E layers need a bubblewrap sandbox on Linux, which this macOS host does not have.

## E2E user journeys
BLOCKED on this host (no Linux sandbox for the local stack). The change adds one entry to a list the connect wizard already renders, and the live check above covers the provider's discovery and chat path. Happy to add or rerun a journey if you want one for this.

## Release
Release category: release:feature (label pending a maintainer, I cannot apply labels)
User impact: Requesty appears as a provider preset in the model connect wizard.
Compatibility and migration: none.

Disclosure: I work at Requesty. Happy to adjust anything to match project conventions.

pr:261.body:
Closes #260. `E2E_SWARM_TASK` was a test-only declaration: `.ci/run-e2e.sh` exported it for the JiuwenSwarm backend and twelve specs gated on it. It verified nothing, was always `1` in CI, and made DRB, TC-E2E-01 and BiomniBench report BLOCKED on the native loop, although that loop delegates sub-agents through the platform `task` tool as well. The stack now says how it runs agent turns, and the journeys check that instead.

## `/health` reports how agent turns run

`services/api/src/http/index.ts`: `/health` and `/api/health` include `agent: { executor, subagents }`, taken from the same `jiuwenSwarmConfigFromEnv()` result the API uses to start agent turns. `executor` is `jiuwenswarm` or `native`; `subagents` is `task` or `jiuwenswarm`, and always `task` on the native loop. This lives in the API rather than the adapter's `/agent/info` because the API decides delegation in both modes, and a native stack has no adapter. The adapter forwards `/health` to the API, so a JiuwenSwarm stack answers the same way.

The L1 contract baseline (`test/contract/baselines/legacy-linux.json`) records `/health` bodies and will show the added `agent` key on a manual `--compare`. The baseline is not regenerated here: its README reserves that to a human review, and the comparison is not part of any CI layer.

## Journeys check the stack instead of a variable

`test/helpers/e2e.ts` adds `requireAgentStack()`. It reads `/health` and fails as BLOCKED, quoting what the stack reported, when sub-agents are not delegated through `task`. With `{ executor: "jiuwenswarm" }` it also requires that executor.

`E2E_SWARM_TASK` is removed from `.ci/run-e2e.sh`, the specs, `jiuwen_swarm/README.md`, `jiuwen_swarm/tests/README.md` and the three benchmark READMEs. `git grep E2E_SWARM_TASK` finds nothing.

**PASS** on `9f8fcc6a`, local isolated stack with the JiuwenSwarm backend. The research batch (20/20) contains every Swarm-gated mocked journey: each one now passes its precondition by reading the stack's `/health` through the adapter, with no `E2E_SWARM_TASK` set anywhere. The standard (44/44) and literature (6/6) batches also passed.

The real research journeys (DRB, TC-E2E-01, BiomniBench) cannot run on a pull request. Their gate now accepts either executor as long as sub-agents use platform `task` delegation, which is what a native Nightly needs. Their next run will show it.

## Summary

Make provider token accounting a diagnostic instead of a real-E2E pass criterion, and keep the usage shapes it depends on pinned by deterministic tests. Functional task/delivery/quality assertions are unchanged.

## Rebased onto `main` (2026-11-07, `b9e5367`)

The branch had been open since 2026-10-14 and was 699 commits behind; it conflicted in three files. After the rebase:

- **The protocol-aware parser is no longer part of this diff.** `normalizeUsage` moved to `packages/model/src/usage.ts` on `main` and already takes the request's dialect, reading `prompt_tokens`/`completion_tokens` for Chat Completions and `input_tokens`/`output_tokens` for Responses ahead of the aliases, with a conflict diagnostic. The reported bug - a probe returning `completion_tokens: 31` next to an extra `output_tokens: 0`, which the shared normalizer used to prefer - is already fixed there, so `packages/model/src/client.ts` is untouched by this PR.
- **One design choice from the original branch was not carried over.** The original parser dropped the fallback to the other dialect's fields and to `total_tokens` arithmetic entirely. `main`'s version keeps a dialect-first-then-fallback design and documents it; overriding that here would be a behaviour change on shared accounting that the maintainers already settled. The assertions that encoded the stricter rule were dropped with it rather than left failing.
- What is left is this PR's other half plus its regression coverage: the documented CI policy, the journey that stops gating on usage, and the mixed/missing-accounting cases exercised end to end.

- `.ci/README.md` - provider usage is diagnostic evidence, not an E2E success or scoring gate; missing accounting is not evidence of zero cost; protocol parsing correctness stays enforced by deterministic tests.
