## Summary

Both long-running engines — the evolution search and the Idea Tree — can be **started** from the command line but cannot be **observed, controlled, or stopped** from it. Their progress is designed to land on a frontend card, so a terminal user gets a run id and then nothing. I would like `evolve` and `idea` subcommands that reuse the HTTP endpoints the Web UI already calls.

## What happens today

Starting works. `ScienceDiscovery run "/evolve-design --algorithm puct …"` reaches the same control plane as the browser, the agent loads the `evolve-design` skill, and it calls `create_evolve_run`. Then the turn ends — deliberately. The tool's own result text instructs the model:

> The search runs for minutes to hours and its card streams live progress on its own — do not wait for it here, and do not poll `get_evolve_run`.

`create_idea_research` says the same thing:

> After success, report the handoff and end this turn; the existing tree card streams progress. Do not poll or start another research to wait for completion.

That is the right call for the agent loop — polling would burn the budget the search itself needs. But it means **the card is the only progress surface**, and the CLI has no equivalent. `ScienceDiscovery run` prints `Search created: <uuid>` and exits while the search keeps running server-side for hours.

`services/launcher/src/cli-options.ts` has no evolve or idea-tree subcommand and no related flag. So from a terminal today you cannot:

- list the searches or researches that exist;
- see how far one has got;
- fetch a candidate;
- stop one, or pause and resume it.

The only workaround is starting another `run` in the same session and hoping the model calls `get_evolve_run` / `get_idea_research` — a whole model turn spent reading a status field, using tools whose descriptions explicitly tell the model not to poll them.

## The endpoints already exist

The Web UI drives all of this over plain HTTP:

**Evolve**
- `GET /api/evolve/runs`
- `GET /api/evolve/runs/<id>/events?after=<cursor>`
- `GET /api/evolve/runs/<id>/candidates/<codeHash>`
- `POST /api/evolve/runs/<id>/stop`

**Idea Tree**
- `GET /api/sessions/<sid>/idea-tree/research`
- `POST /api/sessions/<sid>/idea-tree/research` — `pause`, `continue`, `stop`, `defaults`
- `GET /api/sessions/<sid>/idea-tree/research/<rid>/events`
- `GET /api/sessions/<sid>/idea-tree/graph`

## The client plumbing also already exists

`services/launcher/src/control-plane-client.ts` has an authenticated generic `request<T>(path, init)` and `subscribeRunEvents()`, a working SSE consumer that "mirrors the Web frontend's `subscribeRunEvents`: fetch with `accept: text/event-stream`, split frames". The launcher also already resolves the bearer token from the data directory. A `watch` subcommand is that SSE reader pointed at a different path — this is wiring, not new infrastructure.

## Proposal

```
ScienceDiscovery evolve list
ScienceDiscovery evolve get <run-id> [--candidate <hash>]
ScienceDiscovery evolve watch <run-id>
ScienceDiscovery evolve stop <run-id>

ScienceDiscovery idea list --session <id>
ScienceDiscovery idea get <research-id> --session <id>
ScienceDiscovery idea watch <research-id> --session <id>
ScienceDiscovery idea pause|continue|stop <research-id> --session <id>
```

Conventions, matching what `run` already does:

- **text on a TTY, JSONL when piped.** `run` already switches output mode this way; these commands should not invent a second convention.
- **`watch` resumes rather than replays.** The evolve event endpoint already takes `?after=<cursor>`; a dropped connection should continue from the last event seen.
- **Token and data-dir handling identical to `run`** — sharing a `--data-dir` with `serve` should mean no extra configuration.

One asymmetry to decide: evolve exposes only `stop`, while Idea Tree has `pause` / `continue` / `stop`. Either the CLI mirrors each engine's real capabilities, or evolve gains pause/resume — worth an explicit choice rather than an accident.

## Why it matters

- **Unattended and batch use.** Starting a search from a job script is pointless if the same script cannot poll it, stop it when a budget is spent, or collect the winning candidate.
- **Headless and remote machines.** On a workstation reached over SSH there is no browser to hold the card open. Today that machine can start a multi-hour search it cannot then observe.
- **Consistency.** The CLI is already positioned as the scriptable twin of the Web UI; the two most expensive operations in the product are exactly the ones it cannot drive.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Evolve searches and Idea Tree researches can be listed, inspected, watched, and stopped from the CLI.
- [ ] `watch` streams live and resumes from a cursor after a dropped connection.
- [ ] Output follows the existing TTY/pipe convention, so `| jq` works.
- [ ] No new authentication path: the token comes from the data directory as `run` already does.
- [ ] Commands and options appear in `help` and in the CLI reference.
- [ ] Stopping from the CLI has the same effect as stopping from the UI card.

## Open questions

- Should `run` gain an optional `--wait` that blocks until a started engine finishes? Useful in scripts, but these runs last hours — probably better served by `watch`.
- Should `watch` exit non-zero when the run ends in failure, so a script can branch on it?
- Does `evolve list` need session/project scoping, given `GET /api/evolve/runs` is global today?

Related: [#30](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/30) (introduce the CLI in the README) — that issue is about making the CLI discoverable; this one is about the two workflows it cannot reach.
closed_recent.title: [Feature] CLI subcommands for the long-running engines — evolve and Idea Tree

closed_recent.author: hsliuustc0106
closed_recent.body:
## Context

Since July 2026 an open-source "science workbench" category has formed, triggered by Anthropic's Claude Science launch (2026-06-30). Three direct open-source alternatives appeared the same week and are now at scale: [synthetic-sci/openscience](https://github.com/synthetic-sciences/openscience) (~3.6K★), [aipoch/open-science](https://github.com/aipoch/open-science) (~4.2K★), and [ai4s-research/open-science](https://github.com/ai4s-research/open-science) (~1.7K★). Having compared ScienceDiscovery against them (and against the autonomous-scientist systems: Sakana AI-Scientist, InternScience/InternAgent + MLEvolve), here is a strengths/gaps assessment in the hope it helps prioritization. Facts below are from public repo data collected 2026-09-15.

## Strengths (keep — and communicate)

1. **Sandbox-first security model.** Fail-closed Bubblewrap/Seatbelt execution, operator-scoped NPU chip passthrough, opt-in Broker with fixed entry points and `shell: false`. None of the three competitors communicates a default-isolation story; the highest-engagement technical question on a competitor's launch thread was literally *"are the skills executed within a secure, containerized sandbox by default, or does the user manage isolation?"* — this repo already answers that question, but almost nobody knows it does.
2. **Provenance depth.** CAS with pinned-asset drift rejection, review checks, cross-session/SubAgent citation chains. The strongest provenance story in the category.
3. **Search-camp RSI engine.** The evolve sidecar (flat-PUCT tree + OpenEvolve MAP-Elites, discriminability probe, explicit "no model training, no search-rule modification") is a clean, honest scope with a real cousin in [InternScience/MLEvolve](https://github.com/InternScience/MLEvolve) (#1 on MLE-Bench).
4. **Ascend NPU path.** 910B sandbox passthrough + allowlisted workloads (Protenix/MindScience) is unique in the category and extends machine-verifiable research to device-scale workloads.
5. **Engineering discipline beyond repo age.** Bilingual doc set, CI tiers (UT/ST/mocked E2E), self-documented limitations (e.g., Idea Tree scores are model judgments, not experimental evidence).

## Gaps (ordered by leverage)

1. **Installation/onboarding.** No binaries in Releases — #1 (open since 08-19, rated 1/5) is the only organic user feedback this repo has received, and it is someone who *could not install the product*. All three competitors ship desktop installers and a <10-minute quickstart. This pairs directly with the first-experience goal in #22.
2. **No community surface.** All merged PRs are bots; there are zero human external PRs. For comparison: aipoch merges 6+ human PRs/day; ai4s-research power users file bugs *and* land the fixes (e.g., their stall-guard for looping agents came from a user). A "good first issue" ladder + a contributor guide + weekly maintainer RFC triage would start the flywheel.
3. **Category invisibility + an unverifiable benchmark claim.** 58★ vs 1.7–4.2K for peers; one promotion event found (Sina Finance 2026-08-16) whose headline claim (BiomniBench-DA "业界SOTA") is dual-claimed by aipoch's README badge on the same benchmark. Without published methodology/splits, the claim reads as marketing and hurts credibility with scientists — either publish the eval or drop the superlative.
4. **Adoption levers validated by competitors, still missing here:** headless CLI / task API (repeated cross-repo demand — researchers want CI and agent-to-agent use, not only a GUI), model-provider onboarding (subscription reuse, connectivity-test friction), Windows parity.
5. **Cross-model skill consistency.** The single most-validated complaint in the category: *"one flag switches the model, not whether the skill actually works"* (prompts tuned on one model degrade on smaller/local models). A per-skill model-compatibility matrix or a cross-model smoke-test suite for the 300+ skills would directly differentiate.

## Suggested next steps

- [ ] Ship Linux binaries + a 10-minute quickstart (pairs with #22)
- [ ] Publish evolve/idea-tree efficiency metrics (per-node token cost, CAS reuse rate, surviving-node quality on an independent benchmark) — the pruning+reuse efficiency story is genuinely differentiating and no competitor tells it
- [ ] Benchmark-claim triage: methodology for BiomniBench-DA or remove the SOTA wording
- [ ] Community ladder: CONTRIBUTING good-first-issues + a maintainer-reserved RFC-triage day

Happy to help flesh any of these out.
closed_recent.title: [Feedback] Strengths and gaps vs. the 2026 open-source science-workbench landscape

closed_recent.author: HugoXK
closed_recent.body:
Follow-up to #245, criterion 3. PR #617 delivers the measurement harness and the per-request wire diagnostics, but the real relay-vs-direct measurement is **not** delivered: the team's bot host has no relay or model endpoint credentials.

## What is missing

Criterion 3 of #245 asks for a comparison of a relay endpoint against a direct endpoint with the same model alias, the same request body bytes, the same workload and the same concurrency, with wire latency reported separately from agent duration and token counts. The harness exists (`scripts/model-endpoint-compare.mjs`, delivered in #617 and covered by `scripts/model-endpoint-compare.test.mjs` against local stub endpoints). What does not exist is a run against real endpoints, so #245 stays open as partially delivered.

## Who can run it

Someone on an owner-hosted machine that has both endpoint URLs and their credentials. The team's bot host cannot: it has no model credentials, and this is not a code problem.

## Command (fill the placeholders)

```bash
node scripts/model-endpoint-compare.mjs \
  --model <model-alias> \
  --prompt-file <one-prompt.txt> \
  --a-name relay  --a-base-url <relay-base-url>  --a-token-env A_TOKEN \
  --b-name direct --b-base-url <direct-base-url> --b-token-env B_TOKEN \
  --requests 20 --concurrency 2 --timeout-ms 300000 \
  --out compare.json
```

`--body-file <identical-body.json>` may be used instead of `--prompt-file` when the exact request body must be reused. The script refuses two different model aliases and refuses a workload where the two bodies would differ, so a latency delta cannot come from a body change.

## What to do with the result

Paste the comparison table the script prints (p50/p90/p95 per endpoint, failures, tokens) and attach or link `compare.json` in #245. That closes criterion 3.

## Notes

- Endpoint tokens are read from the environment variables named by `--a-token-env` / `--b-token-env`; they are never written into the report.
- No repository change is expected from this issue: it is a measurement task, not a code task.

Related: #245, #617.
closed_recent.title: [Follow-up] Measure relay vs direct model latency on an owner-hosted endpoint (#245 criterion 3)

Follow-up to #617. This issue tracks **only** the CI packaging that #617 currently carries; it does not re-open the product fix in that PR.

## Trigger

Do not implement this until the maintainers answer the CI-contract question on #617 (comment `6463813036`):

- **A — accept as written**: the packaging stays in #617; close this issue with that reason and make no pipeline change.
- **B — split (our preference)**: #617 is reduced to the product fix, and one PR implements this issue.

If the answer is A, this issue is closed rather than implemented.

## Scope (only if B)

- `real-e2e.yml`: the always-run `Summarize model wire diagnostics` step and the `model-wire-summary.json` staging.
- `.ci/model-wire-summary.mjs` and its test; `prepare-real-e2e-results.mjs` staging; the `real-report.mjs` report section; `.ci/README.md`; the `ci-contract.test.mjs` expectation bump.

Out of scope: the empty-terminal-turn product fix and the wire-diagnostics fields (they stay in #617), and the relay-vs-direct measurement (criterion 3 of #245, tracked in #618).

## Merge condition

A test must exercise the real parse path: feed `[model-sse-summary]` lines as the emitters actually write them through the aggregation and staging path, and assert the resulting document. Hand-built records are not acceptance for that script.

## Context

The packaging is additive evidence — it reports model-wire failures next to research outcomes and does not add a second pass/fail gate. Splitting it keeps a default-branch pipeline change out of a behaviour fix and removes the "contract test edited to expect the change it guards" objection.

## Problem

#494 adds `scripts/lib/venv-launchers.mjs` (trampoline replace + runtime DLL copy) with portable unit tests, but:

1. Nothing in-tree calls `replaceVenvTrampolines` / `copyVenvRuntimeDlls` (`assemble-backend.mjs` / bootstrap not present yet).
2. Comments claim a closed loop with `fixVenvHome`, but that helper does not exist — after swapping the launcher, `pyvenv.cfg` `home` can still point at the build machine, so the real `python.exe` still fails off-machine.
3. Tests only compare bytes; they do not spawn `Scripts\python.exe`, so the field failures (entity not found / `0xC0000135`) are not covered.

## Expected

- Call sites in assemble-backend (pack-time) and bootstrap (first-run repair) invoke the module.
- `fixVenvHome` (or equivalent) rewrites `pyvenv.cfg` `home` to the bundled interpreter root.
- A Windows smoke test builds a uv venv, relocates it, spawns `Scripts\python.exe -c "..."`, and asserts exit 0 with `sys.prefix` at the new path.

## Verification cases

### Case 1 — pack-time wiring
- **Preconditions:** Payload contains a uv-created venv whose `Scripts\python.exe` is a trampoline; assemble-backend runs.
- **Steps:** Inspect `Scripts\python.exe` and `pyvenv.cfg` after assemble.
- **Expected / pass:** Launcher is a real CPython stub (no `uv trampoline` marker); `home` points at the bundled python root; runtime DLLs sit beside the launcher.

### Case 2 — first-run bootstrap repair
- **Preconditions:** `dataDir\envs` still has pre-fix trampolines (reinstall with valid unpack stamp).
- **Steps:** Start the shell once on a clean machine without system Python.
- **Expected / pass:** Bootstrap replaces trampolines, copies DLLs, fixes `home`; each venv `python.exe -c "import sys; print(sys.prefix)"` exits 0.

### Case 3 — Windows spawn smoke (CI or labeled job)
- **Preconditions:** `os:windows` (or equivalent) test runner with a bundled/minimal CPython + uv.
- **Steps:** Create uv venv → move tree → `spawn(Scripts/python.exe, ["-c", "import sys; print(sys.prefix)"])`.
- **Expected / pass:** Exit code 0; printed prefix equals the relocated venv path. Byte-only unit tests alone do not satisfy this case.

## Context

Refs #494, #493. Non-blocking Follow-up from HongyeZhou review of shell.04. #494 should use `Refs #493` until this loop lands (or fold wiring into the same PR).

## Problem

`win-desktop-client/` is an independent pnpm workspace (not listed in the root `pnpm-workspace.yaml` packages: `config / apps/* / services/* / packages/*`). Architecture checks and `tsconfig.tests.json` also skip it. As a result, install / typecheck / unit-test failures under this tree are invisible to GitHub Actions (see #486: missing patch and empty `tsconfig` include were only found by local runs).

## Expected

A CI job (or matrix entry) runs on changes under `win-desktop-client/**` and exercises at least:

- `pnpm install` (lockfile present)
- `pnpm typecheck` (when sources exist)
- `pnpm test` for portable Node tests

## Verification cases

### Case 1 — install gate
- **Preconditions:** PR that only touches `win-desktop-client/` and references a missing `patchedDependencies` file (or otherwise breaks install).
- **Steps:** Open the PR; wait for CI.
- **Expected / pass:** The new job fails with a clear install error; root jobs that ignore this tree may still be green.

### Case 2 — typecheck / test gate
- **Preconditions:** PR adds a TypeScript error under `win-desktop-client/src/` or a failing `test/*.test.ts`.
- **Steps:** Open the PR; wait for CI.
- **Expected / pass:** typecheck or test step fails; merge is blocked by the required check once wired.

### Case 3 — no-op on unrelated paths
- **Preconditions:** PR only changes `apps/web/` (or another root package).
- **Steps:** Open the PR.
- **Expected / pass:** The win-desktop-client job is skipped or stays green without installing Electron unnecessarily.

## Context

Refs #486, #485. Non-blocking Follow-up from HongyeZhou review of shell.01.

closed_recent.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary.** In `设置 › 沙箱网络`, pressing `开放网络` (Open network) does nothing: no confirmation dialog, no mode change, no disabled state and no explanation. The mode stays on `无网络` even with a real mouse click.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Open `设置` → `沙箱网络` (`Settings › Sandbox network`).
2. Press `开放网络`.

**Observed** (`9da58ad6`, two scripts, one programmatic and one real mouse click at the button's centre)

```text
before: buttons = [无网络(active), 域名白名单, 开放网络, 保存]
after : buttons = [无网络(active), 域名白名单, 开放网络, 保存]
        .settings-modal text = NONE
        whitelist textarea disabled = true
```

Neither path produces the confirmation described in the documentation of this setting ("开放网络意味着沙箱里的任何代码都能访问任意地址，只保留私网过滤。确定要这样吗？"), and the active mode never moves. On `bbdbdd5` (2026-11-22) the same step did open that confirmation and, once confirmed, `开放网络` became active — so this is a regression on the current main.

**Expected.** Pressing `开放网络` opens the confirmation; cancelling leaves the mode unchanged; confirming makes it active. If network mode changes are not allowed in this configuration, the button is disabled and says why.

**Impact**

- The mode cannot be changed from the UI at all, while `无网络` stays active: anyone who needs outbound access in the sandbox has no path, and nothing says whether the click was rejected or ignored.
- Because there is no visible state change, a user cannot tell a failed click from a rejected policy, and there is no error to report.
- It also silently removes a confirmation step that used to exist, which is the opposite of what a safety-relevant switch should do.

**Suggested fix.** Restore the confirmation flow; make the control reflect its actual availability (disabled + reason when it cannot switch), and never accept a click that changes nothing.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- ScienceDiscovery desktop client, viewport 1500x950, `zh-CN`.
- Linux (Ubuntu 22.04.5); API `127.0.0.1:4410`, runner `127.0.0.1:4411`, Chromium 1228 via Playwright; sandbox backend `bwrap`.
- Regression window: `bbdbdd5c` (works) → `9da58ad6` (does nothing).

### Additional Information

- Screenshot after the real mouse click is in the comment below (模式仍是「无网络」, no dialog).
- The same page's `域名白名单` + `保存` path does respond (empty whitelist → 「至少填写一个允许的域名。」), so only the `开放网络` control is inert.

### Version Information

- `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` @ `9da58ad619f972e44eb674c5d4cc9118813f7222` (main, 2026-11-24).

closed_recent.author: agent-ci-infra-bot[bot]
closed_recent.body:
Run: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/45212568993 (Nightly #105, attempt 1, `workflow_dispatch`, profile `daily`, backend `jiuwenswarm`)

Head SHA: `9da58ad619f972e44eb674c5d4cc9118813f7222`

## Summary

Two independent external causes made this nightly red. Neither is a product defect, but one of them is recorded wrongly, and the recovery path the run needs does not exist in the failed-jobs rerun.

| Job | Result | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Gate / L4/L5 real E2E / Real E2E (research-11)` | failure | external: model gateway answered 502 / `read ECONNRESET` on both attempts |
| `Gate / L4/L5 real E2E / Account for real cases` | failure | downstream accounting: `- research-11: SHARD_FAILED` |
| `Gate / merge-gate` | failure | downstream: `CI gate failed: real-scheduled: failure; macos-desktop: abandoned` |
| `Report the outcome` | failure | downstream: `RESULT: abandoned` |
| `Gate / macOS desktop installer (arm64)` | cancelled | external: no macOS runner was ever assigned; no step ran |

Everything else passed on this SHA: L1, UT, ST, Docker, both binary releases, the Windows installer, Coverage, all five mocked workers (`Planned 189; executed 189; passed 189`) and 13 of the 14 real workers, so `Account for real cases` counted `Planned 22; executed 22; passed 21`.

## 1. research-11: a provider outage is scored as the product's failure

Job https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/45212568993/job/137825635928, step `Run the frozen real E2E shard`.

The frozen shard held one identity, `test/journey-idea-tree-real.spec.ts › Idea Tree real research › real Idea Tree research completes and its result survives a reload` (plan digest `cc111227c7d7`). First attempt:

```
18:22:32.4688386Z   Error: research settled as "interrupted": Model HTTP 502: {"error":"Model stream failed after response headers: read ECONNRESET"}
18:22:34.0581408Z   ✘  1 [real] › ../test/journey-idea-tree-real.spec.ts:26:3 › … (2.9m)
```

The harness retried the case once in the same job (`18:22:36.7162821Z Repeating 1 failed case(s): …`) and got the identical gateway answer:

```
18:28:46.9978838Z   Error: research settled as "interrupted": Model HTTP 502: {"error":"Model stream failed after response headers: read ECONNRESET"}
18:28:48.8493928Z   ✘  1 [real] › ../test/journey-idea-tree-real.spec.ts:26:3 › … (5.8m)
```

The shard summary then recorded no provider fault at all:

```
| e2e-real | `cc111227c7d7` | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 |   (planned/executed/passed/passed-after-retry/failed/provider faults/skipped)
- e2e-real: PROVIDER_FAULT_RETRY_FAILED: 1
- e2e-real: PLAYWRIGHT_WORKER_FAILED: 1
- e2e-real: FAIL: playwright:test/journey-idea-tree-real.spec.ts::…/Idea%20Tree%20real%20research/…@linux/amd64/jiuwenswarm
```

That is the gateway's own 502 body, not a product verdict, but the harness files it as `FAIL` with `provider faults 0`, and `Account for real cases` repeats it that way (`- FAIL: playwright:test/journey-idea-tree-real.spec.ts::…`). The classifier only recognises a gateway fault when the text carries the gateway's own vocabulary (`181001`, `model call failed`, `openai api`, `chat/completions`) — see `GATEWAY_CONTEXT` in `test/support/tagged/provider-fault.mjs`. Idea Tree's transport raises its own wording instead, `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/vendor/idea_tree/research.py:250`:

```python
raise RuntimeError(f"Model HTTP {error.code}: {detail}") from error
```

which matches no gateway context, so the fault is dropped. Reproduced at this SHA against the exact recorded message:

```
$ node --input-type=module -e '
import { detectProviderFaultFromErrors } from "./test/support/tagged/provider-fault.mjs";
const msg = `research settled as "interrupted": Model HTTP 502: {"error":"Model stream failed after response headers: read ECONNRESET"}

expect(received).toBe(expected) // Object.is equality

Expected: "completed"
Received: "interrupted"`;
console.log("observed  =>", JSON.stringify(detectProviderFaultFromErrors([msg])));
console.log("181001    =>", JSON.stringify(detectProviderFaultFromErrors([msg.replace("Model HTTP 502", "[181001] model call failed, Model HTTP 502")])));
'
observed  => null
181001    => {"code":"provider-transport","status":null}
```

So the same text is a `provider-transport` fault once the gateway's `181001 model call failed` wording is present, and the product's failure when Idea Tree is the one reporting it. `.ci/provider-fault.test.mjs` pins only the gateway vocabulary (`GATEWAY_500`, `GATEWAY_503`), so nothing covers this second reporter.

That matters beyond cosmetics: the failure is attributed to the product in the run summary and in this report's own accounting, while #1238 (the same class of outage, reported by the gateway itself) was classified `external` / `PROVIDER_FAULT`. The product did retry — `research.py` retries 429/5xx up to `MAX_ATTEMPTS = 2` with ≤4 s backoff before raising — and the shard retried the whole case once, so the fault was seen three times over ~10 minutes.

Transient or not: the gateway was healthy again immediately afterwards on the same endpoint. `Real E2E (research-12)` ran 18:29:28–18:32:55 and `Real E2E (research-13)` ran 18:33:27–19:04:23, and both passed, so this is not a configuration or product problem for this SHA.

## 2. macOS desktop installer (arm64): the runner was never assigned

Job https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/45212568993/job/137825643357 (`needs: [policy, l1]`, both succeeded at 16:06:41Z), label `macos-15`.

```
$ gh api /repos/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/jobs/137825643357
{"completed_at":"2026-11-23T16:21:43Z","conclusion":"cancelled","created_at":"2026-11-23T16:06:41Z",
 "labels":["macos-15"],"name":"Gate / macOS desktop installer (arm64)","runner_id":0,"runner_name":"",
 "started_at":"2026-11-23T16:06:41Z","status":"completed","steps":[]}
```

No step ever started, no runner was assigned (`runner_id: 0`), and nothing in the repository can explain it: the same job on the previous run's runner was healthy (`45073284028`, `macos-15`, 18 steps, success 21:40–22:02Z), the workflow's `timeout-minutes: 120` does not apply while queued, and GitHub recorded no incident on 2026-11-23 (`https://www.githubstatus.com/api/v2/incidents.json` has no entry that day). The `needs` context inside `merge-gate` reports the job as `abandoned`, and `tier-policy.mjs gate` correctly refuses to treat that as a pass.

The recovery gap is that a cancelled job is not a failed job. `merge-gate` raised:

```
Error: CI gate failed: real-scheduled: failure; macos-desktop: abandoned
```

and the only offered bulk operation, `POST /actions/runs/45212568993/rerun-failed-jobs`, is documented as "re-run all of the failed jobs and their dependent jobs" — nothing in it recreates a job that never started, so `macos-desktop` would still be `abandoned` in the rerun's `needs` and the gate would fail again with the same message. The specific-job endpoint (`POST /actions/jobs/137825643357/rerun`) is the only thing that can re-run that job, and even that alone cannot pass the gate while `real-scheduled` is still a failure from attempt 1 — recovering this run needs both, or a fresh run.

## 3. Downstream jobs fail as designed

- `Account for real cases` (job 137939547826): `### Real E2E: FAIL`, `Planned 22; executed 22; passed 21; provider faults 0`, `- research-11: SHARD_FAILED`. It runs no model call; it reconciled 14 shard artifacts, including `real-e2e-results-research-11`, and the missing pass is real evidence, not an accounting bug.
- `merge-gate` (job 137939753365): declared `"real-scheduled": {"result": "failure"}` and `"macos-desktop": {"result": "abandoned"}` itself, so the gate message names its own inputs.
- `Report the outcome` (job 137939983308): `RESULT: abandoned` fails the `[[ "${RESULT}" == "success" ]]` step. Expected: "a skipped or cancelled gate is not a pass either".

## What was checked / how a rerun behaves here

- All five job records of this run through `/actions/runs/45212568993/jobs` and each failed job's own log; the `needs` JSON printed by `merge-gate`; the accounting output of `Account for real cases`.
- Whether a failed-jobs rerun re-uses attempt-1 artifacts: it does. In run 45073284028 attempt 2 the identical four jobs were re-run after `Real E2E (research-8)` failed and the run went green, consuming the other shards' attempt-1 artifacts, and re-uploading the same artifact names (`real-e2e-results`, `e2e-results`, `real-e2e-verdict`, `case-execution-details.md`) produced a second artifact per name rather than a conflict.
- Why no failed-jobs rerun was made here: every failed job is downstream of one of the two external causes above, but the resulting rerun cannot turn the run green, for the reason in section 2. A rerun would spend another paid research-11 shard to reproduce a red `macos-desktop` gate. A full re-run (`POST /actions/runs/45212568993/rerun`) or a fresh `Nightly` dispatch re-runs ~14 real workers and ~2 h of gate time, and is a scheduling decision for the repository, not a repair.

## Related work

- #1238 — same class of gateway fault (stream reset mid-answer), but reported by the gateway, so it was classified `external`/`PROVIDER_FAULT`. That is the attribution this run did not get.
- #1239 — an earlier research-11 nightly report; different root cause (managed Python base setup `failed`, case `BLOCKED`, nothing executed). This run executed the case and lost it at the gateway.
- #1327 — Idea Tree ends the whole research as `interrupted` on one unusable model answer. This run's `interrupted` came from a transport 502, not from answer validation, so it is a different entry into the same terminal state.
- #1339 (open) — isolate tagged case retries. It does not change this outcome: the retry ran, and the provider was still returning 502.
- #813 — the earlier L3 version of "one gateway outage fails the gate"; the accounting and retry handling in this run are the later form of that work.

## What would close this

1. Let the provider-fault classifier recognise Idea Tree's own reporter, e.g. a `Model HTTP <5xx>:` raised by `research.py`'s transport beside the body that follows it, so this outage is reported as `PROVIDER_FAULT` (status 502) instead of `FAIL`, and add a regression case for the exact text above to `.ci/provider-fault.test.mjs`.
2. Decide the recovery route for a distribution job that was never started: the gate must keep failing on it, but "re-run failed jobs" cannot fix it, so the documented remedy has to be a specific-job re-run or a fresh run. A person with Actions write decides which.

Environment: `ubuntu-26.04` hosted runners for the Linux jobs, `macos-15` for the desktop job, Windows runner for the installer; CI Node 22.19.0; profile `daily`, backend `jiuwenswarm`, model `deepseek-flash` through the CI gateway; version stamp `nightly-20261124-9da58ad`.

closed_recent.author: agent-ci-infra-bot[bot]
closed_recent.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched existing Issues and PRs for `UNEXPECTED_SWARM_CHECKS`; nothing tracks this failure (the only hit is merged PR #1361, which introduced the check).
- [x] I reproduced the reconciliation failure locally at `e63099ab` with synthetic mocked artifacts; no E2E stack was started.
- [x] This reports a CI reconciliation regression, not a product failure: all 195 planned mocked cases passed in this run.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

[Dispatch Nightly #113](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/46030598150) (attempt 1, `main @ e63099ab3b0b2bb30e9ecea432ee6be69efcc8a1`, `profile=daily`, `backend=jiuwenswarm`, `CI_E2E_LOCAL_CONCURRENCY=2`) failed **only** in `Gate / merge-gate` (job `140705976460`), step `Reconcile mocked results`:

```
##[group]Run node .ci/mocked-report.mjs .ci-mocked-plan/plan.json .ci-mocked-results .ci-results
### Mocked E2E: FAIL

Planned 195; executed 195; passed 195.

- standard-config: UNEXPECTED_SWARM_CHECKS

##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```

The mocked layer that produced those artifacts was green: `Gate / L2 E2E (mocked, standard-config)` (job `140613911090`) concluded **success** with `| e2e | 58a08ac09c38 | 75 | 75 | 75 | 75 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |` (75/75 passed, 1 passed after retry), and the other four mocked shards were green too. `Report the outcome` (job `140706111813`) then failed with `RESULT: failure` for the same reason. So the failure is purely in result reconciliation.

#### Root cause

1. `test/support/tagged/retry.mjs:14` enables the per-case retry only for the `daily` and `release` profiles, so this run retried one failed journey:

   ```
   Repeating 1 failed case(s): playwright:test/issue-143-proxy-settings.spec.ts::mocked/issue-143-proxy-settings.spec.ts/issue-143-proxy-settings.spec/custom%20URL%20remains%20complete%20after%20refresh%20and%20is%20prefilled%20for%20editing
   ```

2. `test/support/tagged/shared.mjs:487-491` names the retry result directory `<batchKey>-retry`, i.e. `mocked-standard-config-global-retry`, and passes it as the retry's `CI_RESULTS_DIR`. `test/support/tagged/retry-runner.mjs:183` uses it for the isolated `.ci/run-e2e.sh` child (the job log shows the retry worktree `.ci-retry/mocked-standard-config-global-retry`).

3. `test/support/tagged/retry-runner.mjs:25-31` (`batchLaunchConfig`) reuses the failed case's batch launch config, including `checks: 'run'` when that batch carries the 9 JiuwenSwarm checks (`test/support/tagged/execution.mjs:177,199` keeps them exclusively on `mocked-standard-config-global`). The retry therefore re-ran the supplemental checks on the retry stack — the job log shows all nine (`history`, `history-names`, `run-shell`, `host-tools`, `approvals`, `skills`, `skill-switch`, `trajectory`, `language`) a second time at `16:22:52Z`-`16:23:25Z`.

4. `.ci/run-e2e.sh:448` writes that evidence to `$CI_RESULTS_DIR/e2e/jiuwenswarm-checks.json`, so the retry produced `mocked-standard-config-global-retry/e2e/jiuwenswarm-checks.json` inside `.ci-results`, which `.github/workflows/ci.yml:688-696` uploads wholesale as the `mocked-e2e-results-standard-config` artifact.

5. `.ci/mocked-report.mjs:36-39` (added by the merged PR #1361, commit `92f40dab9`) audits **every** `mocked-*` sub-directory of a shard artifact and fails with `UNEXPECTED_SWARM_CHECKS` for any of them other than the single designated check batch that contains `e2e/jiuwenswarm-checks.json`. The retry directory is not one of the plan's batches (`mockedBatches()` derives only `-fresh`/`-global`), so the legitimate retry evidence is classified as out-of-bounds.

In short: the audit behaves as written, but the retry path now produces evidence that no accounting consumes and that the audit necessarily rejects. Both halves predate the failure individually; they were only combined when the audit was widened in #1361.

#### Trigger conditions and impact

- Only `daily` (Nightly) and `release` runs can hit it, because only they retry failed cases (`retry.mjs:14`). `pr` and `merge_group` (`merge`) runs never create a `*-retry` directory, so PR CI and the merge queue are unaffected.
- Within a run, it needs a first-attempt failure in the **`mocked-standard-config-global`** batch, i.e. the lane that carries the nine supplemental checks. A retry of `-fresh`, `-global-2`, `standard-journeys`, `research`, `governed` or `literature` runs with `CI_E2E_SWARM_CHECKS=off` and leaves no checks file, so it does not trip the audit today.
- Consequence: a green mocked layer (195/195, as here) is reported as `UNEXPECTED_SWARM_CHECKS`, the whole Nightly/Release gate is red, and the release evidence shows a mocked failure that did not happen.
- Secondary cost of the same defect: the retry re-runs nine live JiuwenSwarm checks (about 45 s of extra stack work), and any spurious check failure on that second stack turns into `PROVIDER_FAULT_RETRY_FAILED`, a flakiness source unrelated to the one case being retried.

### Verification performed

- Read the failing job log (`Reconcile mocked results`, `Report the outcome`), the green mocked job log (`Repeating 1 failed case(s)` at `16:20:52Z`, the retry worktree, and the second run of the nine checks), and the code paths cited above at `e63099ab`.
- Reproduced with the real code: built a `daily` plan plus worker artifacts via `createPlan`/`verifyResults` and ran `reconcileMocked()` from `.ci/mocked-report.mjs`.
  - Without the retry directory: `PASS 0 []`.
  - After adding only `mocked-e2e-results-standard-config/mocked-standard-config-global-retry/e2e/jiuwenswarm-checks.json`: `FAIL 1 ["standard-config: UNEXPECTED_SWARM_CHECKS"]` with `planned 5; executed 5; passed 5` — the same shape as the reported `Planned 195; executed 195; passed 195.`
  - Running the same reproduction against `.ci/mocked-report.mjs` at `92f40dab9^` (before PR #1361) returns `PASS` in both cases, which pins the regression.
- The first-attempt failure that triggered the retry (`test/issue-143-proxy-settings.spec.ts:277`, `toBeVisible()` on the prefilled proxy URL) passed on retry and is not part of this issue; it is ordinary product/journey flakiness absorbed by the retry policy.

### Suggested bounded fix

Make the isolated retry re-run only what it retries — the failed case — and never the exactly-once supplemental checks:

- In `test/support/tagged/retry-runner.mjs`, have `isolatedRetryConfig()` (or `batchLaunchConfig(..., { retry: true })`) emit `checks: 'off'` regardless of `batch.checks`, so `batchLaunchEnvironment()` sets `CI_E2E_SWARM_CHECKS=off` for a retry. The retry verdict already comes from its own Playwright report (`SCIENCE_TAG_PW_REPORT`), and the first attempt's checks evidence stays authoritative.
- Keep `.ci/mocked-report.mjs` strict. Do **not** simply whitelist `*-retry` there: that would silence a real duplicate-checks run instead of preventing it. If a defensive allowance is still wanted, accept a retry directory only when it holds no `e2e/jiuwenswarm-checks.json`, and keep every other `mocked-*` directory failing with `UNEXPECTED_SWARM_CHECKS`.

Suggested regression tests (both fail before the fix, pass after):

- `test/support/tagged/tests/retry-environment.test.mjs`: `batchLaunchEnvironment(isolatedRetryConfig({ ..., batch: { group: 'mocked', fixture: 'standard', checks: swarmChecks } }).launchConfig).CI_E2E_SWARM_CHECKS === 'off'`. Today only batches with `checks: []` are covered; a checks-carrying batch returns `'run'`.
- `.ci/mocked-shards.test.mjs` or `.ci/self-hosted-merge-queue.test.mjs`: a shard artifact containing a `mocked-standard-config-global-retry` directory without checks evidence still reconciles `PASS`, while a `jiuwenswarm-checks.json` in any other `mocked-*` directory still yields `UNEXPECTED_SWARM_CHECKS` (so the audit's intent is preserved).

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-26.04` runner, Actions runner `2.338.2`, workflow `.github/workflows/nightly.yml` (Nightly #113) calling `ci.yml` via `workflow_call`.
- Inputs: `profile=daily`, `backend=jiuwenswarm` (repository variable default), `max-parallel=2`; matrix shard `standard-config` with `CI_E2E_LOCAL_CONCURRENCY=2`.
- The failing step ran `node .ci/mocked-report.mjs .ci-mocked-plan/plan.json .ci-mocked-results .ci-results` at `19:40:01Z`.

### Version Information

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, `main @ e63099ab3b0b2bb30e9ecea432ee6be69efcc8a1` (run head and tested SHA).
- Regression introduced by `92f40dab9b1a1cf65a6716ced5459afc321f38a0` ("ci: run standard mocked E2E shards across 2 isolated local stacks", merged as PR #1361), which added the `mocked-*` directory audit in `.ci/mocked-report.mjs`; the retry directory and its `checks: 'run'` launch config existed before it (`bdc81300b`, "fix: isolate tagged case retries").
- Nightly #111 (`dfdcc9eb`, 2026-11-26) is the last dispatch run in the same series that stayed green, and it had no retried mocked case.

closed_recent.body:
## What happens

Four rules in `apps/desktop/src/styles/design.css` draw secondary text at `#808080`, `#8c8c8c` and `#a6a6a6`. All of it is normal-size text — 11 px, 12 px, 12.5 px — so WCAG 2.1 AA applies at **4.5:1** (SC 1.4.3; the large-text exemption starts at 18 pt, or 14 pt bold). Measured against the surfaces they actually render on, every one is below the floor, and two of them are below 3:1:

| rule | colour | size | surface it is drawn on | contrast |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `.settings-field-hint` | `#808080` | 12.5 px | `#fff` — the settings panel (`.config-panel` and `.config-backdrop` are `#fff`; `.settings-main` is `#fff`) | **3.95:1** |
| the same rule inside `.settings-ability-option.is-selected` | `#808080` | 12.5 px | `#f4f8ff` (`--primary-softer`) | **3.71:1** |
| `.session-flyout-desc` | `#8c8c8c` | 12 px | `#fff` — `.session-menu-flyout` is `#fff` | **3.36:1** |
| the same rule while its row is hovered | `#8c8c8c` | 12 px | `#f5f5f5` — `.session-flyout-row:hover` | **3.08:1** |
| `.session-flyout-note` (added for #1330, same colour) | `#8c8c8c` | 12 px | `#fff` | **3.36:1** |
| `.expert-note` | `#8c8c8c` | 12 px | `#fff` — the 专家 flyout | **3.36:1** |
| `.doc-tab-hint` | `#a6a6a6` | 11 px | `#f0f0f0` (`--surface-sunk`, the workspace panel) or `#fff` inside a `.workspace-section` | **2.14:1 / 2.43:1** |

Ratios are WCAG 2.1 relative luminance against the background named in the same row.

The two darkest cases are worth naming on their own: `#a6a6a6` on `#f0f0f0` is **2.14:1**, and `#8c8c8c` on the hover row is **3.08:1** — the second one only appears while the pointer is over the row the reader is reading, which is exactly when they need it.

## These are user-visible text, not decoration

- `.settings-field-hint` carries the sentence under a settings field: the skill-name rule (`TEXT.settings.skills.nameHint`, and `nameInvalid` in the same element), the specialist instructions hint and the capability hint (`TEXT.settings.system.specialists.instructionsHint`, `capabilitiesHint`) — `views/settings/SkillForm.tsx`, `views/settings/system/SpecialistForm.tsx`. Only the `is-error` variant switches to `--danger`, and that one is not part of this report.
- `.expert-note` carries the flyout's own status: `TEXT.composer.expertsLoading` (“正在读取专家…”) and `TEXT.composer.expertsEmpty` (“没有匹配的专家。”) — `views/Composer.tsx`.
- `.session-flyout-desc` carries the line that explains what each choice does, under the label of every row of 审查档位, 请求批准 and 会话设置.
- `.doc-tab-hint` carries the folder that tells two same-named documents apart in the tab strip — `views/WorkspacePanel.tsx`.

None of them is an icon, a placeholder, a disabled control or decorative text, so none of them is exempt.

## Where it comes from

`apps/desktop/src/styles/design.css` at `main` `d9f5a3da`:

- `:2208` `.session-flyout-desc { color: #8c8c8c; font-size: 12px; … }`
- `:2216` `.session-flyout-note { color: #8c8c8c; font-size: 12px; … }`
- `:2442` `.expert-note { color: #8c8c8c; font-size: 12px; … }`
- `:2993` `.doc-tab-hint { color: #a6a6a6; font-size: 11px; … }`
- `:4225` `.settings-field-hint { color: #808080; font-size: 12.5px; … }`

Two of the three colours are already tokens, so the fix is at token level rather than per selector: `apps/desktop/src/styles/tokens.css:36` `--text-faint: #8c8c8c`, `:35` `--muted-light: #a6a6a6`; `#808080` is written literally. The surfaces in the table are `--surface: #ffffff` (`:20`), `--surface-sunk: #f0f0f0` (`:24`), `--surface-hover: #ededed` (`:23`), `--primary-softer: #f4f8ff` (`:41`), and `.session-flyout-row:hover { background: #f5f5f5 }` (`:2177`).

## Suggested fix

Move all three to one secondary-text value that clears 4.5:1 on the worst surface in the table:

| candidate | on `#fff` | on `#f5f5f5` | on `#f0f0f0` | on `#f4f8ff` | on `#ededed` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `#666666` | 5.74 | 5.27 | 5.04 | 5.39 | 4.90 |
| `#777777` (today's `--muted`) | 4.48 | 4.11 | 3.93 | 4.20 | 3.83 |

`#666666` is the value already agreed for the desktop sidebar hints in #1486, which is the same defect on a different surface; using it here as well keeps one secondary colour across the desktop instead of a third shade. Note that `--muted` (`#777777`) does **not** clear the floor on the darker surfaces, so it cannot simply be reused.

## Related

#1486 reports the same problem for the sidebar and the landing surface. This report is the settings, flyout and document-tab half of it; the two do not overlap.

## Environment

- Windows 11, desktop renderer (React in Chromium), zh-CN and en.
- Colour values, surfaces and sizes read from `apps/desktop/src/styles` at `main` `d9f5a3da8c281829d6791efbbe3ce9392bf936b6`; ratios computed with the WCAG 2.1 relative-luminance formula.
- No backend, no data and no behaviour involved: this is a stylesheet and token change.

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary.** In the Chinese UI, runtime diagnostics that come from the runner and the sandbox egress path are shown as raw English sentences. The user reads `Shell execution timed out after 5000 ms` or `example.org:443 is not in the sandbox network allowed domains` in the middle of a Chinese conversation.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. `设置 › 超时 › 执行超时` → switch `不限` off, set `5` seconds.
2. Ask the agent to run something slower than 5 s (`python3 -c "import time;time.sleep(10)"`).
3. Reset the timeout, then `设置 › 沙箱网络` → `域名白名单` with only `only.example.org`.
4. Ask the agent to fetch `https://example.org` and press `拒绝` on the network consent card.

**Observed** (`933957a`)

```text
run_shell   → failed — Shell execution timed out after 5000 ms
run_direct_shell → failed — Direct shell execution timed out after 5000 ms
egress deny → Permission denied: Sandbox network ... example.org
              example.org:443 is not in the sandbox network allowed domains
proxy path  → Tunnel connection failed: 403 Forbidden
```

The app already has a localized layer for *run failures* — `apps/desktop/src/run-failure.ts:36` maps `/\b(?:execution|evaluation) timed out after (\d+) ms\b/i` to `TEXT.runFailure.timeoutTitles.runner_exec`, and this run even produced the localized 「调整超时」 card with 「Runner 执行超时（毫秒）」. The English string still reaches the user because it arrives through a **tool result**, which is rendered verbatim, and because the egress/proxy reasons have no mapping at all.

**Root cause**

- `services/runner/src/executor.ts:713` builds the terminal message as `` `${timeoutLabel} timed out after ${timeoutMs} ms` `` — an English sentence produced where no locale is known.
- `services/runner/src/egress-gateway.ts:273` builds `` `${host}:${port} is not in the sandbox network allowed domains` `` the same way.
- A `Tunnel connection failed: ...` string comes from the HTTP/proxy client and is forwarded untouched.
- The client translates only structured failure codes (`run-failure.ts`); a diagnostic that arrives inside a tool result is displayed as-is, so none of the strings above can be localized by the existing layer.

**Expected.** Either the runner reports a code plus parameters (`runner_exec` + `timeoutMs`) and the client renders `工具执行已超过 5 秒。…` (the string already exists: `apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts:2342`), or the tool-result surface applies the same translation table the failure card uses. The egress reason should get the same treatment.

**Impact**

- A Chinese user meets an English technical sentence they cannot search for and cannot act on; 「建议缩小单次执行范围后重试，或在系统设置中适当增加执行超时时间」 already exists in `zh.ts` but is never shown.
- The same body of text is also what users paste into bug reports, which makes triage harder than it needs to be.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- ScienceDiscovery desktop client, viewport 1500x950, `zh-CN`.
- Linux (Ubuntu 22.04.5); API `127.0.0.1:4410`, runner `127.0.0.1:4411`; Chromium 1228 via Playwright; sandbox backend `bwrap`.

### Additional Information

The card above the message is localized (`调整超时 / Runner 执行超时（毫秒）`), while the tool result itself stays English:

![timeout card and English tool result](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HongyeZhou/sciencediscovery/evidence/20261125-ux/evidence/2-timeout-english.png)

### Version Information

- `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` @ `933957a3af51600453da7473646ddd46f0a33cf7` (main, 2026-11-25).

### 🚀 Background Description

The desktop client cannot delete a single Scientific-memory record. The memory settings page offers only the global switch, and the citation card is read-only; the API has `cleanup/session` and `cleanup/project`, but `apps/desktop/src` has no call to either, so a wrong or stale record can only be removed by wiping a whole Session's or project's memory.

Motivation: evidence nodes are extracted automatically, so a bad extraction (wrong paper, a garbage abstract, a duplicated record) ends up cited by later reports and there is no way to remove just that node. Today the only remedy is `cleanup` on the whole scope, which throws away the good records with the bad one.

### Design Ideas

- Add `删除这条记忆` to the citation card (`MemoryCardDialog`) for Evidence nodes, with a confirmation line naming what else is linked to it.
- Alternatively (or additionally) a record list in `设置 › 科学记忆` with per-row delete, since the card is only reachable from a citation.
- Keep `cleanup/session|project` as-is for bulk resets; the new action is the single-record counterpart.
- Alternative considered: leave it API-only and document it. Rejected — most users of the desktop client never call the API.

### Involved Public APIs

A single-record deletion endpoint may be needed (or a narrower parameter on the existing cleanup route). It should be explicit about what happens to artifacts and claims that cite the record — dangling citations must degrade the same way an already-missing node does (see #1334).

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- Citation card and the `missing` state (#1334): after a delete, chips that cited the record must render the "not found" path rather than crash.
- Scientific-memory settings page and the sidecar's write path (delete must go through the service, not edit the graph files).

### Test Design and Test Plan

- UI test: delete one Evidence node from its card; assert the card closes, the node disappears from the memory list, and other nodes in the same Session survive.
- Regression: a report citing the deleted record still renders; pressing that chip shows the not-found state (not an error page).
- Bulk path unchanged: `cleanup/session` still removes everything in a Session.
- Command that must pass: `pnpm ci:l1`.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A single Scientific-memory record can be deleted from the desktop client, with a confirmation.
- [ ] Deleting one record leaves the rest of the Session's and project's memory intact.
- [ ] Existing citations to the deleted record degrade to the not-found state instead of breaking the card.
- [ ] Command that must pass: `pnpm ci:l1`

### Additional Information

- Screenshot of today's `设置 › 科学记忆` page (only 启用科学记忆 + 运行正常 + 重新检查) is in the comment below.
- Noted as an aside in #1334; filing it separately because it is a missing action, not the lookup defect.

### Version Information

- `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` @ `9da58ad619f972e44eb674c5d4cc9118813f7222` (main, 2026-11-24).

closed_recent.author: zhaozhaozz
closed_recent.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

`packages/workspace/src/workspace.test.ts` has a clock-boundary flake in `"Shell background mode and management tools do not start additional Shells"` that intermittently fails merge-queue UT runs even on unrelated PRs.

In `packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts` (`run_shell`, around lines 1779-1785), the foreground wait loop calls `Date.now()` twice before invoking `shellExecutions.wait`:

```ts
if (!params.background) {
  const deadline = Date.now() + (params.wait_ms ?? 10_000);
  let cursor = 0;
  do {
    signal?.throwIfAborted();
    execution = await options.shellExecutions.wait(execution.id,
      onProgress ? Math.min(250, Math.max(0, deadline - Date.now())) : Math.max(0, deadline - Date.now()), signal);
```

When the system clock advances by even 1 ms (or the process is briefly preempted) between computing `deadline = Date.now() + 5` and evaluating `deadline - Date.now()`, the first `wait()` call receives `4` ms instead of `5` ms.

Meanwhile, `packages/workspace/src/workspace.test.ts` (lines 2419-2420) asserts exact equality against the un-elapsed `wait_ms`:

```ts
await shell.execute("foreground", { command: "echo next", wait_ms: 5 });
assert.equal(calls.at(-1), "wait:job:5");
```

#### Observed Failure (Merge Queue Run #45954838570, UT Job #140359585337)

8,847 of 8,848 UT cases passed; only this test failed:

```text
AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: Expected values to be strictly equal:
+ actual - expected

+ 'wait:job:4'
- 'wait:job:5'
            ^

    at Object.fn (packages/workspace/src/workspace.test.ts:2420:10)
    at async test/support/tagged/node-worker.mjs:59:7
    at async TestContext.<anonymous> (test/support/tagged/node-worker.mjs:58:5)
    at async Test.run (node:internal/test_runner/test:1054:7)
    at async Suite.processPendingSubtests (node:internal/test_runner/test:744:7)
```

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- **CI Runner**: GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-latest` (`GitHub Actions 1000085687`, Linux x64)
- **Node.js**: `v22.19.0`
- **Test Runner**: `pnpm ci:ut` (`test/support/tagged/node-worker.mjs`)
- **Observed Run**: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/45954838570/job/140359585337

### Additional Information

- Observed during Merge Queue validation of PR #1361 (which did not modify `packages/workspace/`).
- The very next merge-queue run built on top of PR #1361's queue SHA (`45956546822`) passed all UT cases, confirming this is a 1 ms clock-boundary race rather than a deterministic regression.
- Expected fix direction:
  1. Reuse the same timestamp `now` on the first iteration in `packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts` (computing `deadline = now + waitMs` and passing `waitMs` / `deadline - now` without a redundant `Date.now()` call before the first `wait()`), and/or
  2. Keep unit-test coverage deterministic (including verifying first-iteration remaining time and multi-iteration progress clamping under controlled clocks without relying on wall-clock luck).

### Version Information

- **ScienceDiscovery version**: `0.4.0`
- **Commit**: `892130723f66b7fe6baf6c03dd81c6f76e8d04f4` (`main`)
- **Node.js**: `v22.19.0`

closed_recent.author: zhaozhaozz
closed_recent.body:
### 🚀 Background Description
During peak development hours, concurrent PR and merge-queue runs exhaust the organization's shared GitHub-hosted runner concurrency pool, causing 6–14 minute queuing delays across merge-queue and short gate jobs. The longest Linux jobs in `merge_group` are the three heavy L2 mocked E2E shards (`standard-config`, `standard-journeys`, `research`) and `UT`, which together consume ~60 runner-minutes per merge-queue run while waiting in the same hosted pool.

We have a dedicated 16 vCPU / 60 GiB Linux x86_64 host running 4 isolated Dockerized self-hosted GitHub Actions runners (`[self-hosted, Linux, X64, sciencediscovery]`) with verified bubblewrap user-namespace support, isolated per-container network/PID namespaces, pre-warmed local `/ci-cache` storage, and post-job cleanup hooks.

### Design Ideas
- Keep `.github/workflows/ci.yml` as the single shared workflow definition without duplicating jobs or adding per-runner port-allocation shell blocks (each runner container already isolates its own network namespace).
- Gate self-hosted routing strictly behind **both** `github.event_name == 'merge_group'` (trusted code reviewed and enqueued) and a repository variable toggle `vars.CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE == 'true'` (default off, allowing instant fallback to `ubuntu-latest` without a code change).
- Route only the 4 heavy merge-queue Linux jobs to `[self-hosted, Linux, X64, sciencediscovery]`:
  - `ut`
  - `e2e` matrix shards `standard-config`, `standard-journeys`, and `research`
- Keep all `pull_request` runs (including forks), short mocked shards (`governed`, `literature`), `st`, `desktop-mocked`, `real-merge` (L3 with model secrets), `Nightly`, `Release`, and `Package` runs on `ubuntu-latest`.
- Raise `e2e` matrix `max-parallel` from `4` to `5` so the two hosted short shards and three self-hosted heavy shards start concurrently without waiting behind each other.
- Avoid cross-region `actions/cache@v4` download/upload overhead on self-hosted containers by:
  - Skipping `actions/cache@v4` (and `setup-node` / `setup-uv` remote caching) when a job runs on a self-hosted container.
  - Using a small helper script `.ci/use-local-swarm-cache.sh` to lock and reuse a hash-keyed read-only `JIUWENSWARM_SRC` tree under `${SD_CI_CACHE_DIR}/jiuwenswarm` (removing `.git` after first setup so concurrent containers hit `scripts/jiuwenswarm.sh`'s pre-installed verify-only fast path).
  - Making `Provision the bubblewrap sandbox` idempotent (`if ! bwrap ...; then sudo apt-get ...; fi`) so pre-provisioned containers skip `sudo apt-get`.
  - Respecting pre-set `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH`, `UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR`, and `npm_config_cache` in `test/support/tagged/shared.mjs` (consistent with `UV_CACHE_DIR` today) so containers reuse pre-warmed Chromium and Python 3.12 with zero workflow branching.

### Involved Public APIs
None. Internal CI workflow routing, test harness cache environment variable fallbacks, and `.ci/` scripts/tests only.

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules
- `.ci/tier-policy.mjs` and `.ci/mocked-matrix.mjs` (policy routing and mocked E2E matrix generation)
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (`policy`, `e2e-plan`, `ut`, `e2e` jobs)
- `test/support/tagged/shared.mjs` (honoring `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH`, `UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR`, and `npm_config_cache` when set)
- `.ci/use-local-swarm-cache.sh` (local hash-keyed JiuwenSwarm cache helper)
- `.ci/README.md` and `.ci/*.test.mjs` contract tests

### Test Design and Test Plan
- Unit/contract tests verifying:
  - Self-hosted routing is **only** enabled when `event === 'merge_group'` AND `CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE === 'true'`; all `pull_request`, `workflow_dispatch`, `schedule`, and `push` events always resolve to `ubuntu-latest` even if the variable is set.
  - `.ci/mocked-matrix.mjs` assigns `[self-hosted, Linux, X64, sciencediscovery]` + `self_hosted: true` strictly to `standard-config`, `standard-journeys`, and `research` when enabled, while `governed` and `literature` stay `ubuntu-latest` + `self_hosted: false`.
  - `.github/workflows/ci.yml` gates remote `actions/cache`, `setup-node` cache, `setup-uv` cache, and `.ci/use-local-swarm-cache.sh` properly, keeps `max-parallel: 5` on `e2e`, and probes `bwrap` before `sudo apt-get`.
  - Hermetic bash tests for `.ci/use-local-swarm-cache.sh` covering cache miss + `.git` removal + `.ready` marker, cache hit fast path, and failed install cleanup.
  - Regression test verifying `test/support/tagged/shared.mjs` preserves caller-provided `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` / `UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR` / `npm_config_cache` while keeping existing defaults when unset.
- Commands to run: `node --test .ci/*.test.mjs`, `node .ci/test-selector.mjs check`, `node scripts/check-doc-links.mjs`, `node scripts/check-architecture.mjs`, and `node .ci/changed-path-check.mjs`.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `pull_request` (including forks), `workflow_dispatch`, `schedule`, and `push` runs never route `ut` or `e2e` to self-hosted runners, regardless of `CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE`.
- [ ] When `CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE` is unset or not `'true'`, `merge_group` runs keep existing `ubuntu-latest` routing and remote caching unchanged.
- [ ] When `event === 'merge_group'` and `vars.CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE == 'true'`, `ut` and the three heavy mocked shards (`standard-config`, `standard-journeys`, `research`) route to `[self-hosted, Linux, X64, sciencediscovery]` using local `/ci-cache` and skipping remote `actions/cache`, while `governed` and `literature` stay on `ubuntu-latest` with `max-parallel: 5`.
- [ ] `Provision the bubblewrap sandbox` in `ut` and `e2e` skips `sudo apt-get` when `bwrap` already passes its probe.
- [ ] `test/support/tagged/shared.mjs` honors pre-set `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH`, `UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR`, and `npm_config_cache`, falling back to existing defaults when unset.
- [ ] Commands that must pass: `pnpm ci:selftest`, `pnpm ci:l1` (and PR CI `merge-gate`).

### Additional Information
Rollout is two-step: merge with `CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE` unset (no behavioral change), then enable the repository variable `CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE=true` to cut over merge-queue traffic with instant rollback capability.

## What happens

In the desktop app, **会话设置** opens a 320 px panel of rows, and the choices of a row open as a flyout 4 px to the right of that panel. Nothing keeps the flyout inside the window: once the window is narrower than the panel + flyout, the flyout passes the right edge, the window clips it, and the 1 px right border is never drawn — the box looks open-ended on the right, and on narrower windows the tail of the row text is gone too.

Measured in the desktop browser entry (`apps/desktop/e2e`, real `apps/desktop` build, mocked `/api`), opening **会话设置** from the composer and then the row:

| window width | panel (left…right) | flyout | flyout right edge | past the window |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1280 | 472…792 | 审查档位, w 300, left 796 | 1096 | −184 (fits) |
| 1280 | 472…792 | 专家, w 380, left 796 | 1176 | −104 (fits) |
| 1152 | 447…767 | 专家, w 380, left 771 | 1151 | −1 (fits by 1 px) |
| 1100 | 405…725 | 专家, w 380, left 729 | 1109 | **+9, cut** |
| 1024 | 329…649 | 专家, w 380, left 653 | 1033 | **+9, cut** |
| 1024 | 407…727 | 审查档位, w 300, left 731 | 1031 | **+7, cut** |
| 960 | 407…727 | 审查档位, w 300, left 731 | 1031 | **+71, cut** |
| 960 | 265…585 | 专家, w 380, left 589 | 969 | **+9, cut** |

The cut is not reachable by scrolling — it is clipped away:

```
window.innerWidth                     1024
document.documentElement.scrollWidth  1024
document.documentElement.clientWidth  1024      (no horizontal scroll)
document.body.scrollWidth             1024
flyout  .session-menu-flyout.is-experts  left 653  right 1033  width 380
        border-left 1px, border-right 1px        → the right border sits at x=1032..1033, outside the window
nearest clipping ancestors: .page-task (overflow-x hidden), .app-shell (overflow-x hidden)
```

Reproduced on the two flyouts this panel has: **审查档位** (`.session-menu-flyout`, 300 px) and **专家** (`.session-menu-flyout.is-experts`, 380 px). Both are cut at 1024, and 专家 already at 1100.

## What is expected

The flyout stays inside the window the way the rest of the desktop menus do: clamp `left` so `right <= innerWidth - 8`, or open it on the left side of the panel when there is no room on the right. Its border and all of its rows are then visible at any window width the app allows.

## Where it comes from

`apps/desktop/src/styles/design.css` (current `main` `3e65ebdf`):

- `:2021` `.composer-dropdown.is-settings { left: 0; width: max-content; padding: 0; overflow: visible; border: 0; … }` — the panel is only an anchor; its width is the rows' width (320 px measured).
- `:2043` `.session-menu-panel, .session-menu-flyout { … border: 1px solid #ececec; … }`
- `:2054` `.session-menu-flyout { position: absolute; top: 0; left: calc(100% + 4px); }` — always to the right of the row, never clamped.
- `:2064` `.session-menu-flyout { width: 300px; }` and `:2281` `.session-menu-flyout.is-experts { width: 380px; }` — fixed widths, no `max-width` against the viewport.

`apps/desktop/src/views/Composer.tsx` renders those flyouts at `:345`, `:619` and `:735` with no geometry at all (no ref, no measurement, no reposition), so nothing corrects the placement after layout.

The other desktop menus already handle this, which is why only these two are affected: `.composer-dropdown.is-models` grows leftwards (`right: 0`), the row menu clamps itself (`RowMenu.tsx`, `useLayoutEffect` moves it back inside `innerWidth - 8`), and the model-name menu is portalled to `body` with `menuGeometry()` clamping `left` to `innerWidth - width - 8` (`ModelForm.tsx:133-155`).

## Scope of the check

Every other dropdown reachable at 1024, 1280 and 1440 fits inside the window: the composer's 模型 menu (340 px, right-anchored), 请求批准 (300 px), the project/session row menu (clamped), the settings rail, the 添加技能 popover, the MCP 导入 popover and the 界面语言 picker. The settings pages' native `<select>` popups are drawn by the browser and cannot be measured from the DOM, so they are not part of this report.

## Impact

- A menu the reader opened is partly unreadable, and its right border is missing, which reads as a rendering fault rather than as a menu.
- No data is lost and nothing is mis-clicked: the visible part of every row still works.

## Environment

- Windows 11, desktop renderer (React in Chromium), Chinese UI.
- Measured with `@playwright/test` 1.65.1 against `apps/desktop` (`vite` 8.1.4) with `apps/desktop/e2e/fixtures.ts` answering `/api/**`; window sizes 960×720 … 1440×900.
- Code checked against `main` `3e65ebdfa8a8b942b969a5e7f8996c7019f1dd4d`: the rules above and the three flyout call sites are present unchanged there.

## Version Information

- `main`: `3e65ebdfa8a8b942b969a5e7f8996c7019f1dd4d`
- Desktop: installed 0.4.0 (Windows x64); the numbers above were taken from a checkout whose `apps/desktop/src/styles/design.css` and `apps/desktop/src/views/Composer.tsx` match that commit for everything this depends on.
