## Summary

Refs #1360

When GitHub-hosted Linux runner capacity is congested, even short credential-free decision, planning, accounting, and gate jobs in the merge queue (`policy`, `l1`, `e2e-plan`, `coverage`, `merge-gate`, `real-plan`, `real-report`) can sit queued behind hosted runner availability.

This PR adds opt-in merge-queue routing for those seven lightweight jobs to dedicated self-hosted light runner slots (`[self-hosted, Linux, X64, sciencediscovery-light]`), kept separate from the heavy test-runner pool (`sciencediscovery`) so control/gate jobs never contend with long-running UT/E2E shards or hosted runner queues.

### Key Changes

- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`**:
  - Route `policy` to `["self-hosted","Linux","X64","sciencediscovery-light"]` when `github.event_name == 'merge_group' && vars.CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE == 'true'`; otherwise keep `ubuntu-latest`.
  - Route downstream policy-dependent lightweight jobs (`l1`, `e2e-plan`, `coverage`, `merge-gate`) via `needs.policy.outputs.self_hosted_merge_queue == 'true'` (single source of truth matching #1361's `ut`/`e2e` routing; safely falls back to `ubuntu-latest` if `policy` fails).
  - Disable cross-region `actions/setup-node@v4` `cache: pnpm` on `l1` and `e2e-plan` when `needs.policy.outputs.self_hosted_merge_queue == 'true'` so they reuse the container's local `/ci-cache` pnpm/npm stores directly.
  - Leave `ut`, `st`, `e2e`, `desktop-mocked`, `binary`, `docker`, `windows-desktop`, and `macos-desktop` untouched in this PR.
- **`.github/workflows/real-e2e.yml`**:
  - Route `real-plan` and `real-report` to `["self-hosted","Linux","X64","sciencediscovery-light"]` only when `github.event_name == 'merge_group' && vars.CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE == 'true'`; otherwise keep `ubuntu-latest`.
  - Disable remote `actions/setup-node@v4` `cache: pnpm` on `real-plan` when routed to a light slot.
  - Keep credentialed `real-e2e` and `desktop-real` workers strictly on `ubuntu-latest`.
- **`.ci/self-hosted-light-jobs.test.mjs`**:
  - Add contract tests evaluating the actual `runs-on` and `cache` workflow expressions across `merge_group`, `pull_request`, `workflow_dispatch`, `schedule`, and `push` with `CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE` unset, empty, `'false'`, `'TRUE'`, `'1'`, and `'true'`, feeding real `tier-policy.mjs` `route()` outputs into `needs.policy.outputs.self_hosted_merge_queue` (plus a failed-`policy` fallback check for `merge-gate`).
  - Dynamically derive the complement of all other parsed jobs with `runs-on` across `ci.yml` and `real-e2e.yml` to assert none of them reference `sciencediscovery-light`, assert the seven routed jobs target `sciencediscovery-light` (not bare `sciencediscovery`), assert none of them reference `secrets.`, and confirm `real-plan`/`real-report` retain `github.event_name != 'pull_request'`.
- **`.ci/self-hosted-merge-queue.test.mjs`**:
  - Update the post-#1361 contract test so `l1`, `e2e-plan`, `coverage`, and `merge-gate` are asserted to route via `needs.policy.outputs.self_hosted_merge_queue` to `sciencediscovery-light` (while keeping `st`, `desktop-mocked`, and `docker` strictly pinned to `ubuntu-latest` and preserving `doesNotMatch /vars\.CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE/` on `e2e-plan`).
- **`.ci/README.md`**:
  - Document the shared `CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE` toggle, light-runner container deployment steps (`RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE=/opt/hostedtoolcache` + `x64.complete` marker for pinned Node, `/ci-cache` env vars, `--labels sciencediscovery-light`, `/ci-cache` warm-up before enabling so `l1` stays within its 10-minute timeout, enablement order), safety boundaries, and exact outage recovery steps.

### Safety & Rollback

- **Default off**: Without repository variable `CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE=true`, all seven jobs remain on `ubuntu-latest` with zero behavioral change.
- **Strict event boundary**: `pull_request` (including forks), `workflow_dispatch`, `schedule`, and `push` always stay on `ubuntu-latest`, even when `CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE=true`.
- **Credential isolation**: None of the seven light jobs inject any `secrets.*`; model credentials remain strictly confined to GitHub-hosted `real-e2e` and `desktop-real` jobs.
- **Rollback and outage recovery**: Because GitHub Actions evaluates `runs-on` when a job is queued, unsetting or changing `CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE` returns all **newly created** `merge_group` runs to `ubuntu-latest`. During a light-runner outage, clear `CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE` first and then cancel and re-run affected `merge_group` runs already queued on `sciencediscovery-light` (or re-enqueue PRs ejected by the merge queue).

## Verification

- **YAML syntax**: `python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/ci.yml')); yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/real-e2e.yml'))"` -> OK
- **Targeted self-hosted contract tests**:
  - `node --test .ci/self-hosted-merge-queue.test.mjs` -> 8 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped
  - `node --test .ci/self-hosted-light-jobs.test.mjs` -> 3 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped
- **All `.ci` unit/contract tests**: `node --test .ci/*.test.mjs` -> 245 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped
- **L1 & docs checks**:
  - `pnpm ci:l1` -> 4/4 passed (`status: PASS`, 0 failed, 0 skipped)
  - `pnpm docs:check` -> `markdownlint-cli2` 0 issues; `check-doc-links.mjs` passed
  - `node .ci/test-selector.mjs check` -> OK
  - `node scripts/check-architecture.mjs` -> OK
  - `node test/check-e2e-meta.mjs` -> 0 errors
  - `CI_ENFORCE_SOURCE_MAP=1 node .ci/changed-path-check.mjs` -> OK (0/0 mapped)
- **Self-hosted 4 GiB light-container smoke test** (`sd-actions-runner:local`, `--memory=4g`, warm `/ci-cache` mounted):
  - Clone: 6s; `policy` (`tier-policy.mjs`): <1s; `l1` (`pnpm ci:l1`, 409/409 pnpm packages reused from `/ci-cache`, 4/4 PASS): 12s; `e2e-plan` (195 mocked identities, 5 workers): 5s; `real-plan` (9 real identities, 1 worker): 1s; `self-hosted-light-jobs.test.mjs` (3/3 PASS): <1s
  - Combined wall time: 24s; peak container memory (`cgroup memory.peak`): 1.70 GiB / 4.00 GiB limit
- **Not run locally**: Full L2 UT/ST/E2E/distribution matrix (covered by PR CI on GitHub Actions; `CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE` is off on PR runs and `pull_request` never enters the self-hosted branch).

Export could authorize a stale preview, keep polling after the dialog had given up, and report a revision-change failure as "Operation failed".

## What changed
Start export now requires the preview to match the current selection, so a failed or pending recalculation keeps the last estimate (#1057) without authorizing an export; each card stops after six pending answers and restarts on retry; both revision-change sentences map to one localized line; the over-cap key carries the selection. Rebased onto main@e63099ab.

## Frames
The over-cap frame prints `RESEARCH_PACKAGE_MAX_BYTES` (5 GiB default) against a 6 GiB selection, so the dialog's `formatBytes` reads 未压缩上限：5.0 GB; the en "Not included" line still falls below the scroll fold. Both stills are commit-pinned:

![Stalled recalculation, zh-CN, at 2be03a75](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/raw/2be03a75f51a0f5eaa65ee175ea2bef45b0a83d7/docs/screenshots/1440/01-stalled-recalculation-zh-3919db5.png)
![Over-limit re-acknowledged, zh-CN, at fbde0829](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/raw/fbde0829ddbb6de95bfaf3df46cf8682dcf608de/docs/screenshots/1440/03-over-limit-reacknowledged-zh-2be03a75.png)

## Provenance, per reviews 6091727931, 6091780882, 6091862075, 6091897542
The six frames are named after `2be03a75`, the commit that added them; only the names changed, with identical blob IDs across the `git mv`. The README shows the six 100% renames and unchanged code, lists only what `2be03a75` contains (images, spec, zh/en copy, `ResearchPackage.tsx`, trim test, README), and notes that the frames use the fixture the branch already had. `3919db5` appears nowhere.

## Validation
Unit 1808/0 (trim 28/28), typecheck clean, mocked spec 6 passed at `2be03a75`; pre-fix 19/9 and 6/6 fail. Gates on this head: `check-e2e-meta` 139 specs / 0 errors, `docs:links` 156 files, `docs:lint` 185 files / 0 issues; only README and PR text changed, so UT/ST were not re-run. release:fix, no compatibility change.

Closes #1440

### 测试

```
pnpm docs:check && node test/check-e2e-meta.mjs
```

由 agent 自报，平台未重跑。

closed_recent.author: zhaochen39
closed_recent.body:
## Summary

Model setup is the first-run gate: with no provider configured, **Settings → Model registry** opens the *Connect model* wizard automatically (`apps/web/src/ProviderModelSettings.tsx:617-618`). The screen is meant to answer one question — "which model will my runs use?" — but it currently asks it in six different places, uses one label for two different actions, and commits some answers with a Save button while committing others the moment they are clicked. This report is about that flow, not about how any single control looks.

## What the screen offers today

| # | Control | Where | What it writes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `Connect model` → `Save & connect` | registry heading (`ProviderModelSettings.tsx:897-904`) | creates the provider **and** registers every model the vendor lists, immediately |
| 2 | `Fetch model list` → tick rows → `Save & connect` | wizard footer (`ModelConnectWizard.tsx:828-841`) | same, narrowed to the ticked models |
| 3 | `Advanced configuration` → `Manual entries` / `Model identifier` | a fold inside the wizard (`ModelConnectWizard.tsx:745-794`) | same, for models the listing does not return |
| 4 | `Refresh list` → per-row `Add` | expanded provider (`ProviderModelSettings.tsx:346-348`) | one model, immediately |
| 5 | `Add model` (toggle) → manual form | bottom of the expanded provider (`ProviderModelSettings.tsx:505-515`) | one model, immediately |
| 6 | `Global default task model` select | registry heading (`ProviderModelSettings.tsx:879-896`) | `globalSettings.modelId`, immediately |
| 7 | `Edit` provider → `Save` / `Cancel` | expanded provider (`ProviderModelSettings.tsx:703-749`) | provider fields, staged until Save |

Above all of that sits a separate `Model catalog` strip with its own refresh (`ProviderModelSettings.tsx:386-400`).

## Problems

### 1. `Add model` means two different things, one above the other

Inside the same expanded provider, the per-model row action uses `t("providers.models.add")` (`ProviderModelSettings.tsx:348`) and the toggle that opens the manual form uses the *same* string (`:506`). So the row of a listed model offers "Add" (register this model) and a few pixels below the table another "Add model" opens a form. The wizard reuses the label a third time for its manual-entry toggle, but submits with a different one, `Add to list` (`ModelConnectWizard.tsx:779, 791`). A user cannot predict what any of these three controls will do from its label.

### 2. Two incompatible save models in the same panel

Provider fields are a draft: `Save` / `Cancel`, plus a `window.confirm` when another provider's `Edit` would discard the draft (`ProviderModelSettings.tsx:679-687, 693-697`). Everything else writes immediately:

- adding a model — `addModel()` calls the API at once, no confirm (`:784-823`);
- deleting a model — immediate, but guarded by `window.confirm` (`:825-863`);
- deleting a provider — immediate, guarded by `window.confirm` (`:751-754`);
- the default-model select — immediate (`:879-896`).

The same panel therefore mixes revertible and irreversible actions with no visual cue for which is which. Collapsing the row or expanding another one hides an unsaved provider draft with no prompt at that moment (`:699-701`), and the prompt only arrives later, when the settings dialog is closed — by then the user has usually forgotten the draft exists.

### 3. Registering *every* listed model is the silent default, and choosing models is hidden

With no explicit choice, `Save & connect` fetches the vendor list and registers all of it (`ModelConnectWizard.tsx:324-339`). To choose a subset the user must first press `Fetch model list` (`:828-841`) and only then do checkboxes appear. The only warning is the small plan line "Save & connect registers every model the provider lists" (`:838`), while the manual path that most users need when discovery fails is behind `Advanced configuration`, a fold that otherwise looks like protocol/proxy plumbing. Nothing states before saving that the first registered model will become the global default; that effect is only reported afterwards (`:414-421, 433-450`).

### 4. The default task model is edited in two places with different commit semantics

The registry heading has a `Global default task model` select that writes instantly (via `replaceDefaultModelOverride`, `App.tsx:5259-5269`). The same value is also edited in **Settings → Global → Task model**, which is a draft saved by the dialog's own Save (`App.tsx:5217-5219`). Two controls, one field, opposite commit behaviour — the difference is invisible until someone loses an edit.

### 5. Vocabulary: seven labels for four concepts

`Connect model`, `Save & connect`, `Add model`, `Add to list`, `Fetch model list`, `Refresh list`, `Advanced configuration` vs `Advanced connection settings` (`i18n/messages.ts:675-720, 738, 771`). "Connect", "register", "add" and "save" are used interchangeably for one operation, while "fetch"/"refresh" is the only genuinely different one.

### 6. Success does not end the flow

`resetPlan()` clears only the model plan (`ModelConnectWizard.tsx:157-164`); the API key, provider name, base URL and success banner stay (`:433-450`). Pressing `Save & connect` again therefore creates a second provider with the same display name — allowed by the store (`services/api/src/store.ts:2758-2779` has no name uniqueness check) — and there is no explicit "done" state to tell the user the wizard has finished.

## Actual vs expected

| | Actual | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| Entry points | Six ways to register a model across three levels (wizard, provider row, manual form), plus a default-model control duplicated in another tab | One way for each intent: add a provider; add models to a provider; pick the default model |
| Commit model | Provider fields staged, models and default immediate, deletes confirmed one by one | One commit model for the whole registry, with the same confirmation rule for every destructive action |
| Model choice | Register-all unless the user discovers `Fetch model list`; manual entry inside `Advanced configuration` | The listing visible by default with checkboxes, "register all" an explicit choice, manual entry next to it |
| Default model | Same field, two controls, two commit semantics, no indication of which wins | One control, or a link to the canonical one |
| After success | Form keeps the key and name; second press creates a duplicate provider | Clear, collapsed or "done" state; a duplicate name is warned about |

## Where

- `apps/web/src/ProviderModelSettings.tsx` — registry heading, wizard mount, provider rows, per-row add/delete, manual form toggle, default-model select, provider draft.
- `apps/web/src/ModelConnectWizard.tsx` — `resolveModelPlan` (register-all fallback), advanced fold, footer plan summary, success state.
- `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts:675-720, 722-723, 738, 771, 915` — the button and heading vocabulary.
- `apps/web/src/App.tsx:5217-5219, 5250-5280` — Mounting of the registry and of the Global settings group that edits the same default.

## Root cause

One component serves four jobs at once — registry list, provider editor, model picker, default-model setter — and each job brought its own persistence style and its own copy. The wizard was added later to make first-run setup one step, but it kept the provider editor's advanced fields *and* gained model registration, so provider creation and model registration now overlap instead of composing: the wizard can register models, the provider row can only add one at a time, and the provider editor cannot touch models at all. The `Add model` label was reused from the existing manual form for three controls that do different things.

## Suggested direction

1. **One control per intent.** `Add provider` (the wizard) and a single `Add model` per provider, opening one dialog that shows the fetched listing with checkboxes and keeps manual entry as a fallback in the same dialog. Remove the separate advanced/manual toggle, and stop using `Add` both for "register this listed model" and "open a form".
2. **Pick one commit model for the registry** and keep it: either stage every edit behind Save (provider fields, models, default) or make every action immediate with an undo. Apply the same confirmation rule to add, delete model and delete provider.
3. **Make model selection visible in the wizard.** Fetch the listing as soon as the key is entered, show it above the fold, and make "register all listed models" an explicit checkbox instead of the silent fallback. State the "first model becomes the global default" consequence before `Save & connect`.
4. **De-duplicate the default-model control.** Keep one, and link to it from the other place instead of rendering the same field twice with different commit semantics.
5. **End the flow on success.** Clear the key and name, collapse the wizard or show a `Done` state, and warn when a provider with the same name already exists.
6. **Copy pass.** Unify `Connect model` / `Save & connect` / `Add model` / `Add to list`, and keep `fetch`/`refresh` for the vendor listing only.

## Duplicate check

Searched open and closed issues for `model registry`, `Connect model`, `wizard`, `Add model`, `provider` and `usability`. #39 (closed) introduced the one-step connection wizard and is the origin of this overlap; #632 (closed) and #684 cover the *searchable model picker* rather than the registration flow; #686 covers the rendering of the provider `Test` control. None reports the overlapping entry points, the mixed save semantics or the duplicated default-model control.
closed_recent.title: [Usability] Model registration: overlapping entry points and inconsistent save semantics

Actions failure classification: **external**.

Run: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44361037291 (attempt 1, `workflow_dispatch`)

Head SHA: `d57fc2693e0972b5c1040d47a4b74370eb011c3f`

Upstream failing job: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44361037291/job/135002663117 (Gate / L4/L5 real E2E / Real E2E (research-2))

## Current behavior

The only planned case in the `research-2` shard, `DRB-59 easy Swarm research integration`, was classified `PROVIDER_FAULT`. The shard reported `planned 1 / executed 1 / passed 0 / failed 0 / provider faults 1` and failed with `- e2e-real: 1 provider fault(s) — an unverified case is not a pass`. The full job log gives the case's own error:

```
Error: Main run must complete with readable, nonempty declared final artifacts; delivery_status=partial; run_status=failed; delivered_artifacts=1; run_error=[181001] model call failed, reason: openAI API async stream error: APIError: read ECONNRESET
```

The job's `stack.log` identifies the failing request as `model-8f784f89-e866-486a-88b8-9d48d6063774`: HTTP 200, 12,117 SSE records / 3,716,762 bytes over 105.9 s, then `"error":{"classification":"network"}`, with `"attempts":1,"retries":0` and `"hasText":true,"hasToolCalls":true`. The next line is:

```
[jiuwenswarm-agent] run of 670fa97d-b9d0-4410-ad9f-ac0d80e75072 failed: [181001] model call failed, reason: openAI API async stream error: APIError: read ECONNRESET
```

## Expected behavior

DRB-59 completes its declared final artifacts and the shard reports `passed 1 of 1`. A live provider keeping the response open is a precondition of that journey, not a product assertion.

## Causal chain

The gateway accepted the request (`200`), streamed the answer and tool-call deltas for about 106 s, and the upstream connection was reset while answer text had already been exposed. The model gateway's bounded mid-stream retry is deliberately disabled once answer text is visible: `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts:517` throws when `state.text` is true, so the turn was not replayed and the run failed with the original transport error. The accounting then correctly recorded `PROVIDER_FAULT` (the status-less transport classification from #1071 / #1076). Under the repository's documented policy a provider fault is not a pass, so the downstream jobs failed:

- **Account for real cases** (https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44361037291/job/135075589240) reported `Planned 21; executed 20; passed 19; provider faults 1.` and `- PROVIDER_FAULT: ...DRB-59...`.
- **Gate / merge-gate** (https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44361037291/job/135075765132) failed with `Error: CI gate failed: real-scheduled: failure`; `.ci/tier-policy.mjs:52` throws because the daily profile requires the `real-scheduled` job to succeed.
- **Report the outcome** (https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44361037291/job/135075939143) failed with `RESULT: failure`; it only asserts that the gate result is `success`.

The other 19 real cases in this run passed, so the endpoint was not globally down; the fault is confined to one model turn.

## What was checked and what it rules out

- The failed-step output of job 135002663117, its `error-context.md`, and the `real-e2e-evidence-research-2` artifact (id `14455408997`). The artifact's `stack.log` is the wire-level evidence quoted above. I read it with `gh run download`; the artifact belongs to this run and commit, but its contents and attempt association are my observation, not independently verified.
- Source at the failed SHA: `const MAX_STREAM_RETRIES = 4;` (`services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts:188`) and the `state.text` guard at `:517`. The zero retries are the documented behaviour, not a missing retry loop.
- Existing Issues: #1071 / #1076 added the status-less transport classification; #898 documented that a reset after answer text starts is not replayed; #1222 recorded the same class for DRB-58 in run 44199315530. This run is a new occurrence of that class, not a new repository defect. It is not the cause reported in #1157-#1160, which describe run 43760882196 and a different failure.

## Uncertainty

The gateway diagnostics preserve only `classification: network`; the provider's own reason for closing the connection (load, edge reset, upstream timeout) is not visible. One reset in one request does not establish how widespread the provider problem was.

## Next verification

Re-run `research-2` (or the Nightly) once when the gateway is healthy and check that DRB-59 completes; a pass would separate the outage from the commit. A rerun was not requested here because the independent J5 provisioning failure in the same run (job 135002663249) is not yet established as external; see the separate report for that job. If maintainers want a turn-level retry that discards partial text, that is the enhancement space of #898, not a fix for this incident.

closed_recent.author: yuanzhou75
closed_recent.body:
## What happens

Exporting a session, then importing the file that was just written, fails — and the failure depends on what the session's records contain. Two different errors, both seen by the reporter on `main` today, both reproduced here against the exported files:

1. **`File not found`** (HTTP `404 {"error":"File not found"}`, shown as-is in the import dialog). The export succeeds and the file is on disk; the import dies.
2. **`Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'match')`** (HTTP `400` with that JavaScript message as `error`). A different package from the same batch.

These are not upstream/downstream of each other: they are two independent assumptions in the import (`restorePackage`) path, triggered by two different record shapes, in two different packages. Both fail *after* the `inspect` step returns `200` with a valid manifest, so the dialog has already shown the package's contents and title when the import breaks.

## Reproduced

Harness: the in-process API server the repository already uses for import/export tests (`createApiServer` from `services/api/src/http/index.ts`, empty temporary data directory, mocked capacity), driven with the same two requests the desktop dialog makes: `POST /api/projects/<id>/research-package/inspect` with the file bytes, then `POST /api/projects/<id>/research-package/import?inspectionChecksum=<checksum>` with an empty body.

| file | size | inspect | import |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `脓毒症内型评分聚类分析_20261128_1240.sdresearch` | 3,087,068 | 200 | **404 File not found** |
| `脓毒症内型评分聚类分析_20261128_1244.sdresearch` | 3,087,061 | 200 | **404 File not found** |
| `自来水中余氯快速比色检测三方案_20261128_1245.sdresearch` | 32,921,173 | 200 | **400 Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'match')** |
| `新冠刺突蛋白表位 官方DeepSeek_20261128_1248.sdresearch` | 511,345 | 200 | 201 |

SHA-256 of the four files, in that order: `2b375654ba62f5ece7e74a1c4f2cf28477d294b52832798975f5b446b9a4e69b`, `ca4e7c0d1475b6859935e9e0974b8d618ddeed7b0efa95a2322fe4848dd43ece`, `d3dcdbe9c607aa8beff8108d135c03f2687e7ff78cff7bc2860881735b9f6cf3`, `f508a26984c38913a9235285578a513d41288811254e3e50b6cd03d3ecb2fec0`. They are the reporter's own packages and stay on his machine; two later exports of the same sessions (`…_20261128_1309`, `…_20261128_1311`) import with `201`, so this is not "imports never work" — it depends on the records below.

## Root cause 1 — `records.versionObjects` names objects the archive does not carry, and the restore asks for them as if it did

Stack of the 404 (logged from the server's `code === "ENOENT"` branch):

```
Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '…/research-package-uploads/research-package-inspect-2GvSVv/objects/8a702d69f0de171b62fb3793143ede9c557191265a1a75e8ac6121be7eed3283'
    at Object.openSync (node:fs)
    at readFileSync (node:fs)
    at DirectoryObjects.get (packages/research-package/src/index.ts:674)
    at <anonymous> (services/api/src/research-snapshots.ts:1160)
    at async persistImportedResearchPackage (services/api/src/research-snapshots.ts:1513)
    at async Server.<anonymous> (services/api/src/http/index.ts:1895)
```

`research-snapshots.ts:1159-1162` walks `records.versionObjects` and calls `imported.objects.get(ref.digest.slice(7))`, guarding the result with `if (object)`. For the in-memory import (`importResearchPackage`) `objects` is a `Map`, so a missing entry yields `undefined` and the guard works. The HTTP import uses `importResearchPackageStreamed`, whose `DirectoryObjects` (`packages/research-package/src/index.ts:670-684`) implements `Map` over files on disk — its `get` is `readFileSync(...)`, so a digest that is not in the archive **throws** instead of returning `undefined`. The two import paths therefore disagree on their own interface (`PackageObjectDirectory extends ReadonlyMap<string, Uint8Array>`).

What is missing, from the package itself:

* `manifest.omissions` already lists **271** `version:…` entries for this package — the exporter knew those objects could not be read.
* `records.json` still carries all **271** refs in `versionObjects` (pool `agent-state`, e.g. `sha256:8a702d69…`), and 271/271 are absent from `objects/` and from the inventory.
* The digest the restore dies on, `8a702d69…`, is a `workspaceSnapshot.digest` referenced 26 times in `records.json`.

So the package is honest (its manifest says the versions are missing) and the import dies on the very first one instead of importing and reporting the 271 omissions it already carries. Every session whose run records reference `agent-state` version objects that are not stored at export time therefore produces an **unimportable** package.

## Root cause 2 — a `references` key inside tool-call records is treated as a composer reference

Stack of the 400:

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'match')
    at ResearchPackageIds.id (services/api/src/research-package-history.ts:26)
    at visit (services/api/src/research-package-history.ts:106)
    at <anonymous> (services/api/src/research-package-history.ts:102)
    … (run-event tree: sessions[0].runEvents[0].streams[1].events[51] …)
```

`remapRunEvent` decides by **key name only**: line 104 treats any object reached under a key called `references` as a `ComposerReference`, and line 106 does `ids.id(reference.id)` for anything whose `kind` is not `skill`/`dbrecord`. Connector/tool records keep their own citation list under exactly that name: this package has **8** objects like

```json
{ "refsource": "Water Res. 2015 Nov 1;84():378", "reftype": "Erratum in", "pmid": "", "note": "" }
```

inside `…step.details.records[0].structuredData.references` — no `kind`, no `id`. `ResearchPackageIds.id(undefined)` calls `source.match(...)` and throws, so the import answers `400` with the raw JavaScript message, and the dialog shows it verbatim.

## Suggested fix

* **Import tolerance (the 404):** ask `has()` before `get()` at every `imported.objects.get(...)` in `restorePackage` (`research-snapshots.ts:1066`, `:1153`, `:1160`, `:1243`, `:1281`, `:1327`), or make `DirectoryObjects.get` total (return `undefined` for a path that is not in the package) so the streamed and in-memory paths behave the same; a version object that is not in the package should become an omission (`version:<pool>:<digest>:missing object`), the way an absent workspace object already is.
* **Remap by shape, not by key name (the 400):** only treat an object as a `ComposerReference` when it actually is one (e.g. `typeof reference.id === "string"`), or only remap the composer's own `references` arrays, leaving `structuredData.references` untouched.
* Both should be pinned with a test built from a package that carries (a) a `versionObjects` entry whose object is absent and (b) a run event whose `structuredData.references` holds citation records.

## Environment

* Desktop app built from `main` (exported 2026-11-28 12:40–12:48 CST, `Asia/Shanghai`), Windows 11.
* Export profile `complete` for all four packages.
* Reproduction ran in WSL against this checkout with the repository's own API server, empty data directory, no model backend; the export side is untouched (the files are the app's own output).

closed_recent.author: HongyeZhou
closed_recent.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**What happens.** Three semantically invalid bodies for the sandbox network settings are rejected by the store with a precise message, but the HTTP layer answers `500 {"error":"Internal server error"}` and logs the real reason as `unclassified_request_error`. A valid body answers 200, so the route and the payload shape are fine.

**Minimal reproduction.** Four requests against a running API, no Session needed:

```
PUT /api/sandbox-network-settings {"mode":"domain-allowlist","allowedDomains":[]}
→ 500 {"error":"Internal server error"}

PUT /api/sandbox-network-settings {"mode":"open","allowedDomains":["a.example.org"]}
→ 500 {"error":"Internal server error"}

PUT /api/sandbox-network-settings {"mode":"domain-allowlist","allowedDomains":["a.example.org"],"bogus":1}
→ 500 {"error":"Internal server error"}

PUT /api/sandbox-network-settings {"mode":"domain-allowlist","allowedDomains":["a.example.org"]}   # control
→ 200 {"mode":"domain-allowlist","allowedDomains":["a.example.org"],...}
```

**Expected.** `400` with the store's own sentence, e.g. `Sandbox network mode domain-allowlist requires at least one allowed domain`, and no `unclassified_request_error` in the log.

**Actual.** 500 with the message replaced. The server log keeps the real reason, so the information exists but never reaches the caller:

```
event=unclassified_request_error errorMessage="Sandbox network mode domain-allowlist requires at least one allowed domain"
method=PUT path=/api/sandbox-network-settings status=500
```

**Where it breaks.**

- `services/api/src/store/sandbox-network.ts:65-70` throws plain `Error`s whose wording contains none of the tokens `isKnownClientInputError` looks for (`services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts:20-38`: `is required`, `must`, `contains an unknown value`, `cannot`, `does not match`, `invalid`, …):
  - `Sandbox network mode domain-allowlist requires at least one allowed domain`
  - `Sandbox network mode open does not use allowed domains; remove them or use domain-allowlist`
- The catch-all in `services/api/src/http/index.ts:5295-5300` therefore falls through to 500 and replaces the message with `Internal server error`.
- The same wording-driven mapping also affects `services/api/src/subagent-brief.ts:44` (`${field} requires at least one item`).

**Why it matters.** A caller cannot tell a bad request from a server fault, and the one sentence that would explain the rejection is only in the server log. The desktop client pre-validates the empty allowlist, so today this is reachable from API clients and from any future caller — which is why the fix belongs at the route, not in the wording.

**Suggested fix.** Keep the store's message and answer 400 for these validations — e.g. wrap the PUT handler in `ApiStatusError(400, message)` (this repository prefers typed errors over message matching) rather than editing the wording to contain `must`. Adding `must`/`requires` to the classification keywords is the smaller change but keeps the decision dependent on English wording.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Product: source checkout of `main` at `e374837d37a8a536483a9ef8b5d2a98bd23a5aee` (2026-11-28T01:17:17Z), API on `127.0.0.1:4410`.
- Host: Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, x86_64, Node.js v22.23.5.
- The same numbers were reproduced on `a70ef94` earlier the same day, so this is not new to `e374837`.
- Server log lines: `data/logs/api.log`, 2026-11-28T02:45:31Z.

### Additional Information

- No screenshot: the evidence is the four request/response pairs above plus the log line; the desktop client cannot reach the empty-allowlist case because it validates first.
- The unknown-field case (`"bogus":1`) also answers 500, but I did not trace which validator rejects it; the two store messages above are the ones confirmed in the log.

### Version Information

- Repository `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, branch `main`, commit `e374837d37a8a536483a9ef8b5d2a98bd23a5aee` (2026-11-28).
- Files inspected: `services/api/src/store/sandbox-network.ts`, `services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts`, `services/api/src/http/index.ts`, `services/api/src/subagent-brief.ts`.

closed_recent.author: moShangLouTou
closed_recent.body:
### 🚀 Background Description

The desktop Evolve entry point lets a user choose PUCT/OpenEvolve and optionally provide a JSON candidate plus editable fields, but it has no dedicated controls for the search's total token budget, wall-clock budget or expansion budget. The run panel displays token/time consumption only after a run exists.

This prevents a user from directly choosing and verifying a bounded experiment before starting it. In a Windows PUCT run on 2026-11-26, the frozen run used 32 expansions, 4 workers, 600,000 total tokens and 7,200 seconds. These values could be inspected in the run record, but not configured in a desktop budget form.

Current source behavior:

- `DirectionDialog` confirms only the algorithm and optional candidate JSON/edit scope. Custom JSON fields belong to the candidate being evolved; adding a field named `maxTokens` there is not a search-budget setting.
- `BudgetBar` renders progress bars with no budget editor.
- `EvolveRunProposal` / `create_evolve_run` accept `expansions` and `workers`, so an agent can request them through conversation. They do not expose configurable total tokens or total seconds.
- `startProposedRun()` sets total tokens to 600,000 and total seconds to 7,200 using backend constants. The per-call ceiling is derived from algorithm/effective thinking mode.

Related: #1346 addresses range/interaction hints in the existing custom-parameter editor; #780 made the conversational checkpoint disclose a budget plan. This request is for an actual search-budget configuration surface and end-to-end parameter support, not another candidate JSON field or a prose-only plan.

### Design Ideas

Add a clearly labelled search-budget section to the Evolve setup/confirmation flow, separate from the candidate JSON editor:

- Total token cap, with units and validated bounds.
- Total elapsed-time cap, entered in minutes and stored in seconds.
- Maximum candidate expansions, labelled as expansions rather than an ambiguous total node count; state whether the baseline is excluded.
- An optional advanced concurrency setting, with the effective value shown before starting.
- Show the effective per-call token ceiling derived from the selected algorithm and thinking mode. At minimum this should be visible; if manual override is supported, validate it against existing model/algorithm constraints instead of silently changing it.

Display requested and effective values before confirmation, including limitations and concurrency-related budget exposure. Preserve current defaults for clients that omit overrides. Reject invalid values with field-specific messages, and explain any cross-field restriction before the run is created.

A minimal first implementation can be per-run; global defaults/session overrides are not required for this request. Keep the same budget readable in the frozen run and existing usage panel.

### Involved Public APIs

Extend the typed run proposal/tool and server validation with optional budget overrides, including total tokens and total seconds. Thread the confirmed values from the desktop submission through agent/tool invocation into the frozen `EvolveGoal.budget`; do not rely only on prompt wording for user-selected limits. Update `get_evolve_budget`/budget-plan calculation to describe those same effective limits. Existing clients and stored runs must remain compatible.

Do not add a write-only UI whose values are ignored by `proposal.ts` or permit arbitrary candidate JSON fields to override execution policy.

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- `apps/web`: Evolve setup/confirmation, submission state and API types, localized validation copy, current budget display. The Electron shell loads this UI.
- `packages/schema`, `packages/evolve`: proposal/budget types and tool contracts.
- `services/api`: proposal validation, shared budget plan, preflight, persistence and orchestrator enforcement.
- Both PUCT and OpenEvolve share the budget contract; defaults for either algorithm must remain valid.

### Test Design and Test Plan

- Focused UI checks: enter valid limits and see effective values before confirmation; reject zero, negative, nonfinite, malformed and out-of-range values; preserve edits when navigating the setup flow; verify keyboard access and English/Chinese labels.
- A submission-to-persisted-run integration check: user-selected limits equal the tool request, effective plan and saved run budget; omitted overrides retain current defaults.
- Verify per-call ceilings and concurrency/expansion constraints with the same validation used by preflight. Do not silently coerce incompatible values.
- Add focused API/tool tests for new optional fields and backward compatibility; run typechecks for the affected packages.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Before starting an Evolve run, desktop users can set total tokens, total duration and maximum expansions in dedicated controls with units and bounds.
- [ ] Candidate JSON/edit scope is visibly separate from search configuration.
- [ ] Confirmation displays the effective budget and derived per-call token ceiling; invalid combinations cannot silently start with different limits.
- [ ] The user's confirmed limits reach the stored run and enforcement path without being replaced by backend constants or an agent's unrelated choice.
- [ ] Omitted overrides preserve current defaults and existing runs still load.
- [ ] Targeted UI/API/tool tests and affected package typechecks pass. Relevant typecheck commands include `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/web typecheck`, `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api typecheck`, and `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/evolve typecheck`.

### Additional Information

This request was established by inspecting the desktop/web implementation and backend proposal path; no new desktop/browser journey was run for this report. Budget-exhaustion finalization and cancellation diagnostics are tracked separately in #1435.

Checked against local `36476b0ea302b6de3897154f83c3c7c87dc6ec89` and fetched upstream main `3a00fd822e7cd88f0044e7c2e562febb8eb06dd1`; the relevant setup, budget display and proposal budget defaults remain unchanged.

- [Evolve confirmation dialog](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/3a00fd822e7cd88f0044e7c2e562febb8eb06dd1/apps/web/src/evolve/DirectionDialog.tsx#L41-L56)
- [Read-only budget display](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/3a00fd822e7cd88f0044e7c2e562febb8eb06dd1/apps/web/src/evolve/BudgetBar.tsx#L40-L65)
- [Backend budget defaults](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/3a00fd822e7cd88f0044e7c2e562febb8eb06dd1/services/api/src/evolution/call-budget.ts#L60-L70)
- [Frozen proposal budget](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/3a00fd822e7cd88f0044e7c2e562febb8eb06dd1/services/api/src/evolution/proposal.ts#L563-L575)

closed_recent.author: moShangLouTou
closed_recent.body:
### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

The desktop session export dialog still has three related failure-state problems after #1235. #1282 fixed the import omissions requirement from #1024; this report concerns the export path only.

1. **A stalled preview for a changed file selection re-enables export using the previous preview.** After a successful preview, untick a workspace file. If the new preview returns `EXPORT_PREVIEW_PENDING` six times, the dialog shows the stalled-preview message but enables `开始导出` (Start export) again. It still displays the previous selection's estimate and retains that preview's revision and limit decision. The outgoing request combines the current file selection with that retained preview. This does not demonstrate bypassing server-side validation; the confirmed defect is that the UI treats an unsuccessful recalculation as export-ready.
2. **The profile cards keep polling after the selected-preview wait has stopped.** The selected-preview effect has a six-attempt budget, but the necessary/complete card previews each retry every 1.5 seconds without a budget. With a persistent pending response, the dialog displays its stalled message while these requests continue until it closes. A component probe observed six further requests over the next 4.5 seconds.
3. **A known revision-change failure becomes a generic failure notification.** The export task can fail with `会话内容已更新，请使用最新大小预览重新导出。`, but `taskErrorMessage` does not recognize that sentence. The notification says only `操作失败` (Operation failed); the actionable explanation is relegated to technical details in the failed export row.

#### Reproduction

These conditions can be injected from the desktop renderer's DevTools Console. The helper below intercepts only the matching requests in the current window. Refreshing restores the normal implementation. The UI walkthrough is supplied for reproduction; the verification below used component tests rather than a running-browser journey.

With the export dialog closed, run:

```js
window.exportReview = { fetch: window.fetch, mode: "off", hits: 0 };
window.fetch = async function (input, init) {
  const r = window.exportReview;
  const url = new URL(input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input), location.href);
  const method = (init?.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : "GET")).toUpperCase();
  const json = (body, status = 200) => new Response(JSON.stringify(body), {
    status, headers: { "content-type": "application/json" },
  });
  if (url.pathname.endsWith("/research-package/preview") &&
      (r.mode === "all" || (r.mode === "selection" && url.searchParams.has("customFiles")))) {
    console.log("Injected pending response", ++r.hits);
    return json({ error: "Export preview is pending", code: "EXPORT_PREVIEW_PENDING" }, 409);
  }
  if (r.mode === "failure" && method === "POST" &&
      url.pathname.endsWith("/research-package/exports")) {
    return json({ id: crypto.randomUUID(), filename: "review-only.sdresearch",
      status: "failed", error: "会话内容已更新，请使用最新大小预览重新导出。" });
  }
  return r.fetch.call(window, input, init);
};
```

**Case 1: stale preview becomes actionable**

1. Set `exportReview.mode = "selection"`.
2. Open a session with workspace files, then its sidebar row menu → `导出会话`.
3. Wait for the initial preview to finish and note its size.
4. Untick one workspace file. The new custom-file preview now receives injected pending responses.
5. Wait for six attempts, approximately 7.5 seconds after the first pending answer.
6. Observe the stalled-preview sentence, the old size, and the enabled Start export button. No export needs to be started to observe this defect.

**Case 2: requests continue after the stalled message**

1. Close the dialog and set `exportReview.mode = "all"; exportReview.hits = 0`.
2. Reopen Export conversation and wait for the stalled-preview sentence.
3. Watch the Console counter: two profile-preview requests continue every approximately 1.5 seconds. Closing the dialog stops them.

**Case 3: actionable task failure is hidden**

1. Close the dialog and set `exportReview.mode = "failure"`.
2. Reopen Export conversation and wait for a successful preview.
3. Click Start export; if the desktop shell opens a Save dialog, choose a destination. The helper returns a simulated failed task instead of creating a real export task.
4. Observe the generic `操作失败` notification. Reopen the export dialog and expand the failed row's `技术细节` to find the revision-change instruction.

Cleanup without refreshing: `window.fetch = exportReview.fetch; delete window.exportReview`.

#### Expected behavior

- Keep Start export disabled until a successful preview matches the current selection; an old estimate may remain visible but must not authorize the current selection.
- Bound or suspend profile-card retries consistently with the stalled state, and let manual retry start a fresh wait.
- Present the known revision-change reason with the instruction to recalculate and retry, using the interface language.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Affected surface: `apps/desktop`, session export dialog; Chinese interface for the failure-copy example.
- Component verification: Linux x64, Node.js 22.19.0, pnpm 11.1.2, React test renderer with mocked timers and API responses. No running services or persistent SDK state were used.
- Existing `research-package-trim.test.tsx` tests passed. Three temporary probes confirmed the stale-preview enablement, continued profile requests, and missing revision-change mapping. The probes assert the observed faulty behavior; their passing result is evidence of reproduction, not correctness.
- No browser/Electron journey or full test suite was run for this report.

### Additional Information

Relevant code, pinned to the checked upstream revision:

- [Profile-card retries](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/4b9304d067600749d315de4a872bb824de9e8805/apps/desktop/src/views/ResearchPackage.tsx#L355-L363).

closed_recent.body:
## Goal

Make ScienceDiscovery a useful, approachable research product. A researcher should be able to understand what it can help with, get started with clear guidance, complete a task, and return to their work confidently.

The first experience we should deliver is simple:

**Open the app → connect a model → upload a CSV and ask a question → receive a useful chart → refine and save the result.**

The application should handle routine setup and organization, ask only for decisions that matter, and explain the next step in plain language. Technical details should be available when needed.

## Why this matters

During a trial of release 0.2.0, a new user encountered welcome cards that did not navigate, confusing model setup, unexplained `Unauthorized` messages, and an interface that opened even though analysis could not run on that computer. These problems prevented the user from experiencing the product's value.

This evidence comes from one installation. Check fixes in the current release and development branch before opening duplicate work. Related public feedback includes [difficulty finding the download](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/1).

## Improvements

### 1. Make the starting point obvious

- Explain the product with one concrete example and show its finished result.
- Provide prominent **Get started**, **Try an example**, and **Watch the walkthrough** actions.
- Make every suggested action work. Clearly explain unavailable actions and how to enable them.
- Offer a visible English/中文 switch and consistent wording throughout the experience.

### 2. Guide the user through setup

- Provide one recommended download and setup path for each supported computer type.
- Ask for the minimum information needed to connect a model, with helpful defaults and a clear connection test. Explain any required API key, where to obtain it, and that provider usage may incur charges.
- Handle the app's internal connection automatically where possible. If a user must reconnect, take them directly to a guided recovery step.
- Check that analysis can actually run before showing the app as ready. Explain compatibility problems early and provide a concrete next action.
- Keep advanced configuration accessible outside the ordinary setup flow.

### 3. Make everyday work feel straightforward

- Let users start with a question or a file. Create the initial project/session automatically for the guided example.
- Show understandable progress based on what is happening, such as reading data or preparing a chart. Make waiting, required input, completion, and failure easy to distinguish.
- Provide visible stop/retry actions where appropriate. Preserve the user's question and files when something fails.
- Explain errors in plain language with a recovery action; place diagnostic details behind an expandable option.
- Present the result clearly, with an explanation, supporting evidence, and access to the producing code. Make follow-up requests, saving/exporting, and returning later easy to discover.

### 4. Provide two videos that help people understand the product

**Video 1 — From opening the app to a first result (5–7 minutes).** Show a real released version: download/open, connect a model, upload the supplied CSV, ask a question, inspect the chart, request a change, and reopen the saved work. Provide the sample file, prompt, transcript, and English/Chinese captions. Show required preparation and label accelerated waits.

**Video 2 — The same task with and without ScienceDiscovery (6–8 minutes).** Use IMO 2026 Day 2 Problem 5 to compare the same model in direct conversation and in ScienceDiscovery. Focus on the viewer's experience: what they ask, how much guidance they provide, how understandable and complete the answer is, and how easily they can inspect or continue the work. Also report actual time and cost.

Keep the problem, model, and budgets comparable; review the mathematical proofs and report the observed outcome, including ties or failures. The problem's answer is the family `f(x) = x + c`, with `c >= 0`; describe it as the complete solution family. See the [original problem](https://www.imo-official.org/assets/documents/problems/2026/2026_eng.pdf) and [published reference proof](https://github.com/AxiomMath/IMO2026/blob/main/IMO2026/Q5/solution.lean).

Both videos must reflect working released behavior. Their purpose is to explain the experience and demonstrate useful outcomes. Test the app's guidance with new users, including people who have not watched the videos, and fix the points where they get stuck.

### 5. Make feedback and contribution welcoming

- Provide an obvious way to ask for help or report a problem without requiring users to understand the architecture.
- Explain where contributions are reviewed and how GitHub visitors reach that destination. The [current contribution guide](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/907382ce42e1ebfe77e24281905dec0607aaf003/CONTRIBUTING.md) routes code contributions to GitCode.
- Offer a short first-contribution guide and a few bounded tasks with named reviewers. Useful examples include improving a confusing screen, contributing an analysis example, or fixing a connector.
- Document checks newcomers can run without paid model access or special hardware, and how maintainers help with the remaining validation.

## How we know this is better

- [ ] A new user can explain what ScienceDiscovery does and identify how to start.
- [ ] On a supported computer, the user can complete the sample analysis, refine the result, and reopen the saved work without live maintainer assistance.
- [ ] Setup problems are explained before the user starts dependent work; failures preserve their inputs and offer a clear next step.
- [ ] The main journey works in English and Chinese, and the displayed controls and instructions match the released app.
- [ ] Both videos are linked from the project entry page, use actual runs, and include the materials needed to follow or inspect them.
- [ ] A new contributor can find a suitable task, run the relevant checks, submit a change, and understand the review process.

Observe ten unfamiliar users and use eight completing the sample journey without intervention as an initial target. Also record where users get stuck, whether they return the following week, and whether contributors return for another contribution. These are proposed targets, not current results.

## Delivery

Prioritize the first-use journey and recovery from the problems already observed. Validate the downloadable release, record the videos, and improve the experience with a small pilot group before broader promotion. Give each follow-up a named owner.

## Background

ScienceDiscovery is strengthening its end-to-end test coverage. We want to collect the complete user journeys that the community believes must remain continuously protected.

This RFC does not prescribe an implementation. It focuses on four questions: **What task is the user trying to complete? What outcomes must be observable? Does the scenario require a real model? Should it run as a pull-request gate or as a scheduled test?**

## How to contribute

Copy the comment template below and add one row for each proposed test scenario. Maintainers will periodically consolidate actionable feedback into the main table.

Guidelines:

- **Test scenario**: describe a complete flow from the user's goal, rather than an internal function or an isolated component.
- **Observations**: list user-visible outcomes and critical states, such as the final answer, tool calls, permissions, artifacts, citations, and recovery after a refresh.
- **Test method**: use `Mock LLM`, `Real LLM`, or `Both`, and explain why a real model is necessary when applicable.
- **Estimated token usage**: use `0 (scripted)` for Mock LLM cases; for Real LLM cases, estimate total input and output tokens for one run.
- **Estimated duration**: give the target duration for one case, excluding first-time dependency installation.
- **Priority**: use `P0` for basic platform availability, `P1` for core scientific capabilities, and `P2` for enhancements or corner cases.
- **Notes**: record environment requirements, external services, credentials, cost, side effects, candidate benchmark sources, or stability risks.

## Initial candidates

The following entries are both examples of the requested format and an initial backlog. The community is welcome to refine their priority, observations, estimates, and execution method.

| Test scenario | Observations | Test method (Mock or Real LLM) | Related feature | Estimated token usage | Estimated duration | Priority | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| Basic multi-turn conversation and refresh recovery | The run completes; the second turn uses conversation history; message order, terminal state, and refreshed content remain consistent | Mock LLM | Session, Agent Loop, History, SSE | 0 (scripted) | 2–3 min | P0 | No external network |
| Tool call, permission, and continued reasoning | Permission moves from pending to allowed; the tool executes once; its result returns to the model; the Agent continues and finishes | Mock LLM | Tool, Permission, Runner, Agent Loop | 0 (scripted) | 2–3 min | P0 | Use a safe local tool fixture |
| Plan creation, update, and completion | Plan and step states remain ordered and correct; updates do not block tools; the final state persists and recovers | Mock LLM | Plan, Context, Workspace UI | 0 (scripted) | 2–3 min | P0 | Use a deterministic tool-call sequence |
| Subagent delegation and result return | The child Agent lifecycle is complete; tool ownership is correct; the result returns to the lead Agent; reasoning continues; refresh restores the state | Mock LLM | Subagent, Team, Tool, Context | 0 (scripted) | 3–4 min | P0 | No external provider |
| Generate and deliver an artifact | The file exists; deliverables are distinct from temporary files; preview and download work; provenance is traceable; the final answer references the artifact | Mock LLM | Workspace, Artifact, Provenance, Tool | 0 (scripted) | 3–4 min | P0 | Use a local Python or Shell environment |
| Literature review | The Agent searches multiple sources, retrieves and extracts selected papers, produces traceable citations, handles source failures, and delivers a review artifact | Both | MCP, Literature Sources, Governed Download, PDF Extraction, Citation, Review | 0 mocked; 20k–60k real | 10–30 min | P1 | Real run requires network access and may depend on source availability |
| Evolve a solution | The Agent defines an objective and evaluation, runs iterative candidates, preserves checkpoints and logs, compares results, and delivers the best reproducible solution | Both | Evolve, Runner, Artifact, Provenance, Review | 0 mocked; 15k–50k real | 10–30 min | P1 | Candidate source: Terminal-Bench-Science |
| Data analysis | The Agent inspects an input dataset, selects and executes a valid analysis, validates intermediate results, and delivers reproducible code, figures, and conclusions | Both | Workspace, Python/R, Artifact, Provenance, Review | 0 mocked; 10k–40k real | 10–25 min | P1 | Candidate source: BiomniBench-DA |
| AI model workflow | The Agent prepares valid model inputs, invokes the model workload, exposes execution progress, preserves outputs and environment metadata, and explains the result | Both | Scientific Environment, Runner, NPU, Artifact, Provenance | 0 mocked; 10k–40k real | 15–60 min | P1 | Candidate tools/models: Protenix, ProteinMPNN, and similar workloads; hardware availability may constrain scheduling |
| Simulation tool workflow | The Agent prepares a valid simulation, invokes the selected simulator, reports progress and failures, and delivers reproducible configuration, logs, and results | Both | Scientific Environment, Runner, Tool, Artifact, Provenance | 0 mocked; 10k–40k real | 15–60 min | P1 | Real cases may require licensed software, large dependencies, or specialized hardware |
| Memory graph | Research outputs are written to the graph with correct identities and relations; retrieval returns relevant prior context; graph-backed citations remain traceable after refresh | Both | Memory Graph, Context, Provenance, Citation | 0 mocked; 8k–25k real | 5–20 min | P1 | Mocked case can use the local backend; scheduled case may use Neo4j |
| Agent team collaboration | The lead Agent decomposes work across multiple specialists; child scopes remain isolated; progress is observable; results return to the lead and are synthesized without loss or duplication | Both | Agent Team, Subagent, Context, Permission, Trajectory | 0 mocked; 15k–50k real | 10–30 min | P1 | Include concurrent child execution and one recoverable child failure |
| Idea Tree research | The Agent starts an Idea Tree run, expands and evaluates candidates, supports pause and resume, persists the tree, and delivers the selected result with its reasoning trail | Both | Idea Tree, Evolve, Workspace UI, Artifact, Provenance | 0 mocked; 15k–50k real | 10–30 min | P1 | Validate both tree state and the user-visible explorer |

## Comment template

Copy this table into a comment. Add more rows when proposing multiple scenarios.

| Test scenario | Observations | Test method (Mock or Real LLM) | Related feature | Estimated token usage | Estimated duration | Priority | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| Describe the complete user journey | List user-visible outcomes and critical states | Mock LLM / Real LLM / Both | List related capabilities | Estimate | Estimate | P0 / P1 / P2 | Add environment, cost, dependency, or stability notes |

## Suggested areas

- Agent Loop, tools, permissions, planning, and Agent teams;
- MCP, skills, Web Search, and Web Fetch;
- literature retrieval, paper download, PDF extraction, and scientific databases;
- artifacts, provenance, evidence, claims, citations, and review;
- context compression, long-running task continuity, and error recovery;
- local and remote Runners, scientific environments, NPU workloads, and background tasks;
- settings, onboarding, observability, and critical usability journeys;
- scenarios that can reveal issues only with a Real LLM or a real external service.

## Expected outcome

Community feedback will form a prioritized E2E case backlog, divided into:

- fast Mocked E2E cases executed for every pull request;
- comprehensive Mocked and Real LLM E2E cases executed on a schedule;
- real scientific-task acceptance tests executed before a release.

This issue is for collecting and clarifying test requirements. Implementation can be split into follow-up issues and pull requests by scenario.

### 🚀 Background Description

The desktop client has no way to archive a Session. The API exposes archive/restore routes (`services/api/src/http/index.ts` routes `/archive|restore`), but `apps/desktop/src` contains no reference to archiving at all, so the capability is unreachable from the only client most users run.

Motivation: Sessions accumulate (one per experiment), and the sidebar already folds older ones behind `显示更多` (see #1348). Without archive, the only way to shorten the list is to delete, which also removes the artifacts and the evidence trail — so users keep everything, and the fold gets worse.

### Design Ideas

- Add `归档会话` to the Session menu (`会话菜单`), next to 重命名 / 导出会话 / 删除, with a confirmation line saying what archiving keeps (data and artifacts stay, only the list entry moves).
- Surface archived Sessions in the sidebar behind a `已归档` filter/toggle, not mixed into the normal list.
- Reuse the existing API routes rather than adding new ones; the client only needs a client method plus the menu entry and the filter.
- Alternative considered: keep deletion only and lean on the fold. Rejected — deletion destroys the evidence trail and is not reversible.

### Involved Public APIs

No new public API is expected: the archive/restore routes already exist server-side. If a list filter is added, it should extend the existing Sessions listing query rather than change its shape.

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- Sidebar list rendering and the `显示更多` fold (#1348).
- Session deletion flow, which today is the only destructive path in that menu.
- Export (#1347) — an archived Session should still be exportable.

### Test Design and Test Plan

- UI test: archive a Session from the menu, assert it disappears from the active list and appears under `已归档`; restore it and assert it returns with its artifacts intact.
- Regression: archiving must not delete data — after archive + restore, the Session's artifacts, versions and citations still open.
- Guest path: a Session that is running cannot be archived (or the run is stopped first) — assert the state, not a silent failure.
- Command that must pass: `pnpm ci:l1`.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `归档会话` exists in the Session menu and archives the Session without deleting its artifacts or evidence.
- [ ] Archived Sessions are reachable through a visible filter/toggle and can be restored.
- [ ] The active list shrinks accordingly, and the fold count (#1348) reflects the archived set.
- [ ] Command that must pass: `pnpm ci:l1`

### Additional Information

- Screenshot of today's Session menu (重命名 / 导出会话 / 删除, no archive entry) is in the comment below.
- Found while testing D2-09; that test was removed from the map because the entry point does not exist.

### Version Information

- `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` @ `9da58ad619f972e44eb674c5d4cc9118813f7222` (main, 2026-11-24).

`Gate / L4/L5 real E2E / Real E2E (research-6)` failed the desktop SRBench PUCT smoke at the smoke's own bar of three expansions:

```

expect(received).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(expected)

Its own summary step agrees that the planned case is the only failure: the shared plan reads `- e2e-real: passed 0 of 1 planned`, and the problem list names `FAIL: playwright:test/desktop-evolve-srbench-real.spec.ts::…desktop%20%2Fevolve-design%20reaches%20three%20PUCT%20expansions…`.

The job's evidence artifact `real-e2e-evidence-research-6` (artifact id 14490394792; the upload step recorded the zip digest `8e5c0c81…`) belongs to this run and this commit (`E2E_COMMIT_SHA=59d05aa7…`). In it, `real-standard/e2e-real/test-results/desktop-evolve-srbench-rea-ba575-s-on-an-LLM-SRBench-problem-real/` holds:

- `desktop-evolve-metrics.json` — `"search_status": "succeeded"`, `"expansions": 1`; the single search record is `"status": "succeeded"`, `"bestNodeIndex": 1`, `"finishedAt": "2026-11-19T02:10:53.023Z"`, and its confirmed scorecard carries `"solvedThreshold": 0.999` on a `custom_script` criterion.
- `evolve-events.json` (13 events) — the seed (node 0) scored `baselineScore: 0.194226`; the one expansion (node 1) was `"valid": true`, `"score": 1`; then a log event `"planned 24 expansions, made 1; it stopped because target_reward."` and `{"type": "search_finished", "status": "succeeded", "stopReason": "target_reward", "bestTestScore": 1, "expansionsPlanned": 24, "candidates": 2}`.

The search did not stall, lose workers or hit a token ceiling: its first candidate reached the scorecard's solved threshold (test score 1.0 vs 0.999), and the engine stopped there. This run had `E2E_LLM_THINKING_MODE=enabled`, `E2E_LLM_THINKING_EFFORT=low`, so the per-call token ceiling that #1157 described was not involved; provider faults were 0.

That stop is documented product behavior, not a defect in the search. Since #1073 (closing #948) the PUCT engine passes the scorecard threshold as the framework's target stop:

```python
# services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/puct_engine.py:399
            "target_reward": float(spec.scorecard.get("solvedThreshold") or 0.999),
```

and `services/evolve/tests/test_puct_engine.py::test_reaching_the_scorecard_s_solved_threshold_ends_the_run` asserts exactly the event shape this run produced (`stopReason == "target_reward"`, `status == "succeeded"`, fewer expansions than planned).

The smoke, however, hard-codes the count and stops polling on any terminal status, including `succeeded`:

```ts
// test/desktop-evolve-srbench-real.spec.ts:441
          || ["budget_exhausted", "failed", "stopped", "succeeded"].includes(status);
// test/desktop-evolve-srbench-real.spec.ts:449
      expect(expanded.length, `The search must record at least ${target} expansions`).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(target);
```

So the pass condition is only satisfiable when the model's first candidates do not already reach the scorecard threshold — which is model-luck, not a property of the product.

## Same test bytes passed the night before

The spec and workflows are byte-identical between the previous Nightly head and this one: `git diff b2075e4972a5af90804fdd579ee314bfa502be46 59d05aa70a26801e2e907ca49060329028514608 -- test/ .github/` is empty, and `b2075e49` is the last commit touching the spec. Nightly run 44199315530 (head `b2075e49`, final attempt 3) was green, including `Real E2E (research-6)` and `Account for real cases`. This is not a source regression on this head; the difference is whether the design's first candidate already solves the SRBench problem.

## Not the same cause as the open reports

#1157/#1158/#1159 (run 43760882196) describe a different mechanism: two expansions because 22 candidate calls were cut off at the recorded 16000-token per-call ceiling while still thinking, ending on the expansion cap. #1185 (closed, unknown) recorded 0 expansions. Here the search ended `succeeded` on `target_reward` after one expansion, with a valid candidate that scored 1.0. Those reports remain accurate for their runs; this failure needs its own fix.

## Downstream jobs

One cause explains all four failing jobs:

- `Account for real cases` (https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44415877405/job/135286552958) fails "Reconcile every planned identity" with `Planned 21; executed 21; passed 20; provider faults 0.` / `- research-6: SHARD_FAILED` — the only failed case is this one.

- `Report the outcome` (https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44415877405/job/135286834408) runs `[[ "${RESULT}" == "success" ]]` with `RESULT: failure`, so it exits 1. It reports the gate; it does not decide it.

No rerun is requested. A rerun could pass by luck if the model's first candidate falls short of 0.999, but the assertion still contradicts the documented stop, so the same red is expected whenever the design solves the problem on its first candidate.

## Expected behavior

A search that reaches the scorecard's `solvedThreshold` on its first expansion must end `succeeded` with `stopReason: "target_reward"`, and the smoke should accept that ending as a pass while still failing a search that produced fewer than three expansions for any other reason (token ceiling, worker loss, `max_iters`/`max_calls`). Today the smoke cannot tell those apart.

## Requested code change

In `test/desktop-evolve-srbench-real.spec.ts`, step "Watch the search reach three expansions" (the block around lines 419-449): after `await save("evolve-events.json", events)`, read the `search_finished` event out of the collected events and branch before the `toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(target)` assertion:

- `expanded.length >= target` — unchanged: read each candidate back by hash as the code does today.
- otherwise, if the final event is `search_finished` with `status === "succeeded"`, `stopReason === "target_reward"` and `bestTestScore >= scorecard.solvedThreshold` — record the ending (for example `metrics.stop_reason`, `metrics.expansions_planned`) and read back the candidate(s) that were actually recorded by hash, then pass.
- otherwise — keep today's failure, with a message that names `status` and `stopReason`, so a short search that ended at the budget or on an error still fails exactly as it does now (that is the #1157 case).

Please also add a regression test for the branch itself — a small unit test over the extracted predicate is enough, since the journey needs a real model — so a later edit cannot silently drop the distinction between "goal met early" and "stopped short".

I read the artifact's `desktop-evolve-metrics.json` and `evolve-events.json` (and the scorecard embedded in the former) plus the four failed-step logs; I did not open the Playwright trace or the journey report HTML, and I did not run the journey locally. ## Purpose

Carry forward every unfinished or unverified acceptance item from #55, following the feature triage requested under #563 against release scope #249. This is an administrative split of partial delivery, not a declaration that the original feature is fully implemented.

## Existing delivery and evidence

PR56/60 delivered bilingual evolve explanation/how-to/tutorial/reference; current tree has core/evolve.md, domains/evolve-a-solution.md and EN developer-docs/evolve-standalone.md

Reviewed against upstream main `65eddde1` on 2026-10-27. Historical PR test results apply to their recorded candidate revisions only; no new product acceptance tests were run in this triage.

## Remaining work

Audit all original documentation criteria against the reorganized current docs, restore missing operational how-to/index/reference coverage if needed, and record an actual supplied-example tutorial run and bilingual parity/link results. Do not recreate pages that already exist.

## Release

Target: release/0.3.0. This remaining scope supports an explicit #249 release deliverable.

## Completion rule

- [ ] Account for every original criterion: delivered evidence, remaining implementation, explicit approved alternative, or separately linked follow-up.
- [ ] Run matching acceptance checks on the final candidate and retain actual results; do not treat workflow presence, merged status or historical green CI as full acceptance.
- [ ] Reconcile still-open PRs and original dependencies with the successor issue before merge.

## Original specification (preserved for traceability)

## Summary

`/evolve` is one of the largest features in the product and has **no user documentation in either language**. A researcher cannot learn what it does, when to reach for it, or how to drive it, without reading the source. I would like an explanation page, a how-to, and a tutorial — in English and Chinese — plus the existing Chinese architecture note fixed up and made reachable.

## What ships versus what is documented

What ships:

| Surface | Size |
|---|---|
| `services/evolve` Python sidecar | 23 modules, two search engines — flat-PUCT (`puct_engine.py`) and MAP-Elites islands with ring migration (`openevolve_engine.py`) |
| Scoring modes | four domain seams: `scorecard_domain` (dataset metric), `test_gate_domain` (test suite), `script_domain` (a scorer the model writes), `judge_domain` (LLM rubric) |
| Agent tools | `create_evolve_run`, `get_evolve_run` |
| Skill | `evolve-design`, a four-checkpoint design conversation with an algorithm choice |
| Web UI | 13 components — panel, algorithm picker, candidate stream, score chart, search graph canvas and table, budget bar, cell grid |
| UI strings | 188 `evolve.*` message keys |
| HTTP API | `/api/evolve/runs`, `/runs/<id>/events`, `/runs/<id>/candidates/<hash>`, `/runs/<id>/stop` |

What is documented:

| Language | Coverage |
|---|---|
| Chinese | **one** file, `docs/zh/explanation/evolve-standalone.md` (252 lines) |
| English | **zero** — the word "evolve" appears in exactly one English file, `docs/en/reference/web-frontend.md`, in passing |

And the single Chinese file has two problems of its own:

1. **It is unreachable.** `docs/zh/explanation/README.md` does not link it. The index lists `skill-library-management.md` and `skill-self-evolution.md` but not `evolve-standalone.md`, so the only way to find it is to list the directory. (Raised as an orphan page in [#25](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/25).)
2. **It answers a different question.** Its own opening says it covers the two engines' differences and what it would take to run the sidecar as a standalone backend. That is an architecture note for a maintainer. Nothing in it tells a researcher what a search is for, when scoring will actually discriminate, or how to start one.

## What to write

### 1. `explanation/evolve.md` (EN + ZH)

What an evolution search is, and the honest limits: it rewrites a candidate dozens of times and keeps what scores higher, so it succeeds or fails on whether the scoring can tell a good candidate from a bad one — a scoring function that cannot shows up as a flat run, not as an error. Cover the four scoring modes and when each applies, the two engines and when to pick which, and the frozen-scorer rule that `test_gate_domain` enforces, whose upstream note is worth quoting: *"without it the shortest path to a high score is to weaken the thing measuring it."*

### 2. `how-to/run-an-evolution-search.md` (EN + ZH)

The operational path: preparing a starting point and a dataset or test suite, what `--algorithm puct` versus `--algorithm openevolve` changes, reading the score chart and the search graph, budgets and stopping, retrieving the winning candidate, and what the approval card asks for before a run starts.

### 3. `tutorial/…-evolve-a-solution.md` (EN + ZH)

One short end-to-end run a reader can actually complete: a small starting program, a dataset with a metric, the `/evolve-design` conversation answered checkpoint by checkpoint, then what to look at while it runs and how to tell a real improvement from noise. This is the piece [#26](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/26) asks for in general, applied here.

### 4. Fix what exists

Link `evolve-standalone.md` from the Chinese explanation index, give it an English counterpart, and retitle it so its scope is obvious — it is the engine-internals and standalone-deployment note, not the feature's documentation.

### 5. Reference the surface

The four HTTP endpoints belong in `reference/rest-api.md`, and the two agent tools in `reference/builtin-tools.md`, so the feature is reachable from the reference tree as well as the prose.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An English reader can learn what `/evolve` is, when to use it, and how to run one, without reading source code.
- [ ] Explanation, how-to and tutorial pages exist in both languages and are linked from their indexes.
- [ ] The four scoring modes and the two engines are each documented with the case they suit.
- [ ] The frozen-scorer rule is stated where a user designing a search will meet it.
- [ ] The tutorial runs end to end on a supplied example, and says how to judge whether the result is real.
- [ ] `evolve-standalone.md` is linked, translated, and scoped by its title.
- [ ] The evolve endpoints and agent tools appear in the reference documents.

## Open questions

- Should the tutorial evolve a program (dataset metric) or a prompt (LLM judge)? The program case is more convincing; the prompt case is cheaper to run and needs no dataset.
- Can a small example — a starting program plus a labelled dataset — be committed for the tutorial, as [#26](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/26) proposes generally?
- Does the Idea Tree engine want the same treatment in the same pass? It has the same shape of gap: `idea-tree-engine.md` is also Chinese-only.

Related: [#25](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/25) (documentation completeness and the orphan pages), [#26](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/26) (the tutorial series), [#54](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/54) (RSI, which builds directly on this engine and will be much harder to explain if the engine itself is undocumented).
