items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**What happens.** #1319 / PR #1321 added a bounded retry for a reasoning-only empty terminal turn, and a readable failure message once the retries are spent. Both live in the JiuwenSwarm gateway. A deployment that runs the **native agent loop** — the default, `createAgentRun`'s `defaultAgentFactory()` — still gets neither: the first empty terminal turn ends the turn, and the message the user sees is the raw transport diagnostic from the model client.

**Minimal reproduction.** Probabilistic, like the original report: it needs the provider to return a turn with `finishReason=stop` and no text and no tool call.

1. Open a Session with a workspace file to analyse; permission 完全访问.
2. Send a normal request: `写一份 1500 字的技术报告，必须引用 3 条证据（记忆或网页），产出 report.md。主题就写 flip.csv 这组 A/B 指标的解读。`
3. On turn 2 the provider returns an empty terminal turn and the run fails about 7 s after it started.

**Expected.** The behaviour #1321 describes, on whichever loop serves the run: replay the empty turn a bounded number of times before failing, and say what happened in user language ("the model returned nothing this round; retried N times") instead of printing transport identifiers in the primary message.

**Actual.** The whole turn is discarded on the first empty terminal turn, with this text (the run's `run.failed` event, verbatim and untruncated apart from the middle of the ids):

```
Model returned an empty terminal turn (no text and no tool call) [requestId=model-8fcbdc57-ba25-49b9-bfa8-cc59661326f9 endpoint=https://ark.cn-beijing.volces.com model=deepseek-v4.1-flash httpStatus=200 upstreamRequestId=021795837314155c1c101af9eebb417c253ad03e8acb9414ede40 sseRecords=5 sseParseErrors=0 finishReason=stop hasReasoning=true retries=0]
```

- `status=failed`, `errorCode=server-error`, no retry entry point, and no readable sentence — the string is the one built by `EmptyModelTurnError`.
- `api.log` has no `[model-gateway] retrying an empty terminal model turn` line for this run, i.e. the retry loop never ran.
- Re-issuing the same request as a shorter "methods only" turn succeeded, so the session and the provider were fine.

**Where it breaks (read on `main` @ `e374837`).**

- `services/api/src/agent-run/create-agent-run.ts:56-61` — `defaultAgentFactory()` returns the native loop unless `jiuwenSwarmConfigFromEnv()` selects the Swarm executor. This deployment runs native.
- `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts:537-575` — the empty-turn retry (`MAX_EMPTY_TURN_RETRIES = 2`, `EMPTY_TURN_CLASSES` = `reasoning_only` / `empty_completion`) and `:155-162` `EmptyTurnRecoveryExhaustedError`, which is what writes the readable sentence. Neither is on the native path.
- `packages/model/src/client.ts:1774-1779` — the native path throws `EmptyModelTurnError` straight out of the streamer, and `:168-173` gives it the raw message quoted above.
- `services/api/src/run-failure.ts:44` — that message is then classified as `server-error`, so the failure reads like an internal fault.

**Why it matters.** The empty terminal turn is transient provider behaviour, so on the default loop every occurrence still costs the whole turn — and here a turn is minutes and hundreds of thousands of tokens. The user also cannot tell it apart from a broken environment, which is exactly what #1321 set out to fix.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Product: source checkout of `main` at `e374837d37a8a536483a9ef8b5d2a98bd23a5aee` (2026-11-28T01:17:17Z): API on `127.0.0.1:4410`, Runner on `4411` (bubblewrap), desktop web surface on `http://127.0.0.1:5174`.
- Host: Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, x86_64, Node.js v22.23.5.
- Model endpoint: `https://ark.cn-beijing.volces.com`, model `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, thinking on.
- Session `86b859f7-cc8c-4bca-9073-6e4aa1524956`; failed run `4daf006a-9afe-447d-affb-44293de7457f` (started 2026-11-28T03:41:48Z, failed 03:41:55Z).
- The whole run is 24 events, so the failure is cheap to inspect: `data/run-events/86b859f7-…/4daf006a-…/main.jsonl`.

### Additional Information

- The screenshots attached show the failed turn in the transcript.
- Related, and the reason this is filed separately: #1319 (closed) and PR #1321 fixed the Swarm gateway only. This is the same defect on the loop that the default deployment actually uses, not a re-report of a fixed bug.
- A secondary observation, same message: the raw string carries `requestId` / `upstreamRequestId` / `sseRecords`, so a support conversation about it is a transport-debugging conversation, not a product one.

### Version Information

- Repository `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, branch `main`, commit `e374837d37a8a536483a9ef8b5d2a98bd23a5aee` (2026-11-28).
- Files inspected: `services/api/src/agent-run/create-agent-run.ts`, `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts`, `packages/model/src/client.ts`, `services/api/src/run-failure.ts`.

![The failed turn 7 s after it started, with the transport diagnostics in the transcript](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a29911e5-3699-4acf-9102-3312e94f53a0)
items.title: [Bug]: The empty-terminal-turn retry covers only the JiuwenSwarm gateway; the native agent loop still drops the turn on the first one and prints the raw transport diagnostics

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**What happens.** Pressing 暂停 (or 结束) on a running Idea Tree research does not interrupt the model call that is in flight. The status becomes `pausing` immediately and stays there until that call returns; only then, within 0–10 ms, does the research move to `paused` / `ended`. A single call takes 2–3 minutes here, so a 90 s observation shows nothing but `pausing`, and the UI never says what it is waiting for or how long it will take.

**Minimal reproduction.**

1. Send `/idea-tree 为什么冰的密度比液态水小？不需要抓网页`, confirm the parameter card, send it, and wait for `create_idea_research`.
2. Once `status: running`, press 暂停 and sample the status and the UI line every 5 s.
3. At 90 s press 结束 and keep sampling until it settles.

**Expected.** Either the pause takes effect promptly (the call is aborted), or the UI says it is waiting for the current model call and for how long ("正在等待当前模型调用返回，最多约 N 秒"), and offers a hard stop that does not wait.

**Actual.**

- 18/18 samples across 90 s: `status: pausing`, progress line 「正在暂停 ideate 第 0 轮 0 tokens」. No explanation, no elapsed wait, no second action.
- `api.log`: this research's five model calls took 146.4 / 149.3 / 153.4 / 187.0 / 190.6 s. Every state transition (`stopped`) lands 6–10 ms after the matching `evolve_llm_call_finished` returns 200 — i.e. the state machine advances on the call's return, not on the request.
- 结束 pressed during `pausing` is queued, not lost: the research finally reads `status: ended`, `reason: "Ended by user"`, `updatedAt 2026-11-28T05:42:35Z`, about 3 minutes after the click. An intermediate read of `paused` means "the pause finished, the end is still queued".
- Asymmetry: `paused → running` through 继续 completes in about 5 s. Entering `pausing` is the slow and opaque direction.

**Where it breaks.**

- `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/vendor/idea_tree/research_service.py:250-254` — a pause request persists `pendingStop` and sets `s['status'] = 'pausing'`; the SSE stream keeps running, so the UI has nothing but that status to show.
- `research.py` — the engine only observes a stop at `check_stop()` between steps (`Interrupted` is raised there and handled at `:795-796` / `:818-820`). The retry backoff is deliberately sliced so a pause lands promptly (`RETRY_POLL_SECONDS = 0.25`), but the call itself is a single blocking request with no equivalent: nothing can abort it, so the wait is as long as the provider takes.
- The transition to `paused`/`ended` is written after the call returns, which is why the log shows 6–10 ms between `evolve_llm_call_finished` and the activity's `stopped`.

**Why it matters.** The user cannot tell whether the click worked: `pausing` looks identical to stuck, and it can last minutes. It also makes 结束 feel unreliable — two runs of this looked like "the end was swallowed" until the log showed the request had simply been queued behind a 3-minute call. A pause that cannot interrupt anything is a status word, not a control.

**Suggested fix (one of).**

- Abort the in-flight call: pass a cancellation token into the transport (or close the connection) and treat the abort as `Interrupted`, the same way a graceful shutdown already cancels a task.
- Keep the wait but make it honest: in the `pausing` state, show what is being waited on and for how long ("等待当前模型调用返回（已 42 s，最长约 3 分钟）"), and make 结束 apply as soon as the pause settles without a second queue step.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Product: source checkout of `main` at `e374837d37a8a536483a9ef8b5d2a98bd23a5aee` (2026-11-28T01:17:17Z): API on `127.0.0.1:4410`, evolve sidecar on `17676` (`healthy`, `bwrap`), desktop web surface on `http://127.0.0.1:5174`.
- Host: Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, x86_64, Node.js v22.23.5.
- Client: Playwright Chromium, 1600x1000 viewport, locale `zh-CN`; model Ark `deepseek-v4.1-flash`; permission mode 完全访问.
- Session `b681e51a-8ca2-456c-9df4-02162ac5444e`, research `research-98625896-9d96-4fd2-9c0a-6c1e60bc2ff8`. An earlier research on the same stack (`research-d2b76589-da10-47b0-a113-df7bdbb14394`) also sat in `pausing` for 40 s+ before it settled.

### Additional Information

- This is not the status-persistence family already fixed in #1455 / #1464: the final state here is correct (`ended`, "Ended by user"). The problem is the wait itself and the silence during it.
- Log evidence: `data/logs/api.log` — `evolve_llm_call_finished` (written by `services/api/src/evolution/llm-proxy.ts:203`) immediately followed by the research activity's `stopped` event, five times, at the call durations above.
- No screenshot of the `pausing` line: the research was ended at the end of the observation, so that state is no longer on screen. The 18/18 sample table and the five call durations in `api.log` are the evidence.

### Version Information

- Repository `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, branch `main`, commit `e374837d37a8a536483a9ef8b5d2a98bd23a5aee` (2026-11-28).
- Files inspected: `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/vendor/idea_tree/research.py`, `research_service.py`, `services/api/src/evolution/llm-proxy.ts`.

items.author: yuanzhou75
items.body:
## 🚀 Background Description

The workbench search box finds Projects, Sessions and artifacts by **name and title only**. Typing a phrase that exists only inside a conversation returns the empty state, so a user who remembers what was said but not the Session title cannot find that Session.

Verified on `main` `e374837d`:

| Piece | State |
| --- | --- |
| Route | `GET /api/search?q=&limit=&offset=` — `services/api/src/http/index.ts:2052-2056` → `searchWorkbench` (`services/api/src/workbench/index.ts:28-102`) |
| What is matched | Project **name** (`:50`); Session **title**, plus its project name and Session id (`:62`); artifact **name/title**, plus its Session title and project name (`:78`) |
| What is not matched | **message bodies.** `searchWorkbench` never calls `store.readMessages`, and `SessionStore` has no text index: a Session's transcript is one JSON file read whole (`services/api/src/store.ts:7319-7327`) |
| Desktop surface | the magnifier in the Session column's title row, `apps/desktop/src/views/SearchDialog.tsx`; `apps/desktop/src/api/workbench.ts:18-23` states the limit in a comment ("not message bodies") |
| Web surface | the same route from `apps/web/src/api/web.ts:75-77` |
| Current UI copy | `apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts:349` "输入以搜索会话、项目和产物。"; `:353` empty state "没有匹配「…」的会话、项目或产物。搜索只匹配名称与标题，不包含消息正文。" (`en.ts` mirrors both) |

**This is not a regression.** #1251 scoped the search to names and titles on purpose, and its design note 4 asks the field to be honest about it: "Message-content search is a real user need, but `searchWorkbench` only reads titles today; adding it means an index and belongs to a follow-up once this UI exists." The follow-up is this issue.

Reproduction (desktop, current `main`):
1. Click the magnifier in the Session column's title row.
2. Type a phrase that appears in a message body but in no Project name, Session title or artifact name.
3. Observed: 「没有匹配「…」的会话、项目或产物。搜索只匹配名称与标题，不包含消息正文。」 — the conversation containing the phrase is not found, however distinctive the phrase is.

## Design Ideas

The cost is the open question: nothing indexes message text, so a content search has to either read transcripts per query or keep an index.

1. **Bounded scan, no index.** On a content search, read `readMessages` for the Sessions in scope and match the needle. Cheap to write, but it is one full `JSON.parse` of a transcript file per Session per keystroke — acceptable only with a strict scope (for example the current Project, or the most recently updated N Sessions) and a documented depth limit.
2. **In-memory text index, built lazily.** First content search builds Session id → lowercased transcript text, refreshed when a Session's message file changes. Bounded by `limit`, reset on restart. More code, and the memory ceiling and refresh trigger have to be stated.
3. **What a hit is** is a product choice, and the two options differ in client work:
   - **Session hit with a snippet** — the existing `kind: "session"` result, with the matching line in `detail`. No new result kind, so the desktop dialog and the web palette render it as they do today; both copy strings above must change, because they promise the opposite.
   - **Message hit** — a new `kind`, able to open the Session at that message. Needs the shared schema, the desktop filter chips and icons, the web palette, and the contract case in `test/contract/routes.json`.

Whichever is chosen, the copy in `apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts` / `en.ts` has to be rewritten in the same change: the hint and the empty state currently tell the reader that bodies are not searched.

Sequencing note: PR #1256 (open) edits the same desktop text files and the Session column; it is `dirty` against `main`, so the fix should not race it on those files.

## Involved Public APIs

`GET /api/search` is public and consumed by both clients. A Session-with-snippet fix changes no field; a message-hit fix adds a `kind` value to `WorkbenchSearchResult` and a field for the message anchor, so the shared schema and `test/contract/routes.json` move with it. Paging (`limit`/`offset`, `hasMore`, `total`) must keep meaning the same thing when a second matching source is folded in.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- `SessionStore` (`services/api/src/store.ts`) — reading transcripts, and any index refresh hook tied to message writes.
- Desktop Session column and its search dialog; web composer palette — both consume the same response.
- No change to Message, artifact or research storage.

## Test Design and Test Plan

- Unit (`services/api/src/workbench/index.test.ts`): a Session whose title and artifacts do not contain the needle but whose transcript does is returned when content search is requested and is not returned when it is off; the needle is matched case-insensitively and only in message bodies, not in stored JSON keys; `limit`/`offset` still page a mixed result set without duplicates or gaps.
- Index path, if an index is built: the index reflects a Message appended after the first build, and a deleted or renamed Session drops out.
- Performance: name a measured ceiling for a fixed number of Sessions (for example 200 Sessions, and the same with the largest transcript in the fixture set) and record the observed number in the pull request, rather than asserting "fast".
- Desktop/web: mocked `GET /api/search` fixtures that include a content hit, plus the empty state and error state; the copy assertions cover the new wording.
- Contract: the `test/contract` case for `GET /api/search` keeps its shape, or gains the new kind explicitly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Typing a phrase that exists only in a message body returns the conversation that contains it; typing a phrase that exists nowhere still shows the empty state.
- [ ] A Session that matched by title is not duplicated when its transcript also matches.
- [ ] The search copy no longer claims that message bodies are not searched, in both `zh-CN` and `en`.
- [ ] Paging, sort order and the kind filters behave as they do today.
- [ ] A stated cost bound: the measured latency at the documented Session-count ceiling, recorded in the pull request.
- Command that must pass: `pnpm ci:l1`

Run: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44361037291 (attempt 1, `workflow_dispatch`)

Head SHA: `d57fc2693e0972b5c1040d47a4b74370eb011c3f`

Upstream failing job: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44361037291/job/135002663249 (Gate / L4/L5 real E2E / Real E2E (research-11))

## Current behavior

`research-11` planned exactly one case, J5, and executed none. The shard reported `{"status":"FAIL","planned":1,"executed":0,"passed":0,"failed":0,"skipped":1}`, `1 skipped`, and the problem line `- e2e-real: 1 skipped — a skip is not a pass`. The journey report captured in the `real-e2e-evidence-research-11` artifact (id `14460243200`) records the precondition:

```
BLOCKED: managed Python base is not ready (failed: Conda environment setup failed)
```

The environment-setup state was therefore `failed`, not `installing`. The message is the generic non-micromamba failure from `services/runner/src/environment-store.ts:1460` (`Conda environment setup failed`); the store keeps the actual provisioner transcript in `setup.error` / `components.conda.error`, but J5 prints only `setup.message`, and `real-e2e.yml` uploads `.ci-results` only. The runner's operational log at `<CI_RUNTIME_DIR>/real-standard/data/logs/runner.log` is not in the artifact, so the precise conda/provisioning error is missing.

`Account for real cases` (https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44361037291/job/135075589240) reports `- research-11: SHARD_FAILED`; `merge-gate` (https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44361037291/job/135075765132) fails with `Error: CI gate failed: real-scheduled: failure`; `Report the outcome` (https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44361037291/job/135075939143) fails with `RESULT: failure`.

## Expected behavior

The managed Python base reaches `ready` within J5's 180 s wait (the wait added by #286 / #287), J5 executes, and the shard reports planned=executed=passed=1. A setup failure must remain BLOCKED; the journey's reaction is the intended fail-closed behaviour. #286 was about the normal `installing` phase racing the first read; this run observed `failed`, so it is a different failure.

## What was checked

- The failed-step output of job 135002663249 and the `real-e2e-evidence-research-11` artifact (`14460243200`): the journey report and its blocked-step screenshot, `run.log`, `stack.log`, and `api-diagnostics`. The stack log shows three `GET /api/environment-setup 200 OK` requests and no conda/micromamba transcript. I read the artifact with `gh run download`; its origin is this run and commit, but its contents and attempt association are my observation, not independently verified.
- Source at `d57fc269`: `failSetup` (`environment-store.ts:1460`), `runManagedEnvironmentSetup` / `bootstrapStarter` / `validateStarter` (the `conda` component is entered only after micromamba is ready, so this is the Python-base create/validate phase), and `test/journey-real-request.spec.ts:73` (the BLOCKED skip).
- Previous runs: `research-11` succeeded in Nightly 44199315530 (job 134449454466) and 43984975918 (job 133711095274), both with J5 executed. In 43514552368 the job failed *after* J5 executed (a different, post-setup failure). The immediately preceding nightly, 44199315530 on `b2075e49`, ran the same provisioning path and J5 passed.
- Diff: 25 commits separate `b2075e49` from `d57fc269`; none touch `services/runner`, `packages/network`, `services/launcher`, `scripts/start-stack.sh`, `.ci/run-e2e.sh`, or `test/journey-real-request.spec.ts` / `test/helpers/environment-setup.ts`. That makes a regression from this commit in the provisioning path unlikely, but it does not identify the failing precondition.
- Not checked: the runner's operational log and the `setup.error` payload, because neither is uploaded. I did not rerun the paid Nightly to try to reproduce the state.

## Uncertainty

The inner failure is unresolved. Candidates that the missing transcript would separate: conda channel/CDN/network failure while creating the Python base, a runner disk/permission problem, or a latent race in the provisioning code. The job duration (~2 min) and the `failed` state observed before J5's 180 s deadline are consistent with a setup failure during the conda step, not with a wait timeout, but they do not choose among the candidates.

## Why report this / next verification

1. Re-run `research-11` (or the Nightly) on this commit and observe `GET /api/environment-setup`; a transition to `ready` and a J5 pass would support a transient provisioning failure, while a repeat failure would justify a code investigation.
2. Preserve the evidence next time: upload the runner's operational log for the real shard, or include `setup.state`, `setup.error` and the `components.conda` transcript in the journey report on a BLOCKED precondition. That is the one missing fact that would let the next occurrence be attributed to an external channel/network problem or to a repository defect.
3. If the transcript shows an external channel failure, this report can be closed as an environment precondition; if it shows a code error, it becomes a concrete repair issue.

items.body: ## Checklist - [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help. - [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version. - [x] A minimal reproduction and the environment are given below. ## 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem The Desktop mocked E2E spec `apps/desktop/e2e/panel-interactions.spec.ts` still expects each version-menu row to carry only its version number, while the product has rendered a producer/time suffix since commit `1d2c8726d`. The assertion is stale; the product rendering is intentional. ### Failing job - Job: [Desktop UI-ST and mocked E2E, step “Run selected Desktop mocked specs”](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/46106158736/job/140859771443) - Run: [CI #5381](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/46106158736), event `merge_group`, head `4a760cd94a91c711fdf993063fda8ae69d808264`, branch `gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-1411-1d2c8726de2618e882373a9fa4353b6aa26f8198` - Result: 252 passed / 1 failed, and Playwright retry #1 failed the same way - Only failure: `apps/desktop/e2e/panel-interactions.spec.ts:216` › `版本` › “a row opens the newest version and the picker replaces it in the same tab”, at line 239 ```ts await expect(menu.getByRole("menuitemradio")).toHaveText(["v3", "v2", "v1"]); ``` ```text Error: expect(locator).toHaveText(expected) failed Locator: locator('.workspace-panel').getByRole('menu', { name: '版本' }).getByRole('menuitemradio') - Expected - 3 + Received + 3 Array [ - "v3", - "v2", - "v1", + "v3当前会话 · 09:30", + "v2当前会话 · 09:30", + "v1当前会话 · 09:30", ] ``` `09:30` is the fixture's version `createdAt` (`2026-10-01T09:30:00.000Z`) formatted as clock time, and `当前会话` is `TEXT.workspace.currentSession` because the fixture version's `sessionId` is the open Session `session-1`. The downstream `merge-gate` job ([140877392379](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/46106158736/job/140877392379)) fails because of it: its log shows `"desktop-mocked": {"result": "failure"}` and then `Error: CI gate failed: desktop-mocked: failure; real-merge: skipped`. ### Reproduction (local, at head 4a760cd94) Setup mirrors the `desktop-mocked` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: ```bash pnpm install --frozen-lockfile node test/sync-e2e.mjs --write npm ci --prefix .e2e ln -s ../../../.e2e/node_modules apps/desktop/e2e/node_modules pnpm --filter "@sciencediscovery/desktop^..." build .e2e/node_modules/.bin/playwright install chromium ``` Run the single spec through the repository's own Desktop config (`apps/desktop/e2e/playwright.config.ts` documents this entry point): ```bash CI=1 apps/desktop/e2e/node_modules/.bin/playwright test \ --config apps/desktop/e2e/playwright.config.ts \ apps/desktop/e2e/panel-interactions.spec.ts \ --grep "a row opens the newest version" ``` Actual output (Linux x86_64, Node 22.23.5, Playwright 1.61.1, Chromium 149.0.7827.55): ```text Running 1 test using 1 worker ✘ 1 [desktop-chromium] › apps/desktop/e2e/panel-interactions.spec.ts:216:3 › 版本 › a row opens the newest version and the picker replaces it in the same tab (9.9s) ✘ 2 [desktop-chromium] › apps/desktop/e2e/panel-interactions.spec.ts:216:3 › 版本 › a row opens the newest version and the picker replaces it in the same tab (retry #1) (7.6s) - Expected - 3 + Received + 3 "v3当前会话 · 09:30" ... 1 failed [desktop-chromium] › apps/desktop/e2e/panel-interactions.spec.ts:216:3 › 版本 › a row opens the newest version and the picker replaces it in the same tab ``` An earlier attempt in this shared workspace hit `EADDRINUSE` on `127.0.0.1:4175` because another process held the port; the same result was also reproduced with an identical config on port 4275. The failure screenshot is attached. ### Root cause: the product changed, this spec did not - `apps/desktop/src/views/WorkspacePanel.tsx` (`VersionMenu`, see `versionProducer`/`versionTime` above it) now renders two spans per row plus a tooltip: ```tsx v{output.version.version} {meta} // `${producer} · ${time}` ``` - Introduced by `1d2c8726de2618e882373a9fa4353b6aa26f8198` (“fix(artifacts): resolve path-only declarations to the calling Session's own Artifact first”), which also added `.doc-version-meta` to `apps/desktop/src/styles/design.css`, widened the menu, and updated `apps/desktop/tests/workspace-panel.test.tsx` (new test “the version menu names the Session and time behind each version”). It did **not** touch `apps/desktop/e2e/panel-interactions.spec.ts`. - The spec file never changed: `apps/desktop/e2e/panel-interactions.spec.ts` is blob `cee76bda0a915f8333172590239ec4ed8a6314b3` at `4a760cd94`, at `1d2c8726d` and on `main` `e374837d`. - The new rendering is the intended behaviour, not a regression: the code comments state that a bare `v4` cannot say whether it is this conversation's work or another Session's, the CSS rule and the new unit test assert the same suffix, and the attached screenshot shows the aligned, muted meta text as designed. The same test's accessible-name assertions (`getByRole("menuitemradio", { name: "v3" })`, `aria-checked`) still pass because names match by substring; only the exact per-row text list fails. ### Impact - `merge_group` runs set `CI_DESKTOP_SPECS=all`, so this spec always runs there; any merge group whose base contains `1d2c8726d` fails deterministically (retry included), and that queue entry cannot land. Verified on run 46106158736 (base `1d2c8726d`). - The change is not on `main` yet: `/compare/e374837d...1d2c8726d` reports `status: "ahead"`, `ahead_by: 4`. `main` `e374837d` still renders the old rows and passes this spec (run [46111784577](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/46111784577), base `e374837d`: job “Desktop UI-ST and mocked E2E” [140876898579](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/46111784577/job/140876898579) succeeded). Once those four commits reach `main`, every `merge_group` run fails on this assertion until the spec is updated. - `pull_request` runs select Desktop specs from changed paths, so most PRs never run this file. PR #1512 attempt 1 (run [46108981678](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/46108981678)) failed `merge-gate` at “Require all jobs selected by this event” because its `UT` job failed, while its Desktop job succeeded — that failure is unrelated to this assertion. ### Suggested fix Update the E2E expectation rather than the product, and keep the new metadata covered: ```ts const rows = menu.getByRole("menuitemradio"); await expect(rows.locator("span").first()).toHaveText(["v3", "v2", "v1"]); await expect(rows.locator(".doc-version-meta").first()).toContainText("当前会话 · 09:30"); ``` (or `toHaveText([/^v3(当前会话 · \d{2}:\d{2})?$/u, ...])`). A follow-up could also assert that a version written by another Session is named by its title, so the unit test and this E2E spec cannot drift apart again. ## Detailed Environment Information Description - Failing head: `4a760cd94a91c711fdf993063fda8ae69d808264` (merge group of PR #1411 on base `1d2c8726de2618e882373a9fa4353b6aa26f8198`) - CI runner: GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-26.04`, Node 22.19.0, Playwright installed from `.e2e` (`npm ci --prefix .e2e`) - Local reproduction: Linux x86_64, Node 22.23.5, pnpm 11.1.2, Playwright 1.61.1, Chromium 149.0.7827.55 - Config: `apps/desktop/e2e/playwright.config.ts` (isolated Desktop Vite app on `127.0.0.1:4175`, deterministic `/api/**` fixtures, no backend or LLM) - Product files involved: `apps/desktop/src/views/WorkspacePanel.tsx`, `apps/desktop/src/styles/design.css` ## Additional Information - Not intermittent: the CI retry and a local run (both with and without `retries=1`) fail identically. - The `merge-gate` failure is downstream of this job, not a second defect. ## Version Information - `4a760cd94a91c711fdf993063fda8ae69d808264` — failing head - `1d2c8726de2618e882373a9fa4353b6aa26f8198` — commit that added the version-row metadata without updating this spec - `e374837d37a8a536483a9ef8b5d2a98bd23a5aee` — current `main`, does not contain that commit yet

items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**What happens.** Nightly run [46080401663](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/46080401663) (`main` @ `a70ef94`, `workflow_dispatch`, `profile: daily`, backend `jiuwenswarm`) fails on exactly one real case: shard `research-8`, PUCT-COMPRESS. The in-job isolated retry repeats it on a second, fresh stack and fails the same way.

**Evidence** (job [140778085432](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/46080401663/job/140778085432)):

```text
attempt 1        01:18:42  ✘ test/evolve-compression-real.spec.ts:43  (19.3m)
  Error: Search result code must be persisted as an artifact
  expect(received).toBeTruthy()  Received: undefined
  - Timeout 30000ms exceeded while waiting on the predicate
  > 172 | }, { timeout: 30_000, message: "Search result code must be persisted as an artifact" }).toBeTruthy();
        at test/evolve-compression-real.spec.ts:172:93

isolated retry   01:39:08  ✘ test/evolve-compression-real.spec.ts:43  (18.6m)
  same error, same line, run in .ci-retry/real-standard-retry (fresh worktree at a70ef94)
```

Shard accounting (`real-e2e/tagged/summary.json`, printed in the same job):

```text
| e2e-real | `a37b5e87e214` | 1 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
{"status":"FAIL",...,"passed":0,"failed":1,"provider_fault":0}
- e2e-real: PROVIDER_FAULT_RETRY_FAILED: 1
- e2e-real: PLAYWRIGHT_WORKER_FAILED: 1
```

Both problem codes are the retry's own exit classification, not a provider outage: `PROVIDER_FAULT_RETRY_FAILED` is `retryFailed(code)` from `test/support/tagged/retry.mjs` ("the retry process itself failed before producing a usable final result", here exit 1 after the case failed again), `PLAYWRIGHT_WORKER_FAILED` is the first batch exiting non-zero without a recovered case (`test/support/tagged/shared.mjs:554`), and `provider_fault: 0` means the provider-fault detector (`test/support/tagged/provider-fault.mjs`) found no gateway status or transport vocabulary in either failure text. "Account for real cases" ([job 140838600386](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/46080401663/job/140838600386)) reports the same single failure: `Planned 22; executed 22; passed 21; provider faults 0.`

**The search finished; only the delivery assertion failed.** Before line 172 the case already asserts, and passes:

- line 146: `expect(["succeeded", "budget_exhausted"]).toContain(search.status)` — the search reached a terminal state;
- line 151: the `search_finished` event agrees with the persisted run;
- line 157: `expect(expectedHash).toBeTruthy()` — the finished event names a result node (its `bestNodeIndex`) and a code hash.

So this is neither "the evolve search did not run" nor "the delivered code was queried wrongly".

**Why no artifact exists when the search finished.** Publication is a deliberately narrow path:

- `services/api/src/evolution/orchestrator.ts:888-905` (`finish`): the winner is handed to the publisher only when `status === "succeeded" && bestNodeIndex !== undefined`. A `budget_exhausted` run records its state and publishes nothing.
- `services/api/src/evolution/orchestrator.ts:910-925` (`publishWinner`): returns without publishing when no `expanded` event carries `bestNodeIndex`. That is the node-0 / seed case: no candidate beat the starting point, so there is no result to save. Intended, and pinned by the UT "nothing is published when the seed won" (`orchestrator.test.ts:928`).
- `services/api/src/bootstrap/platform.ts:346-348` (`publishResult`): returns silently when the winner source cannot be read.

Therefore one of exactly two outcomes produced this failure, and the case's own earlier assertions already confine it to them:

1. `search.status === "budget_exhausted"` — the control plane tripped the token/cost gate (`tripBudget`), the sidecar stopped, no artifact is published; or
2. `search.status === "succeeded"` with `bestNodeIndex === 0` — the seed stayed best, no artifact is published.

The spec accepts both statuses at line 146 and then still requires an artifact at line 172, so for either outcome the assertion can never pass. Its comment at line 163, "If the seed stayed best, its original artifact is also valid delivery", is not achievable either: the seed version is created only inside `publishResult` (`platform.ts:354`), which is never called on that path. The documented product behavior agrees with the code, not with the spec: `docs/zh/domains/evolve-a-solution.md:88` says only that *a search with an improvement* saves the starting point and the best code as two versions of the same result artifact.

**Why a race or a wrong query path is ruled out.** `finish` awaits `publishWinner` before the terminal record is published to subscribers, and the case looks for the artifact only after it has seen the terminal status (its own loop polls every 10 s) and re-read the `search_finished` event, then polls for another 30 s. If publication had happened, it would already be committed when the poll starts. The routes the case uses (`GET /api/sessions/:id/artifacts`, `.../artifacts/:id/versions`, `.../artifact-versions/:id/content`) are the ones the product exposes, and the same code passed this case the previous night.

**Impact.**

- Nightly/L5 goes red for a search that legitimately completed with nothing to deliver — the case's own criterion ("search finished normally") is met while its delivery criterion is unreachable.
- The failure costs two ~19 minute paid runs (attempt + retry) and cannot be told apart from a real delivery bug by reading the log.
- Every skip path above is silent: no `apiLog` line records "finished, but nothing published", so the only symptom is a 30 s predicate timeout with `Received: undefined`.
- A user who lets an evolve search run out of budget sees a finished search with no result artifact and no explanation of why.

**Suggested fix.**

1. *Use case (recommended, smallest change).* Make the delivery assertion follow the outcome the search actually had: require the artifact, its version hash and its content only when `search.status === "succeeded" && bestIndex > 0`; otherwise assert the terminal state and keep recording the scorecard, with a comment naming the product rule (nothing to deliver when the seed won or the search stopped on budget). The hash-selection and content assertions stay unchanged for an improving search.
2. *Product (a maintainer decision, not a test fix).* Publish the best-scoring candidate also on `budget_exhausted`, because the sidecar already gave that candidate its held-out score — only if the intended meaning is "a budget stop still delivers its best result". This changes the documented behavior above and the pinned UT.

Either way, add one `apiLog.info` when publication is skipped (`bestNodeIndex === 0`, `status === "budget_exhausted"`, or a candidate-read miss) so the next occurrence names its reason instead of a bare predicate timeout.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- GitHub Actions `ubuntu-26.04` runner, workflow **Nightly** (`workflow_dispatch`), `profile: daily`, `CI_E2E_BACKEND=jiuwenswarm`, `E2E_LLM_MODEL=deepseek-flash` over an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, bubblewrap sandbox, `E2E_PUCT_LLM_EVALUATION=1`; `E2E_EVOLVE_RUN_TIMEOUT_MS` unset, so the case's 7 200 000 ms budget applies (not the cause: both attempts ended after ~19 min).
- Per-shard stack: adapter on 4410 in front of the Node API on 4510, runner on 4411, memory-graph, evolve sidecar. The retry ran in `.ci-retry/real-standard-retry` with its own data dir and its own stack.
- Case: `test/evolve-compression-real.spec.ts` "PUCT-COMPRESS documented text compression search" (`@real @category:e2e @tier:l4 @judge:llm @sandbox:bubblewrap`).

### Additional Information

- **Not a regression from `a70ef94`.** That commit touches only `test/support/tagged/retry-runner.mjs`, `.ci/mocked-shards.test.mjs` and `test/support/tagged/tests/retry-environment.test.mjs` (stop the isolated retry from repeating the supplemental JiuwenSwarm checks); no product code changed.
- **The same product code passed this case hours earlier.** Nightly run [46030598150](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/46030598150) (`main` @ `e63099a`) ran shard `research-8` successfully in 24.0 min ([job 140613616137](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/46030598150/job/140613616137), 17:59:53Z-18:23:55Z), so an improving search does publish its artifact. What differs between the runs is the model's own output (the designed search budget and which candidate wins), which is why the outcome - and the failure - is not stable.
- **Evidence limits of this report.** The shard evidence artifact `real-e2e-evidence-research-8` (id 15242194973) is 329 MB, above the 32 MiB download limit available in this investigation, and the artifact download failed, so the attached `evolve-metrics.json` could not be read. To discriminate between the two outcomes, read `evolve-metrics.json` (or `evolve-<run>.json`) in that artifact and check `search.status` and `search.bestNodeIndex`; an `evolve_budget_exhausted` line in the shard `stack.log` would also name the tripped budget gate.
- **No rerun is recommended**: the failure is reproducible only by spending ~19 minutes of paid model calls, and a green rerun would hide the contract mismatch rather than fix it.

### Version Information

- `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` @ `a70ef94c4023a821c6f34a37557c5e650b79e7a0` (main, 2026-11-28).
- Nightly run 46080401663, shard `research-8`, job 140778085432; evidence artifact `real-e2e-evidence-research-8` (id 15242194973), results artifact `real-e2e-results-research-8` (id 15243130449).

items.body:
## Problem
On #381 head `fb2fe785` (Fixes #324), in Ask mode with a domain-allowlist policy, resuming a blocked retrieval takes three cards in a row:
1. **Run a shell script** (approve the original `run_shell`)
2. **Sandbox network** for the observed denied host ("Continue the sandbox retrieval blocked by this execution")
3. **Run a shell script** again, for the NEW `run_shell` that carries `network_authorization_id`

Every step is correct by itself, but together they are heavy for a single user intent ("let this retrieval reach host X").

## Expected
One network decision is enough to resume. The re-run that consumes the one-use network token should not ask again for shell approval the user just gave, as long as it is the same kind of execution.

## Proposal / security considerations
- Reuse the prior shell approval only for the token re-run: same Session/Agent/run, same Runner, and the token is consumed exactly once.
- Do not carry the approval over if the command changes materially. At minimum, show the new command in the network card or require re-approval when it differs from the blocked execution. Otherwise a token re-run becomes a way to run unreviewed code with network access.
- Never inherit Always Allow / direct-execution consent; keep child Agents and later runs excluded, as #381 already does.
- Alternative: merge steps 2 and 3 into a single card ("Allow network to X and re-run this command").

## Context
Refs #381, #324. Observed in a local box run (API + bubblewrap runner + egress gateway, scripted model).

## Verification cases
1. **Baseline repro (current behaviour)**
   - Preconditions: Ask approval mode; sandbox network `domain-allowlist` with `allowedDomains: ["pypi.org"]`; the model calls `run_shell` with `curl -sS -m 8 -o /dev/null -w 'HTTP %{http_code}\n' https://example.com/`.
   - Steps: Allow once on the shell card → allow once on the `example.com:443` network card → the model issues a NEW `run_shell` with the returned `network_authorization_id`.
   - Expected (today): A third "Run a shell script" card appears. After it is approved, the first execution has failed (`CONNECT tunnel failed`, HTTP 000) and the second has completed with HTTP 200 (2 executions in total).
2. **Same command, token re-run: single network decision**
   - Preconditions/Steps: As in 1.
   - Expected (after fix): Exactly 2 cards in total (shell, network). The token re-run with the identical command starts without another shell card and ends with HTTP 200.
3. **Different command must re-ask (security)**
   - Preconditions: As in 1, but the token re-run uses a different command (e.g. appends `; echo changed > marker.txt`).
   - Expected: A shell card is shown again, or the network card displays the new command before approval. It never runs silently.
4. **Token is one-use**
   - Steps: After case 2, the model calls `run_shell` a third time with the same `network_authorization_id`.
   - Expected: The call is rejected ("Unknown, consumed or foreign sandbox network authorization"), and no execution is started.
5. **No carry-over across scope**
   - Steps: Use the token or reused approval from (a) a child Agent, (b) a later run in the same Session, (c) another Runner.
   - Expected: Each is rejected or re-prompts, and no shell approval is reused.
6. **Deny path**
   - Steps: As in 1, but Deny the network card.
   - Expected: No re-run and no third card. The assistant reports the retrieval as blocked/incomplete, and the sandbox network settings are unchanged.

Implementation: ScienceDiscovery (ours) — PR follows within 24h. Do not pick up without a `pickup-ok` comment on this issue.

Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Product
Claimed-by: ScienceDiscovery Product
Claim-Id: 9d9ba398ccce4763b47f946f890661f6
Branch: dev2/fix/777-named-entity-decoding
Base: 7942ad1fd495cc623df67234d8a01201430da204
At: 2026-11-03T02:07:55Z

## ScienceDiscovery evidence-backed issue

**Live main:** `7942ad1fd495cc623df67234d8a01201430da204` (`test(cas): cover the multi-chunk intact layout and align the materialize contract with #708`)
**Area:** `packages/data-source` — HTML text extraction used by the free search engines
**Filed by:** ScienceDiscovery Product

### Problem

`decodeEntities` resolves only five named references (`amp`, `lt`, `gt`, `quot`, `nbsp`) and leaves every other named reference literal, so search-result titles and snippets reach the model and the report as `café`, `5–10`, `—`, `…`, `O'Brien`.

### Reproduction on live main

```
$ cd packages/data-source && node --experimental-strip-types -e '
  import("./src/web/native/html.ts").then(m => {
    for (const s of ["café — 5–10 … O'Brien", "&lt;b&gt; stays text", "♦ … ’"])
      console.log(JSON.stringify(s), "->", JSON.stringify(m.textOf(s)));
  })'
```

Actual output (main `7942ad1f`):

```
"café — 5–10 … O'Brien" -> "café — 5–10 … O'Brien"
"&lt;b&gt; stays text" -> "<b> stays text"
"♦ … ’" -> "♦ … ’"
```

Expected (browser-equivalent text): `café — 5–10 … O'Brien`, `<b> stays text` (single pass preserved), `♦ … ’`.

### Evidence (file:line on this main)

- `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.ts:27-33` — `NAMED_ENTITIES` contains exactly `amp`, `lt`, `gt`, `quot`, `nbsp`.
- `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.ts:46-53` — `decodeEntities` matches **any** named reference (`([a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]*)`) and returns `NAMED_ENTITIES.get(name) ?? match`, i.e. everything else falls through as literal text.
- `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.ts:55-58` — `textOf` (strip tags → decode → collapse) is the shared extractor.
- Call sites that turn this into user-visible text: `packages/data-source/src/web/native/free-engines.ts:64`, `:69`, `:136`, `:141`, `:183`, `:192` (titles/snippets), plus `:68`, `:135`, `:181` for result URLs.

### Impact

DuckDuckGo/Bing/Brave result titles and snippets are what `web_search` returns to the model and what reports cite; a page title like "Café culture — a review" is rendered literally, so the evidence shown to the user (and fed back into the prompt) carries entity codes instead of text. Entity-heavy pages are exactly the older/European and encyclopedia sources a science search hits often.

### Expected vs actual

- Expected: named references decode the same way a browser renders them (at minimum the typographic and Latin-1 names that appear in titles: `mdash`, `ndash`, `hellip`, `rsquo`, `lsquo`, `ldquo`, `rdquo`, `eacute`, `egrave`, `ouml`, `apos`, `middot`, `times`, `deg`, `plusmn`, …).
- Actual: only 5 names decode; the rest stay literal.

### Acceptance

1. `decodeEntities` resolves the named references it matches (full HTML5 named set, or a documented bounded table that covers at least the names listed above).
2. The single-pass guarantee from #672 is preserved: `&lt;` → `<`, `&amp;` → `&`; decoded output is never rescanned.
3. Surrogate / non-character rejection stays as it is (`�` etc. remain literal).
4. `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.test.ts` gains cases for the named references above, and the existing five keep passing.
5. No change to numeric-reference behavior (`A`, `A`, `😀`).

### Not a duplicate

Open-issue search for `entity`, `entity decode`, `html text extraction`, `named entity` returns no open report; the only entity issue is closed #672 (double decoding), whose fix this preserves. No open PR touches `html.ts` (`#663`/`#678` are the UTF-16 truncation family in other modules).

## Summary

The containment added by #857 stops an escaped scheduler write from killing the API (the #816 defect), but two recovery gaps around it remain. Both were raised as `medium, suggestion` in the 2026-11-09 review of `9bf5077f7b4104564bdee110c4f001f7b1d4a403` (F5 and F4), and neither is implemented here.

### 1. An escape raised while re-reading the run list skips the backoff entirely

`services/api/src/runs/index.ts:3738` is the file's own `finally`:

```ts
    } finally {
      scheduledSessions.delete(sessionId);
      const remaining = await store.listSessionRuns(sessionId);
```

If that read rejects (an unreadable `session-runs/` directory — the same ownership/ACL misconfiguration the cap path exists for), the promise rejects before `schedulerEscapes` is touched or `setTimeout` is reached. The `.catch` at `:3762` logs `run_scheduler_failed` and that is all: no timer, no counter, no `run_scheduler_stopped`. The comment at `:3767-3773` names this read as one of the escape sites and states the reschedule "is delayed and capped", which is not true for it.

Measured on `9bf5077f` with `listSessionRuns` mocked to reject: exactly 2 calls, no retry, no rejection reaches the process. The session silently stops scheduling while a run is still `queued`.

**Fix shape suggested in the review:** make the `finally` body tolerant so the escape still takes the backoff branch.

```ts
      let remaining: SessionRun[] = [];
      try { remaining = await store.listSessionRuns(sessionId); } catch { /* fall through with escaped already set */ }
```

### 2. After the cap, the queued run has only a server log

`services/api/src/runs/index.ts:3747`: the sixth consecutive escape (delays 500 + 1000 + 2000 + 4000 + 8000 ms ≈ 15.5 s) logs `run_scheduler_stopped` and stops. The run stays `queued` on disk, and nothing schedules it again in process — `recoverSessionRuns` only handles `running`/`blocked`, so recovery depends on the bootstrap sweep (`services/api/src/bootstrap/platform.ts:747-770`) or another HTTP-triggered `scheduleSessionRuns`.

Measured on `9bf5077f` with `updateSessionRunStatusIfCurrent` made to fail and then to succeed: **6** transition attempts and **12** `listSessionRuns` calls in 19.5 s, then **0** attempts after the fault cleared, with the run still `queued`. Realistic causes are an ownership/ACL problem that outlives 15 s, a full disk, or a long scanner hold.

**Impact:** the chat never starts and the user sees neither a failure nor a message, while #816's expected result asks for an actionable error on the affected run when persistence cannot recover.

## What it should do

- An escape raised inside the `finally` must take the same delayed-and-capped path as an escape raised inside the loop; the comment already promises it.
- After the cap, the affected run should carry an error the API returns (mark it `failed`, or `interrupted` with a reason), or the stop should become a slow fixed retry — `SCHEDULER_RETRY_MAX_MS` already allows 30 s.

## Why this is not in #857

The review classified both as `medium, suggestion`, and the second is marked `[Needs a person]`: choosing between "fail the run with an actionable error" and "retry slowly forever" changes what a user sees after an unrecoverable state write, so it is a decision, not a mechanical fix. #857 carries only its must-fix (the retry closure dropped `executionGovernance`).

## Not implemented

Nothing in this issue is implemented and no pull request is open for it.
items.title: [Bug] a queued run can end up with nothing scheduled: the escaped re-read skips the backoff, and after the cap only a server log remains

## What happens

`test/journey-custom-mcp.spec.ts` → **"Agent uses selected custom MCP servers across runs"** (test declared at `:203`, step 6 `等待修复并恢复调用`, body at `:314`) fails at `test/journey-custom-mcp.spec.ts:332`:

```
  1) [mocked] › ../test/journey-custom-mcp.spec.ts:203:1 › journey-custom-mcp.spec › Agent uses selected custom MCP servers across runs › 6. 等待修复并恢复调用

    Error: expect(received).toBeGreaterThan(expected)

    Expected: > 2
    Received:   2

      330 |       expect(terminal.status, terminal.error).toBe("completed");
      331 |       const recovered = await invocations();
    > 332 |       expect(recovered.length).toBeGreaterThan(before);
          |                                ^
```

Everything before the assertion in step 6 succeeds: the repair card `执行受阻` shows `等待 MCP 修复` with the disabled source id, `GET /api/sessions/<id>/mcp/invocations` stays at 2 while blocked, the server is re-enabled, `已修复，重新检查` is clicked, and `waitForRunTerminal` returns `completed`.

What the run then shows: the assistant's last message in that run is `MCP RECOVERED`, which the scripted model only emits **after** its `mcp_recovered_call` step (`test/journey-custom-mcp.spec.ts:243-247`):

```ts
[
  { tool: "mcp_readiness", arguments: { action: "wait", reason: "This task requires the selected echo source", sourceIds: [second.id] } },
  { tool: "mcp_recovered_call", arguments: { sourceId: second.id, toolId: second.toolId, input: { text: "mcp recovered" } } },
  { text: "MCP RECOVERED" },
],
```

So the scripted model did emit `mcp_recovered_call`, and the run continued past it, but no MCP invocation was recorded for that turn: `/api/sessions/<id>/mcp/invocations` still lists exactly the 2 invocations from the earlier runs (`custom-cbf8e…`, `custom-cea28…`), and the captured trace resource `0000f751….json` holds the same 2. The recovered call therefore never reached `McpSourceCatalog`/broker (`packages/artifact-manager/src/mcp-workspace-tools.ts` `mcpReadiness.invoke`), and the failure is silent to the user: the run completes and the message claims recovery.

## Where it is seen (evidence only)

The same journey, same assertion, fails on three unrelated heads:

| run | job | head | shard window (UTC) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [42619667305](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42619667305) | [129188246374](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42619667305/job/129188246374) | `9bf5077f7b` (#857 tip) | 13:38–13:58 failure |
| [42622133086](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42622133086) | [129181494939](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42622133086/job/129181494939) | `87c5da950b` (`codex/conversation-proxy-resources`) | 13:39–13:59 failure |
| [42615122979](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42615122979) | [129160327871](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42615122979/job/129160327871) | `127bb1fdef` (merge queue, `pr-1005`) | 12:34–12:54 failure |

It also passes on other heads in the same window, including main running the journey while the two 13:3x failures were in flight:

- main `c3678320ac`: run [42621321893](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42621321893) job [129188930633](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42621321893/job/129188930633), `✓ 21 … Agent uses selected custom MCP servers across runs (44.4s)` at 13:39:17Z, shard success (13:34–13:49).
- main `9feafa2730`: run [42562181452](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42562181452) job [128981184690](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42562181452/job/128981184690), `✓ 21` at 04:38:35Z. That shard job is red overall because of a different journey (`journey-first-run.spec.ts:59`), so the shard verdict alone does not describe this journey.

`L2 E2E (mocked, standard-config)` outcomes for completed runs created between 11:30Z and 14:00Z (jobs read one by one; cancelled runs excluded): **3 failure / 16 success**, and the three failures are the table above. Two of the green runs are `dev2/fix/upload-windows-reserved-names` `0c5f26ab03` (13:33:34Z) and `dev/884-bug-comparing-two-binary-artifact-versio` `cefe1ebd79` (13:25:34Z).

## Not caused by the #857 diff

#857 (`9bf5077f7b`) changes exactly two files, `services/api/src/runs/index.ts` and `services/api/src/runs/index.test.ts` (+210/−23); the merge ref `fdf61b56798086e573368bc82120e91e8c5cc52b` for its failing job has parents `9feafa27` + `9bf5077f` and nothing else. The two other failing heads carry none of that diff. The failing journey exercises custom-MCP registration, the repair wait and `mcp_recovered_call` — not the scheduler's delayed retry pass. #857 is linked only because its shard run is one of the three observations, not as the cause.

## What is not yet known

Whether this is a product race (the recovered call is dropped or rejected after `catalog.refresh`, so a real user also loses the recovered invocation while the message claims it ran) or a test that stops waiting too early (it asserts the invocation list immediately after the terminal state). The two need different fixes, and the 3-of-19 rate above is the only discriminator so far: a deterministic loss is a product gap, an occasional one points at the wait.

Not run: local reproduction of the journey (20 consecutive runs on a local stack). The stack could not be started in the reporting environment — the pnpm store lives on a read-only home, the pinned Chromium download did not complete, and the JiuwenSwarm virtualenv install had not finished when this was filed. No code was changed for this report.

items.body:
## User outcome

A reader of a literature report can tell what was searched, what could not be searched, how evidence was selected, and why the report uses its output language.

This consolidates the unfinished scope of #416 and #419. Their original reports, artifacts and screenshots remain the historical evidence. This is an administrative consolidation, not a claim that either feature has been delivered.

## Scope and acceptance

- [ ] Saved literature reports include a concise Methods/Search section naming sources actually used, fallback sources, search date, queries and applicable date/language filters.
- [ ] Record retrieved/screened/included counts when measured. Otherwise state "not computed"; never invent counts or imply a systematic review for a brief scan.
- [ ] Disclose source failures and resulting coverage limitations. A provider failure must not silently narrow the evidence while the report claims broader coverage.
- [ ] State the preprint, grey-literature and non-English inclusion policy, or explicitly mark these categories out of scope. Do not require every brief scan to search every category.
- [ ] Define and document report-language behavior for explicit language requests, English/Chinese UI locales and no explicit output-language request. An English report answering an English prompt is not itself a defect. Provide a locale-aware summary if that is the selected policy.
- [ ] Validate saved artifacts as well as the visible report using the original brief CRISPR/SCD scan and deterministic provider fixtures covering fallback, provider failure and unavailable counts. Verify explicit language requests and both UI locales; report real-provider verification separately from mocked coverage.

## Boundaries

Claim excerpts, citation fidelity, unverifiable evidence states and Quick/Deep review coverage remain in #669. A mandatory standard-of-care comparison table is not part of this issue; that optional template proposal is recorded in #417. Keep disclosure proportional to a brief scan and avoid turning it into a mandatory systematic review.

items.author: agent-ci-infra-bot[bot]
items.body:
Actions failure classification: **code** (real-E2E score aggregation), triggered by a transient model timeout.

Run: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/45897487622 (attempt 1, `workflow_dispatch`, profile `release`)

Head SHA: `9e91f78b751d142ee4d8f23f1c066e23f42e7861`

## Failing jobs

- Gate / L4/L5 real E2E / Account for real cases: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/45897487622/job/140362864155 (step `Reconcile every planned identity`)
- Gate / merge-gate: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/45897487622/job/140363083494 (`Error: CI gate failed: real-scheduled: failure`, `.ci/tier-policy.mjs:164`)
- `Publish the release` was skipped.

## Current behavior

Every planned real case executed and passed, yet the Biomni accounting fails on one case:

```
### Real E2E: FAIL
Planned 69; executed 69; passed 69; provider faults 0.
Biomni public tasks: 44/45; failed; non-regression certified: false.
- da-20-1: MISSING_OR_DUPLICATE_METRICS
```

and in the case table that case keeps the *first* attempt's status:

```
| da-20-1 | incomplete | failed | not_run | — | — | — | — | — | — / — | MISSING_OR_DUPLICATE_METRICS |
```

Because `mean_score`, `sum_e2e_ms` and `p95_peak_rss_gib` then stay `incomplete`, `biomni-gate.json` reports `failed`, `real-report` exits 1, `merge-gate` reports `real-scheduled: failure`, and the release is not published.

## Root cause (two documents for one case, both from the same shard)

`da-20-1` needed one case-level retry, and both attempts' scorecards were uploaded in the same shard artifact.

1. `da-20-1` is carried by shard `research-25` (`CI_BIOMNI_CASE_ID: da-20-1`, job https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/45897487622/job/140175290420).
2. Attempt 1 failed after 3.0h on a transient model slowdown, not a product assertion:

   ```
   journey report (FAIL): .ci-results/real-standard/e2e-real/journey-reports/.../report.html
   Error: Research did not settle with trace.md and answer.txt within the end-to-end budget
   ✘  1 [real] › ../test/biomnibench-da-swarm.spec.ts:78:3 › BiomniBench-da-20-1 ... (3.0h)
   1 failed
   Repeating 1 failed case(s): playwright:test/biomnibench-da-swarm.spec.ts::...BiomniBench-da-20-1%20Public%20analysis%20da-20-1
   ```

   Its `finally` block still wrote `benchmark-metrics.json` with `integration_status: "failed"`, `evaluation.status: "not_run"` (`test/biomnibench-da-swarm.spec.ts:93,213,220`), into `.ci-results/real-standard/e2e-real/test-results/<test>/` (`.ci/run-e2e.sh:237` sets `E2E_OUTPUT_DIR="$results_root/test-results"`, `test/playwright.config.ts:52`).
3. The bounded retry ran in an isolated worktree and passed in 46.3m, writing a second `benchmark-metrics.json` into `.ci-results/real-standard-retry/e2e-real/test-results/<test>/`. That is deliberate: `test/support/tagged/shared.mjs:443-458` keeps one evidence directory per attempt (`retryResultsPath = <CI_RESULTS_DIR>/<instance>-retry`), so a retry never erases the attempt it repeats. The shard's shared plan correctly reports `passed 1`, `passed after retry 1`.
4. `.ci/prepare-real-e2e-results.mjs:80-100` walks the whole `.ci-results` tree and stages **every** file named `benchmark-metrics.json`, so a retried shard uploads two scorecards for one case. Observable in the same job log: `Staged 5 real E2E score/plan files.` and `With the provided path, there will be 5 files uploaded`, where a non-retried case shard stages 4 (`plan.json`, `summary.json`, `preflight.json`, one scorecard — e.g. `research-20`, job https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/45897487622/job/140175286285: `4 files uploaded`).
5. `.ci/biomni-gate.mjs:139-145` collects those documents and requires exactly one per case id:

   ```js
   const matches = documents.filter(doc => doc.case_id === biomniCase(entry));
   ...
   if (matches.length !== 1) { state.reason = 'MISSING_OR_DUPLICATE_METRICS'; ... }
   ```

   Two matches fail the case even though one of them is a complete, valid, official scorecard. The rendered row shows `delivery=failed`, `evaluation=not_run` — those fields come from `matches[0]`, so the gate kept the superseded attempt's document and never looked at the passing one. The plan-level accounting does accept a retried pass (`verifyResults` marks it `passed_after_retry`); only the Biomni metrics gate does not.

So the defect is the aggregation path, not the workflow and not the shard: a daily/release run that recovers any Biomni case with the documented retry can never certify, and the failure is reported as `MISSING_OR_DUPLICATE_METRICS` instead of naming the retry.

## Suggested fix direction (one place, fail-closed preserved)

Make the metrics gate attempt-aware instead of "exactly one file": for each planned case, validate every document that carries its `case_id` and accept the single one that passes `validateMetrics` (`integration_status == "passed"`, evaluation `scored`, matching identity). Keep failing when zero validate (missing/incomplete) and when more than one validates (a genuine duplicate). Alternatively (or additionally) let `.ci/prepare-real-e2e-results.mjs` stage only the scorecard of the attempt the shard's `summary.json` recorded as final, while the full evidence tree stays in `real-e2e-evidence-*`. Either way the report should say "passed after retry", not "missing or duplicate".

Regression test: in `.ci/biomni-gate.test.mjs` (next to `missing, duplicate, foreign, incomplete and non-finite metrics fail closed`), build one shard directory holding a failed `not_run` scorecard for a case plus the retried passing scorecard, and assert the suite certifies the case; a second assertion must keep two *valid* scorecards failing closed.

## What was checked and what it rules out

- Job log of `research-25` (attempt 1 failure, retry decision, retry pass, staged/uploaded file counts), the reconcile output and case table of job 140362864155, and the artifact inventory of run 45897487622 (`real-e2e-plan` 15154118226, `real-e2e-results-research-25` 15171330528 — 4229 bytes vs ~3.2 KB for non-retried shards). Artifact contents could not be downloaded in this environment (the download helper failed for every artifact), so the two-scorecard conclusion rests on the documented staging code plus the 5-vs-4 file count, not on reading the zip.
- Source at the failed SHA: `.ci/biomni-gate.mjs`, `.ci/prepare-real-e2e-results.mjs`, `.ci/real-report.mjs`, `test/support/tagged/shared.mjs`, `test/support/tagged/retry-runner.mjs`, `.ci/run-e2e.sh`, `test/playwright.config.ts`, `test/biomnibench-da-swarm.spec.ts`, `.github/workflows/real-e2e.yml`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.
- This is **not** the previous Release failure: run https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/45586964125 attempt 1 failed with `Planned 69; executed 68`, `- research-23: SHARD_EVIDENCE_MISSING`, `NOT_RUN ... da-19-4` (a cancelled shard), and its attempt 2 is green. Here every shard uploaded evidence and every identity executed.
- It is **not** a `.github/workflows/` problem: no workflow change is needed, and the merge-gate failure is only the documented consequence of `real-report` exiting 1.
- Existing Issues: searched for `MISSING_OR_DUPLICATE_METRICS`, `real-report`, `duplicate metrics`, `biomni` + `retry`, `passed after retry` — nothing tracks this aggregation gap. #1238 / #1222 / #1071 are the external model-timeout family that produced the *first* attempt; they do not cover the retry scorecard collision. Nothing in `.ci/biomni-gate.mjs` or `.ci/prepare-real-e2e-results.mjs` changed on `main` between `9e91f78` and today's main, so the defect is still present.

## Impact

- A release (`L5`) cannot be published whenever any single Biomni case needs the retry that daily/release profiles enable, and the failure looks like missing evidence rather than a recovered case.
- `merge-gate` reports `real-scheduled: failure`; `mean_score` / `sum_e2e_ms` / `p95_peak_rss_gib` remain `incomplete`, so no quality evidence is published either.
- Same for `Nightly` (`daily`), which also enables case retries.

## Not done here

No rerun was requested for run 45897487622 (this analysis has no rerun permission, and a rerun would only paper over the aggregator gap). No workflow change and no merge were attempted.

items.body:
## What happens

Informational text in the desktop sidebar sits below the WCAG AA minimum for normal-size text (4.5:1). Measured from computed styles on the rendered shell, not from the stylesheet alone:

| Text | Element | Colour | Background | Measured | Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `还没有会话` | `.side-empty` (13 px) | `#a6a6a6` | `#f5f5f5` | **2.23:1** | 4.5:1 |
| `8周前` | `.side-session-time` (12 px) | `#808080` | `#f5f5f5` | **3.62:1** | 4.5:1 |
| `8周前` on a hovered row | `.side-session-time` (12 px) | `#808080` | `#e8e8e8` | **3.22:1** | 4.5:1 |
| `科学探索 更高效` | `.landing-tagline` (14 px, zh) | `#8c8c8c` | `#ffffff` | **3.36:1** | 4.5:1 |

The two that carry information are the ones that matter: the empty-state line tells the user the group has no sessions, and the timestamp is the only way to tell two sessions of the same title apart in the list. At 12 px and 3.2:1 the timestamp is the hardest-to-read text on the surface.

## What is expected

4.5:1 for text at these sizes. The muted intent can stay: on the sidebar's `#f5f5f5`, `#6a6a6a` reaches 5.0:1 and still reads as secondary. The exact value is the maintainers' call; the requirement is that the hint and the timestamp clear 4.5:1.

## Where it comes from

- `apps/desktop/src/styles/design.css:445-450` — `.side-session-time { color: #808080; font-size: 12px; }`
- `apps/desktop/src/styles/design.css:472-476` — `.side-empty { color: #a6a6a6; font-size: 13px; }`
- `apps/desktop/src/styles/landing.css:106-118` — `.landing-tagline { color: #8c8c8c; }` (14 px under `:root:lang(zh)`)
- Tokens behind the same family: `apps/desktop/src/styles/tokens.css:34-36` — `--muted: #777777`, `--muted-light: #a6a6a6`, `--text-faint: #8c8c8c`. `--muted` measures 4.48:1 on white and 4.11:1 on `#f5f5f5`, i.e. it misses the same threshold by a hair wherever it is used on a grey surface.

So the values are per-rule literals rather than one token, which is why the same intent lands on three different ratios.

## Impact

Users with reduced contrast sensitivity — and anyone on a dim or glossy laptop screen — cannot comfortably read the session timestamps or the empty-state line. Nothing here blocks a task and no data is affected; the cost is legibility of text the interface chose to keep visible.

This is not a colour-scheme request: the surface is light-mode only and the numbers above are the shipped values.

## How to reproduce

Desktop shell only, with the repository's own desktop harness (`apps/desktop/e2e`, `/api/**` answered by `fixtures.ts`, so no backend):

```
PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=<browsers> \
  apps/desktop/e2e/node_modules/.bin/playwright test \
  --config apps/desktop/e2e/playwright.config.ts
```

A temporary spec (not part of any branch) seeds one session and an empty standalone group, then for every element holding its own text node walks up to the first non-transparent background and computes the WCAG ratio from `getComputedStyle`; the four rows above are that output.

## Environment

- Desktop shell built from source at `main` `cb18c53447b529b44f846c073fa444562b97cc69` (`apps/desktop/src/styles/design.css` blob `1e3f047443ef2059972ec85292da2018d45456ee` matches that commit).
- Windows 11 + WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04; Node 22.23.4; Playwright 1.65.1 with `chromium_headless_shell-1255`; desktop Vite dev server on 4175; interface language zh-CN; viewport 1280×720.
- Device scale factor 1, no OS-level contrast or forced-colours setting.

## Version Information

- Source: `main` `cb18c534`, desktop (`apps/desktop`).
- Reproduced with the repository's desktop e2e harness; the probe spec was temporary and is not part of any branch.

items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help. #1454 is the sibling report (the control plane's own 5 s `get` sweep, and the per-frame snapshot); this report is the remaining path it does not cover, and #1469 fixes #1454 without touching it.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version: `main` at `2b8e4673` still polls this route, and #1469 does not change it.
- [x] The description below carries source locations. No live run was made on this host, as stated under Additional Information.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary.** #1454 asked for two things and #1469 delivers both — the API no longer sweeps a running research with `get`, and an SSE frame now carries a delta — but the desktop still asks the session's research list every 5 s while any research is live, and that route answers with **every research's whole tree**, `result` included. So the cost #1454 described (a full read and re-serialisation per 5 s, per research, on the single ASGI worker that also serves the stream) survives on the client path, and it grows with the number of researches in the session rather than with what changed.

**Current code path** (`main` `2b8e4673`):

1. `apps/desktop/src/app/use-idea-researches.ts` — `LIVE_POLL_MS = 5_000`; the effect starts `setInterval(() => void loadRef.current(), LIVE_POLL_MS)` whenever `views.some(isLive)`. `load()` calls `listIdeaResearches(client, sessionId)`.
2. `apps/desktop/src/api/idea-tree.ts` → `GET /api/sessions/:id/idea-tree/research` → `services/api/src/idea-tree/research.ts` `invoke(sessionId, "list")` → sidecar `POST /idea-tree/research/command {operation: "list"}`.
3. `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/vendor/idea_tree/research_service.py` — the list branch is `return dict(items=[view(s) for s in states])`, and `view(s)` builds `graph=engine.graph()` (`research.py`: every node, `result = json.dumps(n['stages'])`, the insight log). Nothing in the list payload is a summary: the caller receives the same document `get` would answer.
4. The cards only need `research` (status, tokens, phase, reason) from that payload; the tree in it is discarded by every consumer of the list.

**Minimal reproduction.** Open a session with three researches, one of them running, and watch the sidecar's command log: `{"operation":"list"}` arrives every 5 s for as long as that one research runs, and each answer is the sum of all three researches' trees. With a 100-node tree per research and a `stages` text per node, that is the payload #1454 measured for a single research, multiplied by the session.

**Expected behaviour.**

- The list the cards render should be a summary per research (id, status, phase, round, tokens/`usageKnown`, reason, `updatedAt`), not the full graph — or the desktop should poll only what it draws.
- A live research that has a stream listener already receives its state on that stream; the list read should not be the thing that keeps it fresh.
- Nothing here changes what an explicit `get` answers: that stays the heavy, complete document.

This is independent of #1469's frame format: it is the *list* route and the desktop's poll interval, both untouched there.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

Source inspection only; no running stack on this host, so no OS/hardware specifics are claimed. Repository `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, `main` `2b8e4673bbb438cad5ceaa1babe224afaf4f710e`. The affected surfaces are the desktop shell (any OS) and the API's sidecar command worker.

### Additional Information

- #1454 (P2, closed by #1469) named the API's own `setInterval` sweep and the per-frame snapshot. Its reasoning — "720 full-document reads and parses per hour, on the single ASGI worker that also serves the SSE stream and every control request" — applies unchanged to this route.
- #1456 made `state_for()` and `list` read-only, so this is cost, not writes.
- A cheap partial fix exists without touching the wire format: the desktop could subscribe to the live research's stream (it already does when the panel is open) and stop polling the list while the panel holds the only live research.

### Version Information

- `main`: `2b8e46736826ff723e899057e8872835075d77e` (2026-11-26)
- Related: #1454, #1456, #1469
