items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help. #1435 is the PUCT report this is the sibling of, and #1467 fixes it for PUCT only, scoping itself there; #1465 and #1466 touch the same OpenEvolve reporter but not this behaviour.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version (source revision below): with #1467's cancellation marker in place, the OpenEvolve reporter still ignores it.
- [x] The description below carries source locations and a reproduction plan. No OpenEvolve search was run on this host, as stated under Additional Information.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary.** #1467 makes a budget stop distinguishable from broken work for PUCT runs. The OpenEvolve engine shares `completion.py`, the domains and the event stream, but its reporter never uses the new cancellation channel, so a run that exhausts its token budget on OpenEvolve still produces exactly what #1435 reported.

**Current code path** (`main` `8444aa6b`, plus #1467 head `83a9228a` for the PUCT side):

1. `openevolve_engine.py:355-365` — when the run is already stopped, `call()` returns `("", "")` with no marker, and the `complete(...)` call passes only `on_failure`. `completion.py` now offers a separate `on_cancelled` sink, so this side cannot tell an abandoned request from a model that answered with nothing.
2. `openevolve_engine.py:367-372` — empty code becomes `note_empty(iteration, "the model returned an empty reply")`, and `_node` (`:516-521`) keeps that sentence as the node's `error` and appends it to `failures`. The expanded event carries `valid: false` and no `category`, so the web and desktop verdicts fall through to `failed` and the row reads "did not run" / 没跑起来 — the candidate is blamed for the budget.
3. `openevolve_engine.py:601-615` — `finish()` evaluates the best candidate on the held-out shards through the same domain. With the stop set, `script_domain` / `test_gate_domain` / `scorecard_domain` return the cancelled marker and `valid: false`, so this logs `best candidate failed on test shards: <reason>` and leaves `best_test_score` null: both the false claim and the lost score that #1435 asked to remove and keep. (Before #1467 the same branch logs `the search was stopped`; afterwards it logs the cancel reason. Either way the sentence claims a candidate failure that did not happen.)
4. `openevolve_engine.py:556-567` — `note_outcome` copies the framework's `stop_reason` verbatim, so a token-budget stop still reaches `search_finished` as `max_iters`; the sidecar's `StopGate` cause is never consulted, unlike the PUCT reporter.

**Expected behaviour** (the same acceptance #1435 states, for the engine the picker also offers):

- an abandoned model call is not reported as "the model returned an empty reply", and a candidate nobody measured is not shown as one that did not run;
- a token/cost budget stop keeps one bounded held-out evaluation of the winner, and a cancelled or unrun evaluation says "not evaluated: cancelled by <cause>" instead of "best candidate failed", with the cause retained;
- the terminal event keeps the true cause instead of `max_iters`;
- a user stop or a hard wall-clock limit still runs no finalization.

**Minimal reproduction plan.** Start an OpenEvolve run with a small `maxTokens` (so `EvolveOrchestrator.checkSpendBudget()` trips the token gate while expansions are in flight) and a frozen evaluator with reserved test shards. The resulting `events.ndjson` shows the "empty reply" errors for the nodes in flight, no `cancelled` category anywhere, `bestTestScore` absent with the "best candidate failed on test shards" warning, and `stopReason: max_iters`. A unit-level reproduction is smaller: drive `OpenEvolveEngine._Reporter` with a `StopGate` already stopped and a domain that returns the cancelled marker — the reporter still logs the test-shard failure and emits `max_iters`.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

Source inspection only; no OpenEvolve search was executed on this host, so no OS/hardware specifics are claimed. Repository `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`: `main` at `8444aa6b26826ff723e899057e8872835075d77e` plus PR #1467 head `83a9228ab82f6cfda64f279c3b73399ec4050f98`. The affected engine is selectable on every platform from the Evolve algorithm picker (OpenEvolve), so any OS a user runs the desktop or web surface on is affected.

### Additional Information

- #1435 reports the PUCT path and #1467 fixes it there; that review explicitly scoped itself to PUCT, so this is filed as the sibling gap rather than a change request on #1467.
- The shared pieces already exist — `cancellation.py` (`StopGate`, `mark_cancelled`, `stop_allows_finalization`, `cancelled_text`) and `completion.py`'s `on_cancelled` — so the OpenEvolve side mostly needs the plumbing PUCT received, not new machinery.
- #1465 and #1466 both rewrite `openevolve_engine.py` (the `evaluated` event shape and the attempt/depth counters), so a fix here is cheapest after those land.
- Observed on `main` today the same user-visible sentences are produced by a stopped OpenEvolve run: "the model returned an empty reply" rows, a "best candidate failed on test shards: the search was stopped" warning, `bestTestScore: null`, and `stopReason: max_iters`.

### Version Information

- `main`: `8444aa6b26826ff723e899057e8872835075d77e` (2026-11-26T13:49:13Z)
- PR #1467 head reviewed alongside: `83a9228ab82f6cfda64f279c3b73399ec4050f98`
- Related: #1435 (PUCT report), #1467 (PUCT fix), #1465 / #1466 (same reporter)

items.author: moShangLouTou
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] Searched related open issues; #668 tracks the external-runtime bridge, but does not cover the Desktop capability-selection and runtime-editing defects below.
- [ ] Verified against the latest release (this report is based on the source revision below).
- [x] Included source locations, minimal reproduction steps, environment, and validation scope.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

Desktop Settings can create MCP servers and Specialists, but the Specialist form does not consistently match execution behavior. Two source-confirmed defects affect capability selection and preservation of runtime settings; two related UI gaps expose incomplete external-runtime support as if it were available.

These findings come from tracing the form, persistence, session binding, and task execution paths. The reproduction steps below describe scenarios to verify; they have not been executed as browser/product journeys in this review.

#### 1. “Specific capabilities” does not restrict the Specialist to its selected capabilities

Steps:
1. Enable connectors A and B for the parent session.
2. Create a Native Specialist and choose only connector A under specific capabilities.
3. Bind the Specialist to a session, or dispatch a task to it.
4. Inspect the resulting tool catalog or attempt to use connector B.

Expected: B is unavailable, as the form explicitly promises that unselected capabilities remain invisible and uncallable even when globally enabled.

Source behavior: both session and child-task assembly union the Specialist lists with the parent/session lists. B remains in the effective connector set. Skills are also unioned. The stored schema has no separate capability-access mode, so choosing an empty specific list also serializes identically to full access.

Sources at the reviewed revision:
- [Form serialization](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/36476b0ea302b6de3897154f83c3c7c87dc6ec89/apps/desktop/src/views/settings/system/SpecialistForm.tsx#L117-L125)
- [UI capability promise](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/36476b0ea302b6de3897154f83c3c7c87dc6ec89/apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts#L1677-L1687)
- [Session capability union](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/36476b0ea302b6de3897154f83c3c7c87dc6ec89/services/api/src/runs/index.ts#L3365-L3375)
- [Child-task capability union](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/36476b0ea302b6de3897154f83c3c7c87dc6ec89/services/api/src/runs/index.ts#L1905-L1912)

#### 2. Editing a Specialist drops advanced runtime options

Steps:
1. Configure an external Specialist with runtime options such as `fallback: false`, `timeoutSeconds`, `reasoningEffort`, or `execution` through the supported runtime configuration path.
2. Open that Specialist in Desktop Settings.
3. Change only its name or description and save.
4. Read the saved Specialist record.

Expected: unrelated runtime options survive the edit.

Source behavior: the draft retains only runtime kind and model, and `runtimeOf()` reconstructs the entire runtime object from those two fields. The update replaces the previous runtime object, removing all the other settings. In particular, losing `fallback: false` allows unavailable-runtime recovery again.

Sources:
- [Draft and runtime serialization](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/36476b0ea302b6de3897154f83c3c7c87dc6ec89/apps/desktop/src/views/settings/system/SpecialistForm.tsx#L94-L124)
- [Specialist update and normalization](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/36476b0ea302b6de3897154f83c3c7c87dc6ec89/services/api/src/store.ts#L4986-L4993)
- [Fallback decision](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/36476b0ea302b6de3897154f83c3c7c87dc6ec89/services/api/src/specialist-runtime/agent.ts#L86-L93)

#### 3. External-runtime Specialists can select capabilities that are not bridged to them

Create a Codex, Claude Code, or ACP Specialist and add an MCP connector or Skill. Dispatch an explicit `task(specialistId=...)` to that Specialist.

The external adapter receives only a fixed platform-tool allowlist. MCP tools and `read_skill` are filtered out, so saving the capability selection does not make those tools callable through the platform bridge.

This implementation gap is already tracked in #668. The Desktop-specific problem is that the new form offers the same capability configuration without explaining or restricting this unsupported combination. Either complete the bridge under #668 or make the supported combinations clear in the form.

Source: [External adapter tool filtering](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/36476b0ea302b6de3897154f83c3c7c87dc6ec89/services/api/src/specialist-runtime/agent.ts#L70-L78).

#### 4. Selecting an external-runtime Specialist in the composer does not explain explicit delegation

Create a Codex Specialist, select it in the session's expert picker, and send a message. Session binding applies its instructions to the main agent; it does not switch the main conversation to Codex. A child task that merely inherits the session Specialist also does not activate the external runtime without an explicit Specialist ID in the task input.

#668 intentionally requires explicit `task(specialistId=...)` targeting. This is a UI guidance gap, not a request to remove that contract: the picker/form should explain how to invoke the configured external runtime and distinguish session instruction binding from external task execution.

Sources:
- [Session Specialist binding](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/36476b0ea302b6de3897154f83c3c7c87dc6ec89/services/api/src/runs/index.ts#L2440-L2443)
- [Explicit runtime activation condition](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/36476b0ea302b6de3897154f83c3c7c87dc6ec89/services/api/src/runs/index.ts#L1697-L1704)

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Desktop React application and API service, source checkout on Linux/WSL2.
- Node.js v22.19.0; pnpm 11.1.2.
- The capability assembly and serialization findings do not depend on GPU hardware or a particular model provider.

### Additional Information

Validation performed:

```sh
pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop exec tsx --import ./tests/support/css-preload.mjs --test tests/api-settings.test.ts tests/settings-pages.test.tsx
```

Result: 62 tests passed, 0 failed. These tests cover request construction and static page behavior, not the execution scenarios above. No service startup, browser/E2E journey, or live external-provider invocation was performed.

The MCP create/save/test/catalog path did not reveal a definite blocker during source review. Connection testing can succeed while the server remains disabled; actual use requires enabling the service and selecting the source in effective session settings. A passing connection test alone is not evidence that a Specialist can use it.

Suggested acceptance:
- Specific capability selection matches its UI promise in both session and delegated-task execution, including an empty selection.
- Editing unrelated Specialist fields preserves advanced runtime options.
- External-runtime capability limitations and explicit invocation requirements are accurately represented in Desktop until #668 supplies the missing bridge.
- Add targeted coverage for these boundaries and verify the corresponding Desktop journeys.

### Version Information

Reviewed source revision: `36476b0ea302b6de3897154f83c3c7c87dc6ec89`.

Related: #668 and #575.

items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched related issues; the evaluator-validation gap below is distinct from #1435 and #1436.
- [x] The relevant generation guidance and validation paths remain present in the latest upstream main inspected below.
- [x] Environment, a self-contained reproduction and the distinction between observed facts and proposed improvements are included.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

A generated `custom_script` evaluator can pass the current preparation/probe workflow while failing to enforce its own per-call runtime contract or protect scoring inputs. The immediate defects are in an experiment-generated script, not a checked-in scheduling evaluator. The repository-level defect is that the generation/validation workflow gives insufficient coverage of these failure modes before freezing the script and spending the search budget.

**Observed experiment and attribution**

A Windows desktop PUCT scheduling experiment on 2026-11-26 used `schedule(workloads, speeds) -> list[int]`, with a one-second per-call limit. Its frozen evaluator generated instances, recomputed an independent LPT baseline, validated assignments and scored `baseline_makespan / (baseline_makespan + candidate_makespan)`.

The original conversation records the design agent replacing SIGALRM with a daemon thread plus Queue watchdog for Windows compatibility, then validating the change with the fast LPT baseline and declaring it hardened. The resulting implementation uses `Queue.get(timeout=1)` but never terminates the timed-out thread. Three scored candidates later contained per-instance timeout errors. The frozen code establishes that work can continue after timeout; the historical logs do not quantify how much residual thread contention affected subsequent scores.

A separate direct check against that actual frozen evaluator confirmed an input-integrity defect: a synthetic candidate that replaces the received workload list with zeros and returns legal machine indices receives `score: 1.0`, with an empty error. Baseline makespan is calculated before candidate execution, while candidate makespan is calculated afterward from the same mutable objects. There is no evidence that the experiment's winning candidate exploited this defect.

**Why the current preparation/probe can miss it**

- The local Step 2 check in `skills/evolve-design/SKILL.md` explicitly checks only that the baseline executes and emits a number, delegating damaged-candidate checks to the server.
- `references/custom-script.md` specifies result/shard contracts and exception diagnostics, but not a reliable per-call timeout primitive or immutable scoring inputs.
- `proposal.ts:checkEvaluator()` checks script presence, size and required environment-variable markers. Runtime correctness is left to the probe.
- The `custom_script` probe tests the baseline, a hollowed-out candidate, unimportable candidates and baseline repeatability. It does not inject a slow/nonterminating entrypoint or an input-mutating entrypoint, or verify that work stops after the per-case timeout.
- The outer evaluator process has a killable timeout, but that does not enforce each individual call's deadline or prevent timed-out threads from affecting later cases inside that evaluator process.
- Repeating the fast baseline cannot establish timing stability of later near-deadline candidates. The current noise comparison uses the baseline-versus-damaged score gap, not the smaller improvement scale being measured.

The direct implementation mistake and the validation gap should both be addressed. Asking the model to be more careful does not establish the behavior.

**Self-contained reduced reproductions**

Save as `repro_evaluator.py` and run `python repro_evaluator.py`. Only the Python standard library is needed. This reproduces the relevant generated-script semantics, not a claim that a scheduling evaluator is built into the repository. The input-mutating case was also executed against the original frozen evaluator, with the same perfect score.

```python
import queue
import threading

# Reduced from the frozen evaluator: the baseline is measured before the call,
# but candidate makespan is computed from the same mutable input afterward.
def baseline_schedule(workloads, speeds):
    loads = [0.0] * len(speeds)
    assignment = [0] * len(workloads)
    for i in sorted(range(len(workloads)), key=workloads.__getitem__, reverse=True):
        j = min(range(len(speeds)), key=lambda j: loads[j] + workloads[i] / speeds[j])
        assignment[i] = j
        loads[j] += workloads[i] / speeds[j]
    return assignment

def makespan(workloads, speeds, assignment):
    loads = [0.0] * len(speeds)
    for i, w in enumerate(workloads):
        loads[assignment[i]] += w / speeds[assignment[i]]
    return max(loads)

def score_instance(schedule):
    workloads, speeds = [10.0, 8.0, 6.0], [1.0, 2.0]
    baseline = makespan(workloads, speeds, baseline_schedule(workloads, speeds))
    assignment = schedule(workloads, speeds)
    assert len(assignment) == len(workloads)
    assert all(type(j) is int and 0 <= j < len(speeds) for j in assignment)
    candidate = makespan(workloads, speeds, assignment)
    return baseline / (baseline + candidate)

def mutate_input(workloads, speeds):
    workloads[:] = [0.0] * len(workloads)
    return [0] * len(workloads)

print('baseline score:', score_instance(baseline_schedule))
print('input-mutating candidate score:', score_instance(mutate_input))

# The evaluator's thread/Queue watchdog stops waiting but not execution.
release, exited = threading.Event(), threading.Event()
q = queue.Queue()
def slow_candidate():
    try:
        release.wait()
        q.put('done')
    finally:
        exited.set()
worker = threading.Thread(target=slow_candidate, daemon=True)
worker.start()
try:
    q.get(timeout=0.01)  # Shortened from 1 second for this reproduction.
except queue.Empty:
    print('worker still alive after timeout:', worker.is_alive())
finally:
    release.set()
    worker.join(timeout=1)

```

Observed output from the reduced reproduction:

```text
baseline score: 0.5
input-mutating candidate score: 1.0
worker still alive after timeout: True
```

**Expected behavior and acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Provide a reusable, Windows-compatible candidate invocation facility for custom evaluators that need hard per-call limits. Deadline expiry must stop the corresponding work and clean up owned processes/resources before continuing; a daemon-thread wait timeout must not be represented as terminating execution. Define whether startup overhead counts toward the deadline.
- [ ] Keep authoritative scoring inputs/truth outside candidate-controlled mutation. A candidate may modify its own input copy, but this must not alter the data used to validate or calculate its result.
- [ ] Extend evaluator generation guidance and the pre-run checks with behavioral checks for slow/nonterminating calls, exceptions/invalid outputs, and input mutation where the evaluator's entrypoint protocol supports them. Test timeout followed by another valid case, so lingering work is observable. For arbitrary legacy scripts, use an explicit harness/protocol or disclose checks that cannot be performed rather than pretending generic Python is fully verified.
- [ ] Check repeatability of a time-constrained candidate under representative execution conditions, rather than validating timing only with a fast baseline. Preserve legitimate per-case zero penalties and partial scores; do not change every partially failing candidate into an invalid run.
- [ ] Add focused regressions for input-integrity and post-timeout cleanup on Windows and Linux; retain existing custom-script, shard, result and malformed-candidate compatibility checks.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Historical experiment: ScienceDiscovery Windows desktop, PUCT, direct/unisolated execution, four workers; generated instances had 50–300 tasks and 4–16 machines. Each scheduling call was limited to one second by the generated watchdog; the outer candidate/evaluator budget was 180 seconds.
- Evidence inspected: original conversation, frozen evaluator, run metadata, complete event stream and service log. Hardware, exact Windows build and installed Python patch version were not recorded in those artifacts and are not inferred here.
- The input-mutation check against the original evaluator and the reduced reproduction were executed in the Linux/WSL checkout using `python3`; no live search or full suite was rerun.

### Additional Information

- #1435 tracks budget-stop finalization/cancellation reporting, and #1436 tracks desktop budget controls. This issue concerns whether the generated measuring apparatus is reliable before search starts.
- The original evaluation score transform itself is not alleged to destroy flat-PUCT's ranking signal. However, a baseline of 0.5 is not evidence of useful optimization headroom. Task calibration against a known bound/reference is a separate useful improvement; it must not require solving the task during setup or weakening a user-requested baseline.
- Suggested implementation boundary: let the framework own execution/cleanup and input transport, while the model supplies task-specific instance generation, result validation and objective calculation. Preserve legacy scripts during migration rather than relying on a keyword ban on `threading`.

### Version Information

- The operator reports the experiment code matches the local checkout at `36476b0ea302b6de3897154f83c3c7c87dc6ec89`.
- Upstream main checked for this report: `3a00fd822e7cd88f0044e7c2e562febb8eb06dd1`. The affected generation guidance, custom-script probe and script-domain paths remain present.

- [Baseline-only local check](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/3a00fd822e7cd88f0044e7c2e562febb8eb06dd1/skills/evolve-design/SKILL.md#L163-L192)
- [Custom evaluator writing contract](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/3a00fd822e7cd88f0044e7c2e562febb8eb06dd1/skills/evolve-design/references/custom-script.md#L7-L30)
- [Custom-script discrimination probe](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/3a00fd822e7cd88f0044e7c2e562febb8eb06dd1/services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/probe.py#L109-L178)
- [Baseline repeatability check](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/3a00fd822e7cd88f0044e7c2e562febb8eb06dd1/services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/probe.py#L479-L508)
- [Outer evaluator execution](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/3a00fd822e7cd88f0044e7c2e562febb8eb06dd1/services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/script_domain.py#L254-L300)

items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version (the rendering path was checked in upstream main).
- [x] I understand that environment information and a minimal reproduction help maintainers reproduce and resolve the issue.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

The desktop subagent conversation displays internal audit metadata alongside the final `run_shell` result and repeats streamed output under the same Output heading. Users cannot tell which text is command output, progress, or the projected tool result sent to the model.

PR #717 introduced model-facing output projection, but the UI still renders `step.content`, `step.progress`, and pretty-printed `step.details` consecutively. The audit JSON includes execution/agent/runner/workspace IDs, timestamps, `[omitted]` placeholders, and `__detailsBoundary`. These implementation details are not useful in ordinary user-facing output.

**Minimal reproduction**

1. Have a subagent call `run_shell` with a short command such as:
   ```sh
   printf 'batch1 written\n'
   ```
2. Wait for completion and expand the tool step in the desktop subagent conversation.
3. When progress was captured, the same message appears in both the final stdout and progress. Audit details are also rendered under Output.

The equivalent minimal rendering input is a completed tool step with:

```json
{
  "kind": "tool",
  "status": "completed",
  "toolName": "run_shell",
  "content": "{\"state\":\"completed\",\"exitCode\":0}\nstdout:\nbatch1 written\nstderr:\n",
  "progress": "batch1 written\n",
  "details": {
    "stdout": "[omitted]",
    "stderr": "[omitted]",
    "agentId": "subagent:example",
    "runnerId": "local",
    "__detailsBoundary": { "omittedPayloadFields": true, "truncated": false }
  }
}
```

**Observed behavior**

A user-reported successful execution produced this sequence (identifiers shortened):

```text
{"executionId":"shell:example","state":"completed","exitCode":0,"createdFiles":["outputs/literature_sources.json"],"modifiedFiles":[],"recovery":{"schemaVersion":1,"capability":"unknown","reason":"NOT_REPORTED"}}
stdout:
batch1 written

stderr:
batch1 written
{
  "executionId": "shell:example",
  "state": "completed",
  "exitCode": 0,
  "stdout": "[omitted]",
  "stderr": "[omitted]",
  "agentId": "subagent:example",
  "runnerId": "local",
  "workspaceId": "ws_example",
  "__detailsBoundary": {
    "maxArrayItems": 100,
    "maxDepth": 8,
    "maxObjectKeys": 100,
    "maxStringChars": 4096,
    "maxTotalStringChars": 64000,
    "omittedPayloadFields": true,
    "truncated": false
  }
}
```

The second `batch1 written` is consistent with the UI rendering progress after the final result's empty `stderr:` section; it must not be interpreted as proof that the command wrote to stderr.

**Expected behavior**

- Ordinary tool output shows useful command output, completion/failure status, generated files, and actionable error or recovery guidance.
- Internal audit metadata is retained for diagnostics without being rendered in ordinary user-facing output, including inside an additional collapsed audit block.
- Progress can be shown during execution; completion uses the final result without repeating the same streamed text or making progress appear to be stderr.
- Default recovery metadata such as `unknown` / `NOT_REPORTED` and empty bookkeeping lists should not clutter ordinary user-facing output. Actionable recovery information must remain available.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Reported on 2026-11-26 with a successful local `run_shell` execution (`runnerId: local`, exit code 0) in a subagent.
- The desktop subagent renderer matches the reported output ordering. The reporter's exact app build, operating system, and Node version were not supplied.
- Upstream main was inspected remotely to confirm that the affected rendering path remains present. No application/browser journey was run for this report.
- The rendering reproduction is data-only and does not depend on external providers, scientific packages, or special hardware.

### Additional Information

Source on inspected upstream main:

- [Desktop StepBody renders content, progress, and audit details together](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/96763c10053ac4f008a42a59e5c2305f266ef0bd/apps/desktop/src/views/SubagentDetail.tsx#L75-L111).
- Related projection change: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/717.

This is a user-facing presentation issue. The model-facing result and audit metadata are separate: the JiuwenSwarm bridge returns `dispatched.content` to the model, while `details` is retained separately in tool events. The audit JSON visible here does not by itself indicate a model-facing projection failure. Preserve audit storage and actionable execution information when fixing the display.

### Version Information

- Inspected upstream main: `96763c10053ac4f008a42a59e5c2305f266ef0bd`.
- Related merged PR: #717, merge commit `c2cb3119b463c7de76772568d7b054150da0d8d7`.
- Exact version of the originally reported running application: not supplied.

items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding technical details and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which may reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary.** In `设置 › Idea Tree`, the `最大深度` and `最大节点` boxes cannot be cleared and rewrite what is typed into them: every keystroke is parsed and normalised immediately, and a keystroke that does not already parse as a valid number is dropped instead of being kept as a draft. The `最大 token` box right below them behaves differently, so the same form has two editing behaviours.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. `设置 › 智能 › Idea Tree` while a research has values (e.g. `最大深度` = `4`, `最大节点` = `20`).
2. Click at the end of `最大深度`, press `Backspace`.
3. Also try `最大 token`: click at the end, press `Backspace` (or select all and delete).

**Observed** (`645dc7ba`)

```tsx
// apps/desktop/src/views/settings/IdeaTreeSettings.tsx:57-61
function readNumber(raw: string): number | undefined {
  if (raw.trim() === "") return undefined;
  const value = Number(raw);
  return Number.isFinite(value) && value >= 0 ? value : undefined;
}
// :146-153  and  :155-163
onChange={(event) => { const value = readNumber(event.target.value); if (value !== undefined) patch({ maxDepth: value }); }}
value={number(draft.maxDepth)}
```

`Backspace` produces `""`, `readNumber("")` is `undefined`, no `patch` happens, and the controlled input re-renders with the old number — the digit comes straight back. Typing a `-` first (to reach `0`, or just before noticing it is not allowed) is dropped the same way, as is `1.`.

By contrast the token box takes the empty state explicitly, which is why clearing that one works:

```tsx
// :170
onChange={(event) => patch({ maxTokens: readNumber(event.target.value) ?? null })}
```

**Root cause.** The two boxes have no draft: the JSX value is the parsed model value, and the change handler only writes to the model when the text already parses. Any intermediate text (empty, `-`, `1.`) is therefore rejected at the keystroke that created it, and the field snaps back.

**Expected.** All three boxes edit as text and commit on blur (the shape `SettingsNumber` in `views/settings/setting-controls.tsx` already implements for 配额 and 数量), or at least keep the raw text while the field is focused. Empty should be allowed while typing and then either refused or restored on blur with a visible mark.

**Impact**

- Clearing a field is impossible, which is the normal first move when replacing a value; the reader has to select-all (`Ctrl+A`) instead, and a user who does not do that concludes the box is read-only.
- The value under the caret is replaced by the old one, so a mistyped digit cannot be corrected by deleting it — the only fix is to retype the whole number from a selection.
- The form is inconsistent with itself one row apart (`最大 token` clears, the other two do not), which reads as a broken field rather than a rule.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- ScienceDiscovery desktop client, source `645dc7ba3dde868bf7dcdc6f674e937d42284d3a`.
- Derived from `apps/desktop/src/views/settings/IdeaTreeSettings.tsx:55-61, 145-175`; not reproduced in a running client (the test host was unavailable at the time).

### Additional Information

- This is deliberately separate from the value-meaning report against the same page (`readNumber` collapsing "empty" and "invalid" into one `undefined`, which makes `-5` mean "no cap"): that one is about what a stored value means, this one is about the field refusing to be edited. A draft-based field plus an explicit "empty = null" call site fixes both, but they fail differently and are worth their own checks.
- `SettingsNumber` (`setting-controls.tsx:65-96`) is the ready-made pattern: local draft, `onCommit` on blur/Enter, `aria-invalid` plus a message when the committed text does not parse.

### Version Information

- `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` @ `645dc7ba3dde868bf7dcdc6f674e937d42284d3a` (main, 2026-11-25).

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which may reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary.** In `设置 › Idea Tree`, `最大深度` accepts values above `20` and `最大节点` accepts `1` or anything above `10 000`. The form shows no error and leaves `保存` enabled, and the value is only refused by the store after the click, as an English server sentence inside a Chinese pane. Neither field states a range, so nothing tells the reader that `20` is the cap.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. `设置 › 智能 › Idea Tree`.
2. Type `50` into `最大深度`, or `1` into `最大节点`.
3. Press `保存`.

**Observed** (`644730f8`, after #1409)

```tsx
// apps/desktop/src/views/settings/IdeaTreeSettings.tsx:78-82
function parseCount(raw: string): number | undefined {
  if (raw.trim() === "") return undefined;
  const value = Number(raw);
  return Number.isSafeInteger(value) && value >= 1 ? value : undefined;   // no upper bound, nodes min is 1
}
// :197-233  the inputs carry min={1} and no max
```

```
// services/api/src/store/settings.ts:629-631, boundedInteger throws (:579-595)
maxDepth = boundedInteger(input.maxDepth, "maxDepth", 1, 20, current.maxDepth);
maxNodes = boundedInteger(input.maxNodes, "maxNodes", 2, 10_000, current.maxNodes);
```

The pane prints the thrown message verbatim (`IdeaTreeSettings.tsx:162-165`), so the reader gets `maxDepth must be between 1 and 20` / `maxNodes must be between 2 and 10000` only after pressing `保存`, in the middle of a Chinese form.

**Root cause.** The pane's own validation covers "is this a positive integer", not "is this an integer the store accepts", and the two inputs declare `min={1}` for both fields even though the store's node floor is `2`. The bounds exist elsewhere in the same app: the per-run control uses `min={1} max={20}` and `min={2} max={10000}` (`apps/desktop/src/views/idea/IdeaTreeOverrideDialog.tsx:349-362`), and the shared `SettingsNumber` (`apps/desktop/src/views/settings/setting-controls.tsx:65-95`) validates min/max before committing.

**Expected.** The field refuses what the store refuses: depth `1..20`, nodes `2..10 000`, tokens `1..MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`, with the accepted range named in the note (or in the hint) instead of "at least 1". Setting `max={20}` / `min={2} max={10000}` on the inputs would also let the browser say it.

**Impact**

- A reader who wants "a deeper tree" types `50`, sees no complaint, presses `保存`, and is told `maxDepth must be between 1 and 20` in English — the same "the failure surfaces at 保存 with a server message instead of at the field" shape this page was just fixed for `0`.
- `最大节点` literally offers `1` (`min={1}`) as the smallest value and then rejects it, which reads as a broken field rather than a rule.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- ScienceDiscovery desktop client, source `644730f8070c96c3e35cb1ae7e6e8ff34ecc11df` (PR #1409) on top of `main` `645dc7ba3dde868bf7dcdc6f674e937d42284d3a`.
- Derived by reading `apps/desktop/src/views/settings/IdeaTreeSettings.tsx` and `services/api/src/store/settings.ts`; not reproduced in a running client.

### Additional Information

- Found while reviewing #1409, which fixes the sibling half of this page (#1397): the parsing, `badInput` and `0` cases. This report is only about the accepted range; it predates that PR and is unchanged by it.
- Related: #1403 (the same boxes could not be cleared at all), #1397 (invalid text became "no token cap").

### Version Information

- `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` @ `main` `645dc7ba3dde868bf7dcdc6f674e937d42284d3a` (2026-11-25).
items.title: [Bug]: Idea Tree settings accept a max depth above 20 and nodes outside 2-10000, then the store rejects them at Save

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which may reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary.** The timeout inputs in `设置 › 超时` disable themselves as soon as the value being typed becomes `0`, so a sub-second value can never be entered: typing `0.5` (or `0.001`, which the field advertises as its minimum) stops at the first keystroke and turns the timeout into 不限.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. `设置 › 超时`, make sure the row's `不限` switch is off (the input is enabled).
2. Click into `执行超时` and type `0.5`.

**Observed** (`645dc7ba`)

```tsx
// apps/desktop/src/views/settings/system/Timeouts.tsx:143
const unlimited = current[field] === 0;
…
<input
  disabled={unlimited}
  min="0.001"
  step="0.001"
  onChange={(event) => setMilliseconds(field, event.target.value)}
/>
// :113
const setMilliseconds = (field, value) => {
  const text = value.trim();
  if (text === "") return;
  const parsed = Number(text);
  if (base === undefined || !Number.isFinite(parsed) || parsed < 0) return;   // 0 is accepted
  update({ ...base, [field]: Math.round(parsed * 1000) } as SystemTimeoutSettings);
};
```

Typing `0` fires `onChange`, `Math.round(0 * 1000)` is `0`, `0` is the stored code for 不限, so the row re-renders with `unlimited === true`: the input becomes `disabled` and the `不限` switch flips on by itself. The user's next keystroke goes nowhere, and the setting they were editing is now unlimited instead of `0.5` seconds.

**Root cause.** The `0 → 不限` convention lives in the same field the number is typed into. The handler validates `parsed < 0` but not `parsed === 0`, while the markup declares `min="0.001"` — so the one value the input says is invalid doubles as the "unlimited" flag and is reachable by typing.

**Expected.** Typing `0` in an enabled field should be rejected (or clamped to `min`, i.e. 1 ms) instead of silently meaning 不限; only the `不限` switch should write `0`. Removing the input's `disabled` binding to `=== 0` (or deriving the switch from an explicit flag) fixes the mid-typing lock either way.

**Impact**

- Sub-second timeouts cannot be typed at all, although the field advertises `step="0.001"` and the hint explains "到达时限后这次操作会被取消" — a user who wants a 0.5 s execution timeout has no path to it.
- Worse than a rejection: the first `0` silently removes the limit and the field locks, so the user is left with a *more permissive* configuration than they asked for, with no message saying so.
- It is silent, so it will be reported as "the timeout setting does not stick".

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- ScienceDiscovery desktop client, source `645dc7ba3dde868bf7dcdc6f674e937d42284d3a`.
- Derived from `apps/desktop/src/views/settings/system/Timeouts.tsx` (`setMilliseconds` at `:113`, the `unlimited` binding at `:143`); not reproduced in a running client (the test host was unavailable at the time).

### Additional Information

- The same page's `setUnlimited` (`:124`) is correct: turning the switch off restores `base[field] || 60_000`, so only the typed path is affected.

### Version Information

- `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` @ `645dc7ba3dde868bf7dcdc6f674e937d42284d3a` (main, 2026-11-25).

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which may reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary.** In `设置 › Idea Tree`, an invalid number typed into `最大 token` silently becomes "no cap", and `最大深度` / `最大节点` accept `0` although the fields declare `min={1}`. The form never says the value was rejected — it saves something else.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. `设置 › 智能 › Idea Tree`.
2. Put a value in `最大 token` (e.g. `200000`), then type `-5` into it (or `-5` into `最大深度`).
3. Press `保存`.

**Observed** (`645dc7ba`)

```tsx
// apps/desktop/src/views/settings/IdeaTreeSettings.tsx:57
function readNumber(raw: string): number | undefined {
  if (raw.trim() === "") return undefined;
  const value = Number(raw);
  return Number.isFinite(value) && value >= 0 ? value : undefined;   // invalid → undefined
}
// :170
onChange={(event) => patch({ maxTokens: readNumber(event.target.value) ?? null })}   // undefined → null = no cap
// :150 / :160
onChange={(event) => { const value = readNumber(event.target.value); if (value !== undefined) patch({ maxDepth: value }); }}
```

`readNumber` collapses two different inputs into `undefined`: "the box is empty" (which the field documents as *no per-research cap*, `null`) and "the text is not a valid number". `?? null` then turns either into `null`, so `-5` or `1e999` saves as "no cap" instead of being refused. `maxDepth` / `maxNodes` use `>= 0`, so `0` passes even though the inputs declare `min={1}` and a tree of depth 0 cannot exist.

**Root cause.** One helper returns a single `undefined` for "empty" and "invalid", and each call site decides what that means on its own; the `min` attributes are decorative because nothing validates against them before `patch()`.

**Expected.** Invalid text should be refused with the field marked (or clamped to its `min`), and empty should be the only thing that means "no cap"; `0` should be rejected for `maxDepth` / `maxNodes` exactly as `min={1}` says.

**Impact**

- A typo in `最大 token` costs the user the only cost guard on an Idea Tree research — the run then continues until the engine's own limits, and nothing on the page says the cap was removed.
- `0` in `最大深度` may be accepted by the form and rejected by the store later, so the failure surfaces at `保存` with a server message instead of at the field.
- Users cannot tell whether the box they cleared or mistyped is "uncapped" or "invalid", which is the same ambiguity the panel elsewhere is careful to avoid (`score === null` is rendered as 不可用, never as 0).

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- ScienceDiscovery desktop client, source `645dc7ba3dde868bf7dcdc6f674e937d42284d3a`.
- Derived from `apps/desktop/src/views/settings/IdeaTreeSettings.tsx` (`readNumber` `:57`, `maxTokens` `:170`, `maxDepth` `:150`, `maxNodes` `:160`); not reproduced in a running client (the test host was unavailable at the time).

### Additional Information

- The panel's own contract documents the intended distinction: "`maxTokens` null is the API's 'no per-research cap'; an empty box means exactly that" (`:97-98`). Empty is the only state that should produce `null`.

### Version Information

- `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` @ `645dc7ba3dde868bf7dcdc6f674e937d42284d3a` (main, 2026-11-25).

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary.** The "new evolve experiment" dialog lets the user set custom evolution parameters, but shows no range, unit or interaction rule for any of them. Values outside the server's limits are coerced or rejected later, so the run does something other than what was typed.

**Where it happens**

1. Open a Session, then the Session menu (`会话设置`) → `程序演进实验`.
2. Tick `自定义演进参数` (`Custom evolution parameters`).
3. The panel offers `＋ 添加参数`, `上传 JSON`, `生成起始参数`. Add `expansions` and type `40`.

**Actual.** The dialog accepts the value without a word. The run then starts with `expansions: 37`: the server enforces

- `expansions <= 40`
- `maxTokensPerCall * expansions <= maxTokens` (with the defaults `16000 * 37 <= 600000`)
- `maxSeconds` is not settable at all (fixed at 7200 s)

and none of these rules is visible anywhere in the dialog. The parameter panel's only hint is the generic "为参数设定起始值。勾选的参数会由演进自动尝试不同取值；未勾选的始终使用起始值。"

**Expected.** Each parameter names its range and unit next to the field, and a value that cannot be honoured says so while it is typed ("40 exceeds 40? no — but 16000 × 40 > 600000, so it will run as 37"), instead of being quietly rewritten at run-creation time.

**Impact**

- The number the user typed is not the number that runs, with no record of why; the only way to learn the rules is to read a finished run's record and compare.
- A user tuning a search budget cannot tell whether a poor result came from the task, the budget or a coerced parameter.
- `maxSeconds` looks settable (it is just another key in the same editor) but is ignored, which reads as a broken setting rather than a fixed limit.

**Suggested fix.** Render the constraints with the fields (min/max/step/unit plus the cross-field formula), validate on input, and when a value has to be adjusted show the effective value in the dialog before the run is created.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- ScienceDiscovery desktop client (desktop web UI), viewport 1500x950, `zh-CN`.
- Linux (Ubuntu 22.04.5); API `127.0.0.1:4410`, evolve runtime on `127.0.0.1:17676` (`/api/evolve/status` = `ready`, sandbox `bwrap`), Chromium 1228 via Playwright.
- Model backend: `Ark DeepSeek` (deepseek-v4.1-flash).

### Additional Information

- Reproduced on `a8573558` and again on `9da58ad6`; the dialog markup and copy are unchanged between the two.
- Screenshot of the empty parameter panel (no range, no formula, no unit) is in the comment below.
- Related: the run record is the only place the effective `expansions` value appears, which is why this is easy to miss.

### Version Information

- `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` @ `9da58ad619f972e44eb674c5d4cc9118813f7222` (main, 2026-11-24).

items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary.** Importing a `.sdresearch` package that contains an evolution run copies that run into the run list under a **new id**, with every value identical to the original. Importing the same package twice produces three runs that are the same run. Run lists, per-Session statistics and "does this Session have an active run" checks all see the copies as separate runs.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. In a Session that has a finished evolution run, `导出会话` → `必要导出`, save the package.
2. `导入会话` → pick the package → `导入`. Note that the imported Session opens as a read-only snapshot.
3. Import the same package once more.
4. Read `GET /api/evolve/runs`.

**Observed** (2026-11-24, `9da58ad6`)

```text
0098af62  succeeded  session 5293e460  24 candidates  223,006 tokens  best #22  2026-11-24T15:50:59Z
46ea4b76  succeeded  session fe4d2e3c  24 candidates  223,006 tokens  best #22  2026-11-24T15:50:59Z
de2b933f  succeeded  session b163af95  24 candidates  223,006 tokens  best #22  2026-11-24T15:50:59Z
```

All three carry the same `goal` object, including `goal.baselineProgramCas = sha256:28b5262f…` and the same `createdAt`. Only `id` and `sessionId` differ, and the two extra `sessionId`s are the imported snapshot Sessions. Total runs went from 8 to 10 after the two imports.

**Expected.** A package carries the *result* of a run, not a new run. Either the imported Session references the original run (`sourceRunId`/read-only link), or the copy is marked as a snapshot and excluded from run listings and from `isEvolveRunActive`.

**Why it matters**

- **Run list and counters double.** Anything that lists runs (the task panel, counts, token/cost summaries) shows the same run several times after a few imports.
- **`isEvolveRunActive` can be fooled.** The create dialog's "this Session already has a running experiment" branch is computed from the Session's own runs (`App.tsx:1672`). A copied run that is still `running` at export time would arrive as a second active run for the snapshot Session, blocking creation there for a run the user cannot stop in that Session.
- **Cost and score statistics become wrong** in aggregate views, because the same 223,006 tokens are counted three times.

**Suggested fix.** On import, either drop evolution run records from the package (they are observability data, not research material), or persist them with a `sourceRunId` and treat runs with a `sourceRunId` as snapshots: not active, not counted, and linked to the original.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- ScienceDiscovery desktop client (desktop web UI at a vite dev server), 1500x950, `zh-CN`.
- Linux (Ubuntu 22.04.5); API `127.0.0.1:4410`, runner `127.0.0.1:4411`, evolve runtime `127.0.0.1:17676`; Chromium 1228 via Playwright.
- Source Session `5293e460…` (puct run `0098af62`), imported into two snapshot Sessions `fe4d2e3c…` and `b163af95…`.

### Additional Information

- The raw `GET /api/evolve/runs` response taken after the imports is attached in the comment below (three entries with identical `tokens`, `candidates`, `bestNodeIndex`, `createdAt`, `goal`).
- Found while running scenario S-208 (export → import → cite). Related but distinct: #1347 (export estimate), #1334 (cross-Session citations after import).

### Version Information

- `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` @ `9da58ad619f972e44eb674c5d4cc9118813f7222` (main, 2026-11-24).

items.body:
## Purpose

Track the remaining research-team budget and cancellation integration validation for v0.4.0, split from #239 at the user's request. The classification fix in #239 is implemented by merged PR #426 (`7b93f92e898dca1798595fd2fa320c23887e1565`). Closing #239 does not mean the full BRCA1 journey has been revalidated.

## Existing evidence

On a post-merge snapshot (`0c6fa3fb47ccac3b69e870ac7fddc4ee00a51853`), these commands passed 61/61 tests with no paid model calls:

```sh
node --import tsx --test test/helpers/real-delivery.unit.ts scripts/real-e2e-scoring.test.mjs .ci/ci-contract.test.mjs
```

They cover active delivery classification, terminal missing-output failures, scoring, and safe result packaging. They do not execute the full team-spec timeout branch or establish its persisted metrics/cancellation outcomes. PR #426's L3 evidence is not a replacement for the L4 BRCA1 journey.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add and run a deterministic integration test using a local model stub and a short budget, exercising the actual team journey timeout path rather than only helper functions.
- [ ] Verify persisted `team-metrics.json` distinguishes budget exhaustion (`integration=timed_out`) from terminal delivery failure and retains budget, elapsed duration, cancellation request, shutdown outcome, and actual terminal status.
- [ ] Verify cleanup stops the main run, children, pending wakeups, and relevant executions; retain diagnostic evidence on cleanup failure.
- [ ] Cover the terminal race: cancellation coincides with completion, while budget-exhaustion attribution remains correct.
- [ ] Preserve normal delivery contracts: successful completion requires readable, nonempty final artifacts; terminal missing/empty/unreadable output remains a delivery failure.
- [ ] Run or inspect a post-fix L4/Nightly `TC-E2E-01` BRCA1 journey at its configured team budget. Record the immutable SHA, command/configuration, final artifacts, persisted metrics, cancellation outcomes where applicable, and actual passed/failed/blocked/skipped counts. A successful normal completion alone does not cover the timeout branch.

## Execution constraints

The current instruction permits only verification without paid model calls. Do not start a billable model/judge run without authorization; an already scheduled post-fix Nightly may provide the real-journey evidence. Keep unexecuted scenarios explicitly pending.

## Scope

This is validation follow-up for v0.4.0. Any newly discovered product defect should be documented with reproduction evidence and linked here. Related: #239, #426.

- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary.** In the `导出会话` (export Session) dialog, the number shown as `预计大小` (estimated size) is the size of the **uncompressed** archive, while the file that is actually downloaded is gzip-compressed and roughly 4x smaller. The headline number therefore overstates the download by more than a factor of four.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Open any Session → Session menu → `导出会话`.
2. Wait for the size to be computed.

**Observed**

- `必要导出` (essential export): `预计大小 812.5 KB`.
- `完整导出` (full export): `预计大小 102.9 MB`.
- The small print under the list says `未压缩估算 812.5 KB`, and `未压缩上限：5.0 GB` — so the estimate is explicitly the unpacked size.

**Actual download.** Pressing `开始导出` downloads `<Session title>.sdresearch`:

```text
189,132 bytes
$ file <Session title>.sdresearch
gzip compressed data, from Unix, original size modulo 2^32 824320
```

824,320 B unpacked ≈ 805 KB matches the 812.5 KB estimate, so the estimate is internally consistent — it is simply not the size of what the user gets.

**Expected.** The number next to `预计大小` is the size of the file that will be downloaded, or the two numbers are shown together (`约 189 KB（未压缩 812 KB）`).

**Impact**

- Anyone deciding whether an export fits somewhere (attachment limit, disk, upload) plans for 4x the space they need. The same gap was seen earlier on a research-package export: estimate `102.9 MB`, downloaded `29,073,956 B`.
- Because the two numbers never match, a user may suspect the export is incomplete rather than compressed.
- On a large Session the gap is the difference between "this is fine" and "this is too big to send".

**Suggested fix.** Estimate the compressed size (or label the headline as the unpacked size and put the download size next to it), and keep the `5.0 GB` limit labelled as what it measures.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- ScienceDiscovery desktop client (desktop web UI), viewport 1500x950, `zh-CN`.
- Linux (Ubuntu 22.04.5); API `127.0.0.1:4410`, Chromium 1228 via Playwright with downloads enabled.
- Session used: `SK 自旋玻璃基态搜索演进` (11 workspace files, one Evidence-bearing artifact).

### Additional Information

- Screenshot of the dialog with both estimates is in the comment below.
- The same dialog offers `导入` on the receiving side; the extension `.sdresearch` is a gzip container, which is fine — the issue is only the number presented as the download size.

### Version Information

- `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` @ `9da58ad619f972e44eb674c5d4cc9118813f7222` (main, 2026-11-24); also observed on `a8573558`.

items.author: agent-ci-infra-bot[bot]
items.body:
## 🚀 Background Description

`Nightly` (`.github/workflows/nightly.yml`) is the L4 `daily` gate on `main`. It is triggered by a 16:00 UTC cron (`- cron: "0 16 * * *"`, line 33) and by `workflow_dispatch` (line 34). The workflow has no `concurrency` block and no guard job. Its own header already says GitHub "drops or delays runs when its queue is busy — treat a missing night as a scheduling miss and re-dispatch rather than as a build failure".

GitHub is now consistently creating the scheduled run hours late. The ten most recent `event=schedule` runs returned by the Actions API are:

| Scheduled 16:00 UTC | Run created (UTC) | Lateness | Run |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-11-17 | 2026-11-17T23:26:00Z | 7 h 26 m | [44199315530](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44199315530) |
| 2026-11-16 | 2026-11-17T00:07:02Z | 8 h 07 m | [43984975918](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/43984975918) |
| 2026-11-15 | 2026-11-15T20:56:52Z | 4 h 56 m | [43760882196](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/43760882196) |
| 2026-11-14 | 2026-11-14T20:33:14Z | 4 h 33 m | [43638096527](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/43638096527) |
| 2026-11-13 | 2026-11-13T21:52:47Z | 5 h 52 m | [43514552368](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/43514552368) |
| 2026-11-12 | 2026-11-12T22:09:58Z | 6 h 09 m | [43317329014](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/43317329014) |
| 2026-11-11 | 2026-11-11T22:35:07Z | 6 h 35 m | [43112992255](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/43112992255) |
| 2026-11-10 | 2026-11-10T21:44:15Z | 5 h 44 m | [42907916462](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42907916462) |
| 2026-11-09 | 2026-11-10T00:04:30Z | 8 h 04 m | [42725463331](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42725463331) |
| 2026-11-08 | 2026-11-08T20:20:32Z | 4 h 20 m | [42519625781](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42519625781) |

The times above are the run's `created_at` from the API, i.e. when GitHub created the run, not when a step started. Every one was created between **4 h 20 m and 8 h 07 m after the 16:00 UTC occurrence** it belongs to. The run before these ten, [42409367796](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42409367796), was created at 2026-11-07T20:05:46Z and was 4 h 05 m late, so this is not a single bad night.

16:00 UTC is 00:00 in Asia/Shanghai, and the workflow header intends the run to start overnight and "finish by the working morning". A run created at 04:20–08:07 Asia/Shanghai has not done that, and its long real-model suite runs after that creation time.

There is also a same-day dispatch on 2026-11-18: [run 44361037291](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44361037291) was created at 2026-11-18T17:39:13Z as a `workflow_dispatch` by `agent-ci-infra-bot`. At the time of the API read (2026-11-18T19:37Z) there was still no `event=schedule` run for that day's 16:00 UTC occurrence. The API does not record why the dispatch was started; it is consistent with the re-dispatch the workflow header describes.

The result is that the normal 16:00 UTC start depends on GitHub's cron queue, and the workaround is a manual or one-off bot re-dispatch. The plan below makes the normal start independent of that queue and keeps the cron only as a guarded fallback.

## Design Ideas

Both parts below are one plan, not alternatives. Part 1 moves the normal start out of GitHub's cron queue. Part 2 makes the cron safe when it does arrive, so it cannot cancel a running dispatch run or create a duplicate after a successful one.

### Part 1 — start the run from the bot schedule

In the bot console, ask the management assistant, or add a project scheduled task on the project's `定时任务与通知` page. Schedule it shortly after 16:00 UTC (for example 16:05 UTC, or 00:05 Asia/Shanghai if the page uses local time) with this instruction:

> start nightly.yml on main; first check that no run of it is queued or in progress, and if one is, start nothing

That gives the project a primary start that is not GitHub's cron queue, and the check keeps it from adding a run when a person or the fallback has already started one. Keep `workflow_dispatch` so the same task, or a person, can still start the workflow.

### Part 2 — change the workflow

Keep `workflow_dispatch`. Keep `schedule` with `- cron: "0 16 * * *"` only as a fallback. Add a workflow-level `concurrency` group with `cancel-in-progress: false`, so a scheduled run waits for a running dispatch run instead of cancelling it. Add a first `guard` job that, on `schedule` only, checks whether a `workflow_dispatch` run of `nightly.yml` succeeded since the most recent 16:00 UTC; if one did, it sets `run=false` and every other job is skipped. On `workflow_dispatch` it always sets `run=true`.

This is the concrete adaptation for the existing `stamp`, `gate` and `report` jobs:

```yaml
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 16 * * *"   # fallback only; the bot schedule starts the run
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  # A scheduled run queues behind a running dispatch run instead of cancelling it.
  group: nightly-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  guard:
    name: Check for a successful dispatch run
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      actions: read        # gh run list
      contents: read
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.check.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: check
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          run=true
          if [[ "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" == "schedule" ]]; then
            # The most recent scheduled time: 16:00 UTC today, or yesterday
            # when a delayed run is created before 16:00 UTC.
            since=$(date -u -d '16:00 today' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
            if (( $(date -u +%s) < $(date -u -d "$since" +%s) )); then
              since=$(date -u -d '16:00 yesterday' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
            fi
            count=$(gh run list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" -w nightly.yml \
              -e workflow_dispatch -s success --created ">=$since" \
              --limit 1 --json databaseId --jq 'length')
            if (( count > 0 )); then
              run=false
            fi
          fi
          echo "run=$run" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  stamp:
    name: Stamp the build
    needs: guard
    if: needs.guard.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.stamp.outputs.version }}
    steps:
      - id: stamp
        run: |
          date=$(TZ=Asia/Shanghai date +%Y%m%d)
          echo "version=nightly-${date}-${GITHUB_SHA::7}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  gate:
    name: Gate
    needs: [guard, stamp]
    if: needs.guard.outputs.run == 'true'
    uses: ./.github/workflows/ci.yml
    secrets: inherit
    with:
      profile: daily
      release-version: ${{ needs.stamp.outputs.version }}

  report:
    name: Report the outcome
    needs: [guard, stamp, gate]
    if: always() && needs.guard.outputs.run == 'true'
    # ... the existing report steps are unchanged ...
```

The guard job declares `actions: read`; the workflow-level `contents: read` stays. It uses the workflow's own `github.token`, not a new secret. The `--created ">=$since"` filter and `-s success` mean only a successful dispatch created at or after the scheduled time suppresses the fallback; a failed or cancelled dispatch does not. `gh run list --limit 1` is enough because only the existence of a match matters. If the `gh run list` call itself fails, the guard job fails and the workflow is red; it does not silently guess that no dispatch exists.

GitHub keeps at most one pending run per concurrency group. With one bot start and one cron fallback that is enough: the fallback waits for the running dispatch, and after the dispatch succeeds the guard skips the duplicate. A third run arriving while one is running and one is already pending could replace the older pending one; that is GitHub's queue behaviour and is not changed by `cancel-in-progress: false`.

## Involved Public APIs

No product API, UI, CLI or schema changes. The change is limited to `.github/workflows/nightly.yml` and the project-level bot schedule.

The guard job declares `actions: read` so `gh run list` can read workflow runs; the workflow-level `contents: read` remains. No new repository secret or credential is needed: `github.token` is the existing per-run token. The bot scheduled task uses the existing `workflow_dispatch` entry point. The cron trigger stays in place.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- **L4 `daily` gate:** `stamp` produces the `nightly-YYYYMMDD-<sha>` version, `gate` calls the reusable `ci.yml` with `profile: daily`, and `report` writes the outcome. Their bodies and inputs do not change; only the guard condition is added.
- **Release:** `release.yml` is a separate workflow and is not affected by this plan.
- **Product code and tests:** no product path changes. The real-model journeys, case selection and evaluation are untouched.
- **Project automation:** the bot console / `定时任务与通知` task is project automation, not repository code; it needs no repository change from this Issue.

## Test Design and Test Plan

This Issue recommends a change; it does not implement it. The repository's implementation should verify the following, none of which requires a paid real-model run:

- `actionlint` (or at least a YAML parse) passes on the updated `nightly.yml`.
- A `workflow_dispatch` run still executes `stamp`, `gate` and `report`; the guard sets `run=true` for that event.
- A scheduled run with no successful dispatch created since 16:00 UTC sets `run=true` and executes the three jobs normally.
- A scheduled run with a successful dispatch created since 16:00 UTC sets `run=false`; `stamp`, `gate` and `report` are skipped, and the run's conclusion is success rather than a red `report` failure.
- A failed or cancelled dispatch does not suppress the scheduled run, because only `-s success` matches.
- With a dispatch run in progress, a scheduled run queues in the same concurrency group and does not cancel the dispatch; after the dispatch succeeds, the scheduled run's guard skips the duplicate.
- The project scheduled task starts exactly one run when none is queued or in progress, and starts nothing when one is.
- If the repository adds a workflow-contract test, assert the guard's `-e workflow_dispatch -s success` filter and the `needs`/`if` values on `stamp`, `gate` and `report`. The repository already has tests that read `nightly.yml` (for example `.ci/case-execution.test.mjs`), so there is an existing place for such a contract.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The bot console or a project scheduled task on `定时任务与通知` starts `nightly.yml` on `main` shortly after 16:00 UTC, after checking that no run of it is queued or in progress; if one is, it starts nothing.
- [ ] `workflow_dispatch` remains available and starts the full workflow.
- [ ] The 16:00 UTC cron remains as a fallback, and the guard skips the scheduled run when a successful `workflow_dispatch` run was created since the most recent 16:00 UTC.
- [ ] The workflow has `concurrency` with `cancel-in-progress: false`, so a scheduled run does not cancel a running dispatch run.
- [ ] `stamp`, `gate` and `report` keep their current behaviour on the normal path; the guard only adds the skip condition.
- [ ] The workflow change is reviewed and merged through the repository's normal process, not through this task.

## Additional Information

### Prior recommendation search

I searched open and closed Issues in this repository before writing this. The query terms and results were:

- `nightly.yml` — 17 results; the closest are #1160 (a Nightly failure report) and #850 (a per-case execution table). Neither recommends scheduling.
- `workflow_dispatch` — 18 results; the closest are #615 (a manual-validation workflow) and #243 (a merged PR that removed a release-branch dispatch). Neither is about the late Nightly.
- `in:title schedule Nightly` — only #243, the same merged PR.
- `in:title schedule` — #1029 (an unrelated queued-run retry bug) and #243.
- `nightly delayed` — #1035 (export preview OOM) and #283 (L1–L5 test coverage); neither is about the cron delay.
- `in:title delayed`, `in:title late`, `in:title cron`, `cron delayed Nightly` — no matching Issue.
- `scheduled run late` — 30 results, but none of the items inspected is a recommendation for this workflow.
- `定时任务` and `"scheduled task" Nightly` — no scheduling recommendation for this workflow.

No earlier recommendation exists, and no maintainer closed a scheduling recommendation as not wanted. This is a new Issue rather than a comment.

### Decision and scope

This Issue is a recommendation only. I have not opened a pull request, pushed a branch, or edited `.github/workflows/nightly.yml`. Whether to adopt Part 2, and its exact implementation, is the repository's own decision; a maintainer or code owner must review and merge it through the normal process.

The workflow file at the time of writing is [`.github/workflows/nightly.yml` on `main`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/main/.github/workflows/nightly.yml). The run data above was read from `GET /repos/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/workflows/nightly.yml/runs?event=schedule` and `...?event=workflow_dispatch`.

items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

The L1 step `Enforce changed-path test evidence` compares a pull request with the **base recorded in the event payload** while the checked-out tree is the **merge commit**. When `main` moves after the pull request is opened, every commit `main` gained in between is attributed to the pull request. On #1297 that produced seven blocking `added source has no test mapping` lines for files the pull request never touched, and `merge-gate` failed only because L1 failed.

Observed on PR #1297, head `7024be557e9a3174ebb5dec0e8b81dee7ce53b01` (CI run [45309655627](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/45309655627), job `L1 (static checks)` 138162322793):

```
CI_BASE_SHA: 9eab97609655cbd50a41e9e2da6e5c5aa6d848d8
CI_HEAD_SHA: 4f0eaa076575814047c6f713083c06d5725779f4
...
Changed-path source-test policy failed:
- added source has no test mapping: apps/desktop/src/api/reviewer.ts
- added source has no test mapping: apps/desktop/src/permission-summary.ts
- added source has no test mapping: apps/desktop/src/views/reviewer/ReviewCard.tsx
- added source has no test mapping: apps/desktop/src/views/reviewer/presentation.ts
- added source has no test mapping: apps/desktop/src/views/settings/McpImportMenu.tsx
- added source has no test mapping: apps/web/src/permission-summary.ts
- added source has no test mapping: packages/schema/src/permission-description.ts
```

Why those are not this pull request's files:

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` passes `CI_BASE_SHA: github.event.pull_request.base.sha` and `CI_HEAD_SHA: github.sha`. For a `pull_request` run `github.sha` is the merge commit, and `actions/checkout` fetches exactly that (`+4f0eaa07…:refs/remotes/pull/1297/merge` in the same log).
- `4f0eaa076575814047c6f713083c06d5725779f4` is `Merge 7024be55… into d13cead9…`, with parents `d13cead964c04987085a1dfd275b20cd49bcc1b5` (current `main`) and `7024be55…` (the pull request head).
- `9eab97609655cbd50a41e9e2da6e5c5aa6d848d8` is this branch's merge base with `main` — the base recorded when the pull request was opened — and the pull request still reports it after `main` moved to `d13cead9`.
- `.ci/changed-path-check.mjs` therefore ran `git diff 9eab9760 4f0eaa07`, which contains every commit `main` gained between `9eab9760` and `d13cead9`.
- All seven blocking paths were added to `main` in that interval; for example `apps/web/src/permission-summary.ts` does not exist at `9eab9760`.
- The pull request changes five files, and the only inventory source among them is `packages/schema/src/idea-tree.ts`, which the same run reported as `existing changed source has no test mapping` — a warning, not a failure. **The pull request's own diff is clean under this policy.**

Impact: any pull request that is behind `main` fails L1 and, through it, `merge-gate` — on a rule it does not violate, with a message naming files its author never wrote. The workaround is to rebase (that makes the recorded base equal the merge commit's first parent and the check passes), but it is undiscoverable from the failure text and it clears approvals.

This is the same class of defect as #1271 (the release-version gate read the merge tree against the recorded base, so a stale branch looked like a version bump); #1269/#1272 fixed that by comparing the tested merge commit with **its own first parent** and validating the topology.

#### Suggested fix

Use the merge commit's first parent as the comparison base instead of the event's recorded base: require the checked-out head to be a two-parent merge whose second parent is `pull_request.head.sha`, take the first parent as the base, and fail explicitly with a named error when the topology is not that. Note that `git merge-base <recorded base> <merge commit>` returns the stale base itself, so it is not a substitute.

#### Regression case

`.ci/changed-path-check.test.mjs` already builds real temporary histories, so the case belongs there:

1. `main` commit `B`;
2. `main` commit `M` that adds an unmapped behavioral source (e.g. `services/runner/src/New Runner.ts`);
3. pull-request commit `P` on `B` that adds only a test or doc file;
4. merge commit with parents `M` and `P`;
5. run with `CI_BASE_SHA=B`, `CI_HEAD_SHA=<merge>`;
6. expect exit 0 with no blocking entry for `M`'s file (a warning or `0/1 mapped` line is fine).

Today that run reports `M`'s file as an added unmapped source and exits 1, so the case distinguishes the fix from the current behaviour.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Repo state | `main` `d13cead964c04987085a1dfd275b20cd49bcc1b5`; incident on PR #1297 head `7024be557e9a3174ebb5dec0e8b81dee7ce53b01`, merge commit `4f0eaa076575814047c6f713083c06d5725779f4`, recorded base `9eab97609655cbd50a41e9e2da6e5c5aa6d848d8` |
| Where | `.ci/changed-path-check.mjs`, invoked by the `Enforce changed-path test evidence` step in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (L1 job) |
| Introduced by | `d13cead9…` (`test: complete coverage and CI gate hardening`), which added the script, its test file and the sources it now reports |
| CI evidence | L1 job 138162322793 failed on `Enforce changed-path test evidence`; `merge-gate` job 138163564882 failed on `Require all jobs selected by this event` |
| Workaround | rebase onto current `main`; the comparison then starts at `d13cead9` and only the pull request's files are checked |

### Additional Information

- A pull request that is up to date with its base is unaffected: its recorded base equals the merge commit's first parent.
- The warning list of such runs is polluted the same way (`existing changed source has no test mapping` for files `main` touched after the branch was opened), so the output cannot be read as "what this pull request changed".
- The check is correctly load-bearing for the pull request's own additions: the `packages/schema/src/idea-tree.ts` warning in the same run shows the mapping policy still applies to the diff this pull request really produced.

### Version Information

- `main` at filing: `d13cead964c04987085a1dfd275b20cd49bcc1b5`.
- The gate step was introduced by `d13cead964c04987085a1dfd275b20cd49bcc1b5` (`test: complete coverage and CI gate hardening`, committer date `2026-11-24T00:58:49Z`).
- First observed incident: PR #1297, head `7024be55`, base `9eab9760`, run created `2026-11-24T02:04:18Z`.
