oldest.body:
### 🚀 Background Description


`/evolve-design` is the only entry point for program evolution today, but it is a **hidden slash command** — a user must already know to type the `/evolve-design` prefix. The only visible entry is a button inside the artifact detail modal (it fills the composer with `/evolve-design make the artifact X better: ` and still requires the user to complete and send the sentence manually).

Two problems follow:

1. **We assume the user knows the command.** The UI never guides anyone toward `/evolve-design`; ordinary researchers will not type a slash command they have never seen.
2. **The interaction is command-shaped.** The user must learn command syntax (`--algorithm puct/openevolve`) instead of speaking naturally.

Goal: a user expresses improvement intent in **natural language** (e.g. "make this result better", "帮我优化这个程序"), the **framework actively recommends a tree-search evolution**, and the interaction stays natural-language end to end — no slash-command literacy required.



### Design Ideas

Land in three layers, reusing the existing `/evolve-design` chain (`EvolveAlgorithmPicker`, `EvolveToolRuntime`, `/api/evolve/runs`, the native-agent turn). No new capability surface.

#### Layer 1: Composer intent recognition (frontend, minimal)

Lightweight, testable, pure-function intent detection in the composer (no LLM round-trip):

- Match program-evolution intent:
  - the `/evolve-design` slash prefix (existing behavior, kept), **or**
  - a sentence pairing an **improvement verb** with an **evolvable target** (program / code / algorithm / function / model / script / …), in Chinese or English.
- When matched, offer a **low-intrusion suggestion bar** ("It looks like you want to improve a result or program. Run an automated search that keeps the best-scoring variant?") — the user must explicitly accept before anything is started.
- On accept, show the existing `EvolveAlgorithmPicker`; on select, fill `/evolve-design --algorithm X <natural language>` and send.

**Why confirmation before the picker?** Starting a search spends real budget (mutations + sandboxed evaluations). Detection is a guess, so it must only *offer*; the user's explicit accept is the gate. This also protects against misreads — a user saying "优化一下" while discussing formatting is never sent down an expensive search.

#### Layer 2: Agent-driven recommendation (backend, core value)

In the native-agent turn loop, recognise improvement intent in messages that do *not* carry the `/evolve-design` prefix:

- When the user asks to improve a program/result, the Agent **recommends** a tree-search evolution in its reply and offers to start it, reusing `EvolveToolRuntime`'s `create_evolve_run`.
- The interaction stays natural-language: the user replies "yes, go ahead", and the Agent starts the run.

#### Layer 3: Visible entry point (frontend, complete experience)

- A "program evolution" entry in the composer opens a **natural-language prompt** ("Which artifact? What does 'better' mean here?") instead of filling a slash command.
- The artifact-detail modal button opens the same prompt instead of generating `/evolve-design ...` text.

### Intent recognition rules

`detectEvolveIntent(message)` returns true only when **both** an improvement verb and an evolvable target are present, and no non-evolvable target is named:

| Example | Result | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `improve the program` / `优化一下这个程序` | true | verb + program target |
| `make this better` / `把这个做得更好` | false | no explicit evolvable target |
| `optimize the interface layout` / `优化一下界面布局` | false | layout is not evolvable |
| `improve the workflow steps` | false | steps are not evolvable |
| `this result is better than the last one` / `这个更好` | false | no verb+target pair |
| `improve the description` / `改一下格式` | false | formatting/explanation excluded |

`isEvolveDesignCommand(message)` distinguishes the explicit command (goes straight to the picker) from natural language (goes through the suggestion bar).

### API surface

- No new public API; reuse `/api/evolve/runs` and `/api/evolve/runs/:id/events`.
- Layer 2 reuses `EvolveToolRuntime`'s existing tools; no new registration.
- Intent detection is a pure frontend function, unit-testable.

### Affected modules

- `apps/web/src/App.tsx`: composer intent detection; `showEvolveAlgorithmPicker` trigger extension (currently matches only the `/evolve-design` prefix); suggestion-bar state.
- `apps/web/src/evolve/EvolveSuggestionBar.tsx` (new): confirmation bar.
- `apps/web/src/evolve/intent.ts` (new): `detectEvolveIntent` / `isEvolveDesignCommand`.
- `apps/web/src/evolve/EvolveAlgorithmPicker.tsx`: reused unchanged.
- `apps/web/src/api/evolve.ts`: reused.
- `services/api/src/native-agent/index.ts`: turn-loop intent recognition and recommendation (Layer 2).
- `packages/evolve`: `EvolveToolRuntime` reused.
- i18n: suggestion-bar copy, composer entry copy (en + zh).

### Involved Public APIs

_No response_

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

_No response_

### Test Design and Test Plan

**Functional**

- [ ] Unit tests for `detectEvolveIntent`: Chinese/English verb+target, no-target messages, non-evolvable targets, negation phrases.
- [ ] Unit tests for `isEvolveDesignCommand`: command vs natural-language separation.
- [ ] Composer + natural-language improvement intent + artifact reference → suggestion bar appears.
- [ ] Accepting the suggestion → algorithm picker appears.
- [ ] Selecting an algorithm → `/evolve-design` evolution run starts.
- [ ] Ordinary messages (no intent) → nothing appears, normal conversation.
- [ ] Artifact modal button → opens natural-language prompt, not a filled command.

**Regression**

- [ ] Existing `/evolve-design` command path unchanged; explicit `--algorithm` no longer re-opens the picker.
- [ ] Existing evolve E2E / unit tests pass.

**User-perspective E2E**

- User expresses improvement intent naturally → framework recommends → natural-language confirm → evolution run starts.
- A message without improvement intent never triggers the evolution recommendation.

### Notes

- Follows the product direction: "the framework recommends tree search, but the interaction stays natural language."
- Layer 1 (frontend intent recognition + confirmation bar) can land as an independent MR first; Layer 2 (Agent-driven recommendation) depends on the turn-loop change and can follow.


### Additional Information

_No response_

oldest.author: HongyeZhou
oldest.body:
## Problem
On #381 head `fb2fe785` (Fixes #324), in Ask mode with a domain-allowlist policy, resuming a blocked retrieval takes three cards in a row:
1. **Run a shell script** (approve the original `run_shell`)
2. **Sandbox network** for the observed denied host ("Continue the sandbox retrieval blocked by this execution")
3. **Run a shell script** again, for the NEW `run_shell` that carries `network_authorization_id`

Every step is correct by itself, but together they are heavy for a single user intent ("let this retrieval reach host X").

## Expected
One network decision is enough to resume. The re-run that consumes the one-use network token should not ask again for shell approval the user just gave, as long as it is the same kind of execution.

## Proposal / security considerations
- Reuse the prior shell approval only for the token re-run: same Session/Agent/run, same Runner, and the token is consumed exactly once.
- Do not carry the approval over if the command changes materially. At minimum, show the new command in the network card or require re-approval when it differs from the blocked execution. Otherwise a token re-run becomes a way to run unreviewed code with network access.
- Never inherit Always Allow / direct-execution consent; keep child Agents and later runs excluded, as #381 already does.
- Alternative: merge steps 2 and 3 into a single card ("Allow network to X and re-run this command").

## Context
Refs #381, #324. Observed in a local box run (API + bubblewrap runner + egress gateway, scripted model).

## Verification cases
1. **Baseline repro (current behaviour)**
   - Preconditions: Ask approval mode; sandbox network `domain-allowlist` with `allowedDomains: ["pypi.org"]`; the model calls `run_shell` with `curl -sS -m 8 -o /dev/null -w 'HTTP %{http_code}\n' https://example.com/`.
   - Steps: Allow once on the shell card → allow once on the `example.com:443` network card → the model issues a NEW `run_shell` with the returned `network_authorization_id`.
   - Expected (today): A third "Run a shell script" card appears. After it is approved, the first execution has failed (`CONNECT tunnel failed`, HTTP 000) and the second has completed with HTTP 200 (2 executions in total).
2. **Same command, token re-run: single network decision**
   - Preconditions/Steps: As in 1.
   - Expected (after fix): Exactly 2 cards in total (shell, network). The token re-run with the identical command starts without another shell card and ends with HTTP 200.
3. **Different command must re-ask (security)**
   - Preconditions: As in 1, but the token re-run uses a different command (e.g. appends `; echo changed > marker.txt`).
   - Expected: A shell card is shown again, or the network card displays the new command before approval. It never runs silently.
4. **Token is one-use**
   - Steps: After case 2, the model calls `run_shell` a third time with the same `network_authorization_id`.
   - Expected: The call is rejected ("Unknown, consumed or foreign sandbox network authorization"), and no execution is started.
5. **No carry-over across scope**
   - Steps: Use the token or reused approval from (a) a child Agent, (b) a later run in the same Session, (c) another Runner.
   - Expected: Each is rejected or re-prompts, and no shell approval is reused.
6. **Deny path**
   - Steps: As in 1, but Deny the network card.
   - Expected: No re-run and no third card. The assistant reports the retrieval as blocked/incomplete, and the sandbox network settings are unchanged.
oldest.title: [Usability] Resume after a sandbox network block needs three consecutive approvals

oldest.author: wyhohyw
oldest.body:
## Background

After a long-running tool execution fails, an Agent often has to infer completed work, reusable outputs, and possible continuation points from free-form logs. Execution state and logs alone do not provide a consistent basis for deciding where to continue.

Support recovery of failed long-running tasks: after the failure is addressed and the prerequisites are verified, the Agent can reuse completed results and continue from a supported recovery point, reducing unnecessary recomputation.

A shared, optional recovery metadata contract for tools and task adapters provides the supporting evidence. The LLM uses it to decide the next action; the framework persists and exposes it alongside the existing execution record, reusing existing execution tools and permission checks.

## Requested functionality

- Identify the original execution and expose completed stages or work units, the failed stage, and the failure reason when the task adapter can determine them.
- Reference reusable outputs and available task checkpoints using stable artifact/file/version identifiers where supported. Distinguish verified completed outputs from partial files.
- Explicitly report whether continuation is supported, unsupported, or unknown, including available continuation entry points and required inputs when supported.
- Describe conditions that must be checked before continuation, such as original execution termination, input/configuration changes, environment availability, and output validity.
- Preserve the metadata across refresh/reconnect and make it available through existing execution inspection and Agent tool results. Keep existing tools without recovery metadata compatible.
- Let the Agent inspect the evidence and choose repair, continuation, or a fresh attempt through existing execution tools and permission checks. Metadata itself must not automatically launch a replacement task.

The exact schema should follow the existing execution/tool-result architecture. Framework code should remain independent of specific scientific pipeline stages; task adapters supply domain-specific recovery information.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A shared, documented optional recovery metadata contract is available to long-running tools/task adapters.
- [ ] At least one supported long-running task adapter or representative test fixture demonstrates completed work, failed work, reusable result/checkpoint references, and continuation prerequisites.
- [ ] The Agent can retrieve persisted metadata after reconnecting and use it to identify a supported continuation point without relying solely on free-form logs.
- [ ] Unsupported or unknown recovery capability is explicit; the framework does not invent missing checkpoints or treat file existence alone as proof of completion.
- [ ] A running or unknown original execution is not automatically resubmitted because recovery metadata was returned.
- [ ] Tests cover supported/unsupported/unknown continuation, partial or invalid outputs, changed prerequisites, and persistence/readback.

## Scope and related work

- #398 covers reconnecting to the original NPU task, recovering its state/results, and avoiding duplicate submissions. This issue supplies structured evidence for Agent decisions after a confirmed failure.
- #278 covers in-conversation configuration and task continuation.
- This first version does not include arbitrary Agent-history rollback, restoration of process/NPU memory, or implementing model-specific computational checkpointing. Actual computational continuation depends on task-program support.
- Target release: **v0.3.0, October 30, 2026**, tracked in #249.

---

## 需求背景

长任务执行失败后，Agent 往往需要从自由文本日志中推断哪些工作已经完成、哪些结果可以复用、可以从哪里继续。仅有执行状态和日志，缺少统一的信息契约支撑这些判断。

支持长任务失败后的恢复：处理失败原因并确认接续前提后，Agent 能复用已完成结果，从受支持的恢复点继续，减少不必要的重复计算。

工具和任务适配器提供共享、可选的结构化恢复信息，作为上述能力的支撑。LLM 根据这些证据决定下一步；框架负责随现有执行记录持久化和提供查询，复用已有执行工具与权限检查。

## 期望功能

- 标识原执行；任务适配器能够确定时，返回已完成阶段或工作单元、失败阶段及失败原因。
- 通过受支持的稳定产物／文件／版本标识，引用可复用结果和任务检查点，区分已验证的完整结果与未完成文件。
- 明确返回可续跑、不支持续跑或能力未知；支持时给出可用续跑入口及所需输入。
- 描述接续前需要检查的条件，例如原执行已经结束、输入和配置变化、环境可用性及结果有效性。
- 刷新或重连后仍能通过现有执行查询和 Agent 工具结果获取这些信息；兼容不提供恢复信息的已有工具。
- Agent 根据证据选择修复、接续或重新执行，沿用现有执行工具及权限检查；返回恢复信息本身不自动启动替代任务。

具体字段设计应复用现有执行记录和工具结果架构。框架保持通用，由任务适配器提供具体业务阶段及恢复信息。

## 验收标准

- [ ] 提供有文档说明、可选的统一恢复信息契约，供长任务工具／适配器使用。
- [ ] 至少一个受支持的长任务适配器或有代表性的测试夹具，能够展示已完成工作、失败工作、可复用结果／检查点引用及接续前提。
- [ ] 重连后 Agent 能读取持久化信息，识别受支持的接续点，无须仅依赖自由文本日志推断。
- [ ] 不支持或能力未知时明确返回；框架不虚构检查点，也不把文件存在直接当作步骤已完成。
- [ ] 原执行仍在运行或结果未知时，不会因为返回恢复信息而自动重复提交。
- [ ] 测试覆盖支持／不支持／未知续跑能力、部分或无效结果、前提条件变化及持久化读取。

## 范围与关联

- #398 负责找回原 NPU 任务、恢复状态和结果、避免重复提交；本需求为确认失败后的 Agent 接续决策提供结构化证据。
- #278 负责对话内配置和任务接续。
- 首版不包含任意历史 Agent 状态回滚、进程／NPU 内存恢复，也不代替具体模型实现计算检查点。实际计算续跑依赖任务程序支持。
- 目标版本：**2026 年 10 月 30 日 v0.3.0**，在 #249 跟踪。

recent.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**What happens.** While a turn is running the composer is disabled: the textarea has `disabled=true`, nothing can be typed, Enter does nothing, and the only control left is 停止. The API underneath would accept the same message and queue it — `POST /api/sessions/<id>/runs` goes straight to `createQueuedRun` and every run carries a `queueOrder` — so a change of mind has to either wait out the whole turn or throw it away.

**Minimal reproduction.**

1. New Session, permission 完全访问.
2. Send a long request, e.g. `上传 flip.csv 做 A/B 分析：按 batch 分组比较均值差、95% CI 和 p 值，脚本写成 analysis.py。`
3. About 8 s later, try to send `算了，2+2 等于几？`. The textarea is `disabled`; typing does nothing and Enter does nothing.
4. The only available action is 停止, which ends the turn and discards the work in progress.

**Expected.** A follow-up can be handed over while the turn runs — either it is queued and the UI says so ("本轮结束后发送"), or the composer stays editable and offers 停止 / 排队 as two explicit choices. The server already has the queue, so the client is the only thing standing in the way.

**Actual.**

- `apps/desktop/src/views/Composer.tsx:1313` — `disabled={running || jwBlocked !== undefined || readOnlyReason !== undefined}`; the textarea and the send button go dead for the whole turn, and there is no "queue" affordance anywhere (`grep` for a queued-message UI in `apps/desktop/src` finds none).
- `services/api/src/http/index.ts:4278-4283` — `POST /api/sessions/<id>/runs` calls `createQueuedRun` with no "a run is already active" rejection; `services/api/src/store.ts:3798` assigns `queueOrder = max(queueOrder) + 1`, and `scheduleSessionRuns` starts them one at a time.
- Measured cost of having no queue (Session `d2313dd3`, the same 200-row CSV; each row is one user turn, all but the first ended by 停止 or by the driver's 25 min cap):

  | turn | duration | tokens | outcome |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `507de1dd` | 8m47s | 908,269 | completed |
  | `33b16421` | 33m26s | 3,649,292 | cancelled |
  | `da35c445` | 25m00s | 3,011,791 | cancelled |
  | `28a4cafa` | 25m00s | 2,312,731 | cancelled |
  | `560dea78` | 25m00s | 1,881,906 | cancelled |

  **11.8M tokens** for one analysis, ~7.2M of them on three discarded attempts. Each attempt started because the previous one could not be corrected mid-flight; each correctable mistake (a parameter, a grouping) costs the whole turn.

**Why it matters.** "Change the grouping", "use the median instead", "forget it, answer 2+2" are the normal way a user steers an analysis, and on a 25-minute turn none of them is possible without paying for the turn first. 停止 is the only escape and it is destructive — and per #1525 it does not even stop the background shell the turn started.

**Suggested fix.**

1. Submit while running: keep the composer enabled, post the message, and show it as queued ("已排队，本轮结束后发送") with the option to withdraw it. The server path already exists (`createQueuedRun` + `queueOrder`), so this is mostly client state plus a queued-bubble in the transcript.
2. If queueing is deliberately not offered, at least let the reader type and decide at the end: keep the draft editable while the turn runs and offer 停止 / 本轮结束后发送 as two explicit actions.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Product: source checkout of `main` at `e374837d37a8a536483a9ef8b5d2a98bd23a5aee` (2026-11-28T01:17:17Z): API on `127.0.0.1:4410`, Runner on `4411` (bubblewrap), desktop web surface on `http://127.0.0.1:5174`.
- Host: Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, x86_64, Node.js v22.23.5.
- Client: Playwright Chromium, 1440x900 and 1600x1000 viewports, locale `zh-CN`.
- Model: Ark DeepSeek `deepseek-v4.1-flash`; permission mode 完全访问.
- Sessions: `d2313dd3-211a-4132-b619-ff1be5d8f9c7` (the table above), `5b8d2619-29c7-4690-9b33-f7fa8349de3e` (the three-cancel scenario where the same disabled textarea was measured: two cancels settled in 327 ms / 299 ms).

### Additional Information

- Found while running the "user changes their mind" scenarios (S-212 parameter flip-flop, S-213 cancel flip-flop): every attempt to correct mid-turn failed at the composer, not at the model.
- The disabled state is what makes a change of mind expensive, not the model's speed: with a queue, the same 8m47s first turn would have been followed by a corrected second turn instead of a cancel-and-restart.
- Screenshot attached: a turn running with the composer in its locked state.

### Version Information

- Repository `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, branch `main`, commit `e374837d37a8a536483a9ef8b5d2a98bd23a5aee` (2026-11-28).
- Files inspected: `apps/desktop/src/views/Composer.tsx`, `services/api/src/http/index.ts`, `services/api/src/runs/index.ts`, `services/api/src/store.ts`.

![A turn mid-run: the composer is disabled and 停止 is the only control](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f0560634-42ae-4824-a189-accdd97dbae2)

recent.author: yuanzhou75
recent.body:
## What happens

`services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts:20-39` decides whether an exception is the caller's mistake by matching words in its message:

```ts
return [
  /\bis required\b/i,
  /\bmust\b/i,
  /\bcontains? an unknown value\b/i,
  /\bcannot\b/i,
  /\bdoes not match\b/i,
  /\binvalid\b/i,
  /\bis too long\.?\s*$/i,
  /\bunsafe\b.*\b(?:archive|package|path)\b/i,
  /\bplain basename\b/i,
].some((pattern) => pattern.test(error.message));
```

Anything that matches is answered as a **400 whose body is the raw `error.message`** (`services/api/src/http/index.ts:5216` takes `error.message`, `:5295` sends it with 400). An internal fault therefore becomes a user-visible client error, carrying JavaScript text that was never written for a reader.

Observed instance, from #1520: an import walked a tool record whose `references` array holds literature records rather than composer references; `ResearchPackageIds.id` opened with `source.match(...)` (`services/api/src/research-package-history.ts:26`), so the message was

```
Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'match')
```

`/\bcannot\b/i` matched it, and the client received **`400` with that exact string**. The throw site itself is fixed separately (#1521), but the rule that turned it into a 400 is untouched: the next internal `TypeError` whose text contains *cannot*, *must* or *invalid* will be reported the same way.

## What is expected

- An exception raised by the server's own logic is a **500** with the generic body (`services/api/src/http/index.ts:5296-5304`) and an `unclassified_request_error` line, whatever its message says.
- A **400** comes from something that knows the input was wrong — `ApiStatusError`, `SessionStoreHttpError`, or an explicit code — not from matching prose.
- JavaScript text is never echoed to the client. If a 400 does quote a message, it must be a message that was written to be read.

## How to reach it

Any code path where an in-process fault reaches the request handler. The word list covers the most common accidental shapes:

- `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '…')` — matches `cannot`; this is the #1520 instance.
- `RangeError: Invalid array length`, `TypeError: Invalid value used as weak map key` — match `invalid`.
- `TypeError: Cannot convert undefined or null to object` — matches `cannot`.
- Any message containing `must` (e.g. a validator that was written for an operator rather than a client).

A minimal, dependency-free check of the rule: `isKnownClientInputError(new TypeError("Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'match')"))` returns `true` — the first pattern that matches is `/cannot/i`, and the function has no other gate.

## Why the word list exists, and why it is a trapdoor

The comment above the function (`error-classification.ts:15-19`) says it is there for legacy validators that still throw plain `Error` objects, and that new handlers should prefer typed errors. That is the right direction, but the fallback is inverted: it guesses *client mistake* from vocabulary, so every future internal fault with the wrong adjective is misreported, while the genuinely unclassified branch (`:5296-5304`) — the one that logs `unclassified_request_error`, which the team uses to find real faults — becomes harder to reach.

## Impact

- Status codes stop being a contract: a caller cannot tell a bad request from a broken server, so clients show an input error for a server fault and retry logic acts on the wrong signal.
- Internal implementation details (function names, property names, class names) reach the UI as text.
- Real server faults are logged at the wrong level or not classified at all, which is exactly what `unclassified_request_error` exists to prevent.
- A malformed import in the same family as #1520 (`400 Cannot read properties of undefined`) is indistinguishable from a correct refusal.

## Environment

- `main` `e89ba7bb3a5555a945b6edb704c7c1e6f2397932`; lines above are that commit's.
- Found while auditing the import path for #1520; the rule itself was read, not exercised on this host (the analysis tree has no installed dependencies).
recent.title: [Bug]: An internal exception whose text says "cannot" is answered 400 with the raw JavaScript message

recent.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version (checked on `main` = `4f3d75ed7ccb8d7bc3fb5b6792fac6b00bc5b9de`, 2026-11-28).
- [x] A reproduction, the preview and real-export responses and the environment are below.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**What happens.** The export dialog's preview reports a limitation that is not true and that the real export does not carry:

```text
cas::unavailable source object
```

It appears whenever a Session contains a workspace file whose current provenance revision has **no `contentHash`** (a file created by a tool, or one restored by an earlier import — no address is known yet). Nothing is actually missing: the real export hashes the file as it copies it, writes its object, and produces a manifest with **no** `cas:` line. So the dialog shows 5 limitations (ResearchPackageActions.tsx:345 renders every `preview.omissions` entry verbatim) for a package that will say 4, and the extra line is an internal CAS diagnostic, not something a user can act on.

**Evidence, same Session, same profile (`level=complete`)**

| call | result |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/projects/<pid>/research-package/preview?sessionId=<sid>&level=complete&includeFullTrajectory=0&includeFullMemoryGraph=0` | `200`; `omissions` = **5**, including `"cas::unavailable source object"` |
| `GET /api/projects/<pid>/research-package?sessionId=<sid>&level=complete&includeFullTrajectory=0&includeFullMemoryGraph=0` | `200`; 971,944 B, sha256 `cd7578bea04f9cb4ffbd0b52d5b7bcb9b2abb34dee92220680ef7fb7a986b84e` |
| that package's `manifest.omissions` | **4** entries — the `cas::` line is absent |
| `POST .../research-package/inspect` with the same bytes | `200`; 4 omissions |

Preview omissions (verbatim):

```json
[
  "Scientific memory could not be exported because the memory graph service is unavailable.",
  "来源包含必要导入的研究记录；完整导出仅包含当前已有内容，无法补回原包省略的历史。",
  "cas::unavailable source object",
  "Workspace file revision payloads are not retained separately; revision metadata and the current file payload are included.",
  "Notebook execution history is not separately persisted by this ScienceDiscovery version; available .ipynb files are included as workspace objects."
]
```

Manifest omissions (verbatim): the same list **without** `"cas::unavailable source object"`.

The package carries the file: `manifest.inventory` contains `object:objects/56bb6f20283966a4abb47dc6b4d89bbd3b8197b889f96c6006676fa9b47ef368:171`, and `exportProfile.included.workspaceFiles = 3` for the three files of that Session.

**The file that triggers it** (provenance via `GET /api/sessions/<sid>/workspace/provenance?path=notes%2Fplain-notes.txt`):

```json
"currentRevision": { "id": "b53b389e-…", "origin": "unknown", "size": 171, "path": "notes/plain-notes.txt" }
```

No `contentHash` in `currentRevision`; the two uploaded files in the same Session (`air-quality.csv`, `pixel.png`) do have one, and do not produce the line.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Local source stack from `4f3d75ed` (`./scripts/start-stack.sh --mode local --no-node-build --no-jiuwenswarm`).
2. Get a Session with one workspace file whose current revision has no `contentHash`. Two ordinary ways: (a) let the agent write a file (`notes/plain-notes.txt` above came from a normal Session turn); (b) import any package and use its read-only snapshot or “继续研究” copy — the restored revisions have no hash until they are next rewritten. This reproduces on several such Sessions, not one.
3. Open the export dialog, or call the preview route above → `omissions` contains `"cas::unavailable source object"`.
4. Export for real with the same parameters → `manifest.omissions` does not contain it; the file's object is in the archive.

**Root cause (code on `4f3d75ed`)**

* `services/api/src/research-snapshots.ts:633-640` — in preview mode a file whose revision has no `contentHash` gets `objectPath = ""` (its size is booked through `unpinnedObjectBytes`, which is correct: no address is known).
* `:853` — `needed` collects every `record.workspace.map((file) => file.objectPath)`, so the empty string enters the CAS work set.
* `:859-875` — for that entry the preview calls `cas.storedSize("")` / `cas.read("")`, which throws, and the catch records `omissions.push("cas::unavailable source object")` with an empty hash.
* `:812-828` — the real export instead reads the file and assigns it an address (`addObject`/`addFileSource`), so the manifest never contains that line.

**Why it matters beyond the wrong count**

* The dialog presents `cas::unavailable source object` as a user-facing 限制 (ResearchPackageActions.tsx:345). It names an internal concept, has an empty address, and contradicts what the export does, so it reads as “your package is missing something” when it is not.
* The same string is on the fatal-omission list (`research-snapshots.ts:1004`: `cas:.*:unavailable`). If a future path ever writes preview-derived omissions into `manifest.omissions` (or a client echoes them back), a healthy package would be treated as a lossy one — and once #1532's exemption is removed, that would make it non-continuable for no reason.
* The preview is what the dialog uses to decide size/limitations; a phantom entry also makes “预览 5 条 = 实际 4 条” impossible to explain to a user.

**Expected vs actual**

* Expected: the preview only lists limitations the package will really declare. A file with no known address contributes its bytes to the estimate (`unpinnedObjectBytes`) and nothing else; an empty `objectPath` must never be looked up in CAS.
* Actual: `cas::unavailable source object` is reported for a file the export carries in full.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Repository `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, `main` at `4f3d75ed7ccb8d7bc3fb5b6792fac6b00bc5b9de` (2026-11-28T06:34:26Z), clean worktree built from that commit.
- Windows 11 host + WSL2 Ubuntu, Node v22.23.4, pnpm 11.1.2.
- Local source stack: `scripts/start-stack.sh --mode local --no-node-build --no-jiuwenswarm`, isolated data directory, API `127.0.0.1:4330`, Runner `127.0.0.1:4331`; memory graph degraded (only relevant to the memory omission line).
- No model call is involved in the reproduction: preview, export and inspect are ordinary HTTP requests.
- The Session is my own; the package is the same build's own export.

### Additional Information

- Not #1520 and not #1532: those are about genuinely unavailable objects. Here **nothing is unavailable** — the file's object is in the archive; only the preview's CAS lookup of `""` invents the loss.
- The reproduction is a class, not a single Session: every Session with a hash-less workspace revision shows it (tool-created files, imported/continued snapshots).
- No repository code was modified for this report.

### Version Information

- `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` @ `4f3d75ed7ccb8d7bc3fb5b6792fac6b00bc5b9de` (`main`, 2026-11-28).
- Runner reported version: `4f3d75ed`.
recent.title: [Bug]: The export preview reports a false "cas::unavailable source object" limitation for a file that has no revision hash, and the real export does not

recent.author: zhaozhaozz
recent.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

The Runner gives up on managed scientific-environment setup after a single transient network error. Both download steps are tried exactly once:

1. **micromamba provisioner download.** `installManagedMicromamba()` (`services/runner/src/environment-store.ts`) makes one `fetch` to the GitHub release asset. A connect timeout (undici's 10 s default) fails setup with `micromamba setup failed`.
2. **Python base creation.** `bootstrapStarter()` runs one `micromamba create` for the starter packages (python 3.12, numpy, pandas, scipy, matplotlib, pysocks) through `executeEnvironmentCommand()` with a 180 s limit. A failure ends setup with `Conda environment setup failed`.

Once setup is `failed`, it stays failed until someone calls setup again. In CI, J3 (`test/journey-prepare-environment.spec.ts`) and J5 (`test/journey-real-request.spec.ts`) then report `BLOCKED: managed Python base is not ready`, and the run fails. A user on a flaky or congested network sees the same terminal failure for what is only a momentary blip. The micromamba binary is 18 MB, so retrying it is cheap.

**Observed on 2026-11-28 (merge queue, self-hosted runners).** Between 02:59 and 06:16 UTC, J3 failed 14 times in `L2 E2E (mocked, standard-config)`:

- 10 × `micromamba setup failed`. From the Playwright trace of `GET /api/environment-setup`, e.g. run [46099537626](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/46099537626):

  ```
  Could not download the micromamba provisioner from [network URL omitted] UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT: fetch failed:
  Connect Timeout Error (attempted addresses: 185.199.108.133:443, 185.199.110.133:443, 185.199.109.133:443,
  185.199.111.133:443, timeout: 10000ms) (ManagedProvisionerError / TypeError / UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT)
  ```

  The same error appears in [46100083227](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/46100083227) and [46100082508](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/46100082508). Each time setup started and failed within about 12 seconds.
- 4 × `Conda environment setup failed`, e.g. run [46099599068](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/46099599068). There micromamba was ready, then `micromamba create … --channel conda-forge python=3.12 …` failed. The recorded error holds only the command line, without micromamba's output; #1239 / #1240 cover that diagnostic gap.

The release host was reachable outside those moments: from the same machines, TCP connect took about 1 ms, and 20/20 test connections and 6/6 test downloads succeeded. The failures coincide with peak load. At each failure, 4 of 4 heavy runners on the host were busy, mostly with mocked E2E jobs running two local stacks each.

**Why so much concurrent downloading.** Every mocked E2E stack provisions the managed Python base at start-up. `batchLaunchConfig()` in `test/support/tagged/retry-runner.mjs` sets `scientificEnvs: '1'` for every batch, but only J3 needs a ready base. Each stack therefore downloads micromamba (18 MB) plus roughly 330 MB of conda packages. Several stacks sharing one network egress then hit connect timeouts, and with no retry each timeout is fatal.

**GitHub-hosted runners have not hit this.** Over the previous week (971 `pull_request` and `merge_group` CI runs), none of the 37 failed mocked E2E jobs on GitHub-hosted runners was this failure. All 14 occurrences were on self-hosted runners, where many jobs share a host's egress. The missing retry is a product defect regardless: any user whose connection drops for a few seconds during first-run setup ends up in a failed state.

**Expected.** A transient network failure during managed setup is retried with backoff and recovers without manual action. A permanent failure (SHA-256 mismatch, HTTP 404, unwritable data directory, unsolvable specs) still fails promptly and reports its reason.

**Proposed change.**

- Retry the provisioner download in `installManagedMicromamba()` on network-class failures (connect/read timeouts, connection reset, HTTP 5xx and 429), e.g. 4 attempts with jittered exponential backoff within the existing 120 s budget or a slightly larger one. Do not retry a verify failure (SHA-256 mismatch) or a write failure.
- Retry `micromamba create` / `install` in the starter bootstrap when the failure is network-class, using a fresh attempt directory. micromamba's own `remote_max_retries` / `remote_backoff_factor` / `remote_connect_timeout_secs` could also be set explicitly for these calls. Keep the 180 s command limit per attempt, or make it configurable.
- In the mocked E2E plan, enable `E2E_SCIENTIFIC_ENVS=1` only for the batch that runs J3, so the other stacks stop provisioning a base they never use. This cuts managed-setup downloads in every mocked E2E run on both runner types.

**Acceptance criteria.**

- [ ] A unit test with a fake fetcher that fails with `UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT` N−1 times and then succeeds reaches `micromamba: ready`. The same test without the change fails.
- [ ] A SHA-256 mismatch and an HTTP 404 are still reported after one attempt, with the existing guidance.
- [ ] The starter bootstrap retries a network-class `micromamba create` failure and still fails fast on an unsolvable spec. Covered by unit tests with a fake provisioner.
- [ ] Only the batch containing `test/journey-prepare-environment.spec.ts` runs with `E2E_SCIENTIFIC_ENVS=1`. J3 still asserts a ready base and stays BLOCKED when setup really fails.
- Commands that must pass: `pnpm ci:l1`, `pnpm ci:ut`, and the mocked E2E shards (`pnpm ci:e2e -- --shard standard-config` at least).

Once this lands, the self-hosted runner image no longer needs its workaround (a pre-placed pinned micromamba via `SCIENCE_AGENT_PROVISIONER_PATH`), and the runners can go back to the Runner's normal managed-download path.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Self-hosted merge-queue runners (`[self-hosted, Linux, X64, sciencediscovery]`): Docker containers on Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (kernel 6.8.0-136, x86_64), Docker 29.1.3, Node.js 22.19.0, pnpm 11.1.2, uv 0.13.7. Several runners share one host's internet egress.
- Managed micromamba pinned at 2.8.1-0 (`services/runner/src/micromamba-releases.json`), downloaded from `github.com/mamba-org/micromamba-releases` (CDN `185.199.108–111.133`); starter channel `conda-forge`.
- Mocked E2E entry: `pnpm ci:e2e -- --profile merge --shard standard-config` with `CI_E2E_LOCAL_CONCURRENCY=2`, JiuwenSwarm backend.

### Additional Information

- Related: #1239 (managed Python base setup failed, J5 BLOCKED; diagnostic gap) and #1240 (include the setup error transcript in the BLOCKED reason). That work makes the cause visible; this issue is about recovering from the transient cause.
- As a stop-gap, the self-hosted runner image currently pre-places the pinned micromamba (`SCIENCE_AGENT_PROVISIONER_PATH`) and shares a persistent `CONDA_PKGS_DIRS` across jobs. Since that change, all 16 `standard-config` jobs (each running J3) completed between 06:17 and 07:19 UTC have passed. We would rather keep runner images generic, which is why the fix belongs in the repository.
- Note for anyone using a cache: `SCIENCE_AGENT_PACKAGE_CACHE_DIR` is not a plain package cache. When set, the Runner switches to `--offline` / `offline-cache` mode, so it cannot be used to cache downloads for an online setup.

### Version Information

`main` at `e89ba7bb3` (2026-11-28). The failing merge-queue candidates were based on `main` around `e374837d3`.
recent.title: [Bug]: Managed Python environment setup fails permanently on a single transient network error (no retry for the micromamba download or conda create)

recent.author: zhaozhaozz
recent.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

Several UT cases wait for asynchronous work by polling a fixed number of times with a short sleep, then assert the final state. Their real time budget is `attempts × interval` plus the request time, between 0.5 s and 5 s. When the machine is busy, the work under test is still correct but finishes later than that, and the case fails with a state assertion. The PR under test has nothing to do with it, and every such failure also invalidates the merge groups queued behind it.

On 2026-11-28, 5 of 53 merge-queue UT runs on the self-hosted Linux runners failed this way (6 cases). These runners share a host with other merge-queue jobs, so per-request latency varies with load:

| Case | Wait | Budget | Failure | Job |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `services/api/src/run-cancel.test.ts` › `GET session usage reports gateway token usage for a completed run` | `waitForRunStatus` (line 550): `attempts = 200`, 25 ms sleep | ≈ 5 s | `expected run … to become completed`, actual `'running'` | [run 46111784577](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/46111784577/job/140876898564), [run 46115430603](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/46115430603/job/140889874181) |
| `services/api/src/research-package-http.test.ts` › `public chat branching preserves the selected prefix, evidence and immediate source across retries and restart` | `wait` (line 731): 100 × 50 ms | ≈ 5 s | `Chat branch did not finish`, `'copying' !== 'ready'` | [run 46111784577](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/46111784577/job/140876898564) |
| `services/runner/src/server.test.ts` › `managed recovery HTTP contract returns original receipts, scoped conflicts and restart identity without launching a sandbox` | poll at line 2355: 100 × 5 ms | ≈ 0.5 s | actual `'queued'`, expected `'completed'` | [run 46102644507](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/46102644507/job/140848579784) |
| `test/fixtures/app-progress-integration.test.mjs` › `mounted App loads canonical full transcripts for empty, progress-only, result-only and mixed streams` | `mountRecordedApp` (line 228): 50 × 10 ms, then returns without asserting | ≈ 0.5 s | `a stored terminal run is rendered by the mounted App` (line 265) | [run 46116154488](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/46116154488/job/140890702072) |
| `scripts/race-contract.test.mjs` › `RACE contract preserves official criteria and reports evaluation errors accurately` | `execFileSync(…, { timeout: 120_000 })` around `.ci/run-research-python.sh race`, which clones `deep_research_bench` from GitHub and resolves `.ci/research-requirements.txt` with uv inside the UT budget | 120 s | `spawnSync bash ETIMEDOUT` | [run 46109596977](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/46109596977/job/140870219493) |

The `run-cancel` case failed on two different hosts. In the first failing job the whole `run-cancel.test.ts` group took 82 s, against 44 s in a job where it passed. None of these cases failed in the 148 merge-queue UT runs on GitHub-hosted runners since 2026-11-26.

**Expected:** a case fails when the behaviour is wrong, or when the work takes long enough to mean it is stuck.

**Actual:** correct but slower work fails. The loops count attempts, not time, so 200 polls of 25 ms is a 5 s deadline on any machine; a passing run usually finishes well inside it, which is why the budget looked safe.

**Proposed fix**

1. Add one deadline-based helper to the test support code, for example `waitUntil(check, { timeoutMs, intervalMs, describe })`. It polls until a wall-clock deadline of tens of seconds and reports the last observed state when it gives up. A passing case still returns as soon as the state is reached, so it is not slower.
2. Move the four polling waits above to it. In `mountRecordedApp`, wait for the rendered `RunTimeline` with the helper instead of falling through after 50 tries.
3. Take the network out of `scripts/race-contract.test.mjs`: provision the `deep_research_bench` checkout and the uv environment before the UT slice starts (as the JiuwenSwarm install is), or give the subprocess a budget that covers a cold download.
4. A quick grep finds at least 34 more inline loops of the same `for (let i = 0; i < N; i++) { … setTimeout … }` shape in 14 test files. They can move to the helper when they are next touched.

The self-hosted runners will also move the job workspace to tmpfs to cut disk waits. That lowers the odds but does not remove them: the waits should not depend on how fast the machine is.

**Acceptance**

- The five cases above wait against a wall-clock deadline (or, for RACE, no longer download inside the case), and a timeout message names the last observed state.
- The UT slice passes with these cases while the machine is loaded, for example with `stress-ng --cpu "$(nproc)"` running next to `pnpm ci:ut`.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Self-hosted Linux X64 runners in containers (Ubuntu 24.04, Node 22.19.0), several merge-queue jobs per host at a time.
- `pnpm ci:ut -- --profile merge --coverage`, 4 Node workers (`CI_UT_WORKERS`).

### Additional Information

Related: #1493, a clock-boundary flake of the same family in `packages/workspace/src/workspace.test.ts`.

### Version Information

`main` at `40a50e010`; the cases above are unchanged there.

recent.author: HongyeZhou
recent.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**What happens.** A successful 测试连接 does not produce a short confirmation. The model row turns into one long line that carries the model id, a verdict sentence with a latency, and a permanent 26-character disclaimer:

```
deepseek-v4.1-flash · ✓ 基础检查通过（923 ms） · 仅基础检查：不验证完整会话执行路径、思考或工具调用。
```

**Minimal reproduction.**

1. 设置 › 模型 (settings → models).
2. On the configured model's row, press 测试连接 and confirm the paid-token consent when it appears.
3. The test passes in about a second and the row reads as above.

**Expected.** The pass says what the button asked: the connection works. Something like `✓ 连接成功`, optionally with the latency — one short phrase a reader can scan.

**Actual.**

- Three fragments are appended to the row: `· ✓ 基础检查通过（923 ms）` and `· 仅基础检查：不验证完整会话执行路径、思考或工具调用。` (quoted verbatim from the rendered row).
- The same verbosity is in the wizard form, where the pass renders two stacked lines — `✓ 基础检查通过（N ms）` and, underneath, `仅基础检查：不验证完整会话执行路径、思考或工具调用。` — and in the web client's own string `基础检查通过 · {latency} ms`.
- The wording also does not answer the question the button asks: 测试连接 → "did it connect?" is answered with "basic check passed", which is a different claim.

**Where it comes from.**

- `apps/desktop/src/views/settings/ModelSettings.tsx:139` builds the row text as `TEXT.settings.model.testOk(result.latencyMs)`; `:200-214` renders it inside the row's `<small>` together with the model id, and appends the note in `em.model-row-probe-note` whenever the pass is green.
- `apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts:1146-1147` (and `en.ts:1112-1113`): `testOk: (latency) => "✓ 基础检查通过（… ms）"`, `testOkNotice: "仅基础检查：不验证完整会话执行路径、思考或工具调用。"`.
- `apps/desktop/src/views/ModelForm.tsx:668` / `:714` and `zh.ts:1087,1089` render the same two sentences in the add/edit wizard.
- `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts:4304`: `"settings.modelTest.success": "基础检查通过 · {latency} ms"`.
- The note is deliberately visible rather than tooltip-only (`ModelSettings.tsx:206-209`, added for #824: "a reader who never hovers still sees what the pass does not prove"), so shortening it must keep that intent rather than hide it in a `title`.

**Why it matters.** The row is a single line, so a pass makes it longer and denser than a failure; the state that should be the quietest ("nothing to do") is the one that wraps or ellipsizes. The sentence a user needs ("connected") is buried in the middle of the line, and the one after it is a caveat that is read on every test.

**Suggested fix (recommended first).**

1. **Short verdict inline, caveat once per list.** Row text becomes `✓ 连接成功（N ms）` (`✓ Connected` in English, latency optional), and the caveat moves out of the row: one muted line under the model list header — "测试连接只验证连通性，不验证完整会话执行、思考或工具调用" — plus keep it in the row's existing `title`. One sentence per screen instead of one per row, and #824's "visible without hovering" still holds because the line is always on screen.
2. **Short verdict only.** `✓ 已连接`, caveat behind the `title` that is already set. Smallest diff, but it drops the visible caveat and reopens #824.
3. **Keep the text, change the layout.** Muted second line inside the row and shorter wording (`✓ 连接成功`); still two lines, but the row line stops being a paragraph.

All three are text/template changes plus one line of layout; option 1 is the one that keeps both the short confirmation and #824's disclosure.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Product: source checkout of `main` at `e374837d37a8a536483a9ef8b5d2a98bd23a5aee` (2026-11-28T01:17:17Z), desktop web surface on `http://127.0.0.1:5174`, API on `127.0.0.1:4410`.
- Host: Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, x86_64, Node.js v22.23.5.
- Client: Playwright Chromium, 1440x900 viewport, locale `zh-CN`.
- Model tested: Ark DeepSeek `deepseek-v4.1-flash` via `https://ark.cn-beijing.volces.com`; the pass took 923 ms.

### Additional Information

- Screenshot attached: 设置 › 模型 immediately after the pass, showing the row as quoted above.
- A failure on the same row reads `✕ <reason>` and is shorter than the pass, which is the inversion this report is about.
- The proxy settings page composes its own result string (`ProxySettings.tsx:71`), so if the wording changes it should change in the same pass or a reader will see two styles of "connected".

### Version Information

- Repository `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, branch `main`, commit `e374837d37a8a536483a9ef8b5d2a98bd23a5aee` (2026-11-28).
- Files inspected: `apps/desktop/src/views/settings/ModelSettings.tsx`, `apps/desktop/src/views/ModelForm.tsx`, `apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/text/en.ts`, `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/views/ProxySettings.tsx`.

![Settings > Models right after a pass: the row carries the verdict and the disclaimer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d82f4aa3-770e-4be6-aef7-5abdc551d2be)
recent.title: [Bug]: A passing model connection test fills the model row with a verdict and a disclaimer instead of a short success

recent.author: HongyeZhou
recent.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**What happens.** A long `run_shell` submitted in the background keeps running on the host after the user presses 停止. The run ends in ~300 ms and the composer unlocks, so the UI says the work is over, but the shell keeps running; about 100 s after the cancel the files it writes appear as artifact version 1, and the next user message is answered with that finished task's summary instead of the new question.

**Minimal reproduction.**

1. New Session, permission 完全访问, zh-CN UI.
2. Send: `用 python 循环 3 次，每次 sleep 30 秒并打印进度，最后写 progress_a.log。`
3. After ~5 s press 停止. The turn settles in 327 ms with 「已取消」 and the composer unlocks.
4. Send: `改成循环 2 次、每次 sleep 10 秒，写 progress_b.log。`
5. After ~8 s try to send `算了，2+2 等于几？` while it runs — the composer is disabled and the text cannot be typed.
6. Send: `再跑一个：循环 2 次、每次 sleep 20 秒，写 progress_c.log。` After 9 s reload the page and press 停止 again (settles in 299 ms, 「已取消」).
7. Send: `打印 ok`.

**Expected.** Stopping a turn cancels the work the turn started: no new artifact appears after the cancel, and the next message is answered on its own.

**Actual.**

- `loop_progress_c.py` and `progress_c.log` become artifacts (version 1) about 100 s after the cancel — `cc01e1a6-50a8-41b5-88f0-7e61e0918878` and `ef1091f0-59c8-47c2-bf36-51491c72ec20`.
- The answer to `打印 ok` is the cancelled task's completion summary instead of an answer to the question: 「…run_shell 后台提交 loop_progress_c.py（因超过 30 秒前台等待上限），再用 execution_status / execution_logs 跟踪至完成，最后 cat 复核磁盘文件内容一致。 产出 loop_progress_c.py — artifact cc01e1a6…, version 1；progress_c.log — artifact ef1091f0…, version 1」, 283.1K tok.
- The workspace afterwards still holds `loop_progress.py`, `progress_b.log`, `loop_progress_c.py`, `progress_c.log`.

**Where it breaks.** The three 停止 presses all ended the *run* (`run.cancelled`, `reason: "Run cancelled"`), and each one settles in 297–329 ms, so the cancel path itself works. What it does not reach is the execution the run already handed to the Runner: a `run_shell` that exceeds the foreground wait is submitted as a managed Shell Execution that lives in the Runner process (`services/runner/src/server.ts:176` — "Use managed Shell Execution for background tasks"). There is no route in `services/api/src` that cancels a running execution (searching for `cancelExecution`, `executions/:id/cancel`, `stopBackground` finds none), so the abort stops the agent loop but leaves the shell to finish. Its completion is then delivered into the Session and committed as artifact version 1, which is the message the next turn answers.

**Why it matters.** 停止 is the only per-turn escape hatch, and it silently means "stop talking about it", not "stop it". The artifacts are real and versioned, so the workspace and the artifact list disagree with what the user believes happened, and the following answer can belong to the abandoned task.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Product: source checkout of `main` at `e374837d37a8a536483a9ef8b5d2a98bd23a5aee` (2026-11-28T01:17:17Z), started from source: API on `127.0.0.1:4410`, Runner on `4411` (bubblewrap), desktop web surface on `http://127.0.0.1:5174`.
- Host: Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, x86_64, Node.js v22.23.5, 40 cores.
- Client: Playwright Chromium, 1600x1000 viewport, locale `zh-CN`.
- Model: Ark DeepSeek `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, thinking on; permission mode 完全访问.
- Session `5b8d2619-29c7-4690-9b33-f7fa8349de3e`; the cancelled run is `6454af6c`.

### Additional Information

- The 327/297/299 ms settle times are the button's own feedback, so the defect is not "stop is slow" or "stop does nothing" — it is that the work survives the stop.
- Screenshots attached: the third cancel showing 「已取消」, and the workspace/artifact list after it.
- The same run's second turn could not even be corrected: while a turn runs the composer textarea is `disabled`, so a change of mind has to wait for the turn or press 停止.

### Version Information

- Repository `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, branch `main`, commit `e374837d37a8a536483a9ef8b5d2a98bd23a5aee` (2026-11-28).
- Desktop app: source run of `main` (not a packaged release).

![The cancelled turn in the transcript (已取消) after the third stop](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3b546dc8-0e71-4360-80bc-2fe153eae52a)

![The workspace after the cancel: the shell's files are there](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cc76737c-ee51-47b2-a1f5-c0f19d6abbbc)
recent.title: [Bug]: Stopping a turn does not stop the background Shell Execution it started, and its output lands as an artifact that answers the next message

recent.author: yuanzhou75
recent.body:
## What happens

An import decides twice whether a missing immutable payload is acceptable, and the two decisions cancel each other out.

`services/api/src/research-snapshots.ts:1003` lists the omission texts that mean the copy is not whole:

```ts
const isFatalRestoreOmission = (item: string) => /^(workspace:.*:missing object|artifact:.*:(missing object|no target session)|cas:.*:unavailable|version:.*:unavailable|…)/.test(item);
```

`cas:…:unavailable…` and `version:…:unavailable…` are therefore fatal **only if this import produced them itself**. The filter that consumes the predicate drops anything the package already declared:

```ts
// services/api/src/research-snapshots.ts:1448-1451
const restoreFailures = omissions.filter((item) => !imported.receipt.omissions.includes(item)
  && !item.startsWith("This package contains no scientific memory snapshot")
  && isFatalRestoreOmission(item));
if (options.sourceSessionId && restoreFailures.length) throw new Error(`…`);
```

`imported.receipt.omissions` is the package's own `manifest.omissions` (`packages/research-package/src/index.ts:567` and `:808`, copied into `omissions` at `services/api/src/research-snapshots.ts:1109`). A package that honestly declares a lost payload — which is exactly what the exporter writes at `research-snapshots.ts:908` (`version:${key}:unavailable source object`) and `:468`/`:874` (`cas:${hash}:unavailable source object`) — has those strings in the receipt, so they are filtered out and never reach `restoreFailures`.

The same line then decides whether the copy may be continued:

```ts
// services/api/src/research-snapshots.ts:1475
const continuationAvailable = restoreFailures.length === 0;
```

## What is expected

Two acceptable behaviours, both of which the current code silently skips:

- **refuse the continuation** — a copy that is missing immutable evidence (a version object, a CAS object) is not a base for further research, so `continuationAvailable` should be `false` and starting a continuation should be refused with the omissions named; or
- **downgrade explicitly** — allow it, but say in the receipt and in the UI that the copy is incomplete and what is missing, instead of reporting a clean, continuable import.

What must not happen is what happens now: the package declares the loss, the receipt repeats it, and the copy is still offered as a complete base for 继续研究.

## How to reach it

Any package whose `manifest.omissions` carries `cas:…:unavailable source object` or `version:…:unavailable source object`, imported into a new session (the 继续研究 entry point passes `options.sourceSessionId`, which is the branch that throws on `restoreFailures`).

That is the ordinary shape of a package exported after its payload disappeared: `services/api/src/research-package-http.test.ts:132-177` builds exactly such a package (blob removed at `:166`, omission asserted at `:167-169`) — only it never imports it, so this path has no test.

The package in #1520 is the same shape at scale: 271 `versionObjects` references, none of their objects in the archive, all 271 named in `manifest.omissions`.

## Why this is not #1520

#1520 and #1521 are about the missing object becoming a `404 File not found` or a raw `TypeError`. With the `get` fix, the missing version object is reported as `version:<pool>:<digest>:missing object` (or already declared) instead of throwing. This report is about the **decision made after** that: the omission is now correctly known, and it is still not allowed to count as fatal. The two can land independently.

## Impact

- A research copy that silently lacks immutable evidence is presented as complete and continuable; the user carries research forward on a base whose versions cannot be restored.
- The receipt already names the omissions, so the information exists and is contradicted two lines later by `continuationAvailable: true`.
- The fatal-omission rule (`:1003`) is effectively dead for the only class of accidental loss the exporter can report — it can never fire, because the exporter always declares what it dropped.

## Environment

- `main` `e89ba7bb3a5555a945b6edb704c7c1e6f2397932`; repository lines above are that commit's.
- Found while auditing the import path for #1520; no runtime reproduction was run (the analysis tree has no installed dependencies), the chain is read from the source above.
recent.title: [Bug]: A copy missing immutable evidence still offers 继续研究, because an omission the package declared can never be fatal

recent.author: yuanzhou75
recent.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version (checked on `main` = `4f3d75ed7ccb8d7bc3fb5b6792fac6b00bc5b9de`, 2026-11-28).
- [x] A reproduction, package sizes/checksums and the observed import state are below.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**What happens.** A Session that ran Idea Tree research is exported as **完整导出 (complete)** and imported into a clean project. Messages, workspace files, artifacts and run events come back, but the Idea Tree research — its tree nodes, candidates, assessments and scores — is gone: `/api/sessions/:id/idea-tree/research` returns `{"items":[]}` and `/api/sessions/:id/idea-tree/graph` returns `{"graph":null,...}` for the imported Session. The import also reports `201` and `manifest.omissions` contains **no line** saying the research was left behind.

The package has no section for it at all. `records.json` keys are exactly:

```text
exportLevel, exportProfile, project, sessions, artifacts, environmentRevisions, versionObjects
```

and `services/api/src/research-snapshots.ts` only declares one research-feature omission — for evolve runs (`:1119`, “This package does not carry evolution (evolve) search runs…”). Idea Tree research is neither carried nor declared.

**Reproduced twice, with a completed and with a running research**

| source Session | research at export | package | inspect | import | research after import |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| direct `POST /idea-tree/research create`, template `scientific-hypothesis-general/v1` | `completed`, round 2, 11 nodes / 10 edges / 4 candidates | 2,155 B, sha256 `195e0b53847d9df3b8ff83b9802fe9bc2c512fecea47e2ddb37c9e01f4a4f021` | 200 | 201 | `[]`, graph `null` |
| agent-launched `/idea-tree …`, template `water-treatment-materials/v1` | `interrupted`, phase `propagate`, round 2, 14 nodes / 13 edges | 16,054,732 B, sha256 `edbfc09344770a83b71b9bb864b55b94dd658fc9dcc988b9747b1adcccd9d225` | 200 | 201 | `[]`, graph `null` |

For the first package, `manifest.omissions` is only:

```json
[
  "Scientific memory could not be exported because the memory graph service is unavailable.",
  "Workspace file revision payloads are not retained separately; revision metadata and the current file payload are included.",
  "Notebook execution history is not separately persisted by this ScienceDiscovery version; available .ipynb files are included as workspace objects."
]
```

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Local source stack from `4f3d75ed` (`./scripts/start-stack.sh --mode local --no-node-build --no-jiuwenswarm`).
2. Create a Project/Session with a model, then start research: either send `/idea-tree <task>` in the composer (the agent prepares and launches it), or call `POST /api/sessions/<sid>/idea-tree/research` with `{"operation":"create","content":"…"}`. Optionally set `ideaTreeOverride` on the Session first.
3. Wait until the research has nodes (`GET /api/sessions/<sid>/idea-tree/research` shows `nodes`/`edges`), then export:
   `GET /api/projects/<pid>/research-package?sessionId=<sid>&level=complete&includeFullTrajectory=0&includeFullMemoryGraph=0` → `200`.
4. Create a new Project and import the package: `POST /api/projects/<newPid>/research-package/import?sessionId=<newFirstSession>` → `201`.
5. Read the imported Session's research: `GET /api/sessions/<newSid>/idea-tree/research` → `{"items":[]}`; `GET /api/sessions/<newSid>/idea-tree/graph` → `{"graph":null,"hasIdeaTreeRun":false,"treeIds":[]}`. The corresponding source Session still shows the full tree.

**Why this needs a decision (complex, not a one-line fix)**

Two outcomes would both be defensible, and they are not equivalent:

1. **Carry the research:** export the Session's `idea-research` records (tree, nodes, edges, assessments, budgets, template, timestamps) and restore them on import under remapped ids, so the imported snapshot shows the same read-only research card. This touches the package format/records, `research-snapshots.ts`, the Idea Tree repository on restore, and the read-only snapshot rules — a feature-sized change with format-compatibility questions for already-exported packages.
2. **Declare the omission:** keep the current scope and add an explicit `manifest.omissions` line (alongside the existing evolve-run line), so the dialog tells the user the Idea Tree research is not in the package. This is small, but it changes what “完整导出” promises to the user.

Which one is right is a product decision about the complete profile, so this issue is left unassigned for the repository automation instead of being claimed as a simple fix.

**Expected vs actual**

* Expected: either the complete package restores the research tree, or the package says it does not carry it — the user must not be told “完整导出” and then find a Session whose research card silently vanished.
* Actual: export `200`, import `201`, no omission line, and the research content is silently absent.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Repository `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, `main` at `4f3d75ed7ccb8d7bc3fb5b6792fac6b00bc5b9de` (2026-11-28T06:34:26Z), clean worktree built from that commit.
- Windows 11 host + WSL2 Ubuntu, Node v22.23.4, pnpm 11.1.2.
- Local source stack: `scripts/start-stack.sh --mode local --no-node-build --no-jiuwenswarm`, isolated data directory, API `127.0.0.1:4330`, Runner `127.0.0.1:4331`; memory graph degraded (it is only relevant to the memory omission line).
- Model: a real OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017`) was used only to produce the research; export/import are model-free.
- Both packages are exports of my own Sessions from that stack; nothing was hand-edited.

### Additional Information

- Related: #803 (the export/import feature), #1368 (evolve runs are restored as duplicate runs on import — the opposite failure mode for the sibling feature), #1520 (import restores but fails on record shapes).
- No repository code was modified for this report.

### Version Information

- `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` @ `4f3d75ed7ccb8d7bc3fb5b6792fac6b00bc5b9de` (`main`, 2026-11-28).
- Runner reported version: `4f3d75ed`.

recent.author: HongyeZhou
recent.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] The description below includes environment information and a minimal reproduction, so the issue can be reproduced without further questions.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary**

When a model connectivity test fails, the desktop client shows the API's English sentence verbatim — in a Chinese UI, with no status marker and no hint about what to fix. The localized explanations for exactly these failures already exist in `text/zh.ts`, but they are unreachable: the API always fills `message`, and the client prefers `message` over `category`.

**Steps to reproduce** (1500x950 viewport, `zh-CN`)

1. Open 设置 › 模型 and click 添加模型.
2. Keep 服务商类型 `DeepSeek`, and fill: 基础URL `http://127.0.0.1:9/v1`, API key `sk-anything`, 模型名称 `probe-model`.
3. Click 测试连接.
   - Expected: a Chinese sentence such as 「连不上这个地址，请检查网络或自定义地址是否可达。」
   - Observed: `Could not connect to model provider; support is unknown` — English, no `✕` prefix, and nothing says the base URL is the likely culprit.

The same shape appears for the other failure categories (`Compatibility check timed out; support is unknown`, `Base URL or model ID was not found`, …): every one of them is an English sentence rendered as-is.

**Why this matters**

This is the one screen where the user is expected to *fix* the problem — the address they typed. The English sentence names neither the field nor an action, and reads like an internal diagnostic, so the user is left to guess. The success path is equally unhelpful in the other direction: it renders a full technical paragraph (`✓ 基础检查通过（1132 ms） · 仅基础检查：不验证完整会话执行路径、思考或工具调用。`) inside a one-line verdict.

**Root cause pointer**

- The API builds the sentence: `services/api/src/model-connectivity.ts:58` — `message: "Could not connect to model provider; support is unknown"`; same at line 55 (`timeout`), line 61 (`invalid_response`), and in `providerFailure()` at lines 46-52 (`API key is invalid or is not authorized`, `Base URL or model ID was not found`, …).
- The client prefers that sentence over the category it already has: `apps/desktop/src/views/ModelForm.tsx:473-476`
  ```ts
  function failureMessage(test: ModelConnectivityTestResult): string {
    if (test.message.trim() !== "") return test.message;
    return TEXT.wizard.testCategories[test.category] ?? TEXT.errors.generic;
  }
  ```
- The localized text for every category is already written and translated: `text/zh.ts:746-756` and `text/en.ts:721-733` (`network` → 「连不上这个地址，请检查网络或自定义地址是否可达。」). Because the API always sends a non-empty `message`, `TEXT.wizard.testCategories` is dead code in practice.
- The verdict itself has no marker: `ModelForm.tsx:889` renders `{verdict.message}` after a bare `kind === "fail"` style, so no `✕` ever appears.

**Suggested fix**

Let the category decide the sentence, and keep the English text as the detail a developer can still reach:

```ts
function failureMessage(test: ModelConnectivityTestResult): string {
  const localized = TEXT.wizard.testCategories[test.category];
  return localized ?? (test.message.trim() !== "" ? test.message : TEXT.errors.generic);
}
```

and put `test.message` in the verdict's `title` (tooltip) — the raw sentence stays available for diagnosis without becoming the interface. Optionally add the `✕` marker so success and failure differ at a glance.

The alternative — stop sending display text from the API — was rejected: `message` is part of `ModelConnectivityTestResult` in `packages/schema`, and other consumers (the first-run wizard, review tooling) read it for logs.

If a category is genuinely new and untranslated, the fallback path keeps today's behaviour, so no failure becomes less informative than it is now.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Product: ScienceDiscovery desktop client (`apps/desktop`), run as the web dev surface: front end `http://127.0.0.1:5174`, API on `127.0.0.1:4410`, runner on `127.0.0.1:4411`.
- Host: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS, Node.js 22.23.2, pnpm 11.1.2.
- Browser: Playwright's Chromium build 1228 (headless), viewport 1500x950, locale `zh-CN`.
- Reproduced 2 times in the same build (probe run + manual check in the same dialog).

### Additional Information

- Screenshot attached: 添加模型 dialog after a failed 测试连接, with the English sentence under the model-name field.
- Found while walking the 设置 feature area (D8-04 测试模型连接); the map expected `✓ 可用（N ms）` / `✕ <reason>`, neither of which exists.
- Related but separate: #1292 covers run-time failures (`semantic-error` fallback). This one is the *configuration-time* path, with its own category enum, so it can be localized without touching run classification.

### Version Information

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, branch `main`
- Commit: `bbdbdd5c9e7d04de3ff1d33da52eb41b87d60c9a` (2026-11-21)
- Desktop app package version: `0.0.0` (private workspace package)

![d8-04-test-fail](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fb911b99-fd20-4519-80c0-60c74f61d80c)
recent.title: [Bug]: A failed model connectivity test shows the API's English sentence, with no status marker

recent.author: HongyeZhou
recent.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] The description below includes environment information and a minimal reproduction, so the report can be followed without further questions.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary**

A successful run ends with a "用时 N 秒" line. A run that fails while the model is still being reached ends with the failure card and nothing else — no duration at all. The run does know how long it took; the line just lives somewhere that never renders on this path.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Make the selected model unreachable (point its base URL at a dead port, or stop the model service) and send any message in a new session.
2. The run stops with `模型服务连接失败`, the explanation "无法连接模型服务，运行已停止。建议检查网络、代理设置及模型服务地址后重试。" and a folded "技术详情".
3. Nothing says how long the attempt took, although the same conversation's successful runs show `用时 N 秒` under the fold line.

![A failed run: title, explanation and technical details, but no elapsed time](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cd10a991-217f-4147-a660-a645f234bcb1)

**Root cause**

The duration is produced only by the fold line of a run, and the fold line only exists when the run has something to fold:

- `apps/desktop/src/views/AssistantTurn.tsx:605` — `const fold = live || hasMiddleContent(run, shown);`
- `hasMiddleContent` (`:452-465`) requires reasoning, subagents, tool calls, or prose beyond the shown answer. A run that fails before the model answers has none of them, so `fold` is `false` and the `<details>` block is skipped entirely.
- The elapsed label itself is built in `foldLabel` (`:469-482`) from `TEXT.conversation.elapsed(run.finishedAt - run.startedAt)` (`apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts:360`) and rendered only inside that `<summary>` (`:634-655`).
- The failure card is rendered separately (`:379`, `apps/desktop/src/views/RunFailureCard.tsx:31`) from `code`, `message` and `timeout` — no timing is passed to it.

So a failed run with no foldable content can never display a duration, even though `run.startedAt` and `run.finishedAt` are both known.

**Impact**

- A failure that took 4 minutes after retries looks exactly like one that failed instantly; the user cannot tell whether time was spent in the model gateway, in a retry loop, or nowhere.
- Anything that reads `用时` to recognise a finished run (a person skimming, or an automated check) sees no end marker on failed runs.
- The information is present in state, so this is a rendering gap rather than missing data.

**Suggested fix**

Render the duration for every terminal run that has both timestamps, independent of the fold:

- pass `startedAt`/`finishedAt` into `RunFailureCard` and add the same `TEXT.conversation.elapsed(...)` line there, or
- render a standalone `run-duration` line next to the failure card when `fold === false` and both timestamps exist.

A desktop unit test asserting that a terminal run with `startedAt`/`finishedAt` and no turns still shows the elapsed line would keep this from regressing.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Product: ScienceDiscovery `main` at `bbdbdd5c9e7d04de3ff1d33da52eb41b87d60c9a` (2026-11-21). API `127.0.0.1:4410`, Runner `127.0.0.1:4411`, desktop web surface `http://127.0.0.1:5174`.
- Host: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS, Node.js 22.23.2, pnpm 11.1.2.
- Client: Playwright Chromium build 1228, 1600x1000 viewport, locale `zh-CN`.
- The failing run: the selected model's base URL was unreachable, so the run stopped before producing any turn — which is exactly the case with nothing to fold.

### Additional Information

- Found while fault-injecting a broken model in scenario S-203 (fault recovery): the missing duration made it impossible to tell from the transcript whether the run had ended at all.
- Related but separate: #1292 (the failure code and detail text for this same card), #1299 (model connection test localization), #1300 (artifact version numbers).

### Version Information

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, branch `main`
- Commit: `bbdbdd5c9e7d04de3ff1d33da52eb41b87d60c9a` (2026-11-21)
- Desktop app package version: `0.0.0` (private workspace package)
