recent.author: yuanzhou75
recent.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version (checked on `main` = `4f3d75ed7ccb8d7bc3fb5b6792fac6b00bc5b9de`, 2026-11-28).
- [x] A reproduction, the payload sizes, the HTTP statuses and the environment are below.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**What happens.** Uploading a file that is not a valid `.sdresearch` archive — a corrupt download, a truncated copy, or simply the wrong file — to either package endpoint answers `500 {"error":"Internal server error"}`. The archive parser's own message (`incorrect header check`, `unexpected end of file`) never reaches the client or the dialog; the API log records it only as `unclassified_request_error`.

A bad package is the caller's input, not a server fault, so this should be a 4xx with a stable code and a message the import dialog can show (the dialog already renders `error` text from 4xx package refusals, e.g. `507` capacity refusals and the `409 SESSION_EVIDENCE_LOCKED` read-only refusal).

**Measured on the same build, one Session's valid package as the base (349,250 B):**

| payload | bytes | `POST .../research-package/inspect` | `POST .../research-package/import` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 64 KiB of random bytes | 65,536 | **500** `{"error":"Internal server error"}` | **500** `{"error":"Internal server error"}` |
| the valid package truncated to half | 174,625 | **500** | **500** |
| gzip header only (first 12 B) | 12 | **500** | **500** |
| a JSON body (`{"hello":"world"}`) | 17 | **500** | **500** |

Server log for the same requests:

```text
ERROR [api] event=unclassified_request_error errorMessage="incorrect header check"
  method=POST path=/api/projects/<projectId>/research-package/inspect status=500
ERROR [api] event=unclassified_request_error errorMessage="unexpected end of file"
  method=POST path=/api/projects/<projectId>/research-package/import status=500
```

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Local source stack from `4f3d75ed` (`./scripts/start-stack.sh --mode local --no-node-build --no-jiuwenswarm`).
2. `POST /api/projects`, then take any valid package exported by the same build (`GET /api/projects/<id>/research-package?sessionId=<sid>&level=complete`, `200`, 349,250 B here) and truncate it to half its bytes.
3. `POST /api/projects/<id>/research-package/inspect` with those bytes, `Authorization: Bearer <local token>` → `500 {"error":"Internal server error"}`.
4. `POST /api/projects/<id>/research-package/import?sessionId=<sid>` with a fresh project's session and the same bytes → the same `500`.
5. Repeat with 64 KiB of random bytes, a 12-byte prefix of the package, and a small JSON body: same result for both endpoints.

**Root cause (code on `4f3d75ed`)**

* zlib/tar failures are plain `Error`s thrown from `importResearchPackageStreamed` (`packages/research-package/src/index.ts`, e.g. `:768`, `:778`, `:783`, `:804`) — none carries an HTTP status or a stable code.
* `services/api/src/http/index.ts:1820-1831` (inspect) translates only `RESEARCH_PACKAGE_UNPACK_BUDGET_CODE` into a `507`; every other error is rethrown. The import branch below (`:1864`+) does the same.
* The generic handler logs `unclassified_request_error` and answers `500 Internal server error`, so the dialog shows an internal-error string for what is a validation failure.

**Expected vs actual**

* Expected: `400` (or `413` when a declared entry exceeds the metadata bound) with a stable code such as `RESEARCH_PACKAGE_INVALID` / `RESEARCH_PACKAGE_TRUNCATED` and a sentence naming the problem, e.g. “This file is not a valid research package (archive is truncated)”. The dialog then shows that sentence instead of an internal error.
* Actual: `500 Internal server error` for every malformed payload, indistinguishable from a server defect and without any hint that the file itself is broken.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Repository `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, `main` at `4f3d75ed7ccb8d7bc3fb5b6792fac6b00bc5b9de` (2026-11-28T06:34:26Z), clean worktree built from that commit.
- Windows 11 host + WSL2 Ubuntu, Node v22.23.4, pnpm 11.1.2.
- Local source stack: `scripts/start-stack.sh --mode local --no-node-build --no-jiuwenswarm`, isolated data directory, API `127.0.0.1:4330`, Runner `127.0.0.1:4331`.
- The base package is the build's own export of my own Session; the malformed payloads are that file truncated or replaced by random/JSON bytes.
- No model, memory graph or runner involvement: the requests fail while parsing the archive.

### Additional Information

- Related but distinct: #1520 (a package that parses but carries a missing object / a citation record) and #1211 (streaming bounds and write-error robustness). This report is only the response classification for malformed input.
- No repository code was modified for this report.

### Version Information

- `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` @ `4f3d75ed7ccb8d7bc3fb5b6792fac6b00bc5b9de` (`main`, 2026-11-28).
- Runner reported version: `4f3d75ed`.
recent.title: [Bug]: Inspecting or importing a corrupt or truncated .sdresearch answers 500 Internal server error instead of a 4xx

recent.author: yuanzhou75
recent.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version (checked on `main` = `4f3d75ed7ccb8d7bc3fb5b6792fac6b00bc5b9de`, 2026-11-28).
- [x] A reproduction, the package sizes/checksums, the HTTP statuses and the environment are below.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**What happens.** On `main`, exporting a Session as **完整导出 (complete) with 包含完整轨迹 (include full trajectory) ticked** can produce a package that the same build refuses to inspect and import. Both requests answer `500 {"error":"Internal server error"}` and the API log names the real reason: `Research package metadata entry is too large`.

The exporter and the importer disagree on how large `records.json` may be: the streamed importer caps it at 64 MiB (`MAX_METADATA_BYTES`), while the exporter writes it without any matching bound. Because the failure is a plain `Error` and not an API status error, it also reaches the user as a 500 rather than a readable refusal.

**Same Session, only the trajectory checkbox differs:**

| export | package size | `records.json` | inspect | import |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `level=complete&includeFullTrajectory=0` | 16,054,787 B (sha256 `43fbb40f59dc65841e187fe629ea666424ad040df6d444ceee6fb37c8d8a6137`) | 1,784,809 B | 200 | **201** |
| `level=complete&includeFullTrajectory=1` | 190,518,273 B (sha256 `0c0736eb4737fc161ba05284b4c83bd1139c936bcd16a293508ac2f63eabea46`) | **701,240,776 B** | **500** | **500** |

Raw responses for the second row (both endpoints, identical body):

```text
POST /api/projects/<projectId>/research-package/inspect
500 {"error":"Internal server error"}

POST /api/projects/<projectId>/research-package/import?sessionId=<sessionId>
500 {"error":"Internal server error"}
```

Server log at the same timestamps:

```text
ERROR [api] event=unclassified_request_error
  errorMessage="Research package metadata entry is too large"
  method=POST path=/api/projects/<projectId>/research-package/inspect status=500
ERROR [api] event=unclassified_request_error
  errorMessage="Research package metadata entry is too large"
  method=POST path=/api/projects/<projectId>/research-package/import status=500
```

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Start a local source stack from `4f3d75ed` (`./scripts/start-stack.sh --mode local --no-node-build --no-jiuwenswarm`, API on `127.0.0.1:4330`).
2. Register a real model and create a Project/Session; run one `/idea-tree` research so the Session accumulates a long run: this Session ended with 3 messages, 1,164 run events and 11 artifacts (the UIs's “更多会话操作 → 导出” export of the same Session is what produced the files above).
3. Export with the trajectory option on:
   `GET /api/projects/<projectId>/research-package?sessionId=<sessionId>&level=complete&includeFullTrajectory=1&includeFullMemoryGraph=0`
   → `200`, 190,518,273 bytes in 49.7 s, `records.json` = 701,240,776 bytes (669 MiB), `manifest.json` = 94,784 bytes, 479 entries.
4. Feed those exact bytes back to `POST .../research-package/inspect` and to `POST .../research-package/import?sessionId=...` → both `500`.
5. Control: step 3 with `includeFullTrajectory=0` → `200`, 16,054,787 bytes, `records.json` 1.8 MB; the same inspect/import then return `200`/`201`.

**Root cause (code on `4f3d75ed`)**

* `packages/research-package/src/index.ts:29` — `MAX_METADATA_BYTES = 64 * MIB`.
* `packages/research-package/src/index.ts:768` — the streamed parser reads `manifest.json`/`records.json`/`README.md` whole and throws `Error("Research package metadata entry is too large")` when one exceeds that bound.
* Export has no counterpart: `packages/research-package/src/index.ts:366` computes `recordsBytes = jsonByteLength(input.records) + additionalRecordBytes` and writes it straight into the archive; nothing compares it with `MAX_METADATA_BYTES`, so the trajectory-expanded `records.json` is exported happily.
* `services/api/src/http/index.ts:1820-1831` (inspect) and the import path below it only translate `RESEARCH_PACKAGE_UNPACK_BUDGET_CODE` to a 507; every other error is rethrown into the generic handler, which logs `unclassified_request_error` and answers `500`.

**Expected vs actual**

* Expected: a package the application lets the user export can be inspected and imported by the same build, or the export is refused up front with a readable message naming the bound the selection hit and a way to stay under it (shorter trajectory, necessary export, smaller scope). An oversized or malformed package should be a 4xx with a stable code/message, not `500 Internal server error`.
* Actual: the export succeeds and produces an unimportable 190 MB file; both `inspect` and `import` answer `500`, so the dialog cannot even show the package's contents or explain why it cannot be restored.

**Not the same as #1520.** #1520 describes a missing `versionObjects` object (ENOENT → 404) and a `structuredData.references` record (raw JS `400`). This report fails earlier, inside archive parsing, on `records.json` size alone, and reproduces from a package with no missing objects and no citation records.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Repository `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, `main` at `4f3d75ed7ccb8d7bc3fb5b6792fac6b00bc5b9de` (2026-11-28T06:34:26Z), clean worktree built from that commit.
- Windows 11 host + WSL2 Ubuntu (kernel from WSL2), Node v22.23.4, pnpm 11.1.2, uv-managed Python envs reused from the same machine.
- Local source stack: `scripts/start-stack.sh --mode local --no-node-build --no-jiuwenswarm`, isolated data directory, API `127.0.0.1:4330`, Runner `127.0.0.1:4331`, memory graph degraded (not used by this report).
- Model: a real OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017`) used only to produce the Session's history; no model is part of the export/import repro.
- The three packages cited are exports of my own Session from that stack; the bytes were not edited.

### Additional Information

- Related but distinct: #1520 (import record shapes), #1211 (streaming pipeline bounds), #1079 (the trajectory option in the client).
- No repository code was modified for this report; all numbers come from the running build's own export and import endpoints.

### Version Information

- `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` @ `4f3d75ed7ccb8d7bc3fb5b6792fac6b00bc5b9de` (`main`, 2026-11-28).
- Runner reported version: `4f3d75ed`.

recent.author: HongyeZhou
recent.body:
﻿### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] The description below includes environment information and a minimal reproduction, so the report can be followed without further questions.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary**

A product declared in a brand-new conversation can silently continue the version chain of an artifact created in an older conversation: the new session receives `version 4` of an artifact it never created, the older session's product is overwritten with the new content, and neither the user nor the model is told that this happened.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. In session A, ask the agent to write `report.md` in the workspace and declare it as an artifact. It becomes `v1`; publish two revisions so it reaches `v3`.
2. Start a new session B in the same project and ask the agent to write a different `report.md` (this is a separate piece of work — a run log, not a revision of A's report).
3. The agent calls `declare_artifact` with only `{"path": "report.md", ...}`.
4. B's answer says `Artifact 0635ff24…, version 4`, and B's artifact panel lists `report.md` at `v4`. Open session A: its `report.md` is now that same `v4`, carrying B's content.

**What the data shows** (`main` `bbdbdd5c`, `zh-CN`, desktop web surface)

Session B's `/api/sessions/<B>/artifact-outputs` returns exactly one entry:

```
artifact.id            0635ff24-0d7e-4eb2-a253-253d28f5e624
artifact.createdInSessionId     fca861a5-…   (session A)
artifact.createdInSessionTitle  用 Python 创建 report.md 文件
artifact.currentVersion 4
version.sessionId       e9afb9af-…   (session B)
version.version         4
version.turnId          set
```

Session A's `/api/sessions/<A>/artifacts` now reports the same artifact with `currentVersion: 4` and `updatedAt: 2026-11-22T06:41:49.242Z` — the moment session B published. So A's artifact row is visible, and its content has been replaced by another conversation's work.

**Why it happens**

- `services/api/src/store.ts:5752-5755` — when the caller does not pass an `artifactId`, the target artifact is resolved by `(projectId, name, research scope)`. A same-named artifact in the same project, created by *another session*, is a valid target.
- `services/api/src/store.ts:5797` — the new version takes `artifact.currentVersion + 1`, so the first product of a fresh conversation is `v4`.
- The publish result handed back to the model contains only `artifact_id`, `name`, `content`, `origin`, `version` and `version_id` — no `createdInSessionId`, no title, no previous version. The model therefore believes it declared a new artifact and reports "version 4" to the user without being able to explain `v1`–`v3`.
- `apps/desktop/src/views/WorkspacePanel.tsx:378-400` — the version menu labels entries `v{version}` only; there is no session or timestamp, and the picker is only rendered when a session produced more than one version (so in session B there is no picker at all, just `v4`).
- `services/api/src/store.ts:5728` already refuses cross-session rewrites with a 409 — `请在当前研究会话中创建独立产物，不能改写另一个研究副本` — but only when the owning session is a *research copy*. Two ordinary sessions of the same project are allowed to write over each other without any confirmation.
- When the caller passes no `baseVersionId`, the CAS check at `store.ts:5746` is skipped, so the write does not even need to have seen the version it overwrites.

**Impact**

- A fresh conversation's first deliverable starts at `v4`, relative to history the user cannot see in that conversation. Nothing in the panel says where `v1`–`v3` came from.
- The older conversation's product changes underneath it, silently. A user reopening it sees different content at a new version number with no record of which session wrote it.
- The model can "update" a product it has never read, and will describe a foreign version chain as its own work.
- Two sessions writing the same name interleave versions, and without `baseVersionId` the last write wins with no conflict raised. Version-number collisions are a separate defect (#1300, fixed by #1301); this one is about *which* chain a write lands in.
- Cleanup is asymmetric: `store.ts:5579` authorizes `deleteArtifact` against the *creating* session, so the session that can see and revise the artifact is not necessarily the one that may delete it.

**Suggested fix** (approved direction: make the continuation visible, and ask before the first cross-session write)

1. **Disclose the continuation.** Return the origin in the publish result, e.g. `continuedFrom: { sessionId, sessionTitle, version }` when the resolved artifact was created in another session, and let the model say so in its answer. In the panel, label the row with the creating session's title and put the per-version producer in the version menu (`v4 · 本会话 · 06:41`, `v3 · <session A> · 06:22`).
2. **Ask on the first cross-session write.** When the resolved artifact's `createdInSessionId` differs from the calling session, do not append silently: return a conflict that offers "continue this chain" (`baseVersionId` set, so CAS applies) or "publish as a new artifact" — the store already supports the latter as `forceNewArtifact` (`store.ts:5706`). The existing research-copy 409 gives the message shape to reuse.
3. Always require a base for a continuation, so a write that did not read the current version cannot overwrite it.

The project-level chain itself is intended (same path = same product inside one research scope) and should stay; what is missing is that the join is invisible and unavoidable.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Product: ScienceDiscovery `main` at `bbdbdd5c9e7d04de3ff1d33da52eb41b87d60c9a` (2026-11-21). API `127.0.0.1:4410`, Runner `127.0.0.1:4411`, desktop web surface `http://127.0.0.1:5174`.
- Host: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS, Node.js 22.23.2, pnpm 11.1.2.
- Client: Playwright Chromium build 1228, 1600x1000 viewport, locale `zh-CN`.
- Sessions: `fca861a5-…` (A, created `report.md` at 05:29), `e9afb9af-…` (B, published `v4` at 06:41). Container: `27cb6928-…`.

### Additional Information

- Found while exercising fault recovery (scenario S-203): the new session only wrote a run log named `report.md`, and was surprised by `version 4`.
- Related but separate: #1300 / #1301 (version numbers allocated without a uniqueness guard, and the stale-pointer allocation fix).
- The version picker itself (`v3`/`v2`/`v1` with no other identifier) was noted in #1300; this issue adds the missing provenance on top of it.

### Version Information

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, branch `main`
- Commit: `bbdbdd5c9e7d04de3ff1d33da52eb41b87d60c9a` (2026-11-21)
- Desktop app package version: `0.0.0` (private workspace package)
recent.title: [Bug]: A new session silently continues an existing artifact version chain

recent.author: HongyeZhou
recent.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**What happens.** A running Idea Tree research shows its phase as the raw English word `ideate` in an otherwise Chinese interface, next to the Chinese status (「正在暂停」) and the Chinese round/batch line (「第 0 轮」「本轮 0/1」). The engine emits `ideate`; neither client's phase map has a key for it, so the lookup falls through to the raw value.

**Minimal reproduction.**

1. Send `/idea-tree <a purely mechanistic question>` (no web fetching needed), confirm the parameter card, send the command.
2. Wait until `create_idea_research` returns and open the research card (`button.idea-run-card`).
3. Read the progress line: `正在暂停 ideate 第 0 轮 0 tokens`.

**Expected.** The phase is rendered in the UI language — e.g. 「构思」 for `ideate` — like the five phases that do have labels.

**Actual.**

- The progress line prints `ideate`.
- `GET /api/sessions/<id>/idea-tree/research` reports `"phase": "ideate"`, `"status": "running"` (and the engine also persists `phase='ideate'` for a freshly created, paused research).
- `apps/desktop/src/views/idea/IdeaResearchPanel.tsx:212` renders `(t.phase as Record<string, string | undefined>)[research.phase] ?? research.phase`, so an unmapped value passes through untranslated.
- `apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts:2625-2631` and `apps/desktop/src/text/en.ts:2574-2579` map only `preflight_research`, `building_tree`, `executing_leaf`, `aggregating_score`, `propagating_insight`. `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts` has the same five.
- The engine really emits it: `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/vendor/idea_tree/research.py:694` (`s['phase'] = 'ideate'`) and `research_service.py:226` (`phase='ideate'`).

**Why it matters.** Besides the visible English word, `phase` is typed as an open `string` in the shared schema (`packages/schema/src/idea-tree.ts:312`), so the compiler cannot catch a phase the text maps do not know: every new engine phase silently degrades to English in both clients. The five labels were written against an assumption about the engine's vocabulary that the engine does not share.

**Suggested fix.** Add `ideate` to the three text maps (one line each, `构思` / `Ideate`), and decide whether the schema should narrow `phase` back to a union of the engine's values so the next addition is a type error instead of an English word on screen.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Product: source checkout of `main` at `e374837d37a8a536483a9ef8b5d2a98bd23a5aee` (2026-11-28T01:17:17Z): API on `127.0.0.1:4410`, evolve sidecar on `17676` (healthy, bwrap), desktop web surface on `http://127.0.0.1:5174`.
- Host: Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, x86_64, Node.js v22.23.5.
- Client: Playwright Chromium, 1600x1000 viewport, locale `zh-CN`; model Ark `deepseek-v4.1-flash`; permission mode 完全访问.
- Session `b681e51a-8ca2-456c-9df4-02162ac5444e`, research `research-98625896-9d96-4fd2-9c0a-6c1e60bc2ff8`.

### Additional Information

- No screenshot: the research used for this report was later ended, so the line is no longer on screen. The payload quoted above (`"phase": "ideate"` from the live research) is the evidence, and the same word is what the progress line prints.
- This is a text-map gap, not a translation-service gap: `ideate` never had a key, and the same word is missing from the English map too (English falls back to itself, so the bug is only visible in Chinese).

### Version Information

- Repository `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, branch `main`, commit `e374837d37a8a536483a9ef8b5d2a98bd23a5aee` (2026-11-28).
- Files inspected: `apps/desktop/src/views/idea/IdeaResearchPanel.tsx`, `apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/text/en.ts`, `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts`, `packages/schema/src/idea-tree.ts`, `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/vendor/idea_tree/research.py`, `research_service.py`.

stale.author: HugoXK
stale.body:
### 🚀 Background Description


`/evolve-design` is the only entry point for program evolution today, but it is a **hidden slash command** — a user must already know to type the `/evolve-design` prefix. The only visible entry is a button inside the artifact detail modal (it fills the composer with `/evolve-design make the artifact X better: ` and still requires the user to complete and send the sentence manually).

Two problems follow:

1. **We assume the user knows the command.** The UI never guides anyone toward `/evolve-design`; ordinary researchers will not type a slash command they have never seen.
2. **The interaction is command-shaped.** The user must learn command syntax (`--algorithm puct/openevolve`) instead of speaking naturally.

Goal: a user expresses improvement intent in **natural language** (e.g. "make this result better", "帮我优化这个程序"), the **framework actively recommends a tree-search evolution**, and the interaction stays natural-language end to end — no slash-command literacy required.



### Design Ideas

Land in three layers, reusing the existing `/evolve-design` chain (`EvolveAlgorithmPicker`, `EvolveToolRuntime`, `/api/evolve/runs`, the native-agent turn). No new capability surface.

#### Layer 1: Composer intent recognition (frontend, minimal)

Lightweight, testable, pure-function intent detection in the composer (no LLM round-trip):

- Match program-evolution intent:
  - the `/evolve-design` slash prefix (existing behavior, kept), **or**
  - a sentence pairing an **improvement verb** with an **evolvable target** (program / code / algorithm / function / model / script / …), in Chinese or English.
- When matched, offer a **low-intrusion suggestion bar** ("It looks like you want to improve a result or program. Run an automated search that keeps the best-scoring variant?") — the user must explicitly accept before anything is started.
- On accept, show the existing `EvolveAlgorithmPicker`; on select, fill `/evolve-design --algorithm X <natural language>` and send.

**Why confirmation before the picker?** Starting a search spends real budget (mutations + sandboxed evaluations). Detection is a guess, so it must only *offer*; the user's explicit accept is the gate. This also protects against misreads — a user saying "优化一下" while discussing formatting is never sent down an expensive search.

#### Layer 2: Agent-driven recommendation (backend, core value)

In the native-agent turn loop, recognise improvement intent in messages that do *not* carry the `/evolve-design` prefix:

- When the user asks to improve a program/result, the Agent **recommends** a tree-search evolution in its reply and offers to start it, reusing `EvolveToolRuntime`'s `create_evolve_run`.
- The interaction stays natural-language: the user replies "yes, go ahead", and the Agent starts the run.

#### Layer 3: Visible entry point (frontend, complete experience)

- A "program evolution" entry in the composer opens a **natural-language prompt** ("Which artifact? What does 'better' mean here?") instead of filling a slash command.
- The artifact-detail modal button opens the same prompt instead of generating `/evolve-design ...` text.

### Intent recognition rules

`detectEvolveIntent(message)` returns true only when **both** an improvement verb and an evolvable target are present, and no non-evolvable target is named:

| Example | Result | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `improve the program` / `优化一下这个程序` | true | verb + program target |
| `make this better` / `把这个做得更好` | false | no explicit evolvable target |
| `optimize the interface layout` / `优化一下界面布局` | false | layout is not evolvable |
| `improve the workflow steps` | false | steps are not evolvable |
| `this result is better than the last one` / `这个更好` | false | no verb+target pair |
| `improve the description` / `改一下格式` | false | formatting/explanation excluded |

`isEvolveDesignCommand(message)` distinguishes the explicit command (goes straight to the picker) from natural language (goes through the suggestion bar).

### API surface

- No new public API; reuse `/api/evolve/runs` and `/api/evolve/runs/:id/events`.
- Layer 2 reuses `EvolveToolRuntime`'s existing tools; no new registration.
- Intent detection is a pure frontend function, unit-testable.

### Affected modules

- `apps/web/src/App.tsx`: composer intent detection; `showEvolveAlgorithmPicker` trigger extension (currently matches only the `/evolve-design` prefix); suggestion-bar state.
- `apps/web/src/evolve/EvolveSuggestionBar.tsx` (new): confirmation bar.
- `apps/web/src/evolve/intent.ts` (new): `detectEvolveIntent` / `isEvolveDesignCommand`.
- `apps/web/src/evolve/EvolveAlgorithmPicker.tsx`: reused unchanged.
- `apps/web/src/api/evolve.ts`: reused.
- `services/api/src/native-agent/index.ts`: turn-loop intent recognition and recommendation (Layer 2).
- `packages/evolve`: `EvolveToolRuntime` reused.
- i18n: suggestion-bar copy, composer entry copy (en + zh).

### Involved Public APIs

_No response_

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

_No response_

### Test Design and Test Plan

**Functional**

- [ ] Unit tests for `detectEvolveIntent`: Chinese/English verb+target, no-target messages, non-evolvable targets, negation phrases.
- [ ] Unit tests for `isEvolveDesignCommand`: command vs natural-language separation.
- [ ] Composer + natural-language improvement intent + artifact reference → suggestion bar appears.
- [ ] Accepting the suggestion → algorithm picker appears.
- [ ] Selecting an algorithm → `/evolve-design` evolution run starts.
- [ ] Ordinary messages (no intent) → nothing appears, normal conversation.
- [ ] Artifact modal button → opens natural-language prompt, not a filled command.

**Regression**

- [ ] Existing `/evolve-design` command path unchanged; explicit `--algorithm` no longer re-opens the picker.
- [ ] Existing evolve E2E / unit tests pass.

**User-perspective E2E**

- User expresses improvement intent naturally → framework recommends → natural-language confirm → evolution run starts.
- A message without improvement intent never triggers the evolution recommendation.

### Notes

- Follows the product direction: "the framework recommends tree search, but the interaction stays natural language."
- Layer 1 (frontend intent recognition + confirmation bar) can land as an independent MR first; Layer 2 (Agent-driven recommendation) depends on the turn-loop change and can follow.


### Additional Information

_No response_
stale.title: [Feature] Natural-language program evolution: turn /evolve-design from a hidden slash command into a framework-recommended, natural-language interaction

stale.body:
## 背景

Codex/Claude Specialist（Phase2/3）体验中，配置与运维仍偏「懂进程 env + 懂 API」：

- 设置页**没有** runtime/SDK 选择器；UI 保存不发 `runtime`（只能 API 带 `runtime` 创建）。
- `SCIENCE_AGENT_CODEX_BASE_URL` **只能**写进 API 进程环境，改完需重启；主 Agent 工具 `configure_specialist_runtime` 只能改已有外部 runtime 的非密钥项，**不能**设 base URL、代填 key、引导 device-code，也不能把 native 改成 codex/cc。
- 有任务内配密卡（`CodexConfigCard` / `runtime-config`），但**没有**右侧 Specialist CLI 卡片，也**没有**「重启 specialist runtime」。

产品口径（维护者确认）：配置页保持简；复杂鉴权进主对话；保底是用户可直连 specialist，且可重启。

## 目标（三块合一，完整产品面）

### A. 配置页：选 runtime + 拉 SDK

- 配置页增加 **runtime 选择**（至少 `codex` / `claude-code` 等已支持 kind）。
- 选定后，系统下载/安装对应 SDK（失败有明确提示与可重试）。
- 表单保持简：**runtime + Skills + 描述**（名称可保留）；旁侧短文案提示：鉴权 / base URL / device-code 等在主对话由主 Agent 完成。
- 保存时 UI **必须**把所选 `runtime` 写入 create/update API（与现有 schema 对齐）。

### B. 主对话代配：加密输入 + device-code 引导

放开当前限制，主 Agent 在对话中可协助完成：

- **base URL / API key**：向用户发出**加密输入框**；用户把 key 填进输入框，**key 不进入对话正文**。
- **device-code**：主 Agent 把 code 交给用户，并说明如何在外部完成配置。
- 完成后写入平台侧安全存储 / `runtime-config` 路径，供后续委派使用（具体存储形态实现自定，验收看行为）。

### C. 右侧 Specialist 卡片 + CLI + 重启

- 会话右侧增加 **Specialist 卡片**。
- 点击后打开 **CLI 页**：展示主 Agent ↔ 该 specialist 的对话记录；用户也可在此页直接与 specialist 交互。
- 该页左侧提供 **「重启 specialist runtime」**（换 endpoint/凭证或进程异常后可重新拉起，无需整站重启 API）。

## 验收标准

- [ ] **A**：设置页可选 runtime；选定后触发 SDK 拉取；保存后 GET specialist 可见对应 `runtime.kind`；有「剩余配置在主对话完成」提示。
- [ ] **B**：主对话可走加密输入完成 base URL 与 key（正文日志/历史中不可见明文 key）；device-code 流程有用户可见引导；无需手改进程 env 即可完成常见第三方 endpoint 配置（至少覆盖当前 Codex→DeepSeek Responses 类场景的一条端到端路径）。
- [ ] **C**：右侧卡片可打开 CLI 页；可见主 Agent–specialist 记录且用户可交互；「重启 specialist runtime」可用，重启后可再次委派/交互。
- [ ] 不降低现有安全底线：Always Allow 不得代填密钥；密钥不进 specialist 元数据白名单。
- [ ] 有对应自动化或可重复手工验收步骤（可与 `test(specialist): HTTP runtime 契约` 姊妹 issue 互补，不重复）。

## 非目标

- 不在本 issue 只补 HTTP 静默丢 `runtime` 的测试（另开测试 issue）。
- 不要求设置页做成「覆盖所有鉴权形态的巨型表单」。
- 不要求提供完全脱离平台的独立 Codex CLI 产品面；本 issue 的「CLI 页」是平台内嵌的 specialist 交互面。

## 现状锚点（便于实现对照）

- UI 表单：`apps/web/src/Orchestration.tsx`（无 runtime 选择器）
- 主 Agent 工具：`configure_specialist_runtime`（`main-config.ts`）
- 配密卡：`CodexConfigCard` / `POST .../subagents/:id/runtime-config`
- Base URL：`SCIENCE_AGENT_CODEX_BASE_URL` 进程 env
stale.title: [Feature] specialist: 配置选 runtime+拉SDK、主对话加密代配、右侧CLI与重启

stale.author: HongyeZhou
stale.body:
> Converted from bug → feature per HongyeZhou (2026-10-27): this is a product/UX presentation improvement, not a hard defect.

## Feature request
When tool calls fail then recover mid-run, the default timeline narrative shows raw **failed** tool cards before a later success. #335 expected a clearer “retrying with fixed args” (or equivalent) presentation for the same logical operation. PRs #345 / #551 addressed missing required `prompt` on `task` before a deep createSubagent throw; they did **not** deliver the general failure→retry UI narrative (S6).

## Expected
When there is clear association evidence that a later call is a bounded correction of the same logical tool operation, the UI updates in place (or equivalent merged presentation): default view is a concise result; attempt count / errors / recovery detail are available on demand. Unrecoverable failures keep a clear reason. Real execution history and audit evidence are not rewritten as pure success. Do not blindly replay side-effecting operations to reduce cards.

## Verification cases

1. **In-place recovery presentation**
   - **Preconditions:** A recoverable invalid-argument or soft-fail path that retries within one logical operation (browser or hermetic UI fixture).
   - **Steps:**
     1. Trigger a tool call that fails then succeeds on a bounded correction.
     2. Inspect the timeline/card for that operation.
   - **Expected result / pass criteria:** Default view is not a stack of contradictory failed+success cards for the same operation; recovery state/result is shown in place; history of attempts remains inspectable; independent operations are not wrongly merged.

2. **Side-effect boundary**
   - **Preconditions:** A tool invocation that may have already executed with side effects before observation failed.
   - **Steps:**
     1. Observe recovery/UI merge behavior.
   - **Expected result / pass criteria:** No blind resubmit of committed side-effecting work solely to tidy the timeline; audit/failure records stay consistent.

## Context
- Env: _not provided_ for a fresh UI journey this filing; scope from #335 expected narrative and product phase-3 note on that Issue.
- Refs: Parent #335; PRs #345 / #551 (merged) for prompt-path only.
- Notes: Related UX umbrella #330 is adjacent (timeline hierarchy) but not a substitute for this recovery-presentation bug.
stale.title: [Feature] clearer fail-then-retry timeline narrative for tool recovery (from #335 S6)

stale.author: HongyeZhou
stale.body:
## Problem

PR #552 delivers standalone (inbox / 最近会话) chats and project folds, but membership is fixed at create time. Users still cannot move an existing recent conversation into a new or existing project without losing history or artifacts. That remaining acceptance item from #305 is out of scope for #552.

## Expected

A reader can move a standalone (recent / inbox) conversation into a new or existing project, and optionally move between projects or back to Recent, without losing messages, artifacts, or workspace accounting. Navigation and session lists stay consistent (no duplicate rows).

## Verification cases

1. **Move into existing project**
   - **Preconditions:** One Recent/inbox session with messages and at least one artifact; project P already exists.
   - **Steps:** From that session, choose move into project P (or equivalent UI).
   - **Expected / pass:** Session appears under P; history and artifacts intact; no longer listed under 最近会话; session bar / active project shows P.

2. **Move into newly created project**
   - **Preconditions:** One standalone session with history.
   - **Steps:** Move → create project with name only → confirm.
   - **Expected / pass:** Project created; session inside it; history/artifacts intact; gone from Recent.

3. **Move between projects / back to Recent**
   - **Preconditions:** Session already under a project.
   - **Steps:** Move to another project, then back to Recent (if supported).
   - **Expected / pass:** Membership updates; no duplicate rows in sidebar; workspace path and accounting remain consistent.

4. **E2E first-run remainder of #305**
   - **Preconditions:** Fresh user with no projects.
   - **Steps:** Start chat without a project → later move that chat into a project.
   - **Expected / pass:** Covers the #305 E2E acceptance remainder that #552 intentionally deferred.

## Context

- Refs #305 (remaining AC: organize / move conversations into projects later).
- Follow-up from review of https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/552 (`bde9143`); not blocking that PR.
stale.title: [Feature] Move a standalone (recent) conversation into a project

stale.author: HongyeZhou
stale.body:
## Motivation

Long-running offline computations and Agent conversations have different lifecycles. An Agent turn can finish while a training, simulation, or batch-processing task continues running. After evaluation, this is a feature-design topic about coordination between offline tasks and Agents, rather than a defect in turn completion.

This issue replaces #434 and preserves its motivating scenario.

## Motivating scenario

In the NatureBench reproduction session `93f897ca-cefe-4e7b-932d-8339cbef1459`, run `84d71b8a-77dd-42a7-bc81-15e326b14cb1` completed while a background `python run.py --instances mop_sc` computation continued. The final computation took approximately 1,587.7 seconds and produced `predictions.npy` with shape `(5693,)`.

The user had to inspect host processes and wait for the output manually. Starting another Agent run could also launch duplicate work. An Agent promising to return after a wall-clock delay is not a reliable scheduling mechanism.

## Feature scope

Design how long-running offline tasks collaborate with Agents across turns:

- Give supported offline tasks a queryable identity and lifecycle, with ownership linked to the originating session/run.
- Make ongoing computation visible even after the initiating Agent turn finishes.
- Let a later turn inspect, await, or resume coordination with the same task without starting duplicate computation.
- Define how task completion, failure, cancellation, and results become available to the user and Agent.
- Define the default turn-completion policy when a task is still running, including whether explicit detachment is required.
- Document lifecycle limits, including runtime/service restarts and the treatment of processes launched outside the supported task mechanism.

## Design decisions before implementation

- Turn completion: wait for the task, require explicit detach, or register it in the background and notify.
- Ownership and persistence: session-level versus run-level handles, and restart behavior.
- Minimum user interface: how users discover active tasks, inspect progress, and retrieve results.
- Agent continuation: explicit user-driven await/resume versus automatic completion notification or continuation.
- Delivery decomposition: build on existing execution/query/wait capabilities and split implementation into reviewable changes.

These are open design questions; this issue does not select a policy.

## Acceptance criteria

- A user starts a representative long-running computation and can distinguish Agent-turn completion from task completion.
- The same supported task remains discoverable and queryable across turns according to the documented lifecycle.
- The Agent can inspect or await that task and retrieve its final result without launching a duplicate.
- Completion, failure, and cancellation have defined, verifiable user-visible outcomes.
- The chosen turn-completion and restart policies are documented and covered by matching end-to-end scenarios.

## Related work

- #434: original report and evidence; superseded by this feature proposal.
- #439: redirected output buffering. Log buffering is a separate concern; coordinate where progress reporting intersects.
stale.title: [Feature] Coordinate long-running offline tasks with Agents across turns

stale.author: zy95-12

## 背景 / 输入

NatureBench 论文复现任务包（设计上）**不含**论文 PDF/MD（reproduce vs discovery 防火墙）。ScienceDiscovery 会话里仅有：

- `NATUREBENCH_TASK_BRIEF.md` / `data_description.md` / `metadata.json`
- DOI：`10.1038/s43588-024-00689-2`
- 作者代码：`github.com/pachterlab/CGP_2023`

外部获取：Nature 付费墙；bioRxiv 遇 Cloudflare；PMC 预印本偶发可得。

## 问题是什么

「忠实复现论文方法」需要方法细节，但工作区默认**没有**可读全文。Agent 只能靠 brief + GitHub notebook/Monod API 拼方法，复现保真度与可审计性下降；与产品「读论文 → 做事」叙事有缝。

（上传 PDF 解析另见 #333。）

## 我们怎么规避的

- 写入 `REPRODUCE_INSTRUCTIONS.md`：DOI、bioRxiv、作者仓库、Monod `mminference`。
- 浅克隆 `CGP_2023` 进 workspace 作方法参考；用作者实现而非另起无关聚类。

## 期望应该是什么样

1. 复现类会话：支持一键「附着论文」（DOI → OA PDF / 用户上传），并进入 Paper reader 可检索上下文。
2. 若上游 benchmark 故意不带 PDF：产品应引导用户补论文，并在报告里强制记录「方法来源（PDF 页码 / 仓库 commit）」。
3. 对 paywall / bot 墙：明确失败态与人工粘贴摘要的入口，而不是静默只用 brief。

## 相关

- #333 [Bug]: PDF uploaded via Drop files is not parsed by Paper reader
- #98 artifact / provenance / CAS（含 papers）方向

### Background

Follow-up to #96, under the backend migration tracked in #84. This issue carries forward the unfinished scope of #96 for release 0.4.0. Closing #96 is an administrative handover, not a claim that its original acceptance criteria have all passed.

Code review baseline: main at `5a86d0593a887e825d3a3da136f760b62807f797` (2026-10-28). This assessment is based on static inspection, not a fresh full acceptance run.

### Existing behavior to preserve

- Keep the existing Runner and its bwrap / Seatbelt sandbox. Do not switch to jiuwenbox or re-enable JiuwenSwarm host execution/file tools.
- Existing environment, execution and workspace functionality remains available through the legacy API behind the adapter proxy.
- Sandbox network settings already have permission-epoch rotation and persistent-kernel teardown behavior in the legacy API. Preserve and verify it rather than treating it as missing.
- Some L1 contract cases already exist, including sandbox network and package-source settings. The historical claim of 21 uncovered rows must be recalculated against current main.

### Remaining scope

- [ ] Inventory every interface row from #96, including the expanded Runner-specific environment paths. Record its current owner, downstream target, existing coverage and remaining work. Preserve the original interface scope; explicitly justify any row requiring no migration.
- [ ] Complete adapter routing and necessary adaptation for local Runner environments, environment setup/revisions, execution records/status/logs/cancellation, kernel teardown, workspace listing/files/sync/deletion, and local Runner list/detail/connect/probe. Replace reliance on the generic legacy API fallback for this scope with explicit ownership and dispatch; reuse existing implementation where possible instead of rewriting the Runner.
- [ ] Implement the required path rewriting (`/api/environments*` to Runner `/environments*`) and dispatch of `/api/runners/:id/...`, preserving authentication, request/response contracts and errors.
- [ ] Complete `agent-activity` aggregation across Runner executions/transfers, JiuwenSwarm cron/schedules and adapter-owned state, including logs and cancellation. Current main aggregates legacy API stores; that alone does not establish the requested integration.
- [ ] Trace and complete configuration persistence and propagation for sandbox network settings and package-source settings. Verify Runner behavior after saving, permission-epoch rotation and invalidation of previous sandbox authorization where required by #96; preserve existing kernel teardown behavior. Explicitly document the intended epoch behavior for package-source changes and resolve any discrepancy with #91/#96.
- [ ] Evaluate whether the `agent-activity` wrapper can be eliminated; record the conclusion and retain only necessary adaptation.

### Boundaries and dependencies

Local Runner environments, execution and workspace only. Remote-host and NPU implementation remains in #104. Coordinate shared routing/dispatch contracts with that issue without absorbing its scope. Adapter core and settings contracts relate to #87 and #91; downstream consumers include #97 and #102.

The sandbox choice is already settled: retain Runner execution and bwrap / Seatbelt.

### Acceptance

- [ ] Publish a current interface-by-interface coverage matrix for all rows inherited from #96. Each row has an L1 contract diff case or an explicit, justified "no migration needed" classification. Include write operations such as connect, probe, install, uninstall and delete, not just reads.
- [ ] Relevant execution/activity/cancellation and settings-related events have L2 golden traces, with intentional differences documented.
- [ ] Register and run E2E journeys covering environment creation and dependency installation/uninstallation, execution status/logs/cancellation, kernel teardown, workspace inspection/cleanup, and aggregated activity/timer cancellation on the JiuwenSwarm stack.
- [ ] Verify sandbox network-policy changes reach actual Runner execution, out-of-allowlist access is refused, epoch changes do not reuse previous sandbox authorization, and package-source changes affect subsequent package operations. Apply the baseline/assertion and security-case review rules from #84.
- [ ] Demonstrate that the scoped routes use the intended explicit routing/ownership rather than silently succeeding through the generic legacy fallback.
- [ ] Record the wrapper decision, candidate SHA, executed test results and any remaining gaps. Do not mark complete while inherited acceptance items remain uncovered, failed, blocked or skipped.

### References

- Original scope and discussion: #96
- Migration architecture and test layers: #84
- Current routing: `services/adapter/src/sciencediscovery_adapter/app.py`
- Current settings and activity handlers: `services/api/src/http/index.ts`

items.author: yuanzhou75
items.body:
Closes #1540

## What changes

A corrupt, truncated or simply wrong file uploaded to `POST /api/projects/<id>/research-package/inspect` or `.../import` answered `500 {"error":"Internal server error"}`: the decompressor's `Z_DATA_ERROR` / `Z_BUF_ERROR` and the archive parser's own refusal sentences were never classified, so the log line was `unclassified_request_error` and the dialog showed an internal error for the caller's own file.

`services/api/src/http/research-package-refusal.ts` maps them, and the global handler asks it before the generic branch:

| input | answer |
| --- | --- |
| random bytes / a file that is not gzip (`Z_DATA_ERROR`, `incorrect header check`, `not in gzip format`) | `400` `RESEARCH_PACKAGE_INVALID` |
| a truncated archive (`Z_BUF_ERROR`, `unexpected end of file`) | `400` `RESEARCH_PACKAGE_TRUNCATED` |
| a package the parser refused (bad manifest, checksum mismatch, unlisted entry, unsafe path, ...) | `400` `RESEARCH_PACKAGE_INVALID`, with the parser's sentence in parentheses |
| a metadata entry over its bound | `413` `RESEARCH_PACKAGE_TOO_LARGE` |

Each answer carries an `error` sentence the import dialog can show — "This file is not a valid research package: it ends before the archive does." — instead of an internal-error string, so the two endpoints now behave like the refusals that already work (`507` capacity, `409 SESSION_EVIDENCE_LOCKED`).

**The exception list is deliberate.** The refusal sentences are named one by one rather than "any error from the parser is the caller's fault": exporter-side faults (`A synchronous export cannot stream package objects`, `Package object size changed while hashing`), filesystem failures (`ENOSPC`, `EACCES`, ...) and every failure outside the two upload paths keep their `500`. The direction of the trade is written in the module: a refusal the parser adds later keeps its `500` until it is classified here, which is the safe way to be wrong.

## What I ran

- `node --import tsx --test src/research-package-invalid.test.ts` (new, api) — **4/4 pass**. The endpoint test posts the four payloads #1540 measured — 64 KiB of random bytes, an archive truncated to half, a 12-byte gzip header, `{"hello":"world"}` — to **both** endpoints (8 requests) and asserts `400`, a stable `code`, an `error` sentence containing "not a valid research package", and that the body is not `Internal server error`.
- `node --import tsx --test src/research-package-http.test.ts` (existing, api) — **29/29 pass**, so the `413` / `507` / `409` answers that already existed are unaffected.
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api typecheck` — clean.
- Mutation: deleting the new branch from the global handler turns the endpoint test red with exactly the reported symptom — `inspect: 64 KiB of random bytes answered 500 {"error":"Internal server error"}` — and restoring it brings the suite back to 4/4.
- Classifier unit tests pin both directions: the parser's refusals map to 4xx, and an exporter fault, `ENOSPC` and a non-upload path stay `undefined` (500).

## Scope

Backend only: no client change and no visual change, so no screenshots. The dialog already renders `error` from a 4xx package refusal.

Files: `services/api/src/http/index.ts` (the branch, 7 lines), `services/api/src/http/research-package-refusal.ts` (new), `services/api/src/research-package-invalid.test.ts` (new). None of them is in #1521, whose change is in `packages/research-package/src/index.ts` and `services/api/src/research-snapshots.ts`, so the two PRs do not collide.
items.head: i1540-invalid-package-4xx
items.title: fix(api): answer a 4xx for a package the parser refused

items.author: yuanzhou75
items.body:
Closes #1533.

The request catch-all decides whether a failure was the caller's mistake by matching words in the error message, and answers `400` with that message as the body (`services/api/src/http/index.ts`: `isKnownClientInputError(error)` → `sendError(response, 400, message)`). An internal fault whose text happens to say "cannot", "invalid" or "must" therefore reaches the client as a client error, carrying JavaScript that was never written for a reader. #1520's import did exactly that:

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'match')
```

matched /cannot/, so the dialog showed that sentence and the status said the caller was wrong while the server was.

## What changed — one file, no change to the catch-all

`services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts` gains two gates, both consulted before the wording list:

- `isRuntimeFault` answers `false` for `TypeError`, `RangeError`, `ReferenceError`, `EvalError`. They are the interpreter reporting a defect in this server, so their message is not evidence about the caller. The three shapes #1533 names (`Cannot read properties of undefined`, `Invalid array length`, `Cannot convert undefined or null to object`) are pinned by a test.
- `quotesInterpreterFault` answers `false` for any `Error` whose message is one of the engine's own sentences, because a handler that re-wraps `cause.message` keeps the text and loses the class. It covers the `Cannot read|set properties of undefined|null` family, `Cannot convert undefined or null to object` / `a BigInt value to a number` / `object to primitive value`, `Cannot create property … on string|number|symbol`, `Cannot destructure …`, `Cannot use 'in' operator …`, `is not a function` / `is not iterable` / `is not defined`, `Invalid array length|string length`, `Maximum call stack size exceeded`, `Assignment to constant variable`. One representative sentence per pattern is pinned by a test; the patterns keep the part that makes the wording unmistakable, so a validator sentence (`after_ms must be a positive integer`) does not match.
- `SyntaxError` stays a client error: a body that does not parse is the caller's own bytes.
- A plain `Error` whose text is ordinary prose keeps the existing wording rules, because that list is a record of what the legacy validators say — deleting it would turn every one of their `400`s into a `500`, which is the opposite failure.

**There is no edit to `services/api/src/http/index.ts`.** That matters for two open pull requests: #1545 adds a branch to the same `else if` chain (`researchPackageRefusal`), and #1548 rewrites the same chain for its own version of this issue. Keeping the fix in the classifier means this one cannot conflict with either, and it is also the narrowest place that holds the rule. #1548 is not touched, closed or commented on here.

## Honest boundary

The guarantee this change makes is: **no interpreter-raised fault, and no error carrying an interpreter sentence, is answered `400` or echoed.** Those get `500` with `{"error":"Internal server error"}`, and the original text goes to the `unclassified_request_error` log line.

What is still not covered: an `Error` thrown by our own code whose message is ordinary prose containing "cannot", "must" or "invalid" but does not look like engine text — `cannot open the catalog database`, say — is still answered `400` with that text. A prose list cannot tell an internal sentence from a validator's; closing that residue means giving the legacy validators typed errors (`ApiStatusError`) instead of prose, across the stores. The `specialists` routes already do this with their own exact-wording table; the shared catch-all does not.

## Evidence

`services/api/src/http/error-classification.test.ts` — three cases, one added here: "a plain Error quoting the engine's own sentence is not client input either". Sixteen engine sentences (including a prefixed one, `Research package import failed: Cannot read properties of undefined …`) are `false` on a plain `Error`; five legacy sentences that do match the old list (`after_ms must be a positive integer`, `… cannot be deleted`, `… does not match …`, `Unsafe skill package path: …`) stay `true`; `SyntaxError` stays `true`.

`services/api/src/http/internal-error-http.test.ts` — drives the route with a fault thrown once from inside the request handler, the way a store failure surfaces. Two cases: a `TypeError` and a plain `Error` carrying the same sentence. Each must answer

1. `500` with the body `{"error":"Internal server error"}`,
2. free of the interpreter's sentence (`reading 'match'`, `Cannot read properties`), and
3. accompanied by an `unclassified_request_error` line, asserted against the real `apiLog`.

The same file keeps a legacy validator rejection (`Specialist name is required`) at `400` with its own wording, so a future change cannot quiet the whole path instead of narrowing it.

**Mutation:** removing `if (quotesInterpreterFault(error.message)) return false;` and nothing else makes the new unit case fail (`expected false, actual true`, on the first engine sentence) and the plain-`Error` route case fail (`# pass 2 / # fail 1`); restored, the file bytes match the commit and both files pass. The mutated run was filtered to these two files, so it says nothing about other suites.

**No validator's `400` turns into a 500:** every string literal in `services/api/src` and `packages/*/src` (461 files, 59,286 literals without expressions, `*.test.ts`/`*.spec.ts` excluded) was classified by the previous and the current classifier; the number whose answer changed is **0**. That is the check behind keeping the prose list: the repository does not contain a message that the new shapes swallow.

## Checks on this head (`f9da0b2b`)

- `pnpm exec tsc -p services/api --noEmit` → exit 0
- `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` → exit 0
- `error-classification.test.ts` → 4 passed
- `internal-error-http.test.ts` → 3 passed
- neighbour suite `specialists-http.test.ts` (same classifier, 400 wording and a coded `node:sqlite` fault) → 17 passed
- `test/source-test-map.json` is unchanged: the new file is a route test beside its source, and the classifier already has its unit test.

Not verified here: the full `UT`/`ST` layers, `L1`/`L2`, `merge-gate` and a real backend — CI is their evidence. The repository's tests declare `os:linux`; the runs above were on this host with the declarations honoured.

No user-visible surface changes: this is the status code and body of a failure path, and no stylesheet or component is touched.

items.body:
Closes #1543

## What changes

A workspace file whose current provenance revision has no `contentHash` has no address a preview could name: its size is booked in `unpinnedObjectBytes`, and the export hashes it while it copies. But `needed` collected every `record.workspace.map((file) => file.objectPath)`, so `""` entered the CAS work set, `cas.storedSize("")` threw, and the catch recorded

```
cas::unavailable source object
```

— a limitation the dialog renders verbatim (`apps/web/src/research-package/ResearchPackageActions.tsx:345`), five entries for a package that declares four, and the extra one names an internal concept with an empty address.

`needed` now skips an entry that has no address, with the reason in a comment beside it. Nothing else moves: the file still counts once towards the estimate through `unpinnedObjectBytes`, and the export still writes it with a real address and lists it in the inventory. The two `cas:`-pushing sites (`research-snapshots.ts:468` for a streamed export, `:874` in the sizing loop) are both fed from that set, so the filter covers both.

## The assertion the issue asks for

The new test builds a Session with exactly one hash-less workspace file, then previews and exports it:

- the preview's limitations **equal in number** the export's `omissions` — this is the “预览 5 条 = 实际 4 条” difference in the report;
- no limitation starts with `cas:`;
- the file's size is still in `unpinnedObjectBytes`, so the estimate did not lose bytes;
- the export still carries the file, addressed with a 64-hex `objectPath`.

Without the fix the same test shows the issue's line verbatim —
`cas::unavailable source object` — and with it the preview and the export agree.

## What I ran

- `node --import tsx --test src/research-package-preview-omissions.test.ts` (new) — **1/1 pass**.
- Mutation: putting `record.workspace.map((file) => file.objectPath)` back turns it red with the reported line; restoring the fix is green.
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` and `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api typecheck` — both clean.
- `changed-path-check` — `research-snapshots.ts` is an existing file, so the policy reports it as a warning rather than a blocking “added source has no test mapping”.

## Scope

Backend only; no client change and no visual change, so no frames. `#1521` merged as `c06ce8bc` before this branch was cut, which is the file this one touches.

items.author: agent-ci-infra-bot[bot]
items.body:
## What changed

Managed environment setup now retries the failures the pinned micromamba actually reports, and mocked lanes stop provisioning a base they never use.

- `services/runner/src/environment-store.ts`: the micromamba download retries network-class failures (timeouts, resets, HTTP 429/5xx) with a fresh `AbortController` and 120 s timer per attempt plus jittered exponential backoff. SHA-256 verification and writes stay single-attempt. The starter bootstrap retries a network-class `micromamba create` on a fresh revision prefix with the 180 s per-attempt limit; its classifier now recognizes the pinned 2.8.1 transcripts (`Download error (6/7/28/35/56)`, `Could not connect to server`, `Failed to connect to`, `Transfer finalized, status: 408/429/5xx`, `Timeout was reached`, connection refused/reset) and a SIGTERM per-attempt kill. `ERR_CHILD_PROCESS_STDIO_MAXBUFFER`, solver, disk and permission failures still fail once.
- `test/support/tagged/retry-runner.mjs`: `E2E_SCIENTIFIC_ENVS=1` is decided from batch entries, not the batch key. J3 and J5 assert a ready base, so both split keys (`mocked-standard-config-global` and `-2`) and retries work; other mocked lanes use `0`. J5 keeps the real layer from regressing and was accepted as necessary in review.
- Tests use captured libmamba transcripts, assert a marker in the failed prefix is removed, cover 503/timeout/DNS/reset and the per-attempt kill, and drive `installManagedMicromamba` itself through one transient timeout. The CI skill and `.ci/README.md` now describe lane-scoped provisioning.

## Verification

- `pnpm -C services/runner typecheck`: passed.
- `environment-store.test.ts`: 41/41 passed.
- `retry-environment.test.mjs`: 8/8 passed.
- `pnpm test:tagged:selftest`: 84 Node tests passed (1 skipped) plus 8 Python tests.
- `pnpm ci:l1`: planned 4, executed 4, passed 4.
- `pnpm ci:ut`: 8888 identities frozen, 0 executed, preflight `BUBBLEWRAP_UNAVAILABLE`.
- `pnpm ci:e2e -- --shard standard-config`: 75 identities frozen, 0 executed, preflight `BUBBLEWRAP_UNAVAILABLE`. This non-root container has no `bwrap` and cannot enable unprivileged user namespaces. Frozen-plan replay still gives the J3 lane `1` and both non-J3 lanes `0`.

## Risk

A retryable failure can extend worst-case setup by the bounded backoff plus per-attempt budgets. Permanent failures do not wait. UT and mocked E2E still need a bwrap-capable CI runner.

Closes #1531

### Tests

```
pnpm -C services/runner typecheck && node --import tsx --test services/runner/src/environment-store.test.ts && node --test test/support/tagged/tests/retry-environment.test.mjs
```

Reported by the agent; the platform did not rerun it.

items.body: The session column's two headings — 项目 and 会话 — were set at 12px regular, smaller than the Project and Session names under them, so they read as captions of the list rather than as its sections. They now take those names' 14px, and stay **regular**: the heading is a quiet caption, and the first thing the eye should find in the column is the name of a Project or a Session. The controls that belong to a row now wait for the pointer: - 项目's 新建项目 `+` — at the heading's own size (14px) and weight (400); - a Project row's 在项目中新建会话 `+` and its `⋯` menu; - a Session row's `⋯` menu. They float over the row's right end instead of holding width in it, so a long name keeps its full width at rest and does not re-truncate as the pointer enters; a Session's clock steps aside for its `⋯` at the same moment. Hiding is done with `opacity`, never `display: none` or `visibility: hidden`: every control stays in the tab order and comes back on `:hover`, `:focus-within` or its own `:focus-visible`. A device that reports no hover capability (`@media (hover: none)`) gets them outright, because it has no pointer to wait for and a first tap that only opened the row would never reach them. The fold of a Project is its name: the `^`/`v` glyph is gone from `apps/desktop/src/views/Sidebar.tsx`, and pressing the name — by pointer, Enter or Space — folds and unfolds the sessions under it, with `aria-expanded` carrying the state. ## Where this comes from The owner asked for exactly this on 2026-11-27, in PR-bot-3号's chat: > 我需要项目旁边的“+”默认隐藏，鼠标悬浮时，才有“+”，且字号和项目两个字一样大，但不用加粗，项目两个字也不用加粗了；然后真实项目旁边的^和v去除，只需要点击项目名字就可以实现展开或者收起；项目和会话后面的功能选项也是要默认隐藏，鼠标悬浮上去再出现。 ## The strip over a long Project name The strip floats over the row's right end, so it covers the last **54px** of a Project's name box (measured: label 54→231, strip 177→235 in the 296px column). A transparent backdrop would let the name's glyphs show through the `+` and `⋯`; instead, on the same reveal that shows the strip, a mask fades that band of the name out: ```css .side-row.side-project:hover .side-project-toggle .label, .side-row.side-project:focus-within .side-project-toggle .label { mask-image: linear-gradient(to right, #000 calc(100% - 60px), transparent calc(100% - 50px)); } ``` A mask and not a `padding-right`: it paints no differently laid out text, so the name does not re-truncate as the pointer arrives — the width stays 177px at rest and under the pointer. ## Measured (one browser run, same DOM) | | at rest | over 项目 | over a Project row | over a Session row | |---|---|---|---|---| | 项目 / 会话 | 14px / 400 | 14px / 400 | 14px / 400 | 14px / 400 | | 新建项目 `+` | 14px / 400, opacity 0 | **opacity 1, clickable** | opacity 0 | opacity 0 | | Project row strip | opacity 0 | opacity 0 | **opacity 1, clickable** | opacity 0 | | Session row strip | opacity 0 | opacity 0 | opacity 0 | **opacity 1, clickable** | | Project name width | 177px | 177px | 177px | 177px | | `^`/`v` chevrons in the DOM | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | A Project whose name overflows the column: name box 54→231, strip 177→235, so 54px lie under the strip, `mask-image` is `none` at rest and the gradient above under the pointer, and the name still truncates (so the fade sits over a name that was already cut, not over a full one). ## Screenshots Component-level renders of the real `Sidebar` against the app's own `apps/desktop/src/styles/index.css`: one harness, one run, one fixture (two Projects with sessions, two standalone Sessions). The pointer arrives with a real `page.hover()`, never by writing CSS. This is not a recording of the full app — the Electron window is not automated in this environment. Pinned to the storage commit `d04cf9577784c9e157fc7c3de39dbd9dd5129cb0` (`shots/sidebar-labels/`): | zh-CN | | |---|---| | at rest | ![zh rest](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/d04cf9577784c9e157fc7c3de39dbd9dd5129cb0/shots/sidebar-labels/states2-zh-rest.png) | | over 项目 | ![zh hover label](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/d04cf9577784c9e157fc7c3de39dbd9dd5129cb0/shots/sidebar-labels/states2-zh-hover-label.png) | | over a Project row | ![zh hover project](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/d04cf9577784c9e157fc7c3de39dbd9dd5129cb0/shots/sidebar-labels/states2-zh-hover-project.png) | | over a Session row | ![zh hover session](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/d04cf9577784c9e157fc7c3de39dbd9dd5129cb0/shots/sidebar-labels/states2-zh-hover-session.png) | | over a Project whose name overflows | ![zh long name hover](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/d04cf9577784c9e157fc7c3de39dbd9dd5129cb0/shots/sidebar-labels/long-name-zh-hover.png) | | en | | |---|---| | at rest | ![en rest](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/d04cf9577784c9e157fc7c3de39dbd9dd5129cb0/shots/sidebar-labels/states2-en-rest.png) | | over Projects | ![en hover label](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/d04cf9577784c9e157fc7c3de39dbd9dd5129cb0/shots/sidebar-labels/states2-en-hover-label.png) | | over a Project row | ![en hover project](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/d04cf9577784c9e157fc7c3de39dbd9dd5129cb0/shots/sidebar-labels/states2-en-hover-project.png) | | over a Session row | ![en hover session](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/d04cf9577784c9e157fc7c3de39dbd9dd5129cb0/shots/sidebar-labels/states2-en-hover-session.png) | | over a Project whose name overflows | ![en long name hover](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/d04cf9577784c9e157fc7c3de39dbd9dd5129cb0/shots/sidebar-labels/long-name-en-hover.png) | Every frame was taken behind two gates: all `` elements fully loaded (`complete` and `naturalWidth > 0`) and no request answered 4xx, or the run aborts and writes nothing. ## Tests - `apps/desktop` UT — `tests/sidebar.test.tsx`: **18 pass / 0 fail**. The file is tagged `os:linux`; on this Windows host it was run as a copy with only the platform tag changed to `os:windows`, deleted afterwards. Two new assertions hold the strip over a long name (both reveal paths carry the mask) and the no-hover fallback (the three controls are named and set to `opacity: 1` with `pointer-events: auto`). - Desktop mocked E2E — the repository's own `apps/desktop/e2e` suite, all of it: **235 passed / 0 failed**. This is the job the PR's checks skip (`desktop_specs = none` for a source-only change) and the merge queue runs in full; on the previous head it failed three of its cases, all of them clicks and assertions this PR now moves with the behaviour: - `projects.spec.ts` asserted `toBeHidden()` on the two Project controls; `opacity: 0` is still "visible" to Playwright's `checkVisibility()`-based check, so it now asserts the mechanism (`opacity` + `pointer-events`) on the strip that hides them, and that the strip comes back on hover; - `sessions.spec.ts` clicked 会话菜单 and 新建项目 without pointing at the row first — Playwright hit-tests a click point before it moves the mouse, so the press landed on the Session's clock and on the 项目 label. `research-package.spec.ts` had the same pattern in four places, and `export-preview-states.spec.ts` (a spec that landed on `main` after this branch's base) in one. All of them now arrive on the row first through `revealAndClick()` in `fixtures.ts`, which is what a reader does too. - Run here with Playwright 1.65.1 and its bundled Chromium (the pinned 1.61.1 browser build could not be downloaded on this host); CI pins 1.61.1 and the merge-queue job runs the suite there in full. - `tsc -p apps/desktop/tsconfig.json --noEmit`: clean. - The previous head (`9c3676c6`) failed CI, and both failures were this branch's fault, both from taking two files from an older base than `main`. The head was rebuilt on current `main` (`c06ce8bc`); those two files are now current `main` plus this change only, and the file list is eight. - `UT` — `hint-contrast-surfaces.test.ts`, three cases. `apps/desktop/src/styles/design.css` had been carried over from before the `--text-hint` token change, so it reverted nine `color: var(--text-hint)` declarations to raw hex (`#808080` on the settings surface is 3.95:1). Real failure, not the worker crash I first blamed it on. - `Desktop UI-ST and mocked E2E` — `settings-interactions.spec.ts` 专家 › "a prompt example opens a new bound session without submitting a Run". `apps/desktop/e2e/fixtures.ts` had been carried over from before the session request-body passthrough, so the mocked `POST /api/projects/:id/sessions` dropped the body and the Session came back without `specialistId`. - `merge-gate` was red because of those two. `CodeCheck (GitCode)` is red on every head here and is not a required check. What was run here, on a tree of current `main` (`c06ce8bc`) plus these eight files: - `apps/desktop/tests/hint-contrast-surfaces.test.ts` — **7/7** with the new `design.css` (the same file is 3 failures with the old one). - `settings-interactions.spec.ts` 专家 › "a prompt example opens a new bound session" — **fails** with the old `fixtures.ts`, **passes** with the corrected one, same tree, same browser, nothing else changed. - The whole mocked desktop suite — **254 passed, 0 failed** (Playwright 1.65.1 with its bundled Chromium; CI pins 1.61.1). - `apps/desktop/tests/sidebar.test.tsx` — **18/18**. ## Answers to the review on `53965241` - **F1 — hover-only controls break the mocked desktop E2E** (`design.css:407`, `design.css:283` → `sessions.spec.ts:107`, `sessions.spec.ts:271`). Confirmed, and fixed on the specs rather than by putting the controls back: the owner asked for them hidden until hover, so the tests move with the behaviour (`revealAndClick`). A no-hover device is covered by the `@media (hover: none)` rule above rather than by keeping an always-visible control. The whole mocked suite now passes, not only those two specs, including `research-package.spec.ts`, which the finding also flagged. - **F2 — `opacity: 0` is still "visible" to Playwright** (`projects.spec.ts:102-103`). Fixed: the case asserts `opacity` and `pointer-events` on `.side-actions` at rest, and that both come back on hover. (`opacity` is a group property, so the buttons inside report `1` while the strip paints nothing; the strip is what the case has to read.) - **F3 — the action bar covers the tail of a truncated Project name** (`design.css:405`). Fixed with the mask above, measured at 54px of overlap, and shown with a name that overflows the column, hovered, in both languages. - **Empty column, no visible way to add a Project.** The owner's requirement is that 新建项目 waits for the pointer; the 项目 heading is what reveals it, and the composer's project chip still creates one. Left as asked, and called out here rather than changed. - **`#777` on `#f5f5f5` and #1491.** #1491 owns that colour on the same declaration; this PR does not touch it, and whichever lands second rebases. ## Scope The two headings and the hover behaviour of the controls beside a row, plus the desktop E2E specs that press those controls. No colour change (`#777` stays), no change to the rows' heights or padding, no change to the `⋯` menus' items, and the 新建会话 / 导入会话 buttons above the list are untouched.

items.body:
Closes #1485.

The settings surface was modal for the pointer and not for the keyboard: opening it left `document.activeElement` on the 设置 button in the rail, the first Tab walked the page behind the backdrop, and Escape closed the panel without returning focus anywhere useful (#1485 measured 23 Tabs before the dialog was reached and 47 before the focus loop fell out to `BODY`).

**What changed** (four files: `SystemSettingsDialog.tsx`, `SettingsModal.tsx`, the new `settings-keyboard.spec.ts` and the map registration; +324/−3 across the pull request)

- the panel is now `<section role="dialog" tabIndex={-1} ref>` and an effect moves focus into it on open, remembering the element that opened it;
- a keydown trap keeps Tab inside the panel: at the last stop Tab wraps to the first, at the first Shift+Tab wraps to the last, and the panel itself counts as one end so the very first Tab enters the content instead of leaving;
- the focusable list is filtered with `getClientRects()` so hidden items are skipped, and it includes `summary`, which this panel really has (`McpServers.tsx:533`, `SandboxDirectSettings.tsx:147`, `SkillGitImportView.tsx:316`);
- Escape still closes through the existing window listener and `claimsEscape`; the trap's cleanup returns focus to the opener when that element is still connected (the skill-import and MCP-trial paths navigate away instead, so they are left alone);
- the panel keeps holding the boundary for the surfaces that trap nothing (添加模型 and the two skill dialogs), while a nested surface that does trap Tab claims the key first and the panel leaves it alone through `event.defaultPrevented` — that is `McpModal`, and also the skill drawer inside `SettingsModal` (`SettingsModal.tsx:58-72`), whose listener now sits on the drawer surface instead of on `document`. Without that move the panel handler, being closer to the target, ran first and swallowed the drawer's wrap: from 设置 › 专家 › 新增专家 › 指定可用能力 › 配置技能, Tab off the drawer's 确定 walked the form behind it instead of wrapping. The 新增专家 / 编辑专家 screens themselves are panel pages (`specialist-subpage`), not dialogs, so nothing there traps.

**Where focus lands, and why** — on the panel container, not on its first control. That is what `McpModal.tsx:89-109` and `SkillDialog.tsx:49` already do, and this surface should behave like those two rather than like a fourth variant. Two alternatives were built and photographed before choosing: the first focusable control here is the 收起侧栏 button (Enter collapses the navigation), and focusing the selected navigation item (`aria-current="page"`, 「通用」) would add a rule neither existing modal has. Switching to that second option later is a one-line change in the same effect, if it is wanted after seeing the frames.

**Evidence** — `apps/desktop/e2e/settings-keyboard.spec.ts`, six mocked desktop cases on real Tab presses:

1. opening the panel puts focus inside it, and the first Tab lands on a control inside it;
2. Shift+Tab from the panel goes to the last stop, Tab from the last wraps to the first, and 60 consecutive Tabs never leave the panel;
3. keyboard open, focus inside, Escape: focus is back on the 设置 button (`data-guide="settings"`);
4. with 添加模型 open over the panel, twenty Tabs stay inside the panel and reach the nested dialog's own controls;
5. the backdrop starts at the rail's right edge, the rail is still clickable, and the page behind accepts no pointer;
6. with the skill drawer open, twelve Tabs from its 确定 stay inside `.specialist-drawer` instead of walking the form behind it.

On the pre-fix source the first three fail and the backdrop case passes. Mutation runs, each reverting one mechanism only: dropping `node.focus()` fails case 1; dropping the keydown listener fails case 2; dropping `previous.focus()` fails case 3; dropping the "panel holds focus" Shift+Tab branch fails case 2; putting the nested stand-aside back fails the 添加模型 case (that run was filtered to the single case, so it shows 1 failed and says nothing about the other four). The source was restored between runs and matched the committed bytes.

**Frames** — 1440×900 at 2×, mocked desktop harness, the same steps in every frame: Tab to 设置 in the rail, Enter to open, and the focus ring is the browser's own (no styling or annotation added). Before is `a70ef94c` (main, no fix), after is `ff611c9c`. These twelve frames are byte-identical (SHA-256, 12 of 12) to the set rendered before the nested-dialog fix landed, and the only later commit (`6ee27008`) touches `settings-keyboard.spec.ts` alone, so no pixel in these three states moved across the review round.

| state | before (zh) | after (zh) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| on open | ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/34e60614745d9fc5ea4bc1d8f27be55bab3a3a3b/docs/screenshots/1485/ff611c9c/before/on-open-zh.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/34e60614745d9fc5ea4bc1d8f27be55bab3a3a3b/docs/screenshots/1485/ff611c9c/after/on-open-zh.png) |
